jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor, Environmental, you will play a vital role in protecting the environment while enabling safe and sustainable mining operations. You will contribute to the monitoring, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and supporting informed decision-making across site.
This is an opportunity to directly influence environmental performance by delivering accurate data, strengthening monitoring systems, and supporting continuous improvement initiatives in a dynamic and complex operational environment.
As part of our team, you will
You will work both independently and collaboratively to deliver high-quality environmental monitoring outcomes, including:
You will also contribute to continuous improvement and risk management through:
Managing and leading environment monitoring programs to ensure compliance with regulatory and company requirements.
Collecting, analysing, and interpreting environmental data to support operational decisions.
Maintaining and administering monitoring equipment to ensure data accuracy and reliability.
Preparing reports and documentation for internal stakeholders and regulatory submission.
Working across a diverse stakeholder environment, you will:
Support environmental awareness and training initiatives across the operation and the Lihirian communities.
Collaborate closely with environmental technicians and operational teams across site.Liaise with external stakeholders such as regulators, community representatives, and service providers.
Engage with internal stakeholders including mining, waste management, social performance, laboratories, and technical teams.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this role, you will bring a strong balance of technical capability, analytical thinking, and stakeholder engagement skills:
A tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Chemistry, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience in environmental monitoring within mining or a similar operational environment.
Experience in environmental software and data systems, including Geographical Information Systems (GIS), ArcGIS, and environmental monitoring databases preferably MonitorPro.
Technical knowledge and experience managing hydrometeorological monitoring programs and associated equipment.
Technical knowledge in air quality monitoring programs and systems.
Experience in freshwater ecological monitoring and environmental data interpretation.
Capability to evaluate potential environmental impacts of development projects and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
Experience conducting environmental site audits, inspections, and ensuring compliance with environmental standards and regulatory requirements.
In addition, you will bring:
Strong analytical capability, including data interpretation, reporting, and data-driven decision making.
Proven experience contributing to environmental monitoring programs and continuous improvement initiatives.
Effective problem-solving skills, with the ability to work collaboratively to deliver practical and sustainable solutions.
Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, including the ability to influence outcomes and build effective relationships.
You will also demonstrate:
A proactive and solutions-focused mindset.
Strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise and deliver in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
High levels of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.
Your work environment
Based at Lihir Operations, you will operate within a dynamic and technically diverse environment, working alongside multidisciplinary teams across mining, sustainability, and operational functions.
This role provides exposure to a unique and complex environmental setting, including a variety of monitoring programs such as marine and land-based environmental systems, offering strong opportunities to build both technical capability and career experience.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 (day shift), Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be part of a global organisation committed to sustainability, safety, and operational excellence.
This role offers:
Exposure to diverse and impactful environmental monitoring programs.
The opportunity to work in a unique and technically challenging environment.
Collaboration with multidisciplinary teams and key external stakeholders.
Ongoing development opportunities to grow your technical and professional capability.
Join a team where your work contributes to protecting the environment while supporting responsible and sustainable mining operations.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

This organisation is recognised as a key player operating within a dynamic and rapidly expanding energy sector in Papua New Guinea. Committed to aligning people strategies with corporate objectives, the company prides itself on driving talent acquisition, retention, and leadership capability during significant organisational scaling. Operating across a diverse footprint that includes head office environments, power plant operations, and rural mini-grid developments, the organisation focuses on building a high-performance, safety-first culture in a fast-paced, growing environment.
This is a perfect opportunity if you are a highly strategic, results-driven professional with a strong background in change management and multi-site HR operations. This role is ideal for those looking to elevate their career by managing the execution of complex organisational development initiatives—from workforce planning to employee relations—directly impacting sustainable business growth and compliance across all local operations.

As a strategic HR partner, you will collaborate with business leaders to accelerate headcount growth and secure critical talent across both corporate and operational plant sites. Your focus will centre on managing the full talent lifecycle, executing performance evaluation frameworks, and utilising HR metrics to ensure immaculate, audit-ready compliance.

Strategic Partnership & Workforce Planning: Partner with business leaders to provide proactive advice on workforce planning, organisational design, and growth strategies to meet current and future business needs.

Industry & Growth Exposure: Proven track record supporting rapid corporate expansion and large-scale projects, ideally within the energy, resources, or industrial sectors.
Compliance & Technical Knowledge: Deep, comprehensive understanding of PNG Labor Laws, employment contracts, work permits, local tax, and superannuation regulations.
Strategic Competencies: Strong capabilities across strategic HR management, end-to-end talent lifecycles, change management, and organisational capability development.
Interpersonal & Cultural Savvy: High emotional intelligence with exceptional negotiation and conflict resolution skills to build trust across diverse corporate, industrial, expatriate, and local community teams.

Experienced Panel Manager
(The quality-control, no-comebacks kind)
Important: If you do not have proven panel shop or collision repair management experience, please do not submit your CV.
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our workshops and repair operations depend on accuracy, discipline, quality workmanship, and strong leadership.
We’re looking for an experienced Panel Manager to lead panel repair operations and make sure every job is managed properly from assessment through to completion.
This is not a role for someone who only understands the theory. We need someone who knows panel repairs, understands workshop flow, can manage tradesmen, and can keep quality, timelines, and customer expectations under control.
If your experience is limited, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the panel shop, including job allocation, repair planning, workflow, quality control, staff supervision, and customer/job updates.
That includes assessing repair requirements, coordinating panel beating and paint work, checking job cards, monitoring repair progress, managing parts requirements, and making sure vehicles are repaired to a high standard before delivery.
You’ll work closely with service advisors, parts teams, technicians, insurers, customers, and management to make sure each job is handled professionally and completed on time.
You’ll also be responsible for maintaining workshop discipline, safe work practices, productivity, and proper reporting.
The expectation is simple: manage the job properly, control the quality, deliver the vehicle properly.
Who This Suits
This role suits an experienced Panel Manager or senior panel repair professional with real workshop leadership experience.
You understand panel beating, collision repair, paint preparation, refinishing standards, repair estimates, job costing, parts coordination, and workshop scheduling.
You know how to manage people, not just jobs. You can lead tradesmen, control workflow, deal with pressure, and make sure standards do not drop when the workshop gets busy.
You should be confident checking repair quality, identifying poor workmanship, solving bottlenecks, and making sure vehicles do not leave the shop with avoidable defects.
You keep your paperwork accurate, your team accountable, and your standards high.
If people already rely on you to bring order to a busy panel shop, this will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates a busy automotive business with real volume, recognised global brands, and high customer expectations.
You’ll be working with experienced teams who understand that good panel work is not just about fixing damage — it is about safety, appearance, customer confidence, and protecting the reputation of the business.
This is a role where leadership matters, quality is noticed, and strong workshop managers are taken seriously.

About the role
The Superintendent H&S – Underground is responsible for providing visible safety leadership and strategic H&S support to K92's Underground Operations.
The role partners with Underground operational leaders to identify, assess and control critical risks, strengthen operational discipline, improve workforce capability and ensure compliance with company standards and regulatory requirements.
The Superintendent H&S – Underground will spend significant time in the field engaging with leaders and work crews, verifying critical controls, coaching supervisors and supporting a proactive safety culture focused on learning, risk ownership and continuous improvement.

Provide visible and credible safety leadership across Underground Operations.
Develop strong working relationships with operational leaders, supervisors and work crews.
Promote a culture of personal accountability, risk ownership and continuous improvement.
Coach frontline leaders in effective field leadership, risk management and safety engagement practices.
Build leadership capability through coaching, mentoring and field-based learning.
Support the development of a positive reporting and learning culture.
Support the implementation and verification of fatal risk management and critical control programs.
Maintain oversight of underground risk registers, TARPs and critical risk management plans.
Facilitate risk assessments for high risk and non-routine work activities.
Monitor emerging risks and ensure effective controls are implemented and maintained.
Maintain a strong visible field presence underground.
Conduct workplace inspections, leadership interactions and task observations.
Verify compliance with site standards, procedures and critical control requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve operational discipline and workforce behaviours.
Lead investigations into significant and high potential incidents.
Verify corrective actions are practical, effective and sustainable.
Share lessons learned across the organisation.
Support the implementation and continual improvement of H&S management systems including SkyTrust.
Support the development, implementation and verification of H&S standards, critical control standards and safe work practices.
Participate in internal assurance activities and management system audits.
Monitor performance indicators and identify trends requiring intervention.
Support the development of underground safety leadership capability.
Assist with development and delivery of H&S training programs.
Mentor supervisors, safety representatives and emerging safety professionals.
Support underground emergency response preparedness.
Participate in emergency planning, exercises and reviews.
Assist with development of underground emergency procedures and response capability.
Ensure compliance with applicable PNG legislation, MRA requirements and company standards.
Support regulatory inspections and audits.
Prepare reports and documentation required by regulators and company management.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a tertiary qualification in relevant field with a minimum of 4 years’ experience as Safety Superintendent in Mining, Oil or Gas Industry. In addition to this, you will have most or all of the following.
Diploma or Degree in Occupational Health and Safety, Mining Engineering, or related discipline.
Minimum 5 years' experience in a senior H&S role within mining, including experience supporting underground operations.
Demonstrated experience leading incident investigations.
Training in ICAM or equivalent investigation methodology.
Training in auditing and assurance processes.
Underground metalliferous mining experience.
Current PNG Driver's Licence.
Emergency response experience.
Training and assessment qualifications.
Exposure to critical control management systems.

jobs.employer_address:

Lae, Morobe Province 411,
Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is responsible for carrying out electrical breakdown and preventative maintenance repairs on a wide range of mobile equipment’s including Light Vehicles, Boggers, Truck fleet, Excavators, Drills, Dozers, Graders, and support equipment.
Key Accountabilities
Performing scheduled and Breakdown maintenance on a large fleet of Underground Mining Equipment including Sandvik Drills, Trucks and Loaders with an ancillary fleet of CAT and Normet equipment.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment’s and machines.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment’s, and machines.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade certificate in Auto-electrical with at least 3-5 years of relevant work experience in heavy industry preferably mining environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Demonstrated experience in maintaining electrical equipment in the mobile fleet including Drills, Trucks, Loaders as well as Light vehicles, Dozers, excavators, graders,
Relevant experience in automotive air conditioning systems.
Self-motivated with ability to always work autonomously.
Strong safety focus and sound knowledge of standard operating procedures.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

jobs.description:
POSITION TITLE: EXECUTIVE PRINCIPAL, BALIMO COLLEGE
AREA:
Education
LOCATION:
Balimo College, New Town, Balimo, Delta Fly District, Western Province PNG
TYPE / DURATION:
Full time, 1 year contract, with contract extension possible
REPORTING TO:
Chair, Balimo College Governing Council
About Balimo College:
Balimo College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality teaching, research and community engagement. The institute will foster pathways of teachers and health workers who are committed to improving access to vital services in Western Province. Balimo College will be a safe and supportive place for graduates and other professionals across the Western Province catchment region to return for life-long learning and ongoing professional development. The College will develop a community of education and health professionals committed to innovation, excellence and community advancement; by being the training College of choice for Papua New Guineans
Balimo College is an initiative of SDP implemented in partnership with KTF. SDP has a mandate to deliver development programs which provide lasting benefits to the people of Western Province. Our efforts are focused on Health, Education, Infrastructure and Agribusiness. We aim to supplement and complement the efforts of the Fly River Provincial Government (FRPG), in other words, help fill the gaps in the existing systems.
Balimo College is recognised as a Higher Education Institute by the National Higher Technical Education Board of the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST). This recognition has been granted in accordance with the provisions of the Higher Education (General Provisions) Act 2014, as amended in 2020, under Section 14(1)(i) and 55(4)(a).
About the Role:
The Executive Principal is responsible for leading the strategic direction, operations, and administration of both the School of Teaching and the School of Nursing. Reporting to the Chair of the Governing Council, the GM will ensure that the College’s mission, vision, and goals are effectively upheld across all departments, ensuring high standards of education and community service. The GM will lead the executive team, including the Principals of both schools, and oversee all administrative, financial, and human resources functions.
The GM will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College and the principles by which it operates. The GM will have a firm understanding of the Western Province education and health contexts and the objectives of Balimo College to create pathways for rural communities into teaching and community health work.
Responsibilities:
Leadership & Strategy
Lead the strategic development and implementation of Balimo College’s vision, mission, and values.
Supervise and support the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing, ensuring alignment with institutional goals.
Foster collaboration between the schools to create a cohesive, innovative, and community-focused institution.
Establish and nurture a positive and inclusive college culture, promoting care, academic excellence, and integrity.
Drive initiatives to improve academic offerings, operational efficiency, and community engagement.
Operational Management
Ensure effective daily operations of Balimo College, including the coordination of academic programs, facilities, and student services.
Lead the College executive team to optimize the performance of both schools and streamline administrative processes.
Oversee the development and implementation of college policies, procedures, and systems in consultation with the two Principals, and in alignment with governing regulations and standards.
Coordinate the preparation of the academic calendar in collaboration with leadership teams.
Ensure compliance with PNG Department of Higher Education, Research, Science & Technology (DHERST) and other relevant authorities.
Human Resources and Capacity Building
Manage the recruitment, induction, and evaluation of staff in both schools in collaboration with the Principals and Governing Council.
Develop a performance management system and provide ongoing professional development opportunities for staff.
Foster leadership and career development among faculty and support staff.
Chair Staffing Committee meetings, overseeing decisions related to staffing structures, promotions, and performance.
Financial Oversight
Work with the Finance Manager and Finance, Audit & Risk Management Committee to develop and manage the College’s budget, ensuring financial sustainability.
Monitor and review financial performance, ensuring that spending aligns with the College’s strategic goals.
Act as a responsible signatory for financial decisions within the limits established by the Governing Council.
Academic Oversight
Ensure that the College’s educational programs meet high standards of quality and relevance to the community’s needs.
Oversee curriculum development and academic planning, in consultation with the two Principals, ensuring alignment with national and international standards.
Chair the Academic Board and receive reports from the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing in line with the Academic Board charter.
Foster partnerships with external stakeholders, including universities, government departments, and donors, to enhance the College’s programs and resources.
Community Engagement & Stakeholder Relations
Act as the primary spokesperson for Balimo College, building relationships with community leaders, government partners, and external partners.
Ensure active engagement with the local community to strengthen the College’s role as a hub for lifelong learning and professional development.
Promote and sustain a safe and inclusive environment for students, staff, and the broader community.
Risk Management & Compliance
Ensure adherence to all risk management, safety, and compliance requirements, particularly in workplace health and safety (WHS), child protection, Code of Conduct and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment.
Work with the Finance and Risk Management Committee to develop and implement a risk management framework.
Ensure that Balimo College operates in accordance with its safeguarding Policies, safeguarding the well-being of all students and staff.
Required Skills and Attributes:
Knowledge of:
A strong understanding of tertiary education and the specific challenges and opportunities in rural Papua New Guinea.
Experience in leadership roles within education, health or public sector institutions, preferably in PNG or similar contexts.
Proven financial management skills and experience managing budgets for educational institutions.
Familiarity with government policies and standards for tertiary education (DHERST, NDOE, PNG Nursing Council).
Leadership Abilities:
Demonstrated ability to lead, inspire, and manage teams across diverse functional areas.
Strong strategic thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to foster collaborative partnerships and manage stakeholder relationships effectively.
Formal Qualifications:
A Master’s degree in Education, Administration, or a related field.
Relevant professional experience in education leadership and management.
Personal Attributes:
A commitment to advancing education and health in rural PNG communities.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders.
High integrity, resilience, and the ability to lead by example. Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
Important Information:
Balimo College is a child safe organisation committed to the protection of people we serve. Our recruitment and selection procedures are designed to ensure we only recruit people who are suitable and aligned with our policies that ensure the safety of children and protection of all from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. All appointments are subject to appropriate background checks and screening and the successful candidate will be required to get a Working With Children check and/or a Police Certificate. We promote diversity and equality in all our practices and strongly encourage those with diverse backgrounds and/or disabilities to apply for positions with Balimo College.
How to Apply:
We encourage you to apply early. We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis. Qualified candidates will be contacted for an interview and the position will remain open until it is filled.

[email protected]
with the following documents attached:
A cover letter addressing the following:
Your interest in the position of Executive Principal – Balimo College
Your leadership philosophy
Your current resume
A copy of your Bachelor’s Degree (required)
A copy of your Master’s Degree (required)
At least one written reference

Position Title
Audit Manager
Reports To

Position Purpose
The Audit Manager is responsible for planning, executing, and completing audit engagements in accordance with
International Standards on Auditing (ISA)
, and for overseeing the preparation of
IFRS‑compliant financial statements
. The role requires strong technical capability, effective team leadership, and the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with clients, regulators, and internal stakeholders. The Audit Manager ensures high‑quality deliverables, efficient workflow management, and contributes to the firm’s reputation for excellence, independence, and integrity.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Planning & Execution
Lead the planning, risk assessment, and scoping of audit engagements in accordance with ISA.
Develop audit strategies, timelines, and resource plans for multiple concurrent assignments.
Review internal controls, identify key risks, and design appropriate audit procedures.
Ensure all audit work is properly documented, cross‑referenced, and compliant with firm methodology and professional standards.
Perform complex audit areas including revenue, financial instruments, estimates, provisions, and consolidations.
Financial Reporting (IFRS)
Oversee the preparation and review of
IFRS‑compliant financial statements
, including notes and disclosures.
Provide technical guidance on IFRS application, accounting treatments, and emerging standards.
Review client trial balances, general ledgers, and supporting schedules for completeness and accuracy.
Ensure financial statements meet regulatory, statutory, and industry‑specific reporting requirements.
Team Leadership & Staff Development
Supervise a small team of senior auditors, associates, and trainees.
Allocate work, monitor progress, and ensure timely completion of audit tasks.
Provide on‑the‑job coaching, technical training, and performance feedback.
Foster a culture of professionalism, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Client Relationship Management
Serve as the primary point of contact for clients during audit engagements.
Communicate audit findings, issues, and recommendations clearly and diplomatically.
Manage expectations, resolve issues promptly, and maintain strong professional relationships.
Present audit reports, management letters, and financial statements to client management and boards.
Quality Assurance & Compliance
Ensure all engagements comply with ISA, IFRS, the firm’s quality control policies, and ethical requirements.
Review working papers, audit evidence, and conclusions for accuracy and sufficiency.
Identify areas for process improvement and contribute to internal quality initiatives.
Uphold independence, confidentiality, and professional scepticism at all times.
Reporting to the Audit Partner
Provide regular updates on engagement status, risks, resource needs, and emerging issues.
Prepare partner‑level summaries, audit completion reports, and technical analyses.
Support the partner in client meetings, proposals, and business development activities.

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Professional qualification (CPA, CA, ACCA or equivalent).
Minimum 5–7 years of external audit experience, including supervisory responsibilities.
Strong knowledge of
ISA
,
IFRS
, and relevant regulatory frameworks.
Experience managing multiple engagements and leading audit teams.

Strong technical accounting and auditing expertise.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
High level of professional judgement and analytical ability.
Ability to manage deadlines and competing priorities.
Strong leadership, coaching, and interpersonal skills.
Commitment to quality, ethics, and continuous learning.
Personal Attributes
Professional, confident, and client‑focused.
Detail‑oriented with strong organisational skills.
Demonstrates integrity, independence, and sound judgement.
Proactive, adaptable, and solution‑oriented.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Fixed Plant Maintenance team, the Senior Maintenance Planner ensures that all routine maintenance activities for our process plant are appropriately planned (with input from operations and maintenance) so that the work can progress in a safe, environmentally responsible, efficient, cost effective and repeatable manner.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Actively promote a safe and healthy culture. Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions. Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Develop and implement maintenance schedules for both planned and corrective maintenance activities to ensure equipment reliability and operational efficiency in multiple areas
Utilise Pronto to track Planned jobs (Weekly and Shutdowns), work orders, manage maintenance backlogs, and ensure timely completion of tasks.
Assists in the development of Maintenance budgets and reporting actual performance against budgets and plans.
Track and forecast critical component requirements to prevent unscheduled downtime, while monitoring component life cycles and managing replacements in alignment with predictive maintenance strategies.
Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to analyse equipment performance and reliability. Implement corrective actions to enhance equipment reliability and reduce unplanned breakdowns including but not limited to:
Coordinate with procurement team to ensure timely acquisition of parts and components while maintaining optimal stock levels to minimise excess inventory costs. Conduct regular inventory reviews, request stock adjustments, and ensure accurate inventory records within Pronto, updating them as required based on usage trends.
Coordinate with procurement and logistics teams to secure the availability of spare parts and components, reducing delays in maintenance activities.
Prepare structured reports to provide insights into maintenance performance, downtime trends, and cost analysis. Maintain accurate maintenance records and generate data-driven insights for continuous improvement. Check quality of daily, weekly, and monthly KPI reports while also preparing and maintaining quarterly, 6monthly, and annual maintenance forecasts.
Additionally, assist and develop the national workforce in maintenance planning, scheduling, and execution processes, fostering skill development and knowledge transfer.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have mechanical or electrical trade qualifications as well as a technical qualification in Maintenance Planning. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) years’ experience in computer-based maintenance planning/scheduling.
Must have experience in using Pronto ERP
Must have advanced skills in MS Excel and MS Projects.
Strong understanding of Reliability Centered Maintenance.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
About the Opportunity
The Senior Program Manager (SPM), Economic Research & Dialogue (ERD) will work closely with APEP teams and externally with PNG partners and research institutions to shape and deliver high‑quality, policy‑relevant research that supports Papua New Guinea’s economic development.
The position will manage the design and implementation of research activities aligned to priority area of economic and social development including macro-economic policy, strengthening a business enabling environment, and agricultural growth in PNG.
Externally, the position will lead the management of key partnerships with Australia National University and the University of Papua New Guinea, as well as with other Australian academic institutions. The role includes working with national research institutions, individual researchers, GoPNG agencies, and other partners to apply a range of approaches which address existing knowledge and data gaps and strengthen research capacity, quality, and take-up in PNG.
The position will be responsible for managing ERD resourcing and supervising the ERD team on a day-to-day basis.
The role offers opportunities for regional engagement, collaboration with leading Australian and national research institutions, and contribution to high-level economic policy dialog. APEP is supportive of professional development and career growth.

Manage the ERD team to design and develop research concepts and activities.
Develop and maintain strong and effective stakeholder relationships - includes APEP teams, Australian High Commission, GoPNG agencies, and development partners.
Accurately manage ERD monthly budget forecasting and expenditure.
Manage APEP agreements, partnerships, and subcontracts in accordance with corporate and DFAT policies.
Supervise ERD staff to effectively manage performance, ensure accountability and support skills development as required.
Integrate GEDSI, Women’s Economic Empowerment, Climate and First Nations Australian perspectives into all ERD activities.
Other responsibilities as agreed with the APEP Director.

a response to the Selection Criteria below should be provided
.

Experience developing and implementing development or research strategies, plans and budgets.

Experience in managing staff resources and performance to deliver expected outputs and outcomes.
Proven experience integrating key cross-cutting themes such as GEDSI, Women’s Economic Empowerment, climate change and First Nations’ perspectives.
Understanding of the research context, environment, and organisations in PNG preferred.

Job Summary
The Accounts Assistant provides administrative and accounting support to the finance department by assisting with daily financial transactions, maintaining accurate accounting records, processing invoices and payments, and supporting financial reporting activities. The role requires strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to work efficiently while ensuring compliance with company policies and accounting procedures.
Key Responsibilities
Accounting & Financial Support
Assist in maintaining accurate financial records and accounting documentation.
Record and process daily financial transactions in the accounting system.
Prepare and update accounting entries, journals, and ledgers.
Assist in month-end and year-end financial closing activities.
Support the preparation of financial reports and summaries.
Verify the accuracy of invoices, receipts, and supporting documents.
Ensure proper filing and organization of accounting records.
Accounts Payable
Process supplier invoices, payment requests, and expense reimbursements.
Prepare payment vouchers and assist in check preparation.
Monitor due dates and ensure timely payments to suppliers and vendors.
Reconcile supplier statements and resolve discrepancies.
Accounts Receivable
Prepare customer invoices and billing statements.
Monitor customer accounts and follow up outstanding receivables.
Record incoming payments and maintain accurate receivable records.
Coordinate with clients regarding billing concerns and payment schedules.
Bank & Cash Transactions

Record and reconcile cash transactions and petty cash expenses.
Coordinate with banks regarding deposits, transfers, and payment transactions when necessary.

Support compliance with tax regulations and government statutory requirements.
Help prepare documentation for audits and financial inspections.

Support process improvements and efficiency within the accounting department.
Perform other accounting and finance-related duties assigned by management.

About the role
The Supervisor – Social Development Program is responsible for coordinating and delivering social programs that strengthen capacity, improve education and health outcomes, and foster inclusive community development. This role ensures that projects are implemented on the ground in line with company commitments under the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and community development plans
By supporting the Social Development Programs Standard within the Social Performance Management System (SPMS), the Supervisor contributes directly to the Material Issue: Capacity Building & Social Investment, which underpins sustainable community growth and resilience.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Lead the consistent implementation of social development initiatives across the mine lifecycle, delivering training, awareness, and capacity-building programs for communities (schools, health centres, women, youth, and church groups) to support sustainable outcomes beyond the mine.
Supervise, mentor, and develop Community Development Officers, including work planning, resource allocation, performance feedback, and supporting recruitment and capability building.
Execute program standards and workflows, coordinate field activities (health, literacy, empowerment, youth), track participation and outcomes, produce reports, and ensure compliance with IFC standards and internal commitments.
Collaborate with internal teams, government, NGOs, and community partners to align programs, integrate development initiatives, manage expectations, and deliver against formal social development commitments (MOA).

Have a Diploma or degree in Social Sciences, Education, Community Development, or related field.
3-5 years’ experience in delivering community programs, ideally in PNG or Melanesia.
Proven ability to manage small teams and deliver against workplans.
Strong communication and facilitation skills in Tok Pisin and English; local dialects an advantage.
Experience in conducting baseline studies (community, socio-economic, and spatial context) and social impact monitoring (aligned to projects, operations, and tenements/license/permit areas).

Builds trust through consistent follow-through and transparent communication.
Acts as a role model of integrity and collaboration in program delivery.
Models K92’s values of respect, accountability, and teamwork

Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Maintaining a minimum safe standard for all personnel, infrastructure and equipment on site

Degree or equivalent tertiary qualifications in Geotechnical, Civil or Mining Engineering from a recognized University.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. Joining our commercial team, the Team Lead – Contracts provides leadership and guidance to the Contracts team, ensuring high standards of contract administration, negotiation, and compliance. This role combines mentoring of team members with a strong technical focus, taking a lead role in procurement planning and market engagements under the direction of the Principal and Superintendent – Contracts. Provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring, and guidance to Contracts Officers, fostering capability development and professional growth.

Conduct regular feedback, coaching, and performance development for team members.
Act as a role model in professional conduct, supplier engagement, and commercial practice.
Oversee the drafting, review, and negotiation of contractual agreements to secure favourable terms and conditions.
Personally handle high-value or complex contracts to ensure strategic alignment and optimal outcomes.
Ensure all contracts comply with legal requirements, organisational policies, and industry standards.
Identify and mitigate potential contractual risks to protect the organization's interests.
Monitor compliance with contractual obligations, escalating significant risks, disputes, or performance issues to the Superintendent/Principal as appropriate.
Conduct audits and reviews of contract performance, ensuring adherence to obligations.
Foster and maintain strong relationships with vendors and service providers.
Act as a primary point of contact for contractual matters, facilitating communication and collaboration with external partners.
Collaborate with internal departments, including operations, supply and finance, to support contract-related initiatives.
Drive improvements in procurement and contract management processes, including development of templates, evaluation methods, and best practice approaches.
Capture and share lessons learned from market engagements to strengthen future strategies.
Stay abreast of industry trends, regulatory changes, and emerging risks incorporating these into contract strategies.
Provide training and guidance to internal teams on contract management processes and best practices.
About You

Degree Qualified tertiary qualifications in a relevant field (business or legal etc) essential.

Demonstrated knowledge of contract administration, negotiation, and management.
Strong experience in leading tenders, supplier evaluations, and market engagements.
Demonstrated behaviours consistent with K92 Mining core values.
Demonstrated problem solving and decision-making capability.
Strong commercial analysis and evaluation capabilities.
Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, and develop team members with diverse skills and backgrounds.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly to, and influence, internal and external stakeholders.
Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally.

K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

Summary:
The Genset Maintenance Technician is responsible for the preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and servicing of diesel- and gas-powered generators across company facilities. This role ensures a reliable backup power supply, compliance with safety standards, and optimal performance of all generator sets (gensets).
Duties and Responsibilities:
1. Generator Maintenance & Servicing
Perform scheduled preventive maintenance (oil changes, filter replacements, coolant checks, battery testing).
Conduct load bank testing to verify generator performance under load.
Inspect and maintain fuel systems, cooling systems, exhaust systems, and electrical components.
2. Troubleshooting & Repairs
Diagnose and repair mechanical failures (engine issues, fuel injectors, turbochargers, belts, pumps).
Troubleshoot electrical faults (AVR, control panels, wiring, circuit breakers, voltage regulators).
Replace defective parts and ensure proper reassembly and testing.
3. Emergency Response
Provide 24/7 on-call support for generator failures and power outages.
Rapidly diagnose issues and implement corrective actions to minimize downtime.
4. Documentation & Compliance
Maintain detailed service logs, work orders, and maintenance records (CMMS or manual logs).
Ensure compliance with OSHA, NFPA 110, EPA emissions standards, and company safety policies.
Track fuel consumption, runtime hours, and spare parts inventory.
5. Installation & Commissioning Support
Assist in new generator installations, ATS setups, and synchronization checks.
Verify proper operation before handover to operations.
Job Requirements:
1. Education & Certification:
High school diploma or equivalent (required).
Technical certification in Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Generator Maintenance, or a related field (preferred).
Manufacturer certifications (Cummins, Kohler, Caterpillar, Generac) are a plus.
2. Experience
3+ years of hands-on experience in generator maintenance and repair.
Familiarity with diesel/gas generators (10 kVA – 2000 kVA+).
Knowledge of ATS, load banks, and paralleling systems.
3. Technical Skills
Mechanical:
Engine diagnostics (compression tests, fuel system troubleshooting). Ability to disassemble, repair, and reassemble generator components.
Electrical:
Proficiency with multimeters, meggers, and diagnostic tools. Understanding of control panels, wiring diagrams, and synchronization systems.
4. Soft Skills
Strong problem-solving and attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and under pressure.
Good communication skills for reporting and team coordination.
5. Work Requirements

POSITION: Dean, Institute of Higher Education.
LOCATION: Popondetta, (Oro) Northern Province
DURATION: Three-year renewable contract with a 6-month probationary period
REMUNERATION: Competitive remuneration offered
ABOUT THE MODAWA INSTITUTE
The Modawa Institute is a newly established higher education provider in the Northern Province of PNG.  The Institute formally came into being as of 1 January 2024 but builds on more than 70 years of involvement in higher education within Papua New Guinea.  The Instutute is Registered with DHERST. There are three schools, each with a Head of School:
St Margaret’s School of Nursing and community health.
The Bishop Newton School of Theology.
The David Hand School of Teaching.
The institute seeks to develop a learning community where the various disciplines enrich each other, seeking to raise up leaders committed to excellence and innovation in their respective fields.
THE ROLE OF DEAN
The Dean will operate within the functions, roles and responsibilities outlined for the Principal in the Institute’s Canon (constitution) and under the guidance of the Chair of the Governing Council.
The Dean will have oversight of the institution, leading a team of academic, administrative and support employees. He or she will be the Executive Officer of the Council, the team leader within the Institute and its public face in the wider community. The Dean will nurture the academic life of the Institute and teach within one of its schools. He or she will maintain academic currency, model scholarship within the institute and contribute more widely to academic discussion in his or her field. The Dean may initially also be a head of school for one of the schools of the Institute.
He or she will have responsibility to oversight the administrative life of the institute, ensuring its financial and administrative integrity and ongoing viability. The Dean will be expected to encourage partners and build the financial base of the institute.
The Dean will be responsible for:
Maintaining and developing the ethos and vision of the college in line with Council strategies and directions.
Developing and leading a leadership team that will cultivate a positive environment for learning and work.
Collaborate closely with the other heads of schools.
Build the profile of the institute within the broader community and  strengthen relationships with business and industry representatives, donors, other Higher Education Institutions and national and overseas partners.
Contributing to the scholarly life of the institute.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
The Dean will hold, appropriate post-graduate academic qualifications in the relevant field.  He or she will have had significant experience in the higher education sector. The person will have experience in organisational administration, be fluent in written and spoken English, and have excellent presentation and public speaking skills. A commitment to uphold the ethos and values of the Modawa Institute is essential.
The Modawa Institute looks for staff who will are:
Deeply motivated by a care for young people.
Have a passion for learning.
Are self-starters and disciplined in their use of time.
Hold spiritual values in line with those of the Church.
Have a relationship style that evokes contributes to team building.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Under the Canon (constitution) of the Institute the Principal of the Institute (Dean) must be a communicant member of the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea, or of a Church in Communion with the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea.  If the Dean is also a Priest, he or she must hold a licence or permission to officiate from either the Archbishop or the Bishop of Popondetta.
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT
Remuneration:  By negotiation and in accord with qualifications and experience. A house on campus will be provided.  Relocation expenses by negotiation.
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
HOW TO APPLY:
Email your application to Modawa Institute with the following:
A cover letter addressing the following:
Your interest in becoming the Dean of the Institute.
Your educational leadership background and subject specialisations.
A description of your leadership style
Outline your teaching philosophy;
Your current resume;
A copy of your Academic Qualifications.
Two written references.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Coordinate workshop activities through the Mobile Maintenance Supervisors.
Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.
Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.
Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.
Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.
Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.
Ensure training requirements are met.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.
Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Provide coaching for performance improvement.
In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.
Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
Qualifications & Experience
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.
10+ years relevant work experience essential.
Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.
Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.
Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

The parts ordering administrator is responsible for managing and processing branch stock and emergency orders of parts and accessories from various suppliers both locally and overseas. jobs.description:
Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer – Five (5) Positions
CARE International in PNG is recruiting a Monitoring Evaluation, Accountability and Learning MEAL Officers based in Goroka. CARE International has been working in Papua New Guinea since 1989 and established a Country Office in late 2006.  Current program focal areas for CARE PNG include Governance, Women’s Economic Empowerment; Sexual, Reproductive and Maternal Health; Education; Climate Change Adaptation; Disaster Risk Reduction and Emergency Preparedness and Response.  CARE International in Papua New Guinea (CARE PNG) has the goal of achieving significant, positive and lasting impact on poverty and social injustice in remote rural areas through the empowerment of women and their communities, and through effective partnerships. Underpinning this are 4 strategic objectives which focus respectively on enhancing program quality; strengthening women’s empowerment and gender equality; building strategic partnerships with civil society, government and private sector groups; and developing organisational capacity
The Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Officer ensures the effective implementation and continuous improvement of CARE  programs and initiatives. She/he will be responsible for developing and implementing robust monitoring and evaluation frameworks, conducting rigorous data collection and analysis, and synthesising insights to inform evidence-based decision-making and improve program quality. She/he will lead efforts to cultivate a culture of learning and knowledge sharing within the organisation, facilitating capacity-building initiatives and promoting the adoption of best practices in monitoring, evaluation, and learning. This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful social impact by driving accountability, transparency, and learning across all CARE programs and projects in PNG.
This position is in Goroka and expects to travel to remote project locations.
This Position will have indirect contact with Children or vulnerable adults.
SELECTION CRITERIA
Minimum technical diploma and/or vocational training or equivalent and/or higher education in a relevant field; a bachelor’s degree in Community Development, Social Sciences, Statistics, Communications or a related field is an advantage;
At least three (3) years’ relevant work experience in MEL activities, preferably with an International Non-Government Organisation (INGO) and/or private company;
Proven experience in the design and implementation of MEL tools and processes, and in quality M&E data collection, analysis and management;
Demonstrated skills and experience in facilitating training and capacity-strengthening, including an understanding of adult learning principles and participatory methodologies;
Demonstrated understanding of, and commitment to, safeguarding — specifically Child Protection (CP) and Protection from Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse (PSHEA) — and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP);
Demonstrated good interpersonal skills, sound judgment, planning, problem-solving and team-building skills;
Demonstrated organisational and time management skills, with the ability to work in a team, work under pressure and manage workload to meet deadlines;
Demonstrated honesty, reliability and trustworthiness with the ability to maintain confidentiality;
Fluent oral and written communication skills in both Tok Pisin and English; and
Fully conversant in Microsoft Word, Excel and Office 365 applications, with sound numeric skills (knowledge of Kobo Toolbox, SPSS or similar an advantage).

jobs.description:
We are seeking a competent and flexible individual to fill the vacant position of
Earthworks & Road Maintenance Manager
. This position is based in
Kimbe, West New Britain Province
and reports to the Head of Operations – West New Britain.
EARTHWORKS & ROAD MAINTENANCE MANAGER
Job Purpose:
The Earthworks & Road Maintenance Manager is responsible for planning, directing, and overseeing all activities related to earthmoving operations and the maintenance of road infrastructure. The core purpose of this role is to ensure that roads and associated civil works are constructed, maintained, and repaired efficiently, safely, and to required standards, supporting reliable transportation and operational continuity.
Main Responsibilities:
Ensure that all earthworks and road maintenance activities are carefully planned, sequenced, and executed within defined timelines to avoid delays and disruptions.
Planning and allocating site earthwork crews, machinery, and haul trucks to meet strict deadlines.
Ensuring Road design dimensions (camber, slopes, and elevations) accurately match engineering plans.
Develop, enforce, and continuously improve QA/QC procedures in line with project specifications, engineering standards, and regulatory requirements.
Identify defects or non-conformances, implement corrective actions, and ensure proper documentation and reporting of quality performance across all maintenance activities.
Conducting Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) and managing risk around open excavations and heavy traffic zones.
Enforce adherence to occupational health and safety (OHS) standards, company policies, and legal requirements across all earthworks and road maintenance activities.
Prepare and manage budgets for earthworks and road maintenance projects, ensuring efficient allocation of resources (labour, materials, equipment).
Monitoring fuel consumption, tracking material yields, managing sub-contractor billings, and reporting daily progress to stakeholders.
Monitor actual expenditure against budget, identify cost variances, and implement cost-control measures to keep projects financially on track.
Compile regular reports on project costs, resource utilization, progress, and financial performance for management review.
Job Requirements:
Degree or Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.
5 to 10+ years of hands-on experience in heavy civil construction, specifically focusing on earthmoving, cut-and-fill operations, grading, and road paving.
At least 3 to 5 years in a supervisory or management role managing subcontractors, surveyors, and heavy machinery operators.
Proficiency in interpreting civil road design blueprints, grading plans, cross-sections, and surveying benchmarks.
Deep understanding of soil mechanics, compaction levels, moisture density testing, and material selection (e.g., aggregates, asphalt, concrete).
Practical knowledge of heavy machinery operation and production capacities (e.g., excavators, bulldozers, graders, compactors, and scrapers).
Knowledge of stormwater management, sub-grade drainage, culvert installation, and trenching compliance.
Familiarity with project scheduling software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project), CAD viewers, and GPS-guided grading systems (like Trimble or Topcon).
Ability to work in outdoor, high-noise environments exposed to extreme weather conditions, dust, and heavy machinery vibration.
Strong physical stamina to navigate uneven terrain, climb into machinery, and perform regular site walkthroughs.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor People, Training (Electrical Compliance), you will play a pivotal role in strengthening workforce capability by ensuring training programs meet regulatory requirements and operational needs.
You will directly contribute to a safe and compliant work environment by embedding robust electrical competency frameworks, supporting workforce development, and enabling teams to perform critical tasks safely and efficiently. Your work will have a lasting impact on both operational performance and the development of our people.
As part of our team, you will
Design, deliver, and continuously improve electrical training programs aligned with Newmont, industry, and HSE standards, ensuring compliance across all electrical work activities.
Deliver mandatory training and inductions, including Electrical Worker Inductions, High Voltage compliance, Arc Flash, Hazard Awareness, and Low Voltage Rescue.
Develop and maintain engaging training materials, competency frameworks, and verification processes to support both theoretical and on-the-job learning.
Provide hands-on training, coaching, and assessment for electrical workers, including High Voltage Operator training and assessment.
Maintain electrical competencies and worker authorisations within the Learning Management System (LMS), ensuring compliance and audit readiness.
Partner closely with Supervisors, Superintendents, Electrical Engineering, and HSE teams to align training with operational requirements, risk controls, and business needs.
Conduct field observations and training needs analysis to identify capability gaps and refine training programs.
Incorporate learnings from audits, incidents, and workforce feedback into training programs to drive continuous improvement.
Foster a collaborative learning environment that supports knowledge sharing and capability development.
Manage training resources effectively while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
Prerequisites for your success in this role

This position includes health insurance and supportive workplace for parents and carers, including relevant leave and other benefits.
About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
APEP supports the PNGRGC which is an umbrella organisation for civil society organisations (CSOs) with an interest in the extractives sector, including community-based, faith-based, legal, environmental, transparency and anticorruption organisations.  The mission of the PNGRGC is to raise public awareness on resource governance and sustainability issues – and specifically to advocate for accountability and good governance in the planning and management of the extractive sector, including resource allocation and licensing, development options and community participation, and safeguarding of PNG’s national heritage consistent with the National Constitution. The PNGRGC is also mandated to coordinate civil society’s participation in PNG Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (PNGEITI), including providing guidance and support to the CSO representatives on the PNGEITI Multi Stakeholder Group (MSG).
About the Opportunity
The PNGRGC Operations Manager will effectively function as the Executive Officer of the two-person secretariat of the PNGRGC. This role will require the coordination and management of the logistics and administration activities within the PNGRGC office and plays a lead role in implementing the PNGRGC operations plan.
The Operations Manager will take the lead in drafting high quality reporting and manage PNGRGC coordination with key stakeholders and will also have the primary responsibility for ensuring the effective and efficient delivery of the PNGRGC objectives.
Key responsibilities
The PNGRGC Operations Manager is responsible for ensuring the efficient operations of the PNGRGC. The primary responsibilities include facilitating the building of organisational capacity and membership, communication and networking; advocacy; and fundraising. The core responsibilities of this position are but not limited to.
Undertake monitoring and evaluation of engagements among stakeholders.
Ensure programme work plans and timelines are regularly monitored to ensure timely delivery of milestones.
Ensure that all reporting is delivered in a timely manner and in accordance with the PNGRGC constitutional requirements and deadlines.
Ensure APEP objectives are upheld including coordinating GEDSI activities and communication priorities.
Ensure the business of PNGRGC operates with the highest standards of conduct and ethics and maintain the reputation for quality and excellence.
Provide an effective and timely tracking of deliverables, milestones, risks and program progress as well as effective, accurate and regular updates to PNGRGC Council and APEP.
Provide executive support to PNGRGC Secretariat’s office and the Council.

Peopleconnexion is partnering with a nationally owned independent power producer and developer delivering critical energy infrastructure across Papua New Guinea. This is an opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of high-impact projects, including:
Power generation and transmission developments
Transmission and distribution infrastructure projects
Industrial power supply and network expansion initiatives
Renewable energy and rural electrification projects
Remote community mini-grid developments
This is a unique opportunity to play a leading role in nation-building infrastructure projects, with visibility across the entire project lifecycle and the ability to influence outcomes from concept and feasibility through to commissioning and handover.
The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced
Project Manager – Power, Infrastructure & Rural Electrification
to take ownership of the beginning-to-end delivery of complex energy and infrastructure projects. This is a senior leadership position requiring a technically grounded professional with strong commercial acumen, stakeholder management capability, and the ability to successfully deliver projects in dynamic and often remote operating environments.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the full project lifecycle from feasibility, concept development and design through to procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover
Manage feasibility studies, concept design activities, and project development initiatives

Provide CAPEX and OPEX cost inputs to support business cases and financial modelling

Ensure compliance with HSE, regulatory, environmental, and quality standards throughout all phases of project delivery

Monitor project performance, manage variations, and deliver projects safely, on time, and within budget.

10+ years' experience in project management within the power, energy, utilities, or large-scale infrastructure sectors
Demonstrated experience delivering generation, transmission, distribution, renewable energy, or rural electrification projects from concept through to commissioning
Strong commercial capability across budgeting, financial management, cost control, procurement, and contract administration
Proven leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams and complex contractor environments
Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence outcomes across technical, commercial, regulatory, and community interfaces

A hands-on, solutions-focused approach with the ability to balance strategic thinking and operational delivery.
