This is more than a project management role—it is an opportunity to contribute to critical infrastructure that directly impacts industries, businesses, and communities throughout Papua New Guinea.
You will join a growing organisation with a strong pipeline of power and infrastructure developments, offering exposure to both traditional and renewable energy projects, significant autonomy, and the opportunity to leave a lasting legacy through projects that improve connectivity, economic growth, and community electrification across the country.

We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. Management of the diamond drill tooling, inventory and all related machinery and equipment.

Direct and train employees on appropriate and effective drill practices and techniques.
Develop team members through regular feedback, coaching and formal training.

Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure diamond drilling operations are conducted by competent operators in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures and legislation.
About You
To be considered for this position, it is essential that applicants have demonstrated experience in the safe operation of an LM90 Diamond Drill rig. In addition to this, applicants should also
Qualifications in Drilling Operations or equivalent relevant experience.
Minimum 3 years experiences drilling with LM90 and rod handler.

PNG National Driver’s License. (Class 6 preferred)
Knowledge of critical components of the Drills and their functions.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based at Iagifu Ridge, Papua New Guinea, the Mechanical Fitter is a key role in our Santos operated plant and field locations. In this position you will be responsible for the safe execution of preventative and corrective maintenance tasks on plant and field equipment, and provide technical assistance, as required, to the Operations Teams.
This is a 28 day on / 28 day off roster
Key accountabilities include:
Working in accordance with approved procedures, performing preventative maintenance inspections and corrective maintenance on all campaign-assigned equipment, including gas turbine packages and systems
Ensuring scheduled work is executed safely and on time, with constant reference to work instructions and other execution documents
Ensuring high-quality close-out reports are recorded in the computerised maintenance system
Proactively participating in embedded safety systems and the improvement of safety culture
Ensuring emergent and break-in work is planned and executed according to risk ranking and business priorities
Inspecting, testing, adjusting and repairing mechanical equipment to satisfy all appropriate governing standards and procedures
Positioning and installing mechanical equipment, recording test results using precision measurement equipment
Demonstrating a high-quality knowledge of fault-finding, with the ability to troubleshoot autonomously
Driving schedule compliance within the Maintenance Team
Actively participating in the continuous improvement of maintenance systems and procedures, including Master Data Change Requests, Bill of Materials, Parts issues, and Technical Instruction reviews
Serving as the Santos Point of Contact during Campaign Single System Outages, Major projects or Total Plant Shut Downs when required
Consistently demonstrating a high level of quality workmanship
Compliance with the Santos Management System, Delegation of Authority and Corporate Governance and Safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
You will be experienced in:
Mechanical trade work, with a detailed knowledge of turbines, plant processes, equipment and fault-finding techniques
Gas engine turbines and the ability to identify corrective actions
Understanding and interpretation of relevant technical drawings
Working within systems, tools and standards for the mining, resources and energy industry — oil and gas experience is advantageous
Gas engine driven compressor packages, Oil and Gas processing equipment, Rotating Equipment and Reciprocating Engines, TEG units, power generation, pumps, shaft alignment and compressor operations
Computerised SAP systems and Maintenance Management Systems
HYTORQ, alignment tooling, precision measurement equipment and flange management systems
Quantifying and assessing risk and developing risk mitigation strategies.
Ideally, you will hold a Certificate III in Engineering and Mechanical Trade and have completed a four-year apprenticeship with a certified and recognised Trades Certificate. You will bring a minimum of two years post-trade experience working within the mining, resources or energy industry, with background experience in live gas plants being a distinct advantage.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose  - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB 19 June 2026
.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place.  You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Processing Services Operators are multi skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the
•              mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.
•              concrete batching plant and agitator trucks
•              pastefill binder preparation plant
The Processing Services division operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system; concrete batching plant and surface agitator trucks and pastefill binder preparation plant
Effectively operate and maintain mobile equipment including Light Vehicle, Front End Loader, Excavator, telehandler and forklift according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems
Operate fixed plant equipment including jaw and cone crushers, screening plant, concrete batching plant, binder preparation plant, and cement offloading facility according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.
Ensure quality of material being crushed, batched and prepared meets the correct quality standards by taking regular samples
Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.
Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.
Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply within varying site operation.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a Grade 10 Certificate or technical trade Loader and excavator licences and relevant experience as well as Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) or more years relevant work experience
Experience with operation and maintenance of mobile crushing equipment including but not limited to jaw crushers, cone crushers, screens, conveyors and stackers
Experience with concrete batching plant operations.
High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Ability to work shift work
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
Mechanical Technician supports safe and efficient power and utilities operations by executing inspections, repairs, and maintenance activities on mechanical equipment, ensuring asset reliability, compliance, and continuous plant availability.
Essential Duties
Maintenance & Reliability
Perform routine mechanical inspections on plant and utility equipment
Identify defects early and report for planned maintenance intervention
Assist in breakdown repairs to restore equipment functionality
Monitor asset condition and performance trendS
Equipment Maintenance & Repair
Carry out mechanical repairs, adjustments, and component replacements
Support calibration and testing of mechanical systems
Ensure equipment meets operational and reliability standards
Management & Documentation
Maintain accurate maintenance records (repairs, parts, inspections)
Update equipment history and maintenance logs
Provide input for proactive maintenance planning
Spare Parts & Inventory Support
Track usage of critical spare parts
Support availability of essential components
Assist in inventory control processes
Safety & Compliance
Follow all site safety protocols, standards, and procedures
Apply safe work practices during all maintenance activities
Participate actively in safety meetings and initiatives
Stop unsafe work and escalate hazards immediately
Continuous Improvement
Identify recurring mechanical issues and recommend improvements
Contribute ideas to improve maintenance efficiency and reliability
Support a zero-harm safety culture
Training & Experience
Mechanical Trade Certificate (e.g., Fitter, Diesel Fitter, Mechanical Technician) or equivalent recognized qualification
Completion of apprenticeship or formal trade training program
Demonstrated experience in mechanical maintenance within mining, processing, power generation, or heavy industrial environments
Experience with rotating and static plant equipment (e.g., pumps, engines, compressors, conveyors, or utility systems) (contextual application aligned to P&U)
Proven exposure to breakdown maintenance, fault finding, and preventive maintenance activities
Ability to interpret mechanical drawings, manuals, and maintenance procedures
Competence in using maintenance tools and equipment safely and effectively
Basic understanding of condition monitoring and defect identification
Experience with maintenance management systems (e.g., SAP/CMMS) for work order execution and history recording
Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices and adherence to site procedures
Experience in power and utilities systems (diesel generation, water, steam, or fuel systems)
Exposure to reliability maintenance and condition monitoring programs
High-risk work licenses (rigging, confined space, working at heights – if applicable to role)
Working Conditions
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Linesman is responsible for the safe construction, operation, maintenance, and repair of overhead and underground electrical distribution networks (HV/LV) across Lihir operations and associated communities, ensuring reliable power supply and compliance with site electrical safety standards and statutory requirements.
Essential Duties
Distribution Network Operations & Maintenance
Perform installation, maintenance, and repair of overhead distribution systems (poles, cross-arms, insulators, conductors)
Maintain and repair underground cable systems, joints, and terminations
Assist with operation and maintenance of transformers and distribution equipment
Conduct routine inspections and condition monitoring of network assets
Fault Response & Power Restoration
Respond to faults and outages on HV/LV distribution networks
Identify defects (line breaks, insulator failure, cable faults) and perform repairs
Support timely restoration of power to plant, site infrastructure, and community supply areas
Construction & Network Expansion
Erect poles and structures, string conductors, and install fittings
Support new connections, upgrades, and modifications to the distribution network and Ensure all work complies with approved drawings, standards, and procedures
Safety, Isolation & Compliance, Equipment & Work Practices
Apply Lihir Electrical Safety Management Plan requirements in all tasks
Execute isolations, earthing, and permit-to-work activities under authorised supervision
Comply with PNG Electrical Licensing requirements and AS/NZS standards
Stop work during unsafe conditions (e.g. lightning proximity restrictions for line work)
Safely operate EWP, cranes, winches, and line construction tools
Ensure all tools and equipment are inspected and fit for purpose
Complete work orders, inspection records, and defect reports
Update asset condition and maintenance records in CMMS/SAP systems
Contribute to incident investigations and continuous improvement initiatives
Training & Experience
Electrical Trade Certificate or recognized Linesman qualification.
PNG Electrical Worker License (or eligibility to obtain).
Experience in overhead and/or underground electrical distribution systems.
Fault finding and repair of HV/LV networks.
Experience working in mining or heavy industrial environments (desirable).
Strong understanding of electrical safety and risk management.
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings (SLDs, layouts).
Competency in working at heights and rigging.
Teamwork and communication in a remote operational environment.
Working Conditions
Outdoor work in tropical and remote conditions (Lihir environment).
On-call and shift work for outage response.
Physically demanding (climbing poles, lifting, working at heights).

Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.

jobs.description:
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Manager
Position Description
BACKGROUND
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organization, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 120 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection.
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea (SCiPNG) is committed to be a platform for transformative and lasting change for children their families, and their communities. SCiPNGg prides itself in being a child safe organization. For more information, please visit:
www.savethechildren.org.au.
ROLE PURPOSE
The National MEAL Manager, based out of SCiPNG’s head office in Port Moresby, is responsible for the overall design and implementation of MEAL systems (including MEAL Information Systems or MIS) to ensure that all SCiPNG programs are of expected quality, have accountability mechanisms (e.g., share information, are participatory, and have feedback and reporting mechanisms relevant for PNG), and that learning is institutionalized for continuous program improvements. Working with relevant staff, the National MEAL Manager will ensure comprehensive frameworks are in place to support program quality; enhance donor and stakeholder accountability; report on progress; and measure impact.
The National MEAL Manager will be expected to lead the design and improvement of MEAL frameworks, systems, and tools for existing and new SCiPNG program/project designs.  This includes orienting, supporting, and mentoring all relevant staff across SCiPNG to deliver on projects’ MEAL requirements (e.g., data validation, analysis, and visualization), improving internal accountability and donor reporting.
This role reports to the Director of Program Development and Quality, requires close collaboration with the Program Operations team, and will advise the senior management team on issues relating to MEAL. The role will have direct line management of the MEAL team. The responsibilities below are not exhaustive; other tasks may be required according to changing operational and contextual needs.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT, DESIGN, AND QUALITY
Identify needs and opportunities for potential programs through situational analyses, feasibility studies, networking, and leveraging research and evaluation findings.
Catalyze MEAL engagement in all new program designs, both humanitarian and development responses, including development and responsibility for MEAL workbooks.
Ensure consistent MEAL methodology and quality benchmarks/assurance across thematic programs; ensure that all programs have effective MEAL practices throughout the program cycle.
Act as the focal point for all situation analyses, designing study methodologies, tools, and sampling strategies.
STRATEGIC DIRECTION
Provide technical support for developing, reviewing and updating the Country Strategy Plan.
Participate in the Country Annual Planning and Country Annual Reporting, providing oversight and compiling of reports (e.g., Total Reach, strategy goal indicators).
Provide thought leadership and links with Save the Children Australia’s (SCA) regional initiatives, including participation in Pacific MEAL Community of Practice.
Lead the compilation of Program Quality Key Performance Indicators, reporting on a quarterly basis.
Work with the Senior Management Team to guarantee that SCiPNG’s mandate, values, and policies are reflected throughout all operations and activities (e.g., PSEA, child safeguarding, anti-corruption, anti-fraud).
MONITORING, EVALUATION, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND LEARNING
Monitoring:
Lead in the development, implementation, and maintenance of MEAL workbook, databases, trackers, and tools, ensuring standardization of disaggregated data.
Coordinate with relevant program and partner staff on the most viable data collection method(s) for each project targets/research agenda and on providing timely inputs (i.e., data collection that documents progress against targets) required for all SCiPNG and donor reporting (e.g., Total Reach, global outcome indicators, performance trackers, databases). Ensure that all reporting is of high quality and submitted in a timely manner.
Work with program and partner staff to develop selection of project participants; develop and supervise systems to maintain confidential project participant records.
Support program and partner staff to use digital data collection methods (i.e. Kobo).
Accountability:
Ensure that MEAL, program, and partner staff have a clear understanding on program accountability to children and communities through training and coaching.
Ensure that Feedback and Reporting Mechanisms (FRMs) are functional; provide follow-up and support for the investigation of serious complaints and feedback as needed per the established protocols.
Meet with partner organizations to request feedback and follow-up on critical issues and/or complaints from project participants.
Ensure that periodic MEAL reports are stored and debriefed at different levels, and that action plans for addressing quality gaps are developed and followed up.
Evaluation and
Learning:
Take lead in conducting/facilitating strategic program evaluations and after-action reviews.
Work with MEAL, program, and partner staff to develop evaluation (e.g., baseline, mid-term, final) Terms of Reference, methodologies, tools, and sampling strategies. Oversee surveys of program/project impact to ensure that deliverables are on target. Act as the focal point for all evaluations – both internal and external.
Promote cross-thematic and cross-program learning; establish quarterly reflection, reviews, and consolidation of feedback across all programs.
MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM
Manage automated data pipeline (SC system) for PNG and scale-up of projects with PowerBI Dashboards.
Provide data analysis to the relevant program staff to support improvements to program quality and contributions to donor reporting.
Analyze and present data to senior management to be able to make strategic programmatic decisions.
Analyze and present client feedback data to ensure the organization's program is client centered.
CAPACITY BUILDING
In coordination with Program Operations, provide ongoing and one-off technical MEAL support and advice to programs and partners.
Ensure that core MEAL training modules and approaches are effectively rolled out.
COORDINATION AND REPRESENTATION
Liaise with MEAL focal persons from Pacific Regional Office, Save the Children Australia and other Save the Children members for sharing, learning, and updates on new developments on MEAL and related requirements.
Identify relevant technical assistance providers and pull technical assistance as needed for strengthening MEAL systems in PNG.
Represent the SCiPNG through participation in national, regional, and global MEAL initiatives as needed.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practices with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities, and other relevant policies and procedures
Undertake any other reasonable duty as may be assigned by the line manager.
PERSON SPECIFICATIONS
Mandatory Qualifications and Experience
Minimum bachelor’s degree in political science, social sciences, development studies, communications, or other relevant field of study. Master’s level education is preferred.
Minimum of eight (8) years of relevant experience with NGOs in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning reporting – with progressively more responsible positions.
Documented experience in successfully leading and implementing MEAL activities – system design, programmatic quality audits, systematic tracking and analysis, surveys, assessment systems and evaluations.
Thorough knowledge of results-based monitoring frameworks.
Extensive experience in working with digital data collection (i.e. Kobo), data analysis (e.g., Excel) and data visualization (e.g., PowerBI) applications. High level of computer proficiency with a particular focus on MS Word, MS Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint.
Experience integrating quality standards in programs and implementing accountability initiatives, such as child participation, information sharing, and feedback and reporting mechanisms.
A good understanding of and experience in addressing gender-related challenges in monitoring and evaluation of programs.
Ability to think strategically, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.
Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.
Excellent writing and verbal skills in English for reports and communications documents. Ability to write clear reports including data analysis and triangulation.
Proven ability to supervise, train, and coach staff. Previous experience in managing consultants is desirable.
Documented experience in supporting successful funding proposals to donors.
Desirable Knowledge and Experience
Experience with international donor (e.g., DFAT, MFAT) regulations, project design, and reporting requirements.
Experience of different evaluation approaches (e.g., RCTs, quasi-experimental designs, Most Significant Change, outcome harvesting).
Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis software (e.g. STATA, SPSS, NVivo, Atlas.ti).
Previous experience of working within a Payment by Results framework.
Skills/Abilities
Strong analytical, relationship building, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
High level of attention to detail and quality.
High level strategic planning skills.
Willingness to travel to regional areas of PNG.
Strong time management and organizational skills.

“Join our team and be able to contribute to a better business enabling environment and increasing economic diversity for more inclusive economic growth in Papua New Guinea”
Commencement: As soon as possible
Long term role, up to February 2028 (with potential for extension)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG nationals only
*Abt is committed to advancing women’s leadership in PNG’s economic development and are building an environment where women can lead progress and shape economic outcomes. Abt promotes an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment for women and encourages PNG women and men to apply.
This position includes health insurance, and supportive workplace for parents and carers, including relevant leave and other benefits.
About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
About the Opportunity
The Program Manager will be part of the Efficient and Inclusive Markets (EIM) team within the APEP Program and work closely with colleagues from other disciplines in APEP, especially the Agriculture Growth and cross-cutting teams. The Program Manager will mostly focus on financial inclusion and Innovative Finance projects. The Program Manager will play an important role in ensuring the effective and efficient management of selected projects across EIM. This EIM portfolio of projects contains a diverse range of interventions and projects designed to address key bottlenecks, gaps and barriers constraining business activities and economic growth. Projects are designed to support GoPNG and other stakeholders with strong linkages to related digital economy development, small business development services, and financial institution strengthening and support.
The Program Manager will support the Unit Manager and Team Leader to ensure the effective and efficient management of projects throughout the full project management cycle across the Partnership. This includes applying relevant technical sectoral knowledge to support implementation of program delivery through providing informed guidance to implementing partners including managing and coordinating implementing partners and contractors. This role required preparing documents like reports, briefings, meeting minutes, etc.
Additionally, there may be opportunities to work across various projects across APEP, as required to achieve APEP’s Intermediate Outcomes and overall objective.
Key responsibilities
Manage the design and implementation of access to finance, inclusive and innovative financing instruments project activities that lead towards the achievement of EOPOs.
Support the development of project budgets and costings, contributing to expenditure monitoring, tracking and forecasting.
Timely tracking of advisers/contractors, deliverables, milestones, risks and program progress as per the contracts, MoUs and agreements.
Build and maintain open, productive and outcome-oriented relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, including DFAT and GoPNG.
Support project monitoring, reviews, and evaluations that measure the achievement of EOPOs.
Provide technically sound and high quality of written work including policy and project briefs, concept notes on potential new projects, weekly program updates, meeting agendas and minutes, and program reporting.
Contribute to the project-level monitoring and evaluation (M&E).
Lead strategic stakeholder engagements associated with project delivery.
Integrate and promote principles of gender equity and social Inclusion, climate change mitigation and research in all aspects of this role including in project design, implementation, and evaluation.
Represent APEP at internal and external meetings and events and coordinate and organize internal and external meetings, events and seminars with program partners and key stakeholders.
About You
For applications to be considered,
a response to the Key Selection Criteria below must be provided in your application
.
Tertiary qualifications in Business Management, Economics, International Development, Trade & Investment, Social Sciences or related field.
At least 5 years experience in access to finance, innovative financing instruments, banking and finance, or micro finance.
At least 2-3 years experience in program management.
Understanding of access to finance challenges for MSMEs in PNG.
Understanding in risk management, appraisal, and credit facilities.
“
We value capability and potential, and welcome applicants who believe they can succeed in this role”
How to Apply
Please ensure to address the Key Selection Criteria (About You) in your cover letter, and submit your application online, along with your CV as a single document.
Applications must be submitted personally by individuals only. Applications submitted by a company or organisation will not be accepted.
The successful applicant will be engaged through an employment agreement determined by Abt.
We welcome and thank all applications; however, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted

The position is urgently required; applications will be evaluated as they are submitted. We advise all interested candidates to apply promptly.
Abt Global is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to upholding high standards of Child Protection, Anti-bribery and Fraud Protection.
We encourage applications from experienced and capable women, and people with disabilities.

About the Company
We are the exclusive distributor of several leading OEM brands of forklift trucks, container-handling equipment, heavy machinery, and generators in Papua New Guinea.
Our operations support key industries nationwide, providing reliable mechanical and technical services to clients across ports, logistics, construction, manufacturing, and industrial sectors.
The Opportunity
We are seeking a skilled, experienced, and safety-focused
Service Mechanic Technician / Supervisor
to join our Lae-based service team.
This is a hands-on technical and supervisory role suited to a qualified tradesperson with strong experience in
port handling equipment, reach stackers, large forklifts, heavy vehicles, hydraulic systems, electrical control systems, and mobile plant maintenance
.
The successful applicant must be capable of leading a small team, attending field service breakdowns, carrying out accurate diagnostics, and ensuring high-quality repair and maintenance work is completed safely and efficiently.
Key Responsibilities

Carrying out preventative maintenance, diagnostics, repairs, and breakdown support on reach stackers, container handling equipment, forklifts, trucks, generators, and other mobile plant.

Troubleshooting hydraulic, pneumatic, CAN bus, electrical, and electronic control systems.
Carrying out diagnostics using OEM diagnostic software, service tools, and maintenance management systems.
Supervising and coordinating workshop repairs and field service activities.
Leading, mentoring, and training a small team of mechanics and technicians.
Developing and managing maintenance schedules to ensure repairs and services are completed on time.
Installing, commissioning, and maintaining single-phase and three-phase power generation systems.
Ensuring all work is completed to a high standard of safety, quality, and professionalism.
Completing risk assessments, job safety analysis, service reports, and related documentation.
Supporting after-hours breakdowns and on-call service requirements when required.
Qualifications & Experience

A recognised Trade Certificate in Heavy Vehicle, Plant, Diesel Fitting, Motor Mechanics, or equivalent.
Extensive proven experience with
container handling equipment and reach stackers
.
Strong experience with
large forklifts, 30T+ forklifts, heavy vehicles, mobile plant, and generators
.
Strong knowledge of hydraulic systems, pneumatic systems, automotive electrical systems, and electronic control systems.
Experience using diagnostic software, OEM service tools, and modern workshop practices.
Proven ability to diagnose and repair complex mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical faults.
Previous supervisory or team leadership experience.
A strong commitment to workplace safety, quality control, and professional workmanship.
The ability to work independently in the field and as part of a team.
Willingness to support after-hours and urgent breakdown work when required.
What We Offer
Competitive salary based on qualifications and experience.
Company-provided single accommodation or accommodation allowance.
Vehicle and phone for suitable candidates.
Opportunities for OEM training and career development.
A long-term opportunity with a well-established and respected PNG company.
Supportive workshop and field service team environment.

jobs.employer_address: Cameron Road, Waigani, NCD, 121
jobs.description:
Experienced Auto Electrician
(Especially the marine-experience kind)
Important: If you do not have proven auto electrical experience, please do not submit your CV. Marine electrical experience will be a strong advantage.
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our workshops depend on accuracy, discipline, and proper technical skill — especially when it comes to electrical work.
We’re looking for an experienced Auto Electrician to join our Port Moresby team. We are especially interested in candidates with marine electrical experience who understand that wiring, diagnostics, installations, and repairs need to be done properly the first time.
This is not a role for someone learning on the job. If your experience is limited, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and installing electrical systems across vehicles, equipment, and where required, marine-related applications.
That includes fault finding, reading wiring diagrams, tracing electrical issues, repairing wiring faults, testing electrical systems, and carrying out clean, reliable installations.
You may work on starting and charging systems, lighting, accessories, sensors, ECUs, batteries, switches, relays, wiring looms, and electronic faults.
For candidates with marine experience, your ability to understand electrical systems in boats, outboard-related setups, marine accessories, battery systems, switches, pumps, navigation lights, and exposed-condition wiring will be highly valued.
The expectation is simple: diagnose properly, wire it properly, fix it properly.
Who This Suits
This role suits a qualified and experienced Auto Electrician with real workshop experience and the confidence to work without being carried.
You know how to fault-find properly, not guess. You can read wiring diagrams, use diagnostic tools, and understand how electrical faults affect vehicle performance, safety, and reliability.
If you have marine experience, you understand that electrical work around water, salt, vibration, and outdoor conditions needs a higher level of care. Shortcuts do not last.
You work well with technicians, service advisors, parts teams, and customers when required. You keep your work tidy, your job cards accurate, and your standards high.
If people already call you when the hard electrical jobs land, this will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates busy workshops with real volume, real standards, and real expectations. You’ll be working with recognised global brands, proper tools, and experienced teams who understand the value of good technical people.
This is a workshop where skill is noticed, standards matter, and good tradesmen are taken seriously.
For the right person, marine experience will make you even more valuable to the team.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “This is exactly where I should be,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and cover letter to:

jobs.employer_address: Cameron Road, Waigani, NCD, 121
jobs.description:
Marketing Assistant
(The organised, sharp-comms, leads-don’t-get-lost kind)
Location: Head Office
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our marketing team supports multiple brands, dealerships, campaigns, promotions, events, and customer enquiries across the business.
We’re looking for a Marketing Assistant to join our Port Moresby team and help manage customer communication, Facebook enquiries, reception enquiries, CRM updates, and lead referrals to the right dealership teams.
This is not just a “posting on Facebook” role. This is a front-line marketing support role where every enquiry needs to be captured, entered into the CRM correctly, assigned to the right person, and followed up properly.
If the CRM is messy, leads get lost. If leads get lost, sales opportunities are missed. That cannot happen in this role.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for helping manage customer enquiries coming through Facebook, online channels, phone calls, walk-ins, and customer reception.
That includes responding professionally to messages, collecting the right customer details, entering leads into the CRM, updating customer records, assigning enquiries to the correct dealership or sales team, and tracking whether follow-up has happened.
You’ll help keep the CRM clean, accurate, and useful. Customer names, contact numbers, vehicle interest, enquiry source, follow-up status, salesperson assignment, and notes must be entered properly — not guessed, rushed, or left blank.
You’ll also monitor open enquiries, update lead progress, flag missed follow-ups, and help ensure no customer sits in the system without action.
You’ll work closely with sales teams to make sure leads are not only passed on, but properly recorded and followed through. A Facebook message, phone enquiry, or reception walk-in must become a proper CRM lead — not a note on someone’s desk or a message that disappears.
You’ll also support the marketing team with day-to-day campaign activities, social media coordination, basic content support, promotions, events, reporting, and general marketing administration.
The expectation is simple: capture every lead, enter it properly, assign it clearly, and follow it up.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone with strong communication skills, good organisation, and the confidence to deal with customers professionally.
You don’t need to know everything about cars, but you do need to know how to speak to people, ask the right questions, and record information accurately.
You should be comfortable using Facebook, email, Microsoft Office, and customer management systems. Experience using a CRM system will be a strong advantage.
You need to be the kind of person who understands that data matters. Wrong phone numbers, missing notes, duplicate leads, poor follow-up updates, and unclear assignments create problems for the whole business.
If a customer sends an enquiry, you don’t leave it sitting there. If a lead comes in, you make sure it goes into the CRM. If information is missing, you ask for it. If follow-up has not happened, you flag it.
This role suits someone who is sharp, reliable, and does not need to be reminded five times to complete one task.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors is a busy, fast-moving business with strong brands, active campaigns, and real customer demand.
You’ll be part of a marketing team that works closely with sales, service, parts, branches, and management. You’ll gain practical experience across automotive marketing, customer communication, CRM management, social media, campaign support, and lead tracking.
This is a role where good communication matters, accurate data is important, and people who take initiative can grow.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “I can keep leads organised and customers followed up properly,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and cover letter to:
Beatrix Haiai
[email protected]

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining the project construction team, as Cost Controller, you will be responsible for supporting the Projects Controls team with planning, measuring progress, control (purchase orders and payment) and report internally on all services.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Apply cost control work processes to project and EPC services scope
Maintain Control Accounts in the Project Controls System
Import deliverable progress data into the Project Controls System from the different platforms
Coordinate progress updates and reviews with Discipline Leads
Maintain all data related EPC/Contractor rates
Collate and submit weekly workforce summarised report
Compile forecast data to support monthly reporting
Manage and report on EPC services labour and non-labour costs
Project reporting of committed, incurred, and forecast costs
Prepare PERs as per Project Expenditure Request Procedure
Prepare monthly accruals for review
Maintain cost control of flights, accommodation, expenses, and contractor back charges
Cost control and reporting of minor packages
Support management with cost control and reporting of major packages and change management
Reconcile Pronto paid costs with the Project Controls System
Provide consolidated booked hours data (hours and personnel count) to support project health, safety and environment (HSE) reporting requirements
Review and submit monthly accruals to the K92 Commercial department.
CMS- Set up packages, prepare PPC and submit for approval
Review & validate service invoices and maintain relevant registers
Create Service Purchase Orders in Pronto System and maintain relevant registers
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a Tertiary Qualification in Business Management or similar. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
5 years’ experience as a cost controller /specialist.
Good oral and written communication skills.
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Sound planning and organizational skills.
Proficient in computers and Microsoft packages
Previous Pronto and Project cost management software experience will be advantageous
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Ability to maintain good working relationships with team members, K92 Mining Ltd and contractor’s employees.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Overview
The Branch Manager is responsible for overseeing the overall operations, commercial performance, and administrative functions of the branch office. This includes managing vessel operations, customer service, sales, documentation, and ensuring compliance with company policies and international shipping regulations. The role demands strong leadership, strategic thinking, and in-depth knowledge of the shipping and logistics industry.

Senior Contracts & Project Administrator
The position is full-time with a three-month probation period. Upon successful completion of the probation period the employee will have the opportunity to become a full-time employee.
About the Role:
The Senior Contracts & Project Administrator plays a key role in supporting the successful delivery of engineering and infrastructure projects within the Engineering Division. This position is responsible for overseeing contract administration, project coordination, cost tracking, reporting, and operational support to ensure projects are delivered efficiently and commercially.
The successful candidate will work closely with management, engineers, suppliers, subcontractors, and clients to maintain strong project controls, accurate documentation, and effective communication across all stages of project delivery.
This role is ideal for a proactive and commercially minded professional who is highly organised, detail-oriented, and capable of working in a fast-paced project environment while contributing to continuous improvement within the division.
The responsibilities of the role:
Prepare, review, and administer contracts, agreements, purchase orders, and project variations
Support tender submissions, quotations, pricing schedules, and scope documentation
Monitor project budgets, expenditures, profitability, and reporting
Maintain project records, job files, and tracking systems
Coordinate invoicing, progress claims, and project reporting requirements
Liaise with engineers, suppliers, subcontractors, clients, and management
Monitor project timelines and escalate risks or delays when required
Support procurement coordination and operational processes
Ensure compliance with company procedures and contractual obligations
Assist in improving systems, reporting, and operational efficiencies

Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in contracts administration, project coordination, or commercial support roles
Strong leadership, organisational, and communication skills
Strong commercial awareness and attention to detail
Ability to work independently and meet strict deadlines
Strong analytical and reporting capabilities
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel

POSITION
TERMS OF REFERENCE
POSITION TITLE: Deputy Principal, Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy
AREA: Balimo, Delta Fly, Western Province
LOCATION: Balimo College Campus
ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improving
equality
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.
KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
THE BALIMO COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL CAMPUS:
The Balimo College educational campus was established by SDP in 2019 to build the education and health standards and pathways for the Western Province. Through the college, SDP delivers tertiary qualifications in Teaching under the Balimo Teachers College program; provides secondary school certification and GPA upgrades through Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE); supports schools in the area through E-Learning programs; and in 2024, opened the Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy.
HON. ROY BIYAMA BALIMO ACADEMY (the Academy):
The Academy is a PNG Sustainable Development Program initiative implemented in partnership with KTF. The Academy caters for all levels of schooling, including Early Childhood Education, Primary Schooling and Secondary Schooling, and aims to grow to support 1,000 students by the end of 2028. The Academy fosters an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning, being inclusive and responsive to additional needs, and removing educational barriers for local students to learn and grow in a safe and supportive environment.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Deputy Principal – Secondary will work closely with the Principal to provide leadership across academic, pastoral and administrative aspects of the secondary school. The role will help create the conditions for high-quality teaching and learning, strong student support, effective school systems, and a culture of professionalism and continuous improvement.
The successful candidate will contribute to the leadership of areas such as behaviour management, student wellbeing, enrolment and student records systems, family liaison, assessment and examination preparation, intervention and support programs and the strengthening of academic policies and practices in keeping with RBBA’s goals and values.
This is a hands-on leadership role. The Deputy Principal will be expected to model excellent teaching practice, mentor staff, support professional development, use data to improve outcomes and help ensure that school systems are well organised, consistent and student-centred.
Proficiency in educational technologies and strong leadership skills are essential, along with maintaining confidentiality and privacy within the school environment.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Support the Principal in the overall leadership and management of the school, including acting in the role of Principal when required.
Help build and sustain a strong culture of teaching excellence, professionalism, accountability and continuous improvement.
Provide leadership in positive behaviour management, student wellbeing and pastoral care systems, ensuring a safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment.
Support and strengthen teaching and learning practices, including SBC implementation, assessment, moderation, reporting and examination preparation.
Use student data and evidence to monitor performance, inform decision-making and implement targeted intervention and support strategies.
Mentor, coach and support teachers and middle leaders, contributing to staff induction, professional learning and performance development.
Maintain a teaching load and model high-quality classroom practice.
Support the effective operation of school systems, including enrolment processes, attendance, student records, reporting and data management.
Lead and support administrative processes to ensure efficient and consistent school operations, with clear systems and accurate record keeping.
Provide support and coordination for boarding operations, working with designated boarding staff to ensure student wellbeing, appropriate supervision and alignment with school policies.
Contribute to the development, implementation and review of school policies and procedures in alignment with organisational and regulatory requirements.
Ensure compliance with key policies including child safeguarding, inclusion, gender equity and organisational codes of conduct.
Support school improvement planning, review processes and the ongoing strengthening of whole-school systems and practices.
Contribute to the management of school resources and budget oversight to support effective and sustainable operations.
Build and maintain strong relationships with students, staff, families and the wider community, supporting positive engagement and communication.
Work collaboratively with partner organisations and stakeholders to support the effective operation and development of the school.
Support and coordinate targeted academic, behavioural and wellbeing programs for students requiring additional support.
Undertake additional duties as directed by the Principal.
SKILLS, ATTRIBUTES & SELECTION CRITERIA:
The successful applicant will demonstrate:
Leadership & Professional Practice
Proven experience in educational leadership, preferably in a secondary or comparable school setting.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate and inspire staff, and contribute effectively as part of a leadership team.
Strong professional judgement, integrity, resilience and the ability to remain calm, adaptable and solutions-focused in a complex environment.
Teaching & Learning Expertise
Strong instructional leadership with the ability to support high-quality teaching and learning.
Experience in curriculum implementation, assessment, moderation and examination processes.
Demonstrated ability to use student data and evidence to improve learning outcomes.
Staff Development & Capacity Building
Experience in mentoring, coaching and developing teachers and supporting professional growth.
Ability to build a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration and accountability.
Student Wellbeing & Pastoral Care
Strong experience in behaviour management, pastoral care and student support systems.
Commitment to creating safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments for all students.
Operations & Systems
High-level organisational and administrative skills, including experience with student information systems, records, reporting and school operations.
Ability to develop, implement and maintain effective systems, processes and policies.
Policy, Compliance & Governance
Strong understanding of policy implementation, compliance and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated commitment to child safeguarding, inclusion and ethical practice.
Community & Stakeholder Engagement
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build strong relationships with students, staff, families and community stakeholders.
Experience working effectively across cultures and within diverse communities.
Strategic & Operational Capability
Ability to contribute to school improvement planning and strategic development.
Sound understanding of resource management and financial oversight in a school context.
Personal Attributes
High levels of professionalism, initiative and accountability.
Flexibility, adaptability and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
Positive demeanour, strong teamwork skills and an appropriate sense of humour.
Digital & Administrative Capability
Competence in the use of digital tools and systems for communication, data management and school administration.
Qualifications and Experience
A relevant university degree in education or a related field.
A postgraduate qualification is highly desirable; Master’s degree preferred.
Current teacher registration, or eligibility for registration, as required.
Substantial teaching experience across a range of school settings.
A strong track record of effective school leadership and improving student outcomes.
Experience in secondary curriculum, assessment and school operations will be highly regarded.
Have the right to work in PNG.
This position may require travel domestically from time to time.

jobs.description:
About Burnet Institute
Burnet Institute is a leading Australian medical research and public health organisation working to achieve better health for vulnerable communities in Australia and internationally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has been implementing health research and development programs for almost 20 years, with offices in
Port Moresby, Kokopo and Western Province
.
About the HEAL-PNG Project
HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in
Morobe
and
East New Britain
provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.
About the Role
The
Research Health Extension Officer (HEO)
will play a key role in establishing and implementing the HEAL-PNG trial across selected health facilities. Working closely with the Provincial Health Authority (PHA), facility staff, and the HEAL-PNG project team, the Research HEO will support study coordination, site set up, staff training, and data collection activities.
The position will require initiative, attention to detail, and the ability to build strong working relationships across multiple stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
Coordinate study activities at participating facilities, enduring adherence to research protocols and ethical standards.
Facilitate site onboarding, including assessments and staff training in NCD, TB and HIV management.
Manage data collection, entry, and quality assurance in a confidential and timely manner.
Maintain strong communication with facility and PHA staff, fostering collaboration and problem-solving.
Support logistics for meetings, trainings, and field activities.
Assist with procurement, stock control, and management of project materials and consumables.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential:
Health Extension Officer qualification (Diploma + 1-year residency or Bachelors degree + 2-year residency).
Strong understanding of TB, HIV and non-communicable diseases (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, asthma, COPD).
Competency in Microsoft Office applications and willingness to learn new software applications.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with fluency in English and Tok Pisin.
Strong organisational skills and ability to work both independently and in a team.
Ability to build rapport with health staff and community members.
Willingness to be based in Kokopo, ENBP (no accommodation support provided) and work in field-based settings.
Punctual, reliable, and proactive.
Desirable:

About Burnet Institute
Burnet Institute is a leading Australian medical research and public health organisation working to achieve better health for vulnerable communities in Australia and internationally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has been implementing health research and development programs for almost 20 years, with offices in
Port Moresby, Kokopo and Western Province
.
About the HEAL-PNG Project
HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in
Morobe
and
East New Britain
provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.
About the Role
The
Clinical Health Extension Officer (HEO)
will play a key role in implementing the HEAL-PNG trial across selected health facilities. Working closely with the Provincial Health Authority (PHA), facility staff, and the HEAL-PNG project team, the Clinical HEO will support study implementation, staff training, and data collection activities.
The position will require initiative, strong clinical experience with NCDs, HIV and TB, and the ability to build strong working relationships across multiple stakeholders.
__________________________________________________________________________
Key Responsibilities
Support study activities at participating facilities, enduring adherence to research protocols and ethical standards.
Facilitate site onboarding, including assessments and leading staff training in NCD, TB and HIV management.
Manage data collection, entry, and quality assurance in a confidential and timely manner.
Maintain strong communication with facility and PHA staff, fostering collaboration and problem-solving.

Assist with procurement, stock control, and management of project materials and consumables.

Health Extension Officer qualification (Diploma + 1-year residency or Bachelors degree + 2-year residency).

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with fluency in English and Tok Pisin.
Strong organisational skills and ability to work both independently and in a team.
Ability to build rapport with health staff and community members.

Punctual, reliable, and proactive.

Experience in clinical research or health program implementation.

Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG, guided by the National WASH Policy (2015-2030).
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented
Finance and Operations Coordinator
to support the delivery of our East New Britain programs.
The
Finance and Operations Coordinator
is a critical support role responsible for ensuring strong financial management, compliance, and efficient operational systems for WaterAid’s East New Britain Program.
The position oversees financial and operational management for two key grants:
the
PacFresh H2O Program
[1]
in Rabaul and Pomio Districts; and
the
KIWA Initiative Grant
[2]
in Rabaul District.
Working across finance, administration, procurement, and operations, the role ensures accurate financial reporting, adherence to donor and WaterAid policies (including
GIZ and AFD procurement requirements
), and effective support to program implementation. The Finance and operations coordinator will manage internal control procedures to ensure WaterAid and donor policies and procedures are followed; support on project budget development, expenditure tracking and budget monitoring, and coordinating project audits. The position works closely with WaterAid’s East New Britain program team, local government partners, WaterAid PNG headquarters in Port Moresby, and the WaterAid regional support team in Australia.
About the Grants
The Finance and Operations Coordinator will provide support across two key grants:
Funded by GIZ, the
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
Funded by AFD, the
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Financial Management and Compliance
Oversee day-to-day financial management of PacFresh H2O and KIWA grants, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and donor compliance.
Lead project budget development, budget conversions, reforecasting, and ongoing budget monitoring using WaterAid financial systems (including WAPS and SunSystems)
Prepare and submit timely and accurate financial reports for internal management and donors.
Manage internal control procedures to ensure compliance with WaterAid and donor financial policies.
Lead the Finance Compliance Checklist to ensure all documentation is complete before and after payment authorisation
Coordinate and support internal and external audits, including preparation of documentation and follow-up actions.
Lead quarterly project expenditure transactions review to ensure that all project expenditure is correctly coded. If there are any errors or any missing transactions must advise the Operations Manager for adjustments.
Lead the accurate monthly and quarterly cost recovery process for the projects and ensure sufficient supporting documents are attached such as payslips, payroll transactions and timesheets.

Support preparation and processing of payments, ensuring approvals are obtained prior to payment.
Maintain general ledgers and ensure correct coding, GST treatment, and documentation.
Upload payment journals to SunSystems weekly and payroll journals fortnightly.
Create payments via corporate online banking when required.
Ensure all payments complete required Anti-Terrorism checks.
Payroll, Statutory and Tax Obligations
Support or process payroll using Able Payroll software and ensure timely distribution of payslips.
Upload staff NCSL and Nasfund contributions in line with statutory requirements.
Remit Salary and Wages Tax (SWT) and file GST with the IRC, ensuring records are accurate and safely stored
Ensure all project staff's timesheets are signed off and maintained in safe place
Procurement and Administration
Ensure procurement processes comply with GIZ, AFD and WaterAid procurement policies.
Support procurement planning, supplier engagement, contract documentation, and filing.
Follow up with suppliers to ensure complete and accurate supporting documentation.
Maintain organised digital and physical filing systems for financial and procurement records
Maintain project asset registers
Operations and Program Support
Provide operational and administrative support to the East New Britain Program team to enable timely and effective activity delivery.
Work closely with program staff to align financial planning with implementation needs.
Assist with monthly and quarterly reporting processes.
Support capacity building of WaterAid PNG staff and partners through finance training and coaching, in collaboration with the Senior Grants Accountant and Operations Manager.
Undertake other duties as required to support the effective implementation of the Country Program.
People

Provide regular orientation to all staff on People related policies and procedures to ensure adherence, including on the People Manual and Operations Manual.
Supervise the team (Administration, Logistics Officer and Boat Skipper) and ensure performance management reviews are conducted.
Resolve people issues as required, especially Operations staff in sub-offices

Multiple governmental and non-governmental stakeholders
