jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As the
Advisor, Mechanical
– Shovels & Drills
at Lihir Operations, you will provide critical mechanical and maintenance expertise that supports safe, reliable, and efficient asset performance. Your technical advice and hands‑on support will directly contribute to operational uptime, continuous improvement, and the capability development of the national workforce.
Working closely with Maintenance and Operations teams, you will play a key role in troubleshooting, risk management, and process optimisation while ensuring strict adherence to safety and compliance standards.
As part of our team, you will
Provide hands‑on technical support to Maintenance and Operations teams to resolve mechanical issues and improve asset performance
Coach and mentor the national workforce in maintenance, troubleshooting, and safe work practices
Support the investigation, diagnosis, and resolution of complex technical problems
Analyse operational and maintenance data to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities
Conduct regular inspections and audits to ensure compliance with safety, quality, and technical standards
Work closely with the maintenance team to coordinate equipment repairs and manage critical spares
Assist in the design, preparation, and delivery of technical training programs
Develop and provide practical recommendations to improve maintenance processes and reliability outcomes
Manage and monitor inventory for critical spare parts and equipment
Identify technical risks, implement mitigation measures, and continuously monitor risk controls
Stop unsafe work and actively always promote a strong safety culture
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Mechanical Trade Certificate or Degree in Mechanical Engineering
Proven experience maintaining heavy mining equipment (shovels, excavators, drills)
Demonstrated expat experience mentoring and developing a national workforce
Strong practical capability in troubleshooting, machine diagnostics, maintenance support, and process optimisation
Proven experience working within strict safety and compliance frameworks
The ability to analyse data and translate findings into actionable improvements
Sound risk identification and mitigation skills
Strong communication skills with the ability to coach, influence, and work collaboratively across disciplines
A proactive mindset, practical judgement, and commitment to continuous improvement
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster from PNG or Australia approved point of hire to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced professionals for the position of Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) within the Registry Division.
PNGUNRE is undergoing a period of institutional transformation aimed at strengthening governance, operational efficiency, compliance, and service delivery. The University is seeking a highly competent and results-oriented HR professional to support strategic organisational reform and institutional strengthening initiatives.
About the Role
Reporting directly to the Registrar, the Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) will provide strategic and operational leadership in strengthening the University’s human resource management systems, organisational structures, governance frameworks, and administrative processes to support institutional performance excellence.
The successful candidate will work closely with the Vice Chancellor, Senior Management Team, and key stakeholders including the Department of Personnel Management (DPM), to modernise HR systems, improve organisational effectiveness, and support the implementation of the University’s strategic priorities.
Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Strategic Human Resource Management
Leading the review and strengthening of HR management systems and practices.
Providing strategic HR advisory support to senior management.
Supporting workforce planning, succession planning, and talent management initiatives.
Developing strategies to improve organisational culture, accountability, productivity, and staff performance.
Organisational Review & Institutional Strengthening
Reviewing organisational structures, staffing establishments, and reporting frameworks.
Supporting implementation of recommendations arising from organisational and DPM reviews.
Reviewing job descriptions, classifications, and accountability frameworks.
Identifying operational inefficiencies and recommending improvement measures.
Assisting with institutional performance reviews and strategic planning processes.
HR Policy, Compliance & Administration
Reviewing and updating HR policies, procedures, and manuals in line with PNG labour laws and Public Service General Orders.
Improving employee records management systems and HR documentation standards.
Strengthening recruitment, onboarding, probation, disciplinary, leave, and separation processes.
Supporting audit readiness and institutional compliance initiatives.
Performance Management & Capacity Building
Assisting in the development of integrated performance management systems.
Developing HR operational templates, tools, and reporting mechanisms.
Conducting training, mentoring, and capacity-building programs for managers and supervisors.
Strategic Planning & Change Management
Supporting the implementation of the University’s Strategic Plan and operational plans.
Facilitating organisational change management initiatives.
Promoting professionalism, accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement across the University.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential Requirements
Applicants must possess:
A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Organisational Psychology, Business Management, Public Administration, or a related discipline.
A minimum of ten (10) years’ senior-level experience in human resources and organisational development.
Demonstrated experience in organisational review, strategic planning, change management, and institutional strengthening.

Strategic thinking and planning capability
Leadership and organisational influence

jobs.description:
ACCOUNTS PAYABLE - PORT MORESBY
Accounts Payable (AP) manages a company's short-term financial obligations, ensuring vendor invoices are accurately verified, coded, and paid on time
. Key duties include processing invoices, reconciling statements, managing expense reports, and maintaining vendor relationships. This role requires high attention to detail and proficiency in accounting software.
Core Responsibilities and Duties
Invoice Processing:
Receiving, approving, and coding invoices for payment, ensuring they match purchase orders and contracts.
Payment Execution:
Scheduling and preparing weekly or monthly payment batches (checks, ACH, wire transfers) to vendors and suppliers.
Reconciliation:
Reconciling processed work by verifying entries and comparing system reports to vendor statements.
Vendor Management:
Acting as the primary point of contact for vendor inquiries, resolving payment discrepancies, and maintaining updated vendor records.
Expense Reporting:
Reviewing employee credit card statements and expense reports for policy compliance.
Record Keeping:
Maintaining accurate, up-to-date, and organized historical records for auditing purposes.
Required Skills and Qualifications
Technical Skills:
Proficiency in accounting software (e.g., Attache) and Excel.
Attention to Detail:
High accuracy in data entry and numerical analysis to prevent payment errors.
Communication:
Strong verbal and written skills to interact with vendors and internal departments.
Organization:
Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, prioritize, and meet strict deadlines.
Education:
Studied accounting or finance preferred.
This position is available for immediate start with conditions commensurate with experience.
Attractive rates await the successful candidate.

jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Manus , Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a
Supervisor – Asset Management
, you will lead your team to safely deliver planned production outputs while maintaining high standards across
safety, quality, and performance
. Your leadership will directly influence team culture, operational efficiency, and plant reliability across a complex
fixed plant environment
.
You will play a key role in driving proactive safety behaviours, developing team capability, and ensuring maintenance activities are executed effectively across
crushing, grinding, flotation, and associated process plant systems
. Through strong leadership and decision-making, you will support business targets while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead and promote a strong safety-first culture through visible leadership, coaching, and safety interactions
Deliver agreed production and maintenance outcomes in line with plans and Superintendent expectations
Set clear goals and performance standards for your team aligned with operational strategy
Supervise, coordinate and assign daily tasks to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently
Monitor team performance, ensuring compliance with procedures, policies, and safe systems of work
Provide ongoing coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to build team capability
Engage and collaborate with peers, planners, and support teams to achieve site objectives
Participate in shift handovers, reporting, and maintaining accurate records of key events
Identify, escalate, and manage risks, delays, and operational issues impacting performance
Drive cost efficiency, identifying opportunities for savings and minimising waste
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Minimum Grade 12 education with a Mechanical Trade Qualification (essential), NATTB Trades Certificate in Maintenance Fitting highly regarded
Current PNG Driver’s Licence
3–5 years’ experience in fixed plant maintenance, ideally within mining or heavy industry, with demonstrated progression into leadership or supervisory responsibilities
Proven experience leading teams in a safety-critical environment, including conducting safety interactions, coaching, and incident reporting/investigation
Strong hands-on experience in mechanical maintenance, including fitting, machining, fabrication, pump rebuilds, pipe fitting, and HDPE welding
Solid technical knowledge of hydraulic systems, pumps, valves, crushers, mills, and conveyor systems
Strong understanding and application of safe systems of work, PNG Mine Safety Act, and site HSE frameworks
Demonstrated ability to plan, prioritise, and supervise work, ensuring quality and productivity targets are met
Effective communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills with the ability to engage and influence diverse teams
Proven ability to coach, develop, and manage performance while fostering a positive and accountable team culture
High level of organisational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment
Proactive approach to problem-solving, continuous improvement, cost control, and waste reduction
Ability or willingness to obtain mobile equipment tickets (e.g. forklift, gantry crane
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a
28:14 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO)
roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling (see more at
https://lisstm.com.au/)
, quality healthcare services, and household support.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu.  In addition, this position will also play and important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are a NATTB certified electrician, with PPL certification and demonstrated experience within a mining / minerals processing environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control Centre’s, LV and HV transfers and starters.
The ability to fault find and develop appropriate solution in order to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Superintendent Mine Planning, you will be responsible for developing and overseeing mine plans across time horizons ranging from two years to one day, ensuring alignment with long‑term strategies, production goals, and regulatory requirements. Your leadership will shape the accuracy, efficiency, and integrity of mine planning processes, driving continuous improvement, strengthening operational performance, and supporting safe, responsible mining. You will play a central role in coordinating planning activities, guiding technical teams, and delivering high‑quality insights that enable informed decision‑making across the operation.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead the preparation and execution of Monthly, Weekly, and Daily mine plans to support operational delivery.
Develop and oversee <2‑year mine plans (Business Plan and Quarterly Forecast) to ensure alignment with the 5‑Year Plan, production targets, and regulatory obligations.
Manage reconciliation reporting across daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual horizons to track performance against plan and support strategic objectives.
Drive continuous improvement through mine design updates, block model refinements, financial and operational input reviews, and fleet assessments.
Provide direction, support, and influence to mine operations to enhance operational effectiveness while ensuring compliance with safety standards and mining regulations.
Lead and develop a team of 25, coordinating training, capability development, and proactive Fatal Risk Management processes to identify, mitigate, and monitor risks.
Prepare scopes of work, manage budgets, and oversee mine planning consultants and contracts, ensuring adherence to project specifications, safety standards, and organisational goals.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or a related discipline (essential).
Advanced proficiency in mine design, drill and blast, mine scheduling, and performance‑to‑plan reconciliation.
Strong understanding of mine operations, dispatch systems, risk management, and business improvement principles.
Demonstrated experience in project and/or contract management.
Proven leadership capability with experience managing and developing technical teams.
Familiarity with mining software and cost‑modelling tools; advanced proficiency in mine planning and optimisation software (Deswik and MineSight highly regarded).
Strong problem‑solving ability, including the capacity to analyse complex information, identify patterns, and make effective decisions.
Well‑developed social process skills, including self‑awareness, collaboration, conflict resolution, and the ability to foster an inclusive, high‑performance team environment.
Commitment, determination, and follow‑through to deliver productive outcomes aligned with Newmont’s purpose, values, and desired culture
Your Work Environment
You’ll be part of a dynamic mining operation at our Lihir site, collaborating closely with internal teams across mine operations, geology, processing, asset management, and technical services, as well as engaging with external consultants and contractors. The role combines office-based planning with field-based oversight.
The role is offered on a
Residential
basis with a
5:2 roster
, or on a
FIFO
basis from approved points of hire within Australia and Papua New Guinea, operating on an even-time
21:21 roster
.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling (see more at
https://lisstm.com.au/)
, quality healthcare services, and household support.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
TITLE
SENIOR WASH TECHNICAL OFFICER
REPORTING TO
WASH ADVISOR & DOTTED LINE TO WEWAK PROJECT COORDINATOR
LOCATION
WaterAid – Wewak sub office, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea
CLASSIFICATION
E
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
Permanent,
Three-year contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District and Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province and East New Britain Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
WASH in PNG
Papua New Guinea (PNG) faces a severe WASH crisis, with some of the lowest access rates globally. Only 45% of the population has access to basic drinking water, 19% to basic sanitation, and 28% to household handwashing facilities with soap (JMP, 2024). WASH access in healthcare facilities (HCFs) is critically low, with 86% not meeting basic service levels (National Department of Health & WaterAid, 2021). Addressing these gaps is essential for improving public health, particularly for pregnant women and newborns.
The overarching goal of the Advancing Quality Universal Access to WASH in East Sepik Province (AQUA) project is to improve access to safe, clean and sustainable WASH and enhance health outcomes in East Sepik Province. By focusing on target districts, including Wewak district, the project aims to catalyze sustainable WASH system improvements, advancing the Wewak District WASH Plan (2024 – 2027). A particular emphasis on WASH in healthcare facilities will enhance the health and safety of patients and healthcare workers. Additionally, the project will strengthen the capacity, leadership and evidence base of the East Sepik Provincial WASH committee and Health Authority, supporting the future scale-up of essential WASH services.
Inclusive, Climate Resilient WASH in Wewak District, East Sepik, Papua New Guinea (TCCF 2024-2025): This is a continuation of WaterAid's WASH service delivery efforts in the Wewak District, East Sepik province, which has been ongoing for the past three years with support from TCCF (2021-2025). Our activities have primarily centered around increasing access to clean, safe, and reliable water sources, as well as offering appropriate sanitation and hygiene solutions to both communities and healthcare facilities.
By addressing critical WASH challenges, this project will contribute to sustainable, equitable water and sanitation access in PNG’s most vulnerable communities. The goal aligns with Country Strategy aim 2- WaSH in Public Health and increase the political will and commitment for them prioritise WaSH in Health Care Facilities ensuring the policy, practise and investment are aligned well.
Position Summary
The Senior WASH Technical Officer will support in the implementation and partner management projects delivering improved health outcomes through inclusive and equitable water, sanitation and hygiene across PNG.
The Senior WASH Technical Officer works closely with WaterAid Technical Advisor and the wider program and partners’ teams in providing technical assistance to infrastructure projects now focusing on the AQUA project in Wewak District in East Sepik province. PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.
ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE OFFICER
The Finance Department is seeking for an experienced candidate for the position of Accounts Receivable Officer based in
Port Moresby.
This role is responsible to ensure that the company receives payments for goods or services provided to its clients or customers.
Plays a crucial role in maintaining the financial health of the company by ensuring that incoming cash flows are managed effectively and that outstanding receivables are collected in a timely manner.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Generating and issuing invoices for goods sold or services rendered to customers.
Recording and tracking payments received from customers, ensuring accuracy in payment application, and reconciling discrepancies.
Monitoring and managing the accounts receivable ledger, including reviewing aging reports to identify overdue accounts and taking appropriate actions for collections.
Communicating with customers regarding their outstanding balances, payment terms, and any inquiries or disputes related to invoices or payments. Effective communication skills are essential for maintaining positive relationships with customer and resolving any issues that arise promptly.
Initiating and following up on collection efforts for past due accounts, which may involve contacting customers via phone, email, or mail to arrange payment arrangements or resolve disputes.
Assessing the creditworthiness of new customers, establishing credit limits and terms, and periodically reviewing and adjusting credit terms based on payment history and financial stability.
Reconciling accounts receivable balances with general ledger accounts and resolving any discrepancies or issues that arise.
Generating regular reports on accounts receivable aging, cash flow, collections activity, and other key performance indicators for management review and decision-making.
Maintaining accurate and up-to-date records of customer accounts, payment transactions, correspondence, and any collection efforts.
Identifying opportunities to streamline accounts receivable processes, improve efficiency, and enhance cash flow management.
Ensuring compliance with relevant accounting standards, company policies, and regulatory requirements related to accounts receivable management and reporting.
Engage and participate in financial close process by preparing schedules, reconciliations, and reports related to accounts receivable balances. Ensure that all receivables are properly accounted for and reflected accurately in financial statements.
During internal or external audits, provide support by furnishing documentation, answering inquiries, and assisting auditors in verifying the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable records.
Maintain physical filing systems to store hard copies of financial documents. This may involve organizing documents alphabetically, numerically, or categorically in file cabinets or folders. Each document is labeled with relevant information such as vendor name, invoice number, and date to enable quick identification.
Utilize electronic filing systems or document management software to store and manage financial documents electronically. Create digital folders or directories to organize documents by vendor, transaction type, or date, making it easier to search, retrieve, and share files as needed.
Collaborate with other departments such as purchasing, finance, engineering, operations, commercial, support documents and procurement to ensure smooth coordination of activities related to accounts receivable, including customer management, budgeting, and forecasting.

A bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field is often preferred.
Prior experience in accounts receivable, accounting or a related financial role is highly desirable. Experience with invoicing, payment processing, collections, and credit management is often highly valued.
Accounting Knowledge - a strong understanding of basic accounting principles and practices is essential. Familiarity with financial statements, accounting software, and ERP systems may also be required.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Mechanical Technician will execute safe and effective mechanical maintenance activities to support the reliability, integrity, and availability of fixed plant equipment across operational areas. Perform planned, breakdown, and corrective maintenance tasks in accordance with maintenance strategies, procedures, and work management processes to minimise downtime and support continuous plant operations. Contribute to defect identification, equipment improvement initiatives, and quality maintenance execution while maintaining compliance with safety, environmental, and operational standards.
Essential Duties
Conduct routine mechanical inspections across operational equipment and record findings to support proactive and planned maintenance activities.
Execute and assist with breakdown, corrective, and preventative maintenance tasks to restore equipment reliability and operational performance.
Perform maintenance activities in accordance with site safety standards, isolation procedures, statutory requirements, and company maintenance practices.
Support Rotable Refurbishments, Fixed Crane Maintenance, and Fixed Compressor Maintenance activities to ensure equipment availability and reliability targets are achieved.
Maintain accurate maintenance history and equipment records through effective documentation of repairs, inspections, adjustments, and component replacements within maintenance management systems.
Monitor equipment condition and performance trends, identifying defects, risks, and early signs of failure, escalating findings and recommendations to Supervisors for intervention planning.
Assist with calibration, testing, and commissioning activities to ensure equipment operates within required performance and operational standards.
Support spare parts and inventory management through tracking component usage and identifying critical spares requirements for maintenance activities.
Promote a strong safety culture by actively participating in safety interactions, toolbox meetings, hazard identification, and continuous improvement initiatives aligned to FRM objectives.
Training & Experience
Significant demonstrated experience in fixed plant maintenance within heavy industry or mining environments, including Fixed Cranes and Compressor maintenance activities.
Proven experience maintaining and repairing fixed plant equipment including valves, gearbox drives, conveyor systems, pulleys, sprockets, pumps, feeder tracks, interstage screens, vibrating screens, fixed cranes, and compressors.
Relevant Mechanical Trade Certificate or Engineering Certificate essential, with PNG Driver’s Licence – Class 6 required.
Sound understanding of safe work procedures, lifting equipment operations, and site HSE requirements.
Competent in the use of maintenance tools, equipment, and maintenance management systems including SAP and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capability with the ability to proactively resolve maintenance issues.
Effective verbal and written English communication skills with the ability to work across diverse cultural environments.
Strong interpersonal and active listening skills with the ability to work collaboratively within team environments.
Demonstrated ability to manage time effectively, adapt to operational changes, and support continuous improvement and waste reduction initiatives.
Works in accordance with PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Standards, Safety Policies and Procedures,
Newmont Environment policies and all departmental operating procedures.
Skilled in the use of SAP sofware.
Uses interpersonal negotiation skills and influencing skills to maintain the agreed breakdown work against weekly schedules.
Demonstrated knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Word and Excel.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

(Not “I helped my cousin once” experienced)
PNG Motors is looking for a highly experienced Panel Beater to join our growing workshop team supporting some of the world’s leading automotive brands including Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC, and Joylong.
This role is for someone who genuinely knows the trade properly. We are specifically looking for applicants with more than 4 years of real hands-on panel beating experience. Not workshop exposure. Not “assistant” experience. Actual experience repairing damaged vehicles, restoring panels properly, and understanding the difference between a quick patch-up job and professional repair work. If you do not have solid panel beating experience, please do not apply.
The Role
You’ll be responsible for repairing damaged vehicle panels, restoring body alignment, straightening chassis and frames where required, replacing damaged components, and preparing vehicles for paint to a high professional standard. You’ll work across everything from smaller accident repairs through to major collision work on passenger, commercial, and fleet vehicles.
This is a busy workshop environment where quality, efficiency, and workmanship matter equally. Attention to detail is critical because customers notice poor panel gaps, uneven body lines, bad preparation work, and shortcuts immediately. We are looking for someone who takes genuine pride in producing clean, straight, professional repair work and understands the importance of maintaining workshop standards at all times.
What We’re Looking For
We want someone with more than 4 years of proven panel beating experience who can work independently, maintain quality under pressure, and consistently deliver high-standard repairs. You should understand chassis alignment, structural repair work, repair timelines, and workshop efficiency without sacrificing workmanship.
You should also take pride in clean workmanship, understand workshop discipline, and work safely and professionally at all times. Experience using modern repair equipment, measuring systems, welders, and working on commercial vehicles will be highly regarded.
Who Will Struggle Here
People who cut corners will struggle here. People who think filler fixes everything will struggle here. People who need constant supervision or rush jobs out the door without caring about quality will struggle here.
This role suits experienced tradesmen who understand the difference between simply getting a vehicle out of the workshop and repairing it properly.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive organisations, representing globally recognised vehicle brands and operating professional workshop facilities across the country.
You’ll be joining a workshop team that values skill, reliability, professionalism, and workmanship. We take pride in doing repairs properly and maintaining standards our customers trust. jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Planner, Scheduler, you will play a critical role in optimising maintenance planning and scheduling to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable operations across the site. You will be responsible for developing highly executable work plans, enabling maintenance teams to deliver work safely and effectively while driving continuous improvement in work management practices.
As part of our team, you will
Develop and maintain detailed maintenance plans and schedules to support safe and efficient execution of work.
Manage new work requests, ensuring accuracy, prioritisation, and timely conversion into work orders.
Collaborate with Supervisors and stakeholders to scope work, identify required resources, materials, and timelines.
Create comprehensive work packs, including task lists, procedures, safety requirements, and job planning details.
Coordinate scheduling activities, including forecasting, reporting, and stakeholder alignment for weekly and shutdown work.
Monitor work order completion and ensure accurate coding, reporting, and closure in the CMMS.
Analyse performance data and KPIs, identifying improvement opportunities and implementing corrective actions.
Support shutdown planning and scheduling, including critical path analysis and schedule optimisation.
Build strong relationships with site stakeholders, including maintenance, operations, and supply chain teams.
Drive operational excellence by ensuring adherence to work management processes, systems, and standards.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Exposure to mechanical and/or electrical maintenance environments is highly beneficial, with trade or engineering backgrounds (Mechanical or Electrical) considered advantageous.
Demonstrated experience in maintenance planning and scheduling within mining, heavy industry, or a similar environment.
Strong working knowledge of SAP work management systems, including work order planning, scheduling, and reporting.
Proven ability to develop detailed maintenance plans, schedules, and work packs.
Experience in data analysis, KPI tracking, and continuous improvement, with the ability to translate insights into practical outcomes.
Strong understanding of work management processes, maintenance strategies, and shutdown planning.
Strong capability in planning and scheduling tools, including MS Project and advanced Excel, to build clear, optimised schedules and effectively communicate plans to site leaders and maintenance teams.
Experience facilitating and contributing to planning meetings, scheduling discussions, and cross-functional coordination forums, ensuring alignment between stakeholders and clarity in execution priorities.
Well-developed problem-solving skills, including root cause analysis and performance improvement.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across teams.
Ability to manage competing priorities and work within structured systems and processes.
A commitment to safety, with a strong understanding of incorporating hazard controls and safe work practices into planning activities.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:10 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) day shift roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
You will operate within a dynamic and technically focused environment at Lihir Operations, working closely with Maintenance Supervisors, Engineers, Reliability teams, Supply Chain, and external contractors.
This role is highly collaborative, requiring strong engagement across multidisciplinary teams to align maintenance planning with operational priorities. You will be supported by established work management systems, data tools, and business processes to deliver high-quality, timely outcomes.
The role offers the opportunity to contribute to a high-performing maintenance function, driving reliability and efficiency across a world-class mining operation.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be joining a globally recognised organisation committed to safety, sustainability, and operational excellence.
We offer:
The opportunity to work on a world-class mining operation with industry-leading systems and practices.
A strong focus on safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Career development opportunities and the chance to build expertise in planning, reliability, and operational excellence.
A supportive and inclusive team environment where your contributions are valued.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As part of the team, you will lead the delivery of mid- to long-term mine plans that align with production targets, strategic objectives, and regulatory requirements. You will play a critical role in optimising mine design, sequencing, and scheduling to maximise resource recovery and operational efficiency. Working closely with geology, engineering, and operations teams, you will ensure integrated and practical planning outcomes, monitor performance against plan, and implement improvements that enhance productivity, reduce costs, and support safe, reliable mining operations.
As part of the team, you will:
Supervise and coordinate mine planning activities to ensure alignment with operational goals
Develop and maintain mid- and long-term mine plans, schedules, and forecasts
Analyse production data, track performance, and address variances
Provide technical guidance and support to the mine planning team
Foster collaboration across geology, engineering, and operations functions
Identify and drive continuous improvement opportunities in planning processes
Manage risk by identifying, assessing, and implementing mitigation strategies
Lead and contribute to a positive, productive, and safety-focused team environment
Prerequisites for the Role
Degree in
Mining Engineering
Minimum
5 years’ experience
in mining operations, preferably in open cut mining
Strong knowledge of mine design, scheduling, and forecasting
Experience with
MinePlan, Deswik, and Modular Mining systems
Solid understanding of drill & blast and its impact on load and haul
Demonstrated capability in data analysis, performance monitoring, and reporting
Sound knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and mining safety systems
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills
Ability to work effectively in a
multinational and remote operating environment
Your work environment
This role is offered on a
21:21 days only
Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Coordinator
CARE International in PNG is recruiting a Monitoring Evaluation, Accountability and Learning MEAL Coordinator based in Goroka. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
CARE International in Papua New Guinea (PNG) has a focus on Gender Equality, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Peace Building, Agriculture and Health.
The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Coordinator will support the Program Quality (PQ) Advisor in CARE Papua New Guinea (PNG) in delivering comprehensive Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning across Country Office (CO) projects. The main responsibilities include implementing robust MEL frameworks and databases, ensuring projects are aligned with MEAL minimum standards and promoting a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
The role will lead support processes and practices across CARE PNG programs to promote evidence-based reporting, adaptive learning, outcome-focused data for decision-making, reflective practice, and genuine accountability to impact populations, donors, and key stakeholders.
The role is also responsible for the development, coordination, and reinforcement of Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) practices throughout all CARE PNG programming, both within the organization and with partners. The position provides technical support to project teams and partners, ensuring that accountability are integrated at the program and project level, following the accountability framework, developing and strengthening the Community-Response Feedback Mechanism (CRFM) system based on risk matrixes and risk mitigation plans for all projects.
The employee must demonstrate full compliance with all CARE policies and procedures.
This role is based in Goroka but will require travel to CARE PNG’s field offices and project sites as and when required.
SELECTION CRITERIA
Qualification:
Required
: Bachelor’s degree in planning and development studies, Monitoring & Evaluation, Social Sciences, Computer Science, Physics, Statistics or other relevant field.
Desired
: Master's degree in a relevant field such as Monitoring & Evaluation, Knowledge Management, Research, Social Science, Statistics or a recognised postgraduate qualification / accredited short course in Monitoring & Evaluation.
Experience:
Required: A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in a MEAL, of which 3 has been spent on MEAL management role in programming across one of the following sectors; education, health, humanitarian response, livelihood and economic empowerment, and peacebuilding. Intermediate level experience in data analysis using quantitative and qualitative methods, as well as tools development and template, rolling out training.
Desired: 3+ years of experience setting up and managing MEAL systems across multiple programs and sectors, including FAM/CRFM systems and Kobo-based data collection at scale.
Experience coordinating MEAL functions at country or national level for an INGO, including portfolio-level dashboards and consolidated reporting. Experience working in both development and humanitarian contexts, including emergency-response and grant-funded projects. Experience supporting organisational impact reporting process. Experience designing and conducting baselines, mid-term reviews, end-line evaluations and post-implementation/post-distribution monitoring (PIM/PDM).
Skills and knowledge:
Required:
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and to manage multiple competing priorities to consistently meet deadlines.
Strong writing and analytical skills, with proven ability to produce high-quality MEAL reports, technical briefs, monitoring reports and learning products for internal and donor audiences.
Demonstrated ability to independently develop monitoring tools, data collection forms, indicator tracking sheets, logframes, theories of change and results frameworks.
Demonstrated ability to support learning events, reflection sessions, workshops and training for staff, partners and stakeholders.
Proficient in data analysis techniques, including basic statistical analysis (descriptive analysis) and qualitative coding/thematic analysis.
Strong working knowledge of Kobo Toolbox (form design, deployment, data export and troubleshooting) and the ability to train others in its use.
Practical knowledge of M&E methodologies, including logframes, results chains, theories of change, baselines, evaluations and assessments and of writing technical MEAL reports.
Strong knowledge of humanitarian standards including Sphere, Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS), the Red Cross Code of Conduct, Do No Harm (DNH) principles and OECD-DAC evaluation criteria.
Excellent verbal and written English.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, training and facilitation skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills; able to work under pressure and balance competing priorities in a complex environment.
Demonstrated honesty, reliability and trustworthiness, with the ability to maintain confidentiality, with FAM, safeguarding and case-handling work.
Computer skills, including Microsoft Office 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams).
Desired:
3+ years of experience setting up and managing MEAL systems across multiple programs and sectors, including FAM/CRFM systems and Kobo-based data collection at scale.
Experience coordinating MEAL functions at country or national level for an INGO, including portfolio-level dashboards and consolidated reporting.
Experience working in both development and humanitarian contexts, including emergency-response and grant-funded projects.
Experience supporting organisational impact reporting process.
Experience designing and conducting baselines, mid-term reviews, end-line evaluations and post-implementation/post-distribution monitoring (PIM/PDM).
Competencies:
Organizational skills for Information gathering and processing– Able to locate and collect data from a variety of sources and analyze and ability to synthesize complex information in concise reports for program design, program quality, and learning.
Analytical thinking – Able to integrate information from diverse sources, often involving large amounts of data; this includes synthesizing information and summarizing it into key points for use by others
Teamwork – Able to work effectively with other people within a work group and across units and line management boundaries.
Developing others – Able to foster the development of others by providing a supportive learning environment and providing coaching and mentoring as needed.
Influencing – Able to generate commitment and build consensus among others and gain their support
Communicating and sharing ideas and information - Able to present information and express opinions confidently to internal and external audiences

Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas suppliers, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based at our offices in Port Moresby with the Santos Foundation, the Finance Officer is responsible for supporting the Finance Manager, Finance Reporting Senior Manager and Finance Services Senior Manager to execute month-end processes, provide support to core finance services of accounts payable and receivables and to ensure the timely reporting of Santos and other donor grant funds expenditure and revenue for both PNG and Australia jurisdictions.
Key accountabilities include:
Business partnering with Program Management teams to ensure accounting matters are appropriately explained and issues resolved in a timely manner
Ensuring accuracy of SAP journals in regard to WBS and cost centre coding, including cost corrections being done on a timely basis
Monthly review of open POs and preparation of monthly accruals for Finance Manager review
Ensuring bank statement clearing activities are executed in a timely manner
Preparing monthly balance sheet reconciliations for Finance Managers review and ensuring execution of plans to clear aged items for all Foundation trial balances (PNG, Australia, Timor Leste & Alaska)
Monitoring and reconciling inter-company transactions monthly for Finance Manager’s review
Preparing monthly accruals and correcting entries for all Foundation trial balances (PNG, Australia, Timor Leste & Alaska)
Ensuring all asset purchases are recorded in SAP on a timely basis
Planning and executing annual fixed asset verification exercise with recommendations for additions or disposals to Finance Manager
Preparing monthly donation tracker and maintaining the donation register and proper recording of revenue invoices for Santos and all external grants including Bel isi PNG subscriptions
Assisting with completion of budgets and re-forecasts in partnership with program teams
Preparing monthly group cost allocations report, annual financial statements and annual tax returns for Finance Manager reviewAssisting with audit queries by providing required supporting documents
Ad hoc requests and projects as directed by the Finance Manager, Finance Services Senior Manager and Finance Reporting Senior Manager
What you’ll bring:
You will be experienced in:
A minimum of 5 years in a General Ledger or Finance Business Partner role
Demonstrated experience in General Ledger activities
Strong compliance and financial control experience
Proven experience in month-end close activities and preparation of monthly balance sheet reconciliation
Sourcing, sorting and reporting data from SAP or other ERP systems
Medium to advanced Excel skills
Building and maintaining good working relationships within a multicultural workforce
Working independently, using high-level analytical and conceptual thinking
Using initiative and being proactive in resolving issues
Employing high-level communication skills, both oral and written.
You will hold a degree in accounting, finance or business management and be CPA qualified. Post-graduate qualifications in finance management are desirable but not essential.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB 02nd June 2026.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our maintenance team on site, the Crane Operator is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of mobile or overhead cranes to lift, move, and position loads in accordance with lift plans, site procedures, and regulatory requirements. In this role ensures all lifting activities are conducted safely and collaboratively with rigging and ground crews, whilst observing and adhering to the workplace health & safety policies.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Ensuring that the sections daily work plans are executed as directed.
This position reports to the Supervisor FPM team accountable for providing effective operation of crane owned by K92 Mining.
Maintain good working relationship with colleague workers.
Responsible for housekeeping.
Operate cranes to lift and place materials safely and accurately.
Conduct pre-start inspections and report defects immediately.
Follow lift plans, load charts, and supervisor directions.
Work closely with riggers during lifts.
Establish and maintain safe exclusion zones when lifting.
Monitor load stability, weather conditions, and ground conditions.
Stop work when conditions become unsafe and notify supervisor.
Maintain accurate logbooks and equipment records.
Assist in crane setup, assembly, and dismantling as required.
Participate in JSAs/SOP’s, toolbox talks, and risk assessments.
Shift work, overtime, and shutdowns may be required
Outdoor, site-based environments.
Exposure to weather, noise, and heavy machinery.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have all or some of the following
Experience in mining, heavy industry, or major infrastructure projects.
Minimum Grade eight (8) educational qualification, but preferable a Grade ten (10) certificate or PETT courses.
Valid PNG Class 7 driver’s licence
Working at Heights certification.
Proven crane operating experience.
Dogging or Rigging licence
A minimum number of years’ crane experience (e.g., 2–5 years) a prerequisite.
Ability to read and write both Pidgin and English
Strong understanding of crane operations and lifting principles.
Ability to interpret load charts and lifting diagrams.
Excellent situational awareness and hazard recognition.
Effective communication and teamwork.
Problem-solving during complex or changing lift conditions.
High attention to safety and detail.
Must have at least 5 or more years of truck driving.
Must be able to understand the company’s targets and work towards achieving the targets.
Have a strong understanding of the mining cycle.
Flexible, adaptable and be a strong and proactive team player.
Ability to meet agreed schedules and deadlines.
Ability to maintain good working relationships with other team members and K92 Mining Ltd employees.
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining core values
Excellent problem solving and decision-making capability
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Diesel Fitter trade qualification.

Technical and product knowledge of Caterpillar equipment and operating system.
Competent using CAT SIS and ET.
Skills to effectively diagnose and repair electrical systems.
Competent in the repair, rebuild and maintenance of large earth moving equipment.
