jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Analyst – End User Computing, you will play a key role in ensuring the seamless operation, reliability, and security of end-user technology across site. You will support the implementation, maintenance, and optimisation of professional applications and devices, while enhancing digital services through user engagement and continuous improvement.
As part of our team, you will
Provide technical support and maintenance for laptops, desktops, mobile devices, and video conferencing systems.
Ensure the reliable operation of IT equipment, including printers, audio-visual systems, and meeting room technologies.
Troubleshoot and resolve technology issues promptly to deliver a high level of customer satisfaction.
Support end-users with professional applications, ensuring a positive and efficient user experience.
Monitor and maintain the security and integrity of end-user devices and data.
Configure and maintain IT equipment and systems across site operations.
Gather and act on user feedback to continuously improve digital services and support delivery.
Contribute to regional and global IT projects and support vendors and contractors to ensure service delivery standards are met.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a technology-related certification.
Broad knowledge of ITIL processes.
Knowledge of IT infrastructure, including laptops, mobile devices, video conferencing systems, and applications.
Proven experience in technical support, troubleshooting, and maintaining IT equipment and systems.
Familiarity with IT service management best practices and preventative maintenance strategies.
Solid skills in problem-solving and issue resolution, with the ability to apply practical judgement and continuous improvement techniques.
Proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools (Teams, Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work across diverse teams and users.
A proactive approach with a focus on customer experience, teamwork, and service delivery excellence.
Your team and work environment
You will be part of the Digital function, working closely with site-based teams including Operations, HR, Finance, Safety, and end-users, as well as external vendors, contractors, and service providers.
This role operates in a dynamic and service-oriented environment where collaboration, responsiveness, and continuous improvement are critical to supporting site operations and ensuring seamless technology performance across the business.
This role is offered on a 21:21 day shift Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be part of a global organisation committed to safety, innovation, and operational excellence.
We offer:
The opportunity to work within a high-performing and collaborative IT environment.
Exposure to diverse technologies and global systems supporting critical operations.
A strong culture of continuous improvement, learning, and development.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

We are seeking a skilled and safety-focused Hydrostatic Test Technician to join our Calibration and Testing Department at our Motukea facility. Reporting to the Senior Calibration & Testing Technician, this hands-on workshop role is responsible for the safe and accurate pressure testing of hose assemblies, valves, pressure relief valves, pressure vessels, and other pressure-containing items, in accordance with company procedures and applicable industry standards.
Key Responsibilities
Hydrostatic testing of hydraulic, industrial, composite, and UHP hose assemblies.
Pressure and destructive testing of offshore floating hose assemblies.
Seat and shell pressure testing of valves.
Setting, adjustment, and testing of spring-loaded pressure relief valves.

Trade qualification in a mechanical, fitting, hydraulic, or related discipline preferred.
Demonstrated experience in pressure testing, valve servicing, or a comparable workshop environment.
Strong mechanical aptitude and a methodical, safety-first approach to work.
Clear understanding of the hazards of pressurised systems and stored energy.
Familiarity with relevant industry standards (e.g. ISO/IEC 17025, AS 1271, AS 3788, API 527) an advantage.
Ability to read and follow technical procedures and accurately complete test worksheets, with computer literacy in Excel and digital data-logging software.
Good written and verbal English, and the physical capability for workshop work.
Valid Driver's Licence an advantage.

People & Culture Officer
PCS: People & Culture Services - Port Moresby, NCD
Job Title: People & Cultures Officer
Reports To: Head of People & Culture
Location: 11 Mile, Sogeri Road, Port Moresby, NCD
Employment Type: Full-Time
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 34 years. Today we are in one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 11 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and future citizens on Papua New Guinea.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learned skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
POSITION OVERVIEW
The People & Culture Officer is responsible for supporting the administrative and operational functions of the People & Culture Department, ensuring the smooth coordination of HR administration, employee records, payroll support, onboarding, employee welfare, and employee relations activities across the University.
The People & Culture Officer will play a key role in supporting daily HR operations while contributing to a positive, professional, and employee-focused work environment. This position requires a highly organized individual with strong interpersonal skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
The People & Culture Officer is expected to be a conceptual thinker with excellent organizational and time management skills. The person in this role must be reliable, able to follow instructions accurately, multitask effectively, and maintain confidentiality at all times.
Key Responsibilities
HR Administration & Employee Records
Manage and maintain the University’s BambooHR database and employee registry
Ensure all employee records, contracts, and employment details are accurate and up to date
Prepare and manage employment contracts, onboarding documentation, and employee correspondence
Ensure all startup and onboarding forms are completed correctly on the employee’s first day
Produce, file, and distribute HR-related documentation
Create and manage calendars for the P&C team
Schedule HR meetings and employee-related activities
Generate reports on HR activities and departmental performance
Act as a point of contact with public service providers and external stakeholders
Assist in organizing and coordinating staff events and HR activities
Maintain confidentiality of all employees and HR information
2. HR Operations & Payroll Support
Coordinate onboarding and orientation programs for new employees
Support payroll processing and assist in resolving payroll-related issues
Coordinate with banks, Nasfund, and NCSL regarding employee account details and contribution updates
Assist with employee benefits administration, claims, and payment invoice approvals
Manage staff medical cover and liaise with the insurance broker and nominated medical facilities to ensure effective administration and coordination of employee medical benefits
Assist with termination processes, including preparation of exit documentation and conducting exit interviews
Ensure compliance with HR policies, procedures, and employment regulations
Assist in developing and reviewing HR policies and procedures as required
3. Employee Relations & Staff Support
Respond to HR-related queries and provide support to employees on HR policies, procedures, and workplace matters
Handle employee grievances and complaints professionally and confidentially
Support positive employee relations and contribute to a healthy work culture
Create and promote exceptional employee experience for all staff across IBSUniversity
Provide guidance to employees on HR rules, processes, and staff welfare matters
Work closely with management and staff to support fair and consistent HR practices
Assist in resolving workplace concerns and escalating matters where necessary
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in human resource management, Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field
Minimum of 3 years’ work experience in a similar role

Good understanding of PNG Labour Laws and the PNG Employment Act
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu.  In addition, this position will also play and important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are a NATTB certified electrician, with PPL certification and demonstrated experience within a mining / minerals processing environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control Centre’s, LV and HV transfers and starters.
The ability to fault find and develop appropriate solution in order to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
We have an opportunity for a Engineer Reliability, Electrical to join our high-performing team at Lihir. This is a Fly-In-Fly-Out (FIFO) role on a 21:21 roster.
Essential Duties
Design and review maintenance strategies for equipment
Monitor equipment performance data and analyze outcomes
Advise asset planning on work packages and schedule requirements
Adhere to compliance with safety and environmental standards
Prepare reports on equipment reliability and maintenance and conduct defect elimination meetings
Assess relevant risks, implement mitigation measures, and continuously monitor for risks
Conduct or participate in work management meetings weekly
Translate reliability opportunities into cost and/ or performance improvements
Provide guidance and training on root cause analysis to execution team
Provide design for reliability input for capital project
Training & Experience
Degree in Electrical Engineering
Identify practical application proficiency in maintenance planning and risk mitigation that best supports these activities within your organization.
Familiarity with safety and environmental compliance, including the ability to carry out specific activities using advanced tools and processes to achieve defined business outcomes.
Strong administrative skills and attention to detail to review and manage weekly plans
Competent computer skills with Microsoft Outlook, PowerPoint, Word Document, and Excel.
Experience with SAP
Valid drivers license
Working Conditions
This is a Fly-In-Fly-Out (FIFO) role on a 21:21 roster within our Reliability team.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS) began its journey in 1987 as a modest initiative under Nades & Associates, primarily offering revision classes to support the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants, now known as CPA PNG. Over the past 36 years, IBS has grown steadily into a private university-level institution. Today, IBS is recognised as one of the largest business schools in Papua New Guinea, offering degree programmes in Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology. In addition, the institution continues to provide academic pathways for Grade 10 and 12 school leavers, as well as industry-recognised certification opportunities for experienced professionals seeking formal qualifications in their respective fields. This success has been made possible through the dedication and commitment of our team, whose collective efforts continue to make a meaningful contribution to Papua New Guinea by helping to educate and empower both current and future citizens.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but also enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The FE Maintenance Advisor is the senior technical authority. responsible for overseeing the entire work management process to ensure maintenance activities are prioritised, planned, scheduled, and executed to the highest standard. This role provides leadership to Technical Advisors & Supervisors governs the quality of work management data, and ensures maintenance strategies, materials readiness, and schedule commitments are met. The Advisor drives continuous improvement through analysis of performance trends, BI insights, and equipment reliability indicators. Acting as a key support to the Maintenance Superintendent—this position plays a vital part in ensuring operational continuity, technical excellence, and long term equipment health.
Essential Duties
Senior technical and work-management authority
End to end work management & technical governance.
Workflow (identify → plan → schedule → execute → analyse), prioritisation, plan approval, schedule sequencing, data oversight.
Defines strategic maintenance tasks (PMs, inspections).
Reviews and endorses plans.
Verifies priority, materials, labour, tooling, permits, and planning accuracy.
Ensures schedule is technically achievable.
Verifies resource leveling, materials, equipment availability, and timelines.
QA/QC, escalation point for technical issues.
Validates complex work quality and procedural compliance.
Reviews completion quality.
Ensures follow ups and corrective tasks are raised properly.

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.

In this role you will administer our employee technical training programs as we seek to develop our national staff in a range of areas specifically mobile equipment operation. You will ensure that these programs meet K92 Mining standards and external training accreditation where necessary.

Deliver technical and non-technical training as directed, ensuring alignment and compliance with the Technical Training Standard (HR-ST-701).

Ensure accurate training records are maintained.
Actively promote a safe and healthy culture.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure compliance with all legislative, company, and personal HSE systems.
Assist in delivery of site-based training to ensure compliance with HSE and alignment with Mandatory Training (HR-FM-701) and Induction Training (HR-FM-702).

Certificate IV in Workplace Training.
Valid Class 7 PNG license
A minimum of 4 years’ experience in a training delivery role preference in mining and/or construction industry.
Evidence of previous experience on relevant machinery.
Well-developed computer skills with competence in MS Office Suite.
Desirable experience in Pronto, SAP, Safetrac recordkeeping systems.
Well-developed interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills in English

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
The Safety Officer for Projects is responsible for ensuring that all safety regulations and procedures are followed during the execution of the stage 3 expansion for Kainantu Gold Mine. This role is a crucial role in preventing accidents and incidents, protecting the health and safety of employees, contractors and maintaining compliance with Papua New Guinea’s safety laws and regulations.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Ensuring the continuous improvement of, safety inspections, safety training and compliance.
Maintain a safe work environment for all K92 employees, visitors and contractors through audits, inspections, and training.
Maintain the efficiency and cost-effective management of safety in the workplace and project site.
Ensure all incidents are fully investigated and recorded within the site safety data base in a timely and accurate manner.
Conduct safety training programs and initiative.
Conduct scheduled, weekly, monthly safety audits and checks project wide
Collate and submit weekly and monthly reports to Project Director and Operational GM.
Attend site wide weekly and monthly safety meetings.
Ensuring that the camp and project sites safety regulations are observed by all K92 employees including contractors,
Provide safety induction to new intakes, casuals, contractors, and visitors to site.
To ensure the safety rules and other policies of the camp and mine site are observed and report any suspicious activities.
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates must have 10 years minimum Safety work experience in an extractive industry or heavy construction environment. In addition to this, candidates should also (ideally) be able to demonstrate some or all the following.
Appropriate Safety Officer qualifications (Cert IV OHS minimum).
Significant experience with auditing, incident reporting.
Incident investigation training (preferably ICAM)
Well versed with safety systems that deals with compliance records and reports.
Excellent oral and written communications skills.
Very good end user of MS Office Suite: Word, Excel and Outlook.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is responsible for the service and maintenance of heavy underground equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. This includes Trucks, Drills, Front-end loaders, Dozers, Mobile cranes (45T & 100T), and other pieces of equipment.
Key Accountabilities
Undertaking scheduled servicing and preventative maintenance of the company's heavy vehicle fleet, including Sandvik, CAT and Normet vehicles and equipment.
Respond to machinery breakdowns promptly and undertake quality repairs in a timely manner.
Servicing and preventative maintenance on Jumbos, Loaders and Trucks.
Diagnosis and troubleshooting of faults, and recommending servicing interventions that improve the operational efficiency of the company's heavy vehicle fleet
Rectifying machinery breakdowns in an underground environment promptly and undertake quality repairs in a timely manner.

Completing all JSA's, risk assessments and documentation to ensure all work is completed safely and as per schedule.
Give direction, coaching and technical assistance to Trade Assistant’s and apprentice.

Qualifications & Experience

Experience with Mining Equipment like Drills, LHD Loaders, Caterpillar Equipment, Sandvik Equipment etc.
Experience fitter with hydraulics training background.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Life at K92

jobs.employer_address: Cameron Road, Waigani, NCD, 121
jobs.description:
STOREMAN
(Not “I stacked a few shelves” experienced)
PNG Motors is looking for a reliable and hardworking Storeman to support the daily operations of our parts and warehouse team.
This role is not just about moving stock around and hoping for the best. We are looking for someone who understands organisation, urgency, accuracy, and the importance of keeping parts flowing properly through a busy operation. If you struggle with attention to detail, paperwork, systems, or following process, this role will become difficult very quickly.
The Opportunity
PNG Motors supports some of the world’s leading automotive brands including Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC, and Joylong, and our parts operations play a critical role in keeping workshops and customers moving across Papua New Guinea.
In this role, you’ll be responsible for receiving, checking, storing, picking, and dispatching automotive parts and inventory. You’ll assist with stock control, warehouse organisation, order preparation, inventory movement, and ensuring parts are accurately recorded and stored correctly.
You’ll work closely with the warehouse, purchasing, logistics, and parts teams to ensure customer and workshop orders are processed efficiently and accurately. This is a busy operational role where mistakes can create delays across the business, so organisation and attention to detail are essential.
You’ll also assist with stock takes, inventory checks, maintaining clean storage areas, and ensuring warehouse safety procedures are followed at all times.
Who Succeeds Here
This role suits someone who is reliable, organised, physically capable, and able to work efficiently without constant supervision. You’ll succeed here if you are someone who pays attention to detail, follows systems properly, and understands the importance of accuracy in warehouse and inventory operations.
You should be comfortable handling automotive parts, processing paperwork, updating stock records, and working as part of a team in a fast-paced warehouse environment. Good communication skills, time management, and a strong work ethic are essential.
Basic computer knowledge and experience working with inventory systems or warehouse operations will be highly regarded.
Who Will Struggle Here
People who take shortcuts.
People who “guess” part numbers instead of checking properly.
People who struggle with organisation, stock control, or following systems.
This role suits people who understand that small warehouse mistakes can quickly become expensive operational problems.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive organisations, representing globally recognised vehicle brands and operating nationwide parts and service support operations.
You’ll be joining a professional team that values reliability, teamwork, accountability, and operational discipline. Our warehouse and parts operations are critical to the business, and we take pride in maintaining standards our customers and workshops depend on every day.
Qualifications & Experience
Applicants should have a minimum Grade 12 education. Previous experience in warehouse, inventory, logistics, or automotive parts environments will be highly regarded.
Experience using Microsoft Office, inventory systems, or ERP systems will also be viewed favourably.
How to Apply
If you’re reliable, organised, and capable of working in a fast-paced warehouse environment where accuracy matters, we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and a short cover letter outlining your experience to: Gilbert Villarin
[email protected]
Applications close: 4 June 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

PNG Motors is looking for a highly organised and detail-focused Purchasing Clerk to join our National Parts Support Office.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Supervisor, Mechanical, you will play a critical role in managing mechanical operations to ensure safety, efficiency, and compliance across our operations. You will lead and support a team to deliver high-quality maintenance outcomes, optimise performance, and drive continuous improvement in line with Newmont’s operational and safety standards.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support mechanical operations, ensuring equipment performance and operational efficiency.
Champion safety by implementing and maintaining compliance with safety protocols and procedures.
Execute and oversee routine maintenance, inspections, and troubleshooting activities.
Analyse and report on operational data to support informed decision-making.
Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, contractors, and stakeholders to achieve business outcomes.
Allocate work, monitor team performance, and foster a positive and productive team culture.
Identify risks, implement mitigation strategies, and promote continuous improvement initiatives.
Support onboarding and development of team members through coaching and guidance.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
A Mechanical Trade Qualification is essential, with a tertiary qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Maritime Studies, or a related discipline highly regarded.
Practical trade-based experience, with welding and boilermaking experience highly desirable.
Demonstrated experience in mechanical or structural operations within mining, heavy industry, or a similar environment, with strong exposure to heavy diesel and heavy machinery (e.g. Cummins, Caterpillar, Wärtsilä equipment).
Proven expertise in maintenance execution, equipment reliability, and process optimisation, supported by a strong understanding of safety protocols, risk management, and compliance requirements.

jobs.employer_address: Cameron Road, Waigani, NCD, 121
jobs.description:
EXPERIENCED PANEL BEATER
(Not “I helped my cousin once” experienced)
Location: Port Moresby
PNG Motors is looking for a highly experienced Panel Beater to join our growing workshop team supporting some of the world’s leading automotive brands including Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC, and Joylong.
This role is for someone who genuinely knows the trade properly. We are specifically looking for applicants with more than 4 years of real hands-on panel beating experience. Not workshop exposure. Not “assistant” experience. Actual experience repairing damaged vehicles, restoring panels properly, and understanding the difference between a quick patch-up job and professional repair work. If you do not have solid panel beating experience, please do not apply.
The Role
You’ll be responsible for repairing damaged vehicle panels, restoring body alignment, straightening chassis and frames where required, replacing damaged components, and preparing vehicles for paint to a high professional standard. You’ll work across everything from smaller accident repairs through to major collision work on passenger, commercial, and fleet vehicles.
This is a busy workshop environment where quality, efficiency, and workmanship matter equally. Attention to detail is critical because customers notice poor panel gaps, uneven body lines, bad preparation work, and shortcuts immediately. We are looking for someone who takes genuine pride in producing clean, straight, professional repair work and understands the importance of maintaining workshop standards at all times.
What We’re Looking For
We want someone with more than 4 years of proven panel beating experience who can work independently, maintain quality under pressure, and consistently deliver high-standard repairs. You should understand chassis alignment, structural repair work, repair timelines, and workshop efficiency without sacrificing workmanship.
You should also take pride in clean workmanship, understand workshop discipline, and work safely and professionally at all times. Experience using modern repair equipment, measuring systems, welders, and working on commercial vehicles will be highly regarded.
Who Will Struggle Here
People who cut corners will struggle here. People who think filler fixes everything will struggle here. People who need constant supervision or rush jobs out the door without caring about quality will struggle here.
This role suits experienced tradesmen who understand the difference between simply getting a vehicle out of the workshop and repairing it properly.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive organisations, representing globally recognised vehicle brands and operating professional workshop facilities across the country.
You’ll be joining a workshop team that values skill, reliability, professionalism, and workmanship. We take pride in doing repairs properly and maintaining standards our customers trust. This is an opportunity to work in a professional environment where your experience and ability will be respected.
How to Apply
If you’re an experienced Panel Beater who takes pride in quality repairs and professional workmanship, we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and a short cover letter outlining your experience to: Dylan Siketa
[email protected]
Applications close: 25 May 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

All aspects of the trade including, but not limited to understanding of building and industrial electrical maintenance with a proven ability with electrical wiring/termination of new and existing facilities, maintenance, repairs of motors/pumps/water heaters, power generators, electrical panel boards, fault finding, installations and commissioning.

1.    Attend daily maintenance request and are not limited to

New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company committed to safe, responsible, and sustainable mining practices in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, NPL focuses on delivering high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the safety and wellbeing of our people, protection of the environment, and meaningful engagement with local communities. Our operations are guided by strong values, innovation, and a commitment to long-term sustainable development. At NPL, we strive to build a positive legacy by fostering strong stakeholder relationships and creating opportunities that support the prosperity of the regions in which we operate.
The Opportunity
NPL is seeking Expressions of Interest across opportunities in our Inventory team as part of the broader Supply & Business Services Department. These roles play a critical part in ensuring the effective planning, management, and optimization of inventory to support continuous mining operations while minimizing cost, risk, and waste.
We are seeking expressions of interest in the following roles:
Superintendent – Inventory
Specialist – Planning, Inventory
Specialist – Technical, Inventory
Supervisor, Senior – Inventory
Applicants may nominate one or more roles they wish to be considered for.
About the Team
The Inventory team is responsible for developing and implementing appropriate strategies, systems, and policies to optimize stock levels across multiple sites and warehouses across PNG, liaising closely with our Logistics providers to ensure timely supply.
Key responsibilities include:
Developing and executing inventory planning strategies to minimize stock-outs, excess, and obsolete inventory
Providing technical support and guidance to Maintenance and Operations teams, including part identification, availability, and procurement lead times to reduce equipment downtime
Maintaining accurate and compliant inventory records, including item descriptions, stock levels, locations, and movement history using ERP and inventory management systems
Collaborating with internal stakeholders such as Procurement, Logistics, Operations, and Finance to forecast demand, plan replenishment, and optimize       inventory turnover
Managing suppliers and systems while supporting stakeholders to comply with NPL purchasing policies and procedures
About You
To be successful in these roles, you will ideally have:
A bachelor’s degree in business administration, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or a related discipline ideally within mining/oil & gas, heavy industry.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in inventory, supply chain, or sourcing roles.
Team leadership experience is required for the Superintendent role.
Strong working knowledge of SAP, Ariba, ERP systems, and inventory management software.
Proven ability to analyze data, generate reports, and make data-driven decisions utilizing Excel and PowerBI.
Strong leadership capability with a ‘One Team’ mindset.
High energy, with a detailed, hands-on management style and desire to continuously improve you and your team’s knowledge and systems and methods of work.
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with NPL policy and procedures.

Highly competitive remuneration package with both Family medical insurance and life cover
Professional development opportunities

A safe, inclusive, and values-driven work environment

TITLE
Program Coordinator
REPORTING TO
Senior Programs Manager
LOCATION
Wewak, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea
EMPLOYMENT BASIS
Three-years contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Overview
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
Since 2018, WaterAid has been working with district and provincial government stakeholders including the East Sepik Provincial Health Authority (ESPHA) and Wewak District Development Authority (DDA) to implement a district-wide program that aims to support government-led WASH service delivery in Wewak District. The
Inclusive WASH for Wewak District
program, funded under the Australian Government’s (DFAT)
Water for Women Program
, will run for five years. The WaterAid office in Wewak town will take the lead on partner engagement and co-delivery of WASH projects. The Port Moresby office will provide strategic and technical support and lead on engagement with national government.
WaterAid works through supporting local organizations and government and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Our Mission and Vision
WaterAid’s mission is to transform the lives of the poorest and most marginalized people by improving access to WASH. Our vision is that all Papua New Guineans should have access to WASH by 2030.
Our Values
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Respect
Accountability
Courage
Collaboration
Innovation
Integrity
WASH in PNG
In 2015 the government launched the country’s first National WASH Policy, which has led to the setting of clear WASH targets and priority areas for action. PNG has also signed off on a new WASH in Schools policy (as of April 2018), which will help to draw attention to the urgent need for improved WASH facilities in schools.
The implementation of the National WASH Policy is being led by the development of five-year District WASH Plans to drive service delivery in the districts. Several donors are currently working with the WASH PMU to resource the development of District WASH Plans and facilitate learning on the process. District WASH Plans should be supported with annual budgets, to be funded through District Service Improvement Program (DSIP) funding and other government grants.
The drive for district level service delivery within the framework of the national WASH policies creates new opportunities to increase access to WASH services. PNG is now one of only three countries globally that has safe water coverage of less than 50% and has the twelfth highest proportion of people using unimproved sanitation. The positive changes in the enabling environment therefore need to lead to better planning for WASH services and an increase in public expenditure on WASH services.
JOB DIMENSION
Purpose of the Role
Reporting to the Head of Wewak Programs and Operations, the Programs Coordinator Wewak will support and coordinate the implementation of existing grants in Wewak district and in East Sepik Province. The role will initially primarily concern the delivery of the
Water for Women
program and the new “Climate Resilient WaSH” program along with any new programs added under the role as secured.
As the Wewak program expands, the Programs Coordinator Wewak may be responsible for supervising a number of program staff as required. A key aspect of this role will be working with WaterAid partners, including local government offices and representative bodies for women and people with disabilities, to coordinate and implement program activities.
Location
This position will be based in Wewak town, East Sepik Province.
Line Manager
Head of Wewak Programs and Operations
Budget
The role will support budget management.
Team Membership
WaterAid Wewak Programs team.
Documentation and Reporting
Inputs to quarterly reports and general weekly progress reports. Will also assist with documentation concerning monitoring, evaluation, knowledge and learning.
Key Performance Areas
Program Management
Coordinate effective implementation of the Water for Women Program including timely and quality delivery of program activities and financial budgeting, acquittals and reporting on a timely  manner
Build and strenghten WaterAid relationship with district and provincial WaSH stakeholders and implementers including governent and civil society organizations
Manage and oversee program staff to implement field activities for the Water for the Advancing Quality Universal Access (AQUA) to WASH Project are documented and reported
Lead programmes team regualrly use of WaterAid Programme System (WAPS) and projects programmatic and operational data are updated weekly and monthy basis
Work with GEDSI Officer to ensure the integration of GEDSI into program activities and provide support to women and pwd leadership in WaSH and capacity building of rights based organizations.
Develop and coordinate the implementation of periodic workplans with the programs team
Contribute to the development of WaterAid PNG country program and strategy.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge and Learning
Monitor and evaluate program activities and contribute to a team culture that is conducive to learning, sharing and innovation.
Assist the Monitoring & Evaluation Officer and Learning & Effectiveness Advisors in the development of data collection forms and tools suitable to program activities and measuring outcomes and impact
Lead the Monitoring and Evaluation framework, indicator, and results on WAPS for the programs team
Working with WaterAid’s Communications Coordinator, partners and the programs team to identify and compile case studies on program highlights that demonstrate
Documentation of learning and working with the team to measure the impact of programs and the efficacy of program implementation.
Assist partner organisations and the –Head of Wewak Programs & Operations with monthly, quarterly and annually reporting and learning cycles.
Actively engage in learning process within the WaterAid PNG country program working on sector strengthening and contribute to global publications and global learning events.
Equity and Inclusion
Work with the WA GEDSI Officer to support the Wewak district WaSH Coordination Committee and partners to engage effectively with women, people with disabilities and marginalised members of the community in the WaSH sector, through the East Sepik Council of Women (ESCoW) and the East Sepik Disabled Persons Association (ESDPA)
Work with the WA GEDSI Officer to identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.
Promote a ‘Do No Harm’ approach amongst WaterAid staff and local partners and ensure that referral pathways are accessible for stakeholders and beneficiaries affected by WaterAid’s work.
Staff Management
Support the development of WaterAid Wewak program and field staff and build their capacity.
Identify program and field staff priorities and assist them to prepare weekly and monthly workplans in line with the overall program workplan.
Promote a culture of respect, collaboration. Learning and sharing building on WaterAid’s values.
Partner Engagement
Maintain constructive working relationships with WaterAid’s local partners.
Facilitate regular meetings with partners to discuss project design and delivery, reflect on progress, identify risks and challenges and jointly propose solutions.
Mentor and support WaterAid program and field staff to build and maintain constructive partnerships and working relationships.
Coordinate field visits with partners with sensitivity to security and accessibility issues.
Represent WaterAid through local sector coordination bodies.
The role requires engagement with a moderate degree of complexity, due to the need to:
Coordinate with multiple stakeholders, including formal program partners, as well as community leaders, traditional landowners and government agencies.
Ensure that risks concerning financial mismanagement and fraud are adequately managed.

Level of contact with children
The role may involve baseline and supervision work in schools in East Sepik Province, as well as general work on WASH in Communities, Schools and Healthcare Facilities (HCFs). The position will be required to always maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards.

Essential
Experience

Experience in networking and liaising key stakeholders within government and civil society.

Executive Opportunity – Chief Executive Officer
We are partnering with Teachers Savings and Loan Society Limited (TISA Bank) to identify an accomplished Chief Executive Officer to lead the Bank through its next phase of growth and transformation.
About TISA Bank:
TISA Bank is Papua New Guinea’s first homegrown commercial bank, built on a 50+ year legacy of the Teachers Savings and Loan Society. The Bank was granted their commercial banking licence in August 2024 and provides innovative and secure banking solutions across Personal, SME, Corporate, Agency and Digital Banking, supporting individuals, families, start-ups, small businesses, and large corporates. As a locally-owned institution, TISA Bank is committed to delivering better banking options for Papua New Guineans and shaping the development of the local financial sector.
The Role:
Reporting to the TISA Bank Board of Directors and the Group CEO, the incumbent will lead TISA Bank through its next phase of growth, setting and executing the Bank’s strategic direction while ensuring financial strength, regulatory compliance, and sustainable long-term performance. This high-profile role carries full accountability for the Bank’s overall performance, risk management, governance, and stakeholder engagement. You will lead a high-performing executive team, foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and innovation, and act as the Bank’s principal representative with regulators, government, shareholders, and other key stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities:
Steer the Bank’s Strategic Direction
– Develop long-term strategies with the Group CEO and Board, and oversee operational, financial, and risk management functions.
Drive Operational Excellence
– Implement the Bank’s annual operational plan and budget, optimise cost-to-income ratios, and improve financial performance metrics
Cultivate a High-Performing Culture
– Foster an innovative, customer-focused environment that empowers employees and drives exceptional service
About You:
The successful candidate will be a proven executive leader with:
CEO or senior executive experience within a regulated financial institution
Deep experience across Retail, SME, and Corporate banking, including digital and agency channels
Strong track record of delivering financial and operational performance, including profitability, efficiency, and balance sheet growth
Demonstrated capability in risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance
Experience in emerging or frontier markets; Papua New Guinea or similar environments highly regarded
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, including with regulators and government
Ability to lead organisational transformation and inspire high-performing teams

Strong communication, negotiation, people management, interpersonal and influencing skills to build strong business relationships and drive a culture of collaboration and innovation
Ability to satisfy the Fit and Proper requirements as set out under the Bank and Financial Institutions Act
This is a unique leadership opportunity to shape the future of a growing, locally-owned bank, expand access to banking solutions across PNG, and make a lasting impact on the wider financial sector.

Superintendent, Electrical and Instrumentation
Join the world’s leading gold mining company
Be part of Newmont’s Papua New Guinea mine operation
FIFO ex Australia (21 days on, 21 days off) or residential on Lihir Island, PNG
About Newmont
Founded in 1921 Newmont Mining Corporation is one of the largest gold mining companies in the world. Newmont prides itself on safety and embraces diversity, engages employees, fosters innovation, rewards high performance and develops great leaders.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
Reporting to the Manager, Asset Management, Fixed Plant, the
Superintendent, Electrical & Instrumentation
plays a critical leadership role at Newmont’s Lihir Island operations. You will oversee electrical and instrumentation activities to ensure reliable and efficient operations.
As part of our leadership team, you will:
Coordinate the installation, maintenance, and repair of all electrical and instrumentation systems to ensure optimal performance and reliability
Execute regular inspections and audits of electrical and instrumentation systems to identify potential issues and ensure compliance with industry standards
Formulate and execute preventive and predictive maintenance schedules for all electrical and instrumentation equipment to minimize downtime and extend equipment lifespan
Apply diagnostic tools and data analytics to assess the health and performance of electrical and instrumentation systems, enabling timely maintenance interventions
Adhere to all electrical and instrumentation activities complying with relevant health, safety, and environmental regulations and company policies
Facilitate a culture of safety within the electrical and instrumentation team by executing safety training sessions and maintaining strict adherence to safety protocols
Formulate and handle the electrical and instrumentation budget, ensuring efficient allocation of resources and adherence to financial targets
Assess and execute cost-saving measures within the electrical and instrumentation department without compromising on quality or safety
Responsible for assessing relevant risks, executing mitigation measures, and continuously monitoring for risks
Statutory compliance to PNG Mining Resources Authority.
What You Will Bring
Degree qualification in Electrical Engineering or a formal qualification in related field
Several years of experience in electrical and instrumentation maintenance operations and systems management with demonstrated progression through roles of increasing responsibility
Competent experience in leading and developing teams
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders
Advanced understanding of electrical and instrumentation maintenance operations management, safety compliance, process optimization and stakeholder collaboration
Advanced knowledge in electrical and instrumentation safety regulations, maintenance scheduling, performance monitoring, budgeting and compliance with safety and environmental policies & high voltage knowledge
Advanced understanding and application of electrical and instrumentation systems, tools and software programs
Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices
Competent understand of project cost management and financial principles.
Working Conditions
This is a site-based role at Newmont’s Lihir Island operations in Papua New Guinea, offered on either a
21 days on / 21 days off FIFO
roster ex Australia (Cairns, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Adelaide) or
residential on Lihir Island
basis.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
Join us and unearth your potential in a global company that is at the forefront of shaping the future of the mining industry.

Audit Planning & Execution

In Papua New Guinea (PNG), Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods.  Many of these programs focus specifically on child protection, gender-based violence and gender equality. The PNG Country Program is looking for a Gender and Child Protection Manager who will provide operational and technical leadership for all protection and gender-transformative programming in PNG.
Here your skills will be valued - Role Purpose
The Gender and Protection Program Manager (GPPM) reports to the Program Operations Director and will provide leadership and oversight of all Save the Children protection and gender equality / gender-based violence (GBV) programming across PNG. The GPPM ensures the quality and timely delivery (within budget) of all projects in the protection and GBV programming sector and will contribute to designing new projects and proposals as relevant. The GPPM contributes to the development of gender equality, GBV, and protection-related technical documents, briefs, and strategies – and is responsible for ensuring that all protection program objectives are met and are in line with evidence-base programming approaches.

Protection Programming Management

Ensure all protection and gender/GBV programming meaningfully integrates principles of gender equality, disability and inclusion at all levels; and recognizes the common linkages between different groups experiencing violence.

Ensure that all relevant project method management (PMM) and mandatory tools are prepared, disseminated, and regularly updated as needed in line with project and/or external changes.

Budget and Financial Management

Review and approve all financial transactions within delegated limits, ensuring the application of all financial and procurement policies and compliance standards.
Ensure all gender/GBV/protection project budgets are properly forecasted and reviewed monthly; review transaction listings, monitor and address variances within SCA and donor requirements.
Support the preparation of budgets for new gender/protection projects and proposals.

Comply with the Child Safeguarding Code of Conduct and child safeguarding and protection. policies and standards, as well as all other related policies, including reporting requirements.

The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.

Community Conservation Coordinator
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program-PNG
JOB DESCRIPTION
Position Title:
Community Conservation Coordinator (PNG National)
Position type:
Full Time
Reports to:
Protected Area Manager, TKCP-PNG
Location:
Based in Lae, Morobe Province with frequent travel to the YUS Conservation Area Remuneration
:
A competitive salary package including family medical coverage, Nasfund contributions, worker’s compensation, and professional development opportunities.
Background:
The Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program has worked with communities and landowners in the Yopno Uruwa-Som (YUS) landscape since 1996. Together with YUS landowners and the PNG Government, TKCP helped establish the country's first nationally-protected Conservation Area in 2009. The YUS Conservation Area is wholly owned by local people and supported by the PNG Government for long-term protection.  The YUS landscape has extremely high biodiversity value but faces pressure from subsistence-level habitat conversion and unsustainable resource use. Today, TKCP and the YUS Conservation Area serve as a national model for community-based conservation in PNG.
Purpose:
The Community Conservation Coordinator provides outreach, guidance, and support to YUS communities in sustainable land-use management. He/she will advise and facilitate community representatives in monitoring, reviewing, and periodically updating ward-level Land-use Plans, which identify each ward’s conservation and development priorities and define boundaries for land-use zones including protected areas, buffer zones, reforestation areas, and livelihoods/garden areas. Together with the Protected Area Manager and TKCP's Conservation Officers, the Coordinator will promote adherence to Land-use Plans, solicit community input on resource needs, and strengthen conservation engagement throughout YUS.
Summary of key responsibilities
Facilitate community implementation and monitoring of 18 ward-level Land-use Plans, including periodic review and updating
Manage activities of Land-use Plan Monitoring Officers to ensure data quality and coverage; lead annual refresher trainings
Clean, manage, and maintain Land Use Plan Monitoring database
Establish secondary land-use monitoring systems (e.g. remote sensing, GIS, other methods) to ensure local adherence to Land-use Plans and to inform YUS Landscape & Conservation Area management 5. Work with Conservation Officers to guide, and monitor community outreach and awareness efforts, tailored to specific gender/age groups as necessary (e.g., develop structured awareness programs to ensure target audiences in YUS communities have an up-to-date understanding of TKCP’s work). 6. Facilitate community trainings and stakeholder workshops to support Land-use Planning & Management processes and guidance to ensure community input and participation.
Contribute to marine resource values mapping process to inform future monitoring efforts 8. Oversee landowner pledging of new and mapping of existing land parcels in the YUS Conservation Area 9. Conduct frequent field visits to ensure that activities align with work plans and technical requirements, while also strengthening networks to capture community acceptance and engagement.
With support from Protected Area Manager, represent TKCP and YUS Conservation Area in community conservation and sustainable land-use initiatives.
Review existing programming and make recommendations for areas of expansion. 12. Serve as focal point for technical proposal writing for conservation and sustainable resource use projects. 13. Submit monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc reports based on field data collection, analysis, and documentation.
Selection criteria
Bachelor’s degree in natural resource management, conservation, environmental studies, or related fields • 3+ years of experience with protected areas conservation and/or community-based conservation. • Experience working with NGO or government agency in positions of increasing responsibility. • Confidence and ability to liaise with governments representatives and community leaders/landowners • Experience in project management including planning, budgeting, and reporting.  • Experience maintaining
Competency with geospatial data management and analysis (e.g. ArcGIS, QGIS, remote-sensing data products) and/or digital data collection platforms (e.g., SMART - Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool, KoboToolbox, EarthRanger) is an asset.
Demonstrated problem-solving skills.
Experience working with local communities and traveling to remote areas in PNG. • Physical capabilities for remote field work and hiking in mountainous terrain
Well-developed interpersonal and communication skills.
Detail-oriented, organized, and able to meet deadlines.
Proficient spoken and written English and Tok Pisin language skills required.

ABOUT KTF
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education

healthcare

equality

leaders
