ABOUT
The Balimo College educational campus was established by SDP in 2019 to build the education and health standards and pathways for the Western Province. Through the college, SDP now proudly delivers tertiary qualifications in Junior Primary Teaching and in Nursing under the Balimo College program; secondary school certification and GPA upgrades through Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE); and e-Learning programs in schools around the area. SDP now embarks on an exciting new chapter expanding the campus and operating the Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy (RBBA).
HON. ROY BIYAMA BALIMO ACADEMY (RBBA)
The school commenced in 2024 and is growing rapidly, aiming to cater for 1000 students in Grades K–12 by 2028. The Academy operates in an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning that is inclusive and responsive to additional needs and removing educational barriers for local students to learn and grow in a safe and supportive environment.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are recruiting passionate experienced educators to join our growing team in 2026. We are seeking educators who will foster a positive school culture and the ability to drive academic excellence among their students.  Successful candidates will be part of a team of approximately 15 secondary teachers (Grades 9–12) and deliver across a combination of core and elective subjects.
Subject specialisms we are particularly seeking include:
English & Language & Literature
Social Science (History, Geography, Social Science)
Business & Economics (Business Studies, Economics)
ICT (Grades 9–12, stand-alone subject)
Teachers should be able to deliver at least one major subject and one minor (related) subject in line with the RBBA’s staffing model. Other major/minor combinations of the above subjects may be considered. Well qualified applicants with diverse skill sets will be highly received.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Teaching
: Develop and deliver lesson plans aligned with the SBC curriculum and PNG educational standards; conduct assessments and provide feedback; utilise varied teaching methods.
Student support and classroom management
: Foster a positive and inclusive classroom environment; implement effective classroom management strategies; support students as they prepare for examinations.
Student Assessment:
Conduct marking and assessment; provide constructive feedback; create individualised learning plans where needed.
Collaboration
: Work collaboratively with colleagues within RBBA, SDP and KTF; participate in meetings and professional development activities.
Parent and Guardian Communication
: Maintain open communication with parents and guardians regarding student progress; attend parent-teacher conferences and school events.
Operations
: Maintain accurate student records, attendance, and assessment data; report to the Principal, Deputy Principal and Head of Teaching and Learning.
Professional Development
: Stay abreast of current educational trends and participate in ongoing training.
Other
: Any other duties as directed by RBBA management; adherence to all KTF policies and safeguarding standards.
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor of Education – or equivalent - ESSENTIAL
Minimum 2 years teaching experience - ESSENTIAL
Full (secondary) teaching registration – ESSENTIAL
Please note that if these requirements are not met, your application will not be considered.
SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES
Knowledge of PNG educational regulations and compliance standards.
High-level communication, mentoring and interpersonal skills.
Ability to research and apply a range of teaching strategies for diverse learners.
Competence with information and communication technologies for teaching and administration.
Openness to learning new and innovative approaches to teaching and learning.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG
Willingness to relocate to Balimo during the academic year
Compliance with KTF safeguarding standards (police check, child protection, etc.)

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Processing Services Operators are multi skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the
•             mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.
•             concrete batching plant and agitator trucks
•             pastefill binder preparation plant
The Processing Services division operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system; concrete batching plant and surface agitator trucks and pastefill binder preparation plant
Effectively operate and maintain mobile equipment including Light Vehicle, Front End Loader, Excavator, telehandler and forklift according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems
Operate fixed plant equipment including jaw and cone crushers, screening plant, concrete batching plant, binder preparation plant, and cement offloading facility according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.
Ensure quality of material being crushed, batched and prepared meets the correct quality standards by taking regular samples
Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.
Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.
Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply within varying site operation.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a Grade 10 Certificate or technical trade Loader and excavator licences and relevant experience as well as Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) or more years relevant work experience
Experience with operation and maintenance of mobile crushing equipment including but not limited to jaw crushers, cone crushers, screens, conveyors and stackers
Experience with concrete batching plant operations.
High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Ability to work shift work
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician, Processing, you’ll play a key role in operating critical sections of the process plant, including grinding circuits, flotation, and thickener operations. Your work ensures safety, efficiency, and production targets are met shift by shift, contributing directly to Newmont’s operational success.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Prioritize Safety: Ensure compliance with all HSE policies, report hazards, and actively monitor plant conditions.
Collaborate Effectively: Work constructively with diverse teams and participate in shift handovers, toolbox meetings, and training.
Drive Production: Operate plant equipment, complete inspections, and maintain housekeeping standards.
Control Costs: Identify and report cost-saving opportunities and minimize waste.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Proven experience in heavy industry, preferably mining (essential).
Grade 10 education minimum.
Tertiary qualifications and metalliferous processing certificates are highly regarded.
Class 6 PNG Driver’s License.
Strong communication, attention to detail, time management, and technical knowledge in mineral processing.
Safety-conscious, proactive problem solver, team player, and adaptable to changing work conditions.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 rotating roster.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in mining committed to safety, sustainability, and innovation.
Grow your career through training and development opportunities.
Work in a supportive environment that values your contribution and well-being.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 10 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Quality Assurance Auditor Pool – Strongim Wok Long TVET
Short-term as required
Travel within Papua New Guinea
Open to international and PNG national candidates
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.
The program aligns with the broader goals of the
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasises locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.
This Opportunity
A pool of qualified
Quality Assurance Auditors
is being sought to work in collaboration with the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) Quality Assurance Division (QAD), as well as other appointed auditors, to conduct quality assurance audits of PNG’s public Technical Colleges (TCs).
These audits will assess institutional and program compliance with the PNG National Standards for Higher Education Institutional Registration and the PNG National Standards for Program Accreditation. The audit process is relatively new in this context and, accordingly, additional time and flexibility will be built into auditor engagements to enable appropriate support to TC’s throughout the audit process.
Auditors will be engaged on an as-needed basis in accordance with the PNG National Standards and Palladium policies. It is anticipated that between five and ten auditors will be identified through this recruitment process to support audits at up to ten (10) TC’s across PNG.
Each audit will have a defined number of input days, which will vary depending on the audit readiness of the individual Technical College, typically ranging from eight (8) to twelve (12) days per audit. By way of example, an audit may include three (3) days of remote preparation and report writing, one (1) day of in-country coordination, and five (5) days of on-site audit activities.
Primary responsibilities and activities may include:
Conducting a thorough review of all documentation relating to the quality assurance process
Participating, as a panel member or Panel Chair, in the DHERST Quality Assurance review process, including in all aspects of the site visits, interview sessions and panel-only discussion and decision making to ensure compliance of TVET institutions with national accreditation and quality standards.
Identifying gaps and providing recommendations and actions to strengthen quality assurance systems and mechanisms
Accepting responsibility for one or more Standards during the audit process and write/contribute to the audit report against those Standards.
Participation in the development of questions to be asked by the panel at the site visit
Developing conclusions or findings based on the evidence that is presented
Contributing effectively to the development of the audit report
Developing an understanding of the nature and vision of the institute or programme being reviewed
Working effectively with DHERST staff and fellow panel members, and treating all colleagues, fellow panel members, DHERST staff and institutional staff or stakeholders with respect and courtesy
Supporting TC’s, DHERST and fellow auditors to work through institutional audit process including supporting with the understanding audit standards, collection of evidence and explanation of audit recommendations
Providing feedback to DHERST on the entire quality assurance review process
Understanding and contributing to SWLT and DHERST gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required
Adhering to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately
Contributing to office learning culture by seeking out knowledge, sharing fresh perspectives and ideas, and taking initiative in problem-solving
Understand and work in line with SWLT principles at all times.
Palladium, through the Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT) program, will provide support to auditors, including costs associated with travel, accommodation, security and per diems.
About you
You will have experience:
Conducting and participating in quality assurance review (audit) processes against a set of standards in vocational education and training, or in other industry settings. Experience in Papua New Guinea or the Pacific is advantageous.
Extensive knowledge of TVET training institutional environments as a trainer or manager meeting national quality assurance framework standards
Strong commitment to quality assurance outcomes and effective peer review participation
Positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion, through good communication and effective relationship management skills
Strong analytical and report-writing skills
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position to
[email protected]
.
Closing date:
Friday 15 May 2026
Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.
Should you require any adjustments to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at
[email protected]
and we will be in touch to discuss.
Safeguarding -
We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
To support the Mine Geothermal Team and other professionals to provide geothermal risk management and geothermal technical support to the Mine Technical and Operations teams.
Essential Duties
Drives and influence proactive safety behaviours within workgroups through visible leadership.
Ensures all personnel, visitors and contractors comply with site and contractual HSE requirements and hold people accountable for adherence.
Plans work so that it can be conducted safely; and considers environmental conditions, nearby activities, and the people and other resources needed to complete the work
Creates opportunities for people to work together to enable them to contribute to the business and learn from each other.
Provides training of mine technical and operational personnel in geothermal hazards and controls
Identify and manage geothermal hazards and associated risks successfully in the open pit by capturing and analysing geotechnical drilling, mapping and temperature data and through field regular inspections
Develops and communicates mine geothermal risk reviews for monthly and weekly mine plans
Delivers work within approved budget managing any variances in accordance with escalation process.
Actively seeks cost reduction opportunities.
Training & Experience
Tertiary qualified Bachelor of Science (Geology) or Engineering (Geotechnical, Reservoir) is essential and accreditation from the Institute of Engineers PNG Inc. and will be completed as part of work permit process. PNG Drivers License essential.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Embodies Newmont’s vision and values leading by example.
Develops & implements mid to short-term departmental plans, changes and initiatives to achieve overall business goals by providing positive leadership, direction & guidance within the department and wider organisation.
3+ years relevant work experience in a mining environment in a geotechnical/geothermal position is desirable.
Exposure in geothermal, geotechnical/geothermal monitoring systems is desirable.
Proficient in English with excellent verbal, written communication and public speaking skills.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.

We’re looking for an experienced

You work well with technicians, service advisors, and parts teams. You keep your work tidy, your job cards accurate, and your standards high.

About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Electrical Engineer is responsible for providing minor electrical design and modifications within the process plant and associated mine site infrastructure that shall meet company specifications, comply with operational requirements, agreements and relevant standards.

Efficiently manage minor to medium projects to ensure they are completed as per agreed schedule, on budget and as per quality standards.

Recommend solutions to address issues that arise during construction work.

Bachelor’s Degree qualification in Electrical Engineering
Registered with IEPNG

3-5 years of electrical engineering experience in a mining industry environment.
Demonstrated competence in the application of Australian Standards in electrical design.
Strong technical capability in power systems and industrial instrumentation.
Experience in the use of PowerPac Software.
Strong capability to perform relevant engineering calculations to support designs.
Able to read, understand and prepare engineering drawings.
Capability to review engineering drawings and red-line in consultation with the design team to ensure accurate design and construction drawings.
Strong attention to detail and documentation capability.
Excellent communication skills and ability to work with minimal supervision.
Good computer literacy and understanding of Microsoft software suite.
Understanding of safety compliance and regulations.

Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Project Manager
to be based in
Port Moresby, National Capital District.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The purpose of this role is to oversee grant implementation and operational activities within Morobe, Western Highlands and Central provinces for the UNICEF Smarter and Safer Schools (3 S) project, delivered by World Vision Papua New Guinea
The role is responsible for leading, supporting, and ensuring the accountability and performance of project staff based in the three provinces. It will also ensure that project implementation and expenditure are effectively and accurately monitored, donor requirements and program objectives are met, and any emerging risks or issues are promptly identified and addressed.
Project Planning and Implementation
Lead the development and execution of detailed project plans, workplans, timelines, budgets, and risk management frameworks.
Ensure effective implementation of smarter and safer school interventions, including safe infrastructure, disaster risk reduction (DRR), WASH, child protection measures, digital learning readiness, and school safety policies.
Coordinate field activities to ensure schools meet safety, inclusiveness, and resilience standards.
Reporting and Communication
Prepare high-quality narrative and financial reports for donors and internal management.
Document lessons learned, success stories, and best practices.
Communicate project progress, challenges, and results effectively to diverse audiences.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL)
Oversee monitoring of project indicators, milestones, and outcomes.
Ensure accurate data collection, reporting, and documentation aligned with donor requirements.
Sustainable results and long-term impact are realized for beneficiaries.
Support learning and adaptive management to continuously improve project effectiveness.
Financial and Resource Management
Manage project budgets and expenditures in compliance with organizational and donor policies.
Approve activity expenditures, track spending, and contribute to financial reporting.
Ensure efficient use of resources and value for money
Staff Management
Recruit and retain a skilled, diverse team focused on improving child well-being
Provide strong leadership while ensuring staff accountability and performance
Identify, coordinate, and support training to build staff capacity for high-quality, consistent
Project delivery
Project team performs effectively and meets performance expectations
Maintaining good relationship with external stakeholders
Establish and maintain relationships with government and non-government education partners at a Province level. Support staff to effectively engage with government and non-government stakeholders at District, LLG, and community levels. Directly coordinate with project staff and consortium partners to ensure delivery of needed support within the province.
Strong coordination and collaboration with stakeholders and partners are maintained
Coordinate with departments responsible for finance, procurement and logistics, and human resources to ensure compliance of project and staff with key policies and protocols.
Work alongside the World Vision Area Programme Manager and other World Vision project teams to support mutual accountability, coordinate activities, and speak ‘with one voice’ to communities and stakeholders.
Visit project sites and communities on a regular basis.
WV Christian Work Living
Lead and support Christian activities that enrich and develop mutual growth in Christ
Perform any other tasks assigned by the Program Operations Director.
Convey World Vision identity and core values in life, word, and deed in the workplace and outside of the workplace.
Participate in World Vision PNG core staff activities, such as regular staff Christian reflection activities and regular programmatic Learning & Reflection days.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Project Management, Engineering, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
At least 5 years of professional experience in project management; including experience leading a team or office of similar size and scope of accountability required.
Technical or programming experience in education, gender, WASH, or child protection preferred.
Direct experience in managing staff, donor and stakeholders especially in the education sector
At least 2 years work experience in managing projects in the field offices
Direct experience in working with multicultural teams
Demonstrated ability to lead teams and deliver consistent quality programming and reporting in complex organisational and operational environments required.
Proactive working style and proven ability to identify and mitigate risks, problem solve, and effectively manage conflict required.
Strong planning, organisational, and project management skills required.
Strong interpersonal skills required. Experience managing cross-cultural teams preferred.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and email required
Fluency in English and Tok Pisin required.

based in Port Moresby
and may involve occasional travel to our operational site.
Internal Audit Officer
Job Summary
The Internal Auditor is responsible for
planning, conducting, and reporting audits
across all KutMor systems, policies, and processes to ensure compliance with internal standards, ISO requirements, and regulatory obligations.
This role focuses solely on
independent assurance
, identifying non-conformances, evaluating effectiveness of controls, and driving corrective and preventive actions.
Key Responsibility Areas
Internal Audits and Compliance:
Plan, schedule, and conduct internal audits across all business functions.
Define audit scope, criteria, and methodologies.
Ensure audits align with ISO 9001:2015 and other applicable standards.
Audit Execution:

Risk and Control Evaluation:
Evaluate effectiveness of internal controls and risk management processes.
Identify gaps and recommend improvements.
Stakeholder Engagement:
Liaise with function heads and employees during audits.
Provide guidance on compliance requirements without compromising independence.
Qualifications, Skills, and Experiences
Bachelor’s degree in quality management, engineering, or a related field.
Certified Internal Auditor / Certified Quality Auditor preferred.
Strong experience in auditing systems and processes.
Experience with auditing ISO standards is a bonus.
Strong auditing and investigation skills
Knowledge of ISO standards
Analytical and critical thinking
High integrity and independence

High attention to detail

jobs.employer_address: Suite 7, Ground Floor, CHM Corporate Park One, Gordons.
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION
TITLE
Programs Coordinator - WaSH and Nature based solutions (nbs)
REPORTING TO
Senior Program Manger
LOCATION
Pomio, East New Britain Province
EMPLOYMENT BASIS
Three-years contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Overview
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
WaterAid is open to employing and working with People Living with any forms of impairment and disability and other marginalized population.
JOB DIMENSION
About the Project
The PacFresH2O (Protecting Freshwater Resources for Increased Climate Resilience in the Pacific Islands) project is a multi-year initiative running from February 2024 to January 2031, aimed at enhancing climate resilience in rural communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands (SLB). Funded through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and led by GIZ in partnership with the Pacific Community (SPC) and various national government bodies, the project responds to pressing climate-related challenges like drought, flooding, and cyclones that threaten water resources and infrastructure. It seeks to address the low levels of access to safe drinking water—particularly in rural and marginalised communities through integrated water management and sustainable, community-based interventions.
The project’s core strategy is built around three outputs: strengthening governance, coordination, and data use; implementing phased, climate-resilient water and sanitation solutions; and embedding Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) priorities into national policy frameworks. A key focus is on showcasing underutilised resources such as groundwater, improving meteorological and hydrological capabilities, and training local and national actors, including women and marginalised groups in climate finance and evidence-based water resource management. Through these efforts, PacFresH2O aims to create scalable and replicable models for rural water resilience, boosting the adaptive capacity of Pacific Island nations in the face of climate change
Purpose of the Role
The Program Coordinator – WaSH and NBS will play a crucial role in ensuring the successful implementation of project activities, strengthening coordination, and supporting strategic alignment with consortium partners and stakeholders. Additionally, the Program Coordinator will have supervisory responsibilities, overseeing the work of Program Officer for Pomio District to ensure effective delivery of project components
The Program Coordinator will be responsible for facilitating multi-level coordination, overseeing project implementation, supervising staff, and ensuring compliance with donor and partner requirements. This includes working closely with WaterAid, GIZ, SPC, and government agencies to ensure effective planning, execution, and reporting of activities in Pomio District, while preparing for full-scale implementation upon project commissioning (expected late 2025).
Location
This position will be based in Pomio District, East New Britian Province.
Line Manager
Senior Program manager ENB
Budget
The role will support budget management for local operations.
Team Membership
WaterAid Rabaul, NCD and Central Programs team.
Documentation and Reporting
Inputs to quarterly reports and general weekly progress reports. Will also assist with documentation concerning monitoring, evaluation, knowledge and learning.
Key Performance Areas
Project Coordination & Implementation Oversight
Lead the implementation of preparation phase activities, ensuring alignment with project goals and timelines.
Manage target community selection, coordinating with the Pomio District Development Authority (DDA) and District WASH Committee (DWC) to reaffirm priorities based on Pomio District’s 5-year climate-resilient WASH plan and the National WaSH Policy (2015-2030).
Oversee WASH and Water Resource baseline, ensuring data-driven decision-making and targeted interventions within the target communities.
Lead data collection processes in target communities, including undertaking Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) Survey
Stakeholder Engagement & Multi-Level Coordination
Serve as the primary liaison between WaterAid, GIZ, SPC, and government partners in East New Britain to streamline project implementation.
Strengthen collaboration with the East New Britain Provincial Administration (ENBPA), District Development Authority and East New Britain Provincial Health Authority (ENBPHA) for policy alignment.
Ensure effective communication with Rabaul District Development Authority regarding project adjustments due to implementation focus on Pomio District.
Supervision & Team Leadership
Provide guidance and oversight to the Program Officer for Pomio District, ensuring efficient execution of their responsibilities.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment, supporting professional growth and skill-building for staff.
Conduct regular check-ins, mentoring, and performance evaluations to maintain high-quality project delivery.
Policy Support & Institutional Strengthening
Support policy reviews and advocacy efforts, ensuring integration of climate adaptation and gender-responsive WASH governance into PNG’s national frameworks.
Work with GIZ and SPC to align local WASH interventions with PNG’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP), Medium-Term Development Plan IV (MTDP IV), and climate resilience strategies.
Ensure district and provincial WASH committees receive technical capacity building and structured support for improved governance.
Data Management & Knowledge Generation
Oversee the development of baseline data collection frameworks, ensuring inclusion of key informant interviews, focus group discussions, household surveys, and participatory rural appraisals
Lead Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) surveys to assess community freshwater resource management and climate change adaptation needs.
Work with consortium partners to analyse findings and integrate lessons into project adaptation strategies.
Compliance, Reporting, & Financial Oversight
Ensure compliance with donor requirements, working closely with WaterAid PNG’s finance and grant management team to uphold transparency and contractual obligations.
Lead project documentation and reporting, ensuring timely submission of updates to consortium partners.
Coordinate with WaterAid National Program Manager – WaSH system Strengthening, Australia’s Technical Lead – Planning and Monitoring and Program Coordinator in Melbourne to maintain strategic alignment and donor engagement.
The role requires engagement with a moderate degree of complexity, due to the need to:
Coordinate with multiple stakeholders, including formal program partners, as well as community leaders, traditional landowners and government agencies.
Ensure that risks concerning financial mismanagement and fraud are adequately managed.
Relationships
Internal
WaterAid PNG
WaterAid Australia (participation in learning events etc)
WaterAid global intranet (participation in webinars and other online learning platforms)
External
Pomio District Development Authority
East New Britain Provincial Health Authority
Provincial Community Development & Youth and Religion
Provincial Education Office
National & Provincial Weather Services
Provincial Office of Climate Change
East New Britain Public Works Department
Local partners, as determined by grants and advised by Senior Management Team (SMT)
Local NGOs operating within Pomio and Rabaul Districts
Physical Environment and Demands
High travel requirements within Pomio District. Occasional travel to Port Moresby. Possible travel to other districts in the East New Britain Province, as needed.
Level of contact with children
The role may involve baseline and supervision work in schools in East New Britian Province, as well as general work on WASH in Communities, Schools and Healthcare Facilities (HCFs). The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.

Experience
Proven WASH experience in working with schools, health care facilities and communities in PNG context.
Proven experience in community development, which includes and health care facilities with communities
Experience in networking and liaising key stakeholders within government and civil

WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Coordinator to join our team in East New Britain Province. The role will work collaboratively with the project implementation team to coordinate collection, analysis, reporting and use of project monitoring from two key projects: The PacFresh H20 Program implemented in Rabaul and Pomio districts and the KIWA Initiative implemented in Rabaul district. The role will also involve close collaboration with WaterAid PNG Headquarters located in Port Moresby, and the Regional team based in Australia. They will also contribute to broader organisational learning initiatives, helping to share key lessons from East New Britain across the region.
About the Projects
The Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
The Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key performance areas / Accountabilities
Project Monitoring
Work with Programs Team members to develop, implement and review project-level monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks and theories of change to ensure they are feasible, meaningful, and fit for purpose.
Lead development of data collection tools and coordinate regular collection of quantitative and qualitative project monitoring data aligned with project MEL Frameworks.
Lead and oversee the MEL framework in WaterAid Programme Systems (WAPS) updating the indicator and results for the projects and report to the SMT and WA Regional Team.
Ensure all the indicators and results are updated and reviewed on monthly and quarterly basis and reported aligning to the CCPM.
Build capacity of project staff and partners in MEL and support regular analysis of data to inform project activities and reporting.
Ensure that cross cutting issues, such as gender equality, disability equity, climate change and sector strengthening are adequately and appropriately reflected in project MEL Frameworks and reporting.
Identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.
Leader the use of dashboard in WAPS to monitor the programming work and the support to provide fortnightly and monthly.
Support the filling of the WA Risk template offline and upload to WAPS register and regular monitor and update in WAPS.

WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province
Since 2018, WaterAid has been working with district and provincial government stakeholders including the East Sepik Provincial Health Authority (ESPHA) and Wewak District Development Authority (DDA) to implement a district-wide program that aims to support government-led WASH service delivery in Wewak District. The
Inclusive WASH for Wewak District
program, funded under the Australian Government’s (DFAT)
Water for Women Program
, will run for five years.The WaterAid office in Wewak town will take the lead on partner engagement and co-delivery of WASH projects. The Port Moresby office will provide strategic and technical support and lead on engagement with national government.
WaterAid works through supporting local organizations and government and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Our Mission and Vision
WaterAid’s mission is to transform the lives of the poorest and most marginalized people by improving access to WASH. Our vision is that all Papua New Guineans should have access to WASH by 2030.
Our Values
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
--       Respect
--       Accountability
--       Courage
--       Collaboration
--       Innovation
--       Integrity
WASH in PNG
In 2015 the government launched the country’s first National WASH Policy, which has led to the setting of clear WASH targets and priority areas for action. PNG has also signed off on a new WASH in Schools policy (as of April 2018), which will help to draw attention to the urgent need for improved WASH facilities in schools.
The implementation of the National WASH Policy is being led by the development of five year District WASH Plans to drive service delivery in the districts. Several donors are currently working with the WASH PMU to resource the development of District WASH Plans and facilitate learning on the process. District WASH Plans should be supported with annual budgets, to be funded through District Service Improvement Program (DSIP) funding and other government grants.
The drive for district level service delivery within the framework of the national WASH policies creates new opportunities to increase access to WASH services. PNG is now one of only three countries globally that has safe water coverage of less than 50% and has the twelfth highest proportion of people using unimproved sanitation. The positive changes in the enabling environment therefore need to lead to better planning for WASH services and an increase in public expenditure on WASH services.

About the Project
The PacFresH2O (Protecting Freshwater Resources for Increased Climate Resilience in the Pacific Islands) project is a multi-year initiative running from February 2024 to January 2031, aimed at enhancing climate resilience in rural communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands (SLB). Funded through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and led by GIZ in partnership with the Pacific Community (SPC) and various national government bodies, the project responds to pressing climate-related challenges like drought, flooding, and cyclones that threaten water resources and infrastructure. It seeks to address the low levels of access to safe drinking water—particularly in rural and marginalised communities through integrated water management and sustainable, community-based interventions.
The project’s core strategy is built around three outputs: strengthening governance, coordination, and data use; implementing phased, climate-resilient water and sanitation solutions; and embedding Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) priorities into national policy frameworks. A key focus is on showcasing underutilised resources such as groundwater, improving meteorological and hydrological capabilities, and training local and national actors, including women and marginalised groups in climate finance and evidence-based water resource management. Through these efforts, PacFresH2O aims to create scalable and replicable models for rural water resilience, boosting the adaptive capacity of Pacific Island nations in the face of climate change

The Program Officer will play a critical role in supporting the implementation of the PacFresh H2O Project. This role will focus on coordinating field activities, managing data collection processes, and ensuring effective engagement with community and government stakeholders. WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission. WaterAid is open to employing and working with People Living with any forms of impairment and disability and other marginalized population.
About the Project
The Kiwa Initiative funds regional programs that enhance climate resilience in Pacific Island countries and territories by supporting biodiversity conservation and nature-based solutions. Its focus includes empowering local communities, fostering regional collaboration, and addressing the interconnected challenges of climate change and ecosystem preservation. The initiative prioritizes projects that strengthen sustainable practices and promote inclusive, long-term impact.
Within this funding opportunity, WaterAid is proposing to collaborate with Live and Learn in Papua New Guinea to implement a program similar to the Climate Resilient Islands program, with the overarching objective to enhance climate resilience across Pacific Island communities, ecosystems, and economies by embedding community traditional knowledge and fostering inclusive, participatory action.
The objective of PRESERVE is that Pacific Islands communities, ecosystems and economies have enhanced resilience to climate change. The project enhances ecosystem and economic resilience to climate change by addressing vulnerabilities in water security, food production, and livelihoods through Nature-based Solutions (NbS), traditional knowledge and sharing, and inclusive governance.
JOB DIMENSION
Purpose of the Role
The specific purpose of the Program Coordinator is to oversee effective implementation of the PRESERVE Project, with a focus on strengthening the capacity of country program staff through training, mentoring and accompaniment to effectively manage grants, and all the quality program processes this entails.
The project is led by WaterAid Australia, the primary beneficiary and contracting entity with the French Development Agency (AFD) through the Kiwa initiative, a regional multi-donor fund (EU, France, NZ, Australia and Canada). WaterAid Australia will oversee all aspects of project governance, including financial management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and regional knowledge-sharing, as well as implementing activities project activities in Papua New Guinea and Timor-Leste
Live & Learn Environmental Education will act as an implementing partner, focusing on activities in Papua New Guinea and Samoa. Permatil Global, another implementing partner, will lead efforts in Timor-Leste.
Both Live & Learn and Permatil will also serve as on-grantees, receiving part of the grant to implement activities in their respective regions.
The project will commence in May 2026 with a deadline for implementation of the project by 30 September 2029.
Location
This position will be based in Rabaul, East New Britain Province.
Line Manager
Senior Program Manager, East New Britain
Budget / Operational duties
The role will support budget management and operational duties for East New Britain Office.
Team Membership
WaterAid East New Britain Programs team.
Documentation and Reporting

Key Performance Areas

Build and strengthen WaterAid relationship with district WaSH stakeholders and implementers including government and civil society organizations
Manage and oversee to implement field activities for PRESERVE are documented and reported
Lead programmes team regularly use of WaterAid Programme System (WAPS) and projects programmatic and operational data, and organization risk are updated weekly and monthly basis.
Work with GEDSI Officer to ensure the integration of GEDSI into program activities and provide support to women and PWD leadership in local community and capacity building of rights-based organizations.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge and Learning

jobs.description:
JOB ADVERTISEMENT
Be Part of a National Model for Community‑Led Conservation
This consultancy offers a rare opportunity to contribute to one of PNG’s most respected community‑based conservation initiatives. Your expertise will help strengthen governance systems that protect biodiversity, support local livelihoods, and shape national best practices for protected area management. If you’re passionate about conservation, governance, and community empowerment in Papua New Guinea, we’d love to hear from you.
Consultancy Opportunity: YUS Conservation Area Governance & Management Effectiveness
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program – Papua New Guinea (TKCP‑PNG)
Contract Duration:
May 2026 – December 2027 (actual duration may change)
Location:
Lae, with travel to YUS Conservation Area in Kabwum, Morobe Province.
About YUS Conservation Area and Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program
The YUS Conservation Area is Papua New Guinea’s first Conservation Area, spanning 162,683 hectares from the Saruwaget Range to the Bismarck Sea. Most of the conservation area is located in YUS Local Level Government, Kabwum District, Morobe province. The conservation area was gazetted in 2009 under the Conservation Areas Act of 1978. The area provides protection for a broad range of endemic and endangered species, promotes sustainable management of natural resources by its 15,000 indigenous residents among 50 remote villages, and serves as a national model for the conservation of customary-owned land. The YUS Conservation Area is governed by Conservation Area Management Committee comprising of all levels of government representative and community representative through their community-based organisation.
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program-PNG is a local NGO based in Lae, Morobe Province that provides technical support in the management of the YUS Conservation Area. Formally established in 2013, its technical staff implement programs across wildlife research and monitoring, community livelihoods and sustainability.
About the Opportunity
The Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program – PNG (TKCP‑PNG) is seeking a highly qualified
specialist organisation or individual consultant
to lead a major governance and community‑capacity strengthening initiative across the YUS Conservation Area.
This consultancy is part of TKCP’s multi‑year effort to strengthen community‑based governance, improve stakeholder accountability, and enhance management effectiveness for PNG’s first nationally designated Conservation Area. The work is supported by the British Government under the Darwin Initiative.
The successful consultant will work closely with TKCP’s Governance & Engagement Manager to deliver targeted training, coaching, participatory assessments, and practical tools that empower Ward Councillors, Community‑Based Organisations (CBOs), and community leaders to fulfil their roles in conservation governance.
Why This Work Matters
The YUS Conservation Area spans 163,000 hectares and protects globally significant biodiversity, including the endangered Matschie’s tree kangaroo. It is home to more than 15,000 people across 50 villages, all of whom rely on customary land and local governance systems.
Recent assessments (METT 2021, SAPA 2021) highlight critical gaps in governance, representation, and coordination between communities and government stakeholders. Strengthening these systems is essential to ensuring long‑term conservation success and improved community well‑being.
This consultancy will directly contribute to:
Improved community participation in protected area governance
Stronger Ward‑level planning and representation
Increased capacity of newly formed CBOs
More effective stakeholder coordination through the YUS Conservation Area Management Committee (CAMC)
Scope of Work
The consultant will deliver an interlinked series of activities across 2026–2027, including:
Community‑Based Organisation (CBO) Capacity Strengthening
Conduct a literature review on CBOs in PNG protected areas
Develop an Organizational Capacity Assessment (OCA) template and interview guide
Train interviewers and support OCA implementation in YUS
Analyse OCA results and produce a comprehensive report
Develop training manuals covering:
Effective leadership
Public advocacy
Group facilitation
Conflict resolution
Persuasive presentation & public speaking
Project management
Deliver a Training‑of‑Trainers (ToT) program for CBO leaders
Develop coaching and guidance tools for ongoing mentoring
Strengthening Community Engagement in Ward & LLG Planning
Support Ward Councillors and Ward Development Committees in participatory planning
Facilitate community forums and governance workshops
Provide mentoring and monthly coaching transcripts
Support integration of community priorities into Ward, LLG, and District planning processes
Monitoring, Evaluation & Reporting
Develop Monitoring & Evaluation questionnaires and tools
Deliver M&E training and produce workshop reports
Produce a comprehensive end‑of‑project report
Deliverables & Compensation
Payments are tied agreed deliverables upon contracting. Additionally, TKCP will cover consultant travel, accommodation, workshop venues, and approved materials.
Required Qualifications
We are seeking organisations or individuals with:
Demonstrated experience in
community‑based conservation
,
protected area governance
, or
customary land management
in PNG
Strong background in
capacity building
,
training design
, and
facilitation
Experience working with
Ward Councils, LLGs, or community governance structures
Proven ability to produce high‑quality analytical reports and training materials
Excellent communication skills and cultural competency working with rural PNG communities
Ability to travel to remote areas and work collaboratively with TKCP staff
How to Apply
Interested organisations or individuals should submit:

cover letter
outlining relevant experience

technical proposal
describing your approach to the Scope of Work

financial proposal

Examples of previous similar work
IPA and IRC documents to confirm business entity.

Job Type:

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our growing exploration team as our drilling program expands in 2026 and 2027, you will provide front line leadership, support, mentoring and service in all geology activities, associated with exploration and resource drilling, core processing, sample analysis and resource evaluation. Observe and adhere to the workplace health & safety policies to ensure safety of employee’s contractors and stakeholders.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide appropriate leadership, guidance mentoring and support in geology services to exploration.
Manage all Exploration sampling activities – including but not limited to drilling, rock chip, soil sampling.
Surveying and mapping designated areas / prospects.
Analysing geological data using specialist computer applications.
Preparing reports, both internal and statutory, physicals and forecast. Complete all reports in a timely manner, adhering to strict deadlines.
Ensure correct QA/QC protocols are adhered to.
Drill hole planning, designs and roll out.
Ensuring / authorising that geotechnical inspections of drill pads are completed, pre- and post-construction and pre-drilling. Ensure that regular monitoring of drill pads is carried out.
Coordinate drill pads design and construction in a timely manner.
Ensure logging of core by geologist is accurate, consistent, and complete; includes inspecting core logs and comparing with drill core.
Carry out weekly database checks to ensure logging is complete and following up where incomplete.
Maintain accuracy at all times of processing data collected by core shed technicians and data base assistants (core mark-up, recovery, RQD, magnetic susceptibility, ASD, XRF, core photography, cutting and sampling).
Ensure that Camp Managers send core photos, timesheets, and daily reports daily.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to achieve a high level of performance and by rewarding and recognising high performance.
Ensure effective processes are in place for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members.
Direct and train employees on the Exploration SOP.
Continuously mentor and coach geology technicians on effective sampling, core processing techniques.
Actively review the work performance of geology and technicians and provide feedback to the Vice President (Exploration and Deputy Exploration including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure exploration drilling and sampling is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
To be considered for this position, it is essential that applicants have the following
Bachelor`s Degree in Geology (Preferable), Geophysics or Geoscience
7+ years relevant mining or exploration work experience essential.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite and the ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
At Newmont, our people and safe performance are fundamental to our success. As Advisor, Advisor People, Training (Asset Management Fixed), you will be instrumental in building and sustaining workforce capability across Fixed Plant Maintenance, with a strong focus on electrical training and compliance.
Your work will ensure our people are competent, authorised, and trained in line with regulatory requirements and Newmont standards, directly supporting operational safety, reliability, and continuous improvement across site.
As part of our team, you will
In this role, you will:
Evaluate Fixed Plant training needs, with a strong focus on electrical compliance and competency assurance, and identify skill gaps.
Design, develop, and coordinate comprehensive training programs aligned to internal, statutory, and regulatory requirements.
Create engaging training materials and learning modules that support continuous improvement and adult learning principles.
Deliver and coordinate training sessions across Fixed Plant Maintenance teams.
Maintain and assure electrical competency frameworks, including authorisation, verification, refresher, and gap‑closure processes.
Ensure training programs align with site electrical safety rules, statutory obligations, and Newmont standards.
Partner with Electrical Engineering, HSE, site leadership, and external training providers to ensure training reflects current risk controls and best practice.
Incorporate learnings from audits, inspections, and incident investigations into training content and on‑the‑job training.
Maintain and manage electrical competencies, authorisations, and compliance records within the Learning Management System (LMS).
Develop, review, and continuously improve training materials, facilitator guides, verification of competency processes, On‑the‑Job Training (OJT), and online learning content.
Conduct field observations and engage with operational leaders to understand workforce capability needs and tailor training solutions.
Maintain audit‑ready training and competency records demonstrating compliance.
Support safety leadership by coaching teams, participating in investigations, and reinforcing safe work practices.
Promote proactive safety behaviours, coach employees, and contribute to incident investigations and continuous improvement initiatives.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will bring:
Electrical trade certification (instrumentation desirable).
Formal qualifications in Training & Assessment, Education, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience in technical training, ideally within mining, processing plants, or the resources sector.
Strong understanding of electrical compliance frameworks, competency assurance, authorisation systems, and refresher training requirements.
Proven ability to design and deliver training aligned to regulatory and site standards.
Experience working with compliance, audit, and regulatory environments.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across a diverse workforce.
Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and training management systems
Auditor certification and leadership experience (desirable)
Proven facilitation, coaching, and mentoring capability across diverse operational teams.
Strong technical writing skills with the ability to translate standards into effective training materials.
Proficiency in adult learning principles and vocational education (VET) frameworks
Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office.
The capability to work with autonomy and minimal supervision, effectively managing priorities when provided with clear direction and resources.
A solutions‑focused mindset.
A clear commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and Newmont’s values.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 day shift Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will operate in a dynamic operational environment, supporting compliance across Fixed Plant Maintenance without holding operational electrical authority, while providing assurance that all electrical training and competency requirements are met.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global organisation committed to safety, integrity, inclusion, and sustainability. We offer:
The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on workforce capability and safety.
A supportive and inclusive workplace where expertise is valued.
Exposure to world‑class mining operations and systems.
Ongoing development opportunities within a global organisation.
The chance to contribute to safe, responsible, and sustainable mining.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 42058 before the advertised closing date: 7 May 2026.
