jobs.title: Communications and Public Diplomacy Manager
jobs.description:
Fixed term contract up to 30 June 2028 (with possible 2 year extension)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG national candidates only
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.
The program aligns with the broader goals of the Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029, which emphasizes locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020002E.
Purpose of Position
The Communications and Public Diplomacy Manager is responsible for the delivery of SWLT’s communications and public diplomacy activities, helping to showcase SWLT in an engaging way, to raise awareness of Australia’s support for PNG’s TVET sector, and to draw public attention to TVET education as a successful pathway to in demand careers.
Primary Responsibilities
The
Communications and Public Diplomacy Manager
will be required to manage the implementation of the Public Diplomacy Strategy and workplan, coordinate stakeholder engagement, and contribute to content development and reporting:
Work with the Public Diplomacy Specialist in the initial development of SWLT Communications and Public Diplomacy Strategy and associated Public Diplomacy workplan (DFAT deliverable), ensuring alignment to PNG-Australia Partnership key messages and branding
Actively contribute to on-going management, delivery and updating of strategy and workplan documents to keep them relevant, impactful and effective
Build collaborative relationships with team members, drawing on technical advice and individual experience and expertise.
Work with the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) public diplomacy unit and other key public diplomacy stakeholders to leverage and extend reach
Assist in developing locally relevant communications materials, including social media content, newsletters, and case studies, working with the SWLT MEL team to capture content for public diplomacy efforts
Support the planning, tracking and management of communications and public diplomacy budgets, including supplier costs and event expenditures with support from Operations and Finance
Lead communications and public diplomacy reporting, including tracking performance, contributing to MEL inputs, and preparing regular updates on workplan delivery and results.
Managing aspects of program photography and videography, including permissions, editing, storing and publishing
Seek to develop new and innovative ways of developing and delivering content with key messaging sought through direct student engagement
Utilise digital analytics and survey mythologies to measure impact of messaging
Manage the media relations and monitoring for SWLT, including developing a media contact list, creating media releases and op-eds, acting as Media Liaison as authorised, keeping track of media coverage and public engagement, and contributing to MEL reporting on reach and effectiveness
Coordinate logistics and planning for public diplomacy events, campaigns, and stakeholder engagements, including supporting terms of references for events and developing budgets
Collaborate with technical teams to ensure communications reflect SWLT principles and program objectives
Provide strategic advice and support in the recruitment of the Public Diplomacy Coordinator, and provide leadership and coaching to this role on an ongoing basis
Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required
Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately
Model, contribute to and support an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts
This role supports and upholds the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices
Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles are embedded within program delivery.
Reporting Requirements
This role reports to the Deputy Director – Development Priorities and will have approximately one (1) direct report.
Reporting requirements may include but are not limited to:
Supporting inputs to the SWLT MEL Framework and Plan
Other project reporting as required.
Minimum Experience Required
The candidate needs to demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:
Delivering effective communications and marketing campaigns, with past experience in private sector or with donor funded programs
Strong writing, editing and storytelling skills
Ability to use of a range of communications and public diplomacy modalities and the hardware and software needed in their creation including:
- Social media platforms and content
- Videography
- Photography
- Visual graphics – charts, animations, infographics
- Newspaper and TV news ready content
Events planning and coordination
An understanding of the political and cultural context in PNG with the ability to work respectfully with partner government counterparts
Proven ability to work with MEL frameworks or communication monitoring tools
Experience coaching and mentoring junior colleagues and providing positive and constructive support that enables them to learn and grow
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team
Experience and/or knowledge of the TVET or higher education sector in PNG would be advantageous
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position via
https://palladium.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/2/home/requisition/25090?c=palladium&referralToken=_WbZuulmjEWkhAkMjzcBPg
Closing date:
Wednesday 06th May 2026,
11.59pm AEST

Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.

We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. Position Description
Reporting to:

Role Purpose and Scope
The Advocacy and Communications (A&C) Manager will take lead in designing and delivering innovative communications and advocacy strategies that inspire public support and actions, influence policy decisions and drive the agenda for children in Papua New Guinea. She/He is expected to organise and deliver advocacy initiatives aimed at changing practices for betterment of children’s lives at community and national levels, including advocacy workshops and mentoring young activists and groups. Working with the Program Development and Quality Director (DPDQ), they will lead on implementing the Save the Children’s Pacific Advocacy Strategy in PNG.
The A&C Manager is responsible for managing the PNG Country Office’s media-related activities as well as its social media and online platforms to ensure published information is up to date, of a high quality, accurate and in line with organizational policies and procedures. She/He will also support the capacity building of Save the Children PNG staff in identifying and undertaking communications to achieve brand consistency in line with organizational branding policy standards and donor requirements.
Dimensions:
The A&C Manager has both an internal and external orientation but works closely with the DPDQ, the Pacific Communications Manager and program implementation teams internally in facilitating the planning, implementation and monitoring of advocacy, media and communication initiatives. Externally, the role will be expected to strategically position Save the children in PNG as a leading provider of life changing interventions for children and their families around the Country.
Working contacts
Internal: PDQ team members, program managers and various implementation team members, thematic leads, consultants, visitors, communication and advocacy teams from the regional office and member countries.
External: Media, child rights groups, other civil society organisations, service providers, local authorities, and consortium members, partners, international and domestic publics.

Advocacy
With the PDQ Director, lead the development and coordination of Save the Children PNG’s Advocacy Strategy under the guidance and support from Save the Children Australia Policy Team.
Support the programme teams in implementing advocacy activities taking advantage of key moments to deliver on the Country Office advocacy objectives.
Work closely with thematic advisors involved in advocacy campaigns, public mobilization and engagements to create moments and opportunities for advocacy and change.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with Save the Children’s Australia Policy Unit, other Pacific Country Offices, to ensure common messages and effective advocacy efforts.
Build and maintain effective relationships with government stakeholders, civil society representatives, UN, INGOs, and Academia to advance Save the Children’s advocacy efforts.
Support Save the Children PNG’s engagement in regional and global advocacy efforts through contribution of stories, videos, photos etc. to highlight Country Office achievements within such initiatives.
Advocacy campaigns
Support the co-creation of advocacy campaigns at national and global levels with children and youth activists, including Save the Children Project Managers to explore opportunities for Children’s voices to be heard in project designs.
Work closely with thematic advisors involved in advocacy, public mobilization and engagements to create moments and opportunities for campaigning.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with Save the Children’s Australia, Pacific Country Offices, Pacific regional and global advocacy teams ensuring consistent approaches, common messages and effective campaign events.
External
Communications
Develop a communication strategy, guidelines and plan for the Country Office.
Lead the development and dissemination of relevant real-time humanitarian and development situational reports/materials.
Lead the dissemination of Save the Children brand to make it recognised, respected, accepted, and protected at all levels.
Support project leads and technical specialists to identify and document stories of change and case studies, success stories that communicate the impact of our work and for use in media work and for quality reporting purposes.
Take lead in reviewing and presenting stories, photos, messaging, fact sheets and multimedia products for Save the Children’s key public audience.
Support the field program teams in ensuring Save the Children brand and donor requirements are fulfilled for visibility and communications materials.
Work closely with the program teams on graphic design and production of materials for fundraising and advocacy campaigns.
Produce other external targeted products on an ad hoc basis as necessary and requested by the supervisor.
Train key senior staff on communications and media and support the Country Director and Senior Management teams in their roles as the Save the Children PNG designated spokespersons.
Media
Develop media strategy/guidelines to guide the engagement of Save the Children in PNG office with media.

Ensure that all media messages and engagements are approved by the line manager and Country Director.
Identify media issues, prepare media messages, assess appropriate media for communicating those messages and facilitate the process of disseminating/communicating those messages.
Take lead in media relations and, as appropriate, establish proactive and beneficial relationship with media houses that can help in advancing children’s rights at policy and program levels as well as identify opportunities to profile Save the Children work.
Ensure that any action undertaken to implement communications or media work in country is compliant with Save the Children’s communications and branding standards and has been duly approved by the Country Director.

Management of internal communications content including archiving, uploading on content hub, website and other platforms.

The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mobile Maintenance Department as a
Supervisor – Underground Electrical.
About the role
Reporting to the Forman - Underground Maintenance, the Supervisor - Underground Electrical will oversee the electrical maintenance and installation activities within New Porgera Limited’s (NPL) underground operations. This role ensures that all electrical systems and equipment are maintained, repaired, and installed to the highest standards, supporting safe and efficient mining operations. The Supervisor will lead a team of electricians, ensuring compliance with all safety standards and operational objectives while providing technical expertise and leadership.
In this role, you will
:
Supervise and lead a team of electricians and trade assistants providing guidance, support and technical expertise.
Carry out maintenance, fault finding, and repair of underground electrical infrastructure and associated mining assets
Install, inspect and verify electrical installations in accordance with electrical codes and New Porgera Limited requirements

A Trade Certificate in Electrical.

Background:
SCHEDULE 1
Duties and Responsibilities of Position
The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
Reporting to the Site Supply Chain Lead at Lihir, the Advisor, Contract Management supports the effective delivery and performance of site‑based contracts, ensuring alignment with procurement strategies, governance frameworks, and operational requirements, and contributes to the overall success and continuity of site operations.
The role coordinates and oversees post‑award contract management activities across the contract lifecycle, maintains effective supplier relationships, supports cost optimisation initiatives, and ensures site contracts deliver agreed safety, operational, and commercial outcomes. The role also supports local content, community engagement, and sustainability objectives through monitoring supplier compliance with contractual requirements.

Reports To: Head of School / Pro-Vice Chancellor (Academic)

Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners.
Position Overview
The Lecturer of School of Law is responsible for delivering high-quality teaching, learning, and academic support in Law courses offered at IBSUniversity in collaboration with Southern Cross University. The role ensures that teaching aligns with international academic standards while contextualizing learning to Papua New Guinea’s legal environment.
The lecturer contributes to student success through innovative teaching practices, research, and industry engagement consistent with the Southern Cross Modules, which emphasizes focused, applied, and student-centred learning.
Key Responsibilities
Teaching & Learning
Deliver undergraduate (and/or postgraduate) law units in accordance with SCU-approved curriculum.
Facilitate lectures, tutorials, workshops, and online learning sessions.
Apply student-centred and interactive teaching methodologies aligned with the SCU teaching model.
Develop lesson plans, teaching materials, and case-based learning activities.
Support blended learning (face-to-face and digital platforms).
Assessment & Academic Administration
Design, administer, and grade assessments in line with SCU academic standards.
Provide timely and constructive feedback to students.
Maintain accurate academic records and reporting.
Ensure compliance with academic integrity and quality assurance policies.
Student Support
Provide academic advising and mentoring to students.
Identify and support students at risk.
Facilitate consultation sessions and academic support workshops.
Research & Scholarly Activity
Engage in legal research relevant to Papua New Guinea and the broader region.
Contribute to publications, conferences, and academic forums.
Support IBSU’s research initiatives and journal contributions.
Industry & Community Engagement
Maintain connections with legal practitioners, courts, and regulatory bodies.
Incorporate practical legal perspectives into teaching.
Participate in community outreach and legal awareness initiatives.
Quality Assurance & Compliance
Ensure delivery meets both IBSU and SCU academic standards.
Participate in moderation, curriculum review, and accreditation processes.
Adhere to university policies, procedures, and ethical standards.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential
Master’s Degree in Law (LLM) or related field (PhD preferred)
Bachelor of Laws (LLB) from a recognized institution
Teaching experience in higher education
Strong knowledge of legal systems (PNG and/or common law systems)
Desirable
Admission to legal practice (PNG or other jurisdiction)
Experience with international or transnational education programs
Research publications in law or related fields
Experience with blended or online learning platforms
Skills & Competencies
Strong teaching and presentation skills
Curriculum development and assessment design
Research and analytical skills
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Ability to adapt to international academic frameworks
Cultural awareness and contextual understanding of PNG
Working Relationships
Internal: Faculty members, academic administration, student services
External: Southern Cross University academic teams, legal professionals, regulatory bodies
Work Environment
Academic setting with blended teaching (classroom + online)
Structured teaching terms aligned with SCU model (short, intensive delivery cycles)

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You’ll play a critical role in keeping Newmont’s mining fleet safe, reliable, and production‑ready by delivering high‑quality fabrication and welding solutions that directly support mining operations at Lihir. Your workmanship will help minimise downtime and ensure equipment performs to standard in a demanding operating environment.
As part of our team, you will

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As
Team Lead, Mine Training
, you will coordinate and deliver end‑to‑end mining training programs that build a safe, skilled, and high‑performing workforce. Leading a team of trainers, you will support competency‑based training for mine operators, maximise the effective use of simulators, and work closely with leaders to assess capability needs and plan impactful training solutions. By maintaining up‑to‑date training materials, ensuring safety and compliance, monitoring effectiveness, and reporting on outcomes, you will play a key role in delivering practical, results‑driven training. Your leadership will ensure our people have the skills, confidence, and capability to perform at their best.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support a team of trainers, fostering consistency, quality, and compliance across all training activities. Through strong people leadership and hands-on technical involvement, you will ensure competency‑based training is delivered effectively, records are accurately maintained, and safe work practices are upheld at all times.
Implement and execute mining training programs aligned with departmental objectives.
Liaise with the Lead Technical Training and department heads to assess needs and plan training strategies.
Maintain and continuously improve training materials in line with industry standards and technology.
Monitor and evaluate training effectiveness using feedback and performance data, reporting outcomes accordingly.
Supervise, mentor, and guide trainers to ensure consistent delivery of training content.
Deliver and oversee competency‑based training for mine operators, including simulator utilisation.
Ensure full utilisation and ongoing support of training simulators.
Maintain accurate training documentation and compliance records.
Provide hands-on technical support during training sessions as required.
Ensure adherence to safety and operational protocols, with authority to stop unsafe work.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To succeed in this role, you will bring a strong blend of technical expertise, training capability, and people leadership, underpinned by sound judgement and a practical, solutions‑focused mindset.
Trade or tertiary qualifications in Mining, Training, or a related technical discipline, supported by relevant industry experience.
Demonstrated experience in mining training program development, delivery, and assessment, ideally within operational mining environments.
Proven people leadership capability, with the ability to mentor, guide, and motivate trainers while fostering a positive and productive team culture.
Strong working knowledge of mining operations, including safety, operational, and compliance requirements.
Ability to complete structured procedural tasks while adapting methods where required.
Confidence in following established processes, while identifying opportunities to improve ways of working through experience and observation.
Practical problem‑solving skills, using judgement, trial and error, and collaboration to overcome challenges or seek support when needed.
Advanced proficiency in technical training development, delivery, and team leadership, appropriate to a Team Lead level.
Experience with competency‑based training frameworks, training simulators, and Learning Management Systems (LMS).
Strong understanding of training effectiveness assessment, performance monitoring, and compliance documentation.
High level of computer literacy, with the ability to manage training records, systems, and reporting requirements efficiently.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) day shift roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea,
You will work within Newmont’s People and Technical Training function, partnering closely with operational leaders and technical specialists. This role provides the opportunity to work in a dynamic mining environment where safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement are core to how we operate.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our people are at the heart of our success. We offer:
A strong commitment to safety, inclusion, and sustainable mining practices
Opportunities to lead, influence, and make a lasting impact on workforce capability
Career development and learning opportunities within a global organisation
A values‑driven culture that supports teamwork, respect, and accountability
If you are passionate about developing people, leading teams, and driving training excellence in mining, we encourage you to apply and be part of Newmont’s future.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. (The experienced, organised kind)

PNG Motors Port Moresby

We are looking for an experienced Service Advisor to join our service team in Port Moresby and support the daily operation of our workshop.
This is not an entry-level role. If your experience with vehicle servicing is limited to owning a car, this position probably isn’t for you.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be the main point of contact between customers and the workshop. That means booking vehicles in for service, preparing job cards, explaining service requirements to customers, and coordinating with technicians to ensure work is carried out efficiently and accurately.
You’ll provide updates to customers on repair progress, assist with service quotations, manage service documentation, and ensure all service records and invoices are prepared correctly. Clear communication and strong organisation are essential.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone who already understands how a service department works. You should have experience in an automotive service advisor role or a similar workshop coordination position.
You’re comfortable dealing with customers, technicians, and parts departments at the same time. You understand service processes, vehicle repairs, and the importance of accurate documentation.
Strong computer skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure are essential.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates nationwide and supports customers who rely on their vehicles every day for work, transport, and business. Our service departments are professional, well-structured environments where experienced staff are trusted to do their job properly.
You’ll work with recognised global automotive brands and be part of a team that values reliability, professionalism, and getting the job done right.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Crane Operator will play a vital part in safely operating cranes and lifting equipment to support mining, maintenance, and infrastructure projects across our world-class site. Your expertise will help keep our operations running smoothly and safely.
Essential Duties
Conduct Prestart Checks – Conduct comprehensive inspections of the crane that has been allocated for operation. Documenting crane maintenance status and reporting any faults or non-compliances.
Plan and Risk Assess – Conduct site inspections prior to set up of the crane commences in which they will assess the site for hazards and determine the most suitable crane and approach for the lift.
Preparation and Set Up – Set up the crane correctly at all times according to WHS legislation, site policies and procedures and manufacturer’s instructions.
Operation – Operate the crane in accordance with WHS legislation, site policies and procedures and manufacturer’s instructions. Interpret load charts correctly to calculate safe working loads ensuring that all lifts are within the crane’s capacity. Monitor the rigging of loads and commence lifting only when safe to do so.
Critical / Non-Standard Lifting – Understand the complexities of critical and non-standard lifting activities and comply with both site and industry standards while performing the lifts.
Pack Up / Post Operational Checks – Strict adherence to WHS legislation and Newmont policies and procedures. Pack up and post operational checks performed as per the manufacture’s instruction.
Reporting of any operational issues, faults or defects via supervision and documenting in the maintenance logbook.
Team leadership – Act in a leadership capacity and make crucial decisions that maintain the safety of the surrounding work area.
Ensure that all controls are always in place when the work area specific to their crane is operational.
Training & Experience
3 – 5 years relevant work experience essential in fixed plant maintenance and heavy industry.
Must be familiar with and understand safe work procedures that are relevant to the operation of mobile lifting equipment.
Proficient in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Sound, analytical, and critical thinking skills. Ability to solve problems in often high-pressure situations.
Excellent communication skills.
Strong active listening & people skills
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 day and night rotational roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Senior Finance Officer
jobs.description:
SENIOR FINANCE OFFICER – FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING
The Senior Finance Officer is a key member of the finance team, responsible for delivering accurate, timely, and high-quality financial management and accounting support. The role oversees day-to-day financial operations, including cash management, supplier payments, reconciliations, and month-end processes.The position also plays a lead role in coordinating institutional audits and supporting the effective management of financial systems. The Senior Finance Officer ensures the delivery of reliable internal financial reporting and maintains full compliance with organisational financial policies, statutory requirements, and sector standards.
KEY DUTIES
Completing month-end procedures, cost allocations, depreciation journals, bank reconciliations, balance sheets and accruals on a timely manner.
Work with Finance Coordinator CORE Finance to ensure Revenue allocations are done quarterly and accurately.
Managing cash flow and treasury by ensuring cash advances are made available as per project needs i.e., working closing with project finance Assistant for accurate and timely cash issuance and acquittal process.
Assist the Finance Coordinator CORE Finance in ensuring adequate compliance to organisation internal controls, finance, and procurement policy and conduct trainings as and when required.
Act as the lead support staff for institutional audits including external and internal audit and verification exercises.
Financial accounting system (SAGE) management - ensure staff and supplier details are added and support and training provided to staff on how to use SAGE.
Ensure supplier listing is updated and accurately keeping track record of supplier invoices and reconciliations of various account payables and receivables.
Conduct thorough procurement due diligence checks including counter terrorism checks.
Ensure systematic filing of all financial documents including payment vouchers and supporting documents.
Ensure weekly processing of online payments as per approvals via SAGE and suppliers are notified once payments are processed.
Maintain good working relationship with key suppliers including bank and other treasury partners.
Promote and integrate gender equality, disability, and social inclusion into day-to-day work.
Ensure compliance with CF policies and procedures
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in accounting /finance
A CPA graduate.
3 years’ experience in Financial Accounting and Grant management.
Understanding of Accounting software’s in particular Sage Intacct.
High level administrative and organisational skills, ability to prioritise heavy and varied workload and meet deadline for routine tasks whilst coping with the unexpected.
Excellent work ethics (including attendance, timekeeping, meeting deadlines, respect for others and willingness to share information).
DESIRABLE
Experience in working with NGOs and/or UN in cross-cultural setting.
A member of CPA Papua New Guinea.
SKILLS
Good coordination skills (planning, organising and monitoring
Excellent negotiation, communication and interpersonal skills
Maintain a high level of confidentiality and credibility
Non-judgment outlook and willingness to work with all kinds of people
Adaptable and flexible, driving and responding to change
Understanding development in country context and child-focused development programs

Parts Interpreter
(The detail-focused kind — the ones who get the right part, the first time)
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Behind every vehicle on the road is a parts operation that has to be accurate, efficient, and responsive. When the right part is supplied quickly, workshops run smoothly and customers stay loyal.
We’re looking for a capable Parts Interpreter to join our Port Moresby team.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be the link between the workshop, the customer, and the warehouse.
Your role is to correctly identify, source, and supply parts for service jobs, retail customers, and trade clients. That means interpreting parts using catalogues and systems, checking availability, preparing quotes, processing orders, and ensuring accurate documentation.
You’ll work closely with technicians to confirm specifications and avoid errors. You’ll liaise with suppliers when required, follow up backorders, and keep customers informed. Accuracy is critical — one incorrect part can delay a job, increase costs, and damage trust.
You’ll also support stock control processes, assist with inventory management, and help maintain an organised and professional parts counter environment.
Speed matters. Accuracy matters more.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone organised, technically minded, and confident communicating with both workshop staff and customers.
You’re comfortable using parts catalogues and computer systems. You pay attention to detail. You double-check part numbers. You don’t guess.
Experience in automotive parts interpretation is strongly preferred, particularly within dealership or branded environments. However, strong automotive knowledge, discipline, and willingness to learn will also be considered.
If a technician asks for a part — you confirm it properly.
If stock is low — you flag it early.
If a customer needs clarity — you explain it clearly.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is a national business with established brands, structured systems, and long-term investment in the PNG market.
Safety, accuracy, and professionalism are taken seriously. Performance is recognised, and capable operators have room to grow.
If you want a role where technical knowledge, accuracy, and professionalism are valued — this is it.

You’ll be the link between the workshop, the customer, and the warehouse.

Speed matters. Accuracy matters more.

You’re comfortable using parts catalogues and computer systems. You pay attention to detail. You double-check part numbers. You don’t guess.

If a technician asks for a part — you confirm it properly.

Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based at our campsite in Moro, Kutubu, Southern Highlands Province, this position is accountable to the Field Operations Senior Manager (FOSM) and is responsible for transforming strategy into the delivery of Santos Foundation program activities in partnership with key stakeholders in Southern Highlands and Gulf Provinces, respectively.  The FOM provides oversight of governance, risk management and security. The role provides leadership and mentoring to staff and partners.
This is a FIFO role with 28 days on / 28 day off roster.
Key accountabilities include:
Working closely with FOSM to develop and maintain effective partnerships with the Southern Highlands Provincial Health Authority (SHPHA), Gulf Provincial Health Authority (GPHA), Provincial and District Governments etc. to enable the effective implementation of programs and activities.

Collaborating with Santos field-based leads (Community Affairs, Security, Aviation, Operations Support, Safety, Environment) to achieve Santos Foundation’s objectives.
Working closely with the Santos Foundation and Santos security teams in monitoring and escalating security/threats as required.

Implementing Santos Foundation’s monitoring, performance and reporting processes to ensure that the program objectives and targets are met, trends recognised, gaps rectified, and required reports are issued in a timely manner.
Providing strong leadership to staff and continuously monitoring staff performance to ensure high performance
Supporting SHPHA and GPHA in responding to humanitarian and public health emergencies, ensuring communities receive timely and appropriate care.
Leading the implementation of SHP and Gulf security procedures and processes and ensures all staff are orientated and adhere to all policy requirements.
What you’ll bring:
Essential
Extensive experience as a senior manager in a development environment
Highly computer literate – demonstrated experience in using MS Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
Degree in a related discipline
Demonstrated leadership and change management skills
Strong cross-cultural communication skills including public speaking
People Skills, Negotiation, Dispute Resolution, Analytical, Investigative, Program Planning, Budgeting, Team building, counselling, performance monitoring, Project Management.

High attention to detail and good communication skills
Strong time management and administration ability
Current PNG Class 6 driving license

Community Affairs, Security operations, Safety, camp management experience

Formal qualifications in Dispute Resolution, Social Studies, Project Management, Security and Incident Reporting

Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.

Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose  - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
As our site continues to grow with production doubling in 2026, we have created a new role that will lead the site services and utilities planning function.
In this role you will be responsible for the effective planning, scheduling, and coordination of maintenance activities to optimise equipment performance and reliability. Utilising Pronto as the core CMMS, you will be charged with forecasting component requirements, tracking critical equipment metrics, and ensuring efficient resource allocation. This role plays a key part in minimising equipment downtime through structured planning, monitoring, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Develop and implement maintenance schedules for both planned and corrective maintenance activities to ensure equipment reliability and operational efficiency.
Work with Maintenance and Power Station teams to ensure schedules are achievable and that they are achieved.
Train and direct the Data and Parts Clerks to ensure they work as required to support the Planning and Scheduling activity and to ensure they correctly prepare work order work packages for the supervisors.

Responsible for initial screening of work orders and analyse of required level of planning, arrange for parts, skilled tradesman and TA and hours required to perform task,
Liaise directly with suppliers for quotation and raise Purchase order as instructed by Superintendent and Managers
Daily Report, Weekly Report and Monthly Reports updated as required
Communicate clearly with contractors’ resources on specific task assigned to contractors.
Ensure work orders are closed once task completed within 24 hrs and parts required for next service are sourced and planned in to forecast.
Ensure weekly schedules and daily service sheets on all equipment are provided
Daily Updating of Generator machine hours
About You
Mechanical/electrical trade and/or Bachelor of Engineering degree (Mechanical or Electrical)
Strong understanding of Construction, General Building Maintenance and Fixed Plant, mainly Generators.
5 years of practical experience in a maintenance-focused industry, preferably in a mining environment.
Proficiency in Pronto ERP or other CMMS platforms.
Advanced skills in Microsoft Excel and Power BI for data analysis and reporting.
Strong knowledge of condition monitoring, failure analysis, and reliability metrics..
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, Project, Outlook).
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.

The Efficient & Inclusive Markets Unit Team Leader will report directly to the Director, APEP. The Team Leader will ensure that projects are implemented in close collaboration with other APEP teams, especially the Foster Inclusive Agricultural Growth and Expanded Livelihoods team, and in accordance with annual work plans, milestone deliverables and international development standards, and will leverage opportunities for collaborative programming with other Australian Government assistance programs, ministries, departments and agencies and the private sector. jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor - Registered Mine Electrician (RME) Delegate, you will play a critical role in ensuring electrical safety, compliance, and operational excellence across site operations. Your work will directly support a safe and efficient workplace by upholding standards, mentoring others, and maintaining regulatory compliance.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Conduct field critical control checks and ensure proper isolation processes.
Lead investigations into electrical safety incidents and implement corrective actions.
Authorize and issue electrical permits, access keys, and maintain compliance records.
Support training, coaching, and development of electrical personnel.
Ensure all electrical work meets Australian standards and Newmont specifications.
Liaise with departments to clarify site electrical requirements and standards.
Review and approve energization notifications and electrical licenses.
Participate in audits, risk assessments, and compliance documentation.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
At Newmont, our success is built on strong, respectful partnerships with the communities who host our operations. As Advisor, Community Relations, you will play a critical role in coordinating meaningful engagement with Lihir Island communities, supporting grievance management, and strengthening trust with local stakeholders. Your work will directly contribute to maintaining Newmont’s social licence to operate while supporting sustainable community and mine development that delivers shared value.
As part of our team, you will
In this role, you will:
Proactively support community engagement initiatives that strengthen relationships with host communities and government stakeholders.
Share accurate and timely information on company activities, including employment, procurement, operational performance, and community investment initiatives.
Listen to, document, and follow up on community feedback, concerns, and grievances in line with Newmont policies and standards.
Assist with organising community meetings, site visits, and participation in local events.
Support community investment programs by contributing local insight into community needs, priorities, and capabilities.
Build trust‑based, collaborative relationships with community leaders and key stakeholders.
Contribute to transparent communication, reporting, and ethical engagement practices.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will bring:
Tertiary qualifications in stakeholder engagement, communications, community relations, planning, management, commerce, or a related discipline
Relevant experience in mining operations (preferred), with expertise in community relations, agreement implementation, stakeholder management, and grievance resolution.
Prior experience in a similar community‑facing or stakeholder engagement role, ideally within complex operational environments such as mining, oil and gas, or large infrastructure projects.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining trusted relationships with local community members, leaders, and stakeholders.
Proven capability in managing community grievances and complaints, ensuring issues are addressed transparently, respectfully, and in line with company standards.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively across diverse cultural groups.
A practical, solutions‑focused mindset, applying sound judgement and seeking support when required.
Experience using stakeholder management, grievance management, and reporting systems.
A data‑driven approach, using insights and information to guide continuous improvement in community engagement initiatives.

This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly‑In, Fly‑Out (FIFO) day‑shift roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea, and is also available on a residential 5:2 roster for local Lihir‑based candidates. You will work closely with community members, internal teams, and external stakeholders. You will operate in a dynamic, culturally diverse environment where collaboration, respect, and communication are essential to success.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global organisation committed to safety, integrity, inclusion, and sustainability. We offer:
The opportunity to make a meaningful impact at a community level.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. About the role
Reporting to the Shotcrete Supervisor this role will be required to ensure delivery of concrete mixes from the batch plant to required locations on the surface of the mine are carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedure

Operate and maintain the Agitator Truck according to all K92 Plan Operations & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.

Actively monitor the condition of mixed product to ensure product does not set prematurely in the mixing bowl.

Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment and commitment to safety.
Knowledge of concrete additives and aggregates.
Previous experience working within the mining industry.
General knowledge of underground mining equipment.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
Our Lihir operation is seeking a skilled Instrumentation Technician to become a vital member of the Fixed Plant Maintenance team. This role is essential to maintaining the safety, availability, and reliability of equipment within the Processing Plant. As a key technical expert, you will perform daily instrumentation maintenance tasks. Troubleshoot and resolve instrumentation issues promptly and contribute to the continuous improvement of equipment reliability and plant uptime. We’re looking for someone who thrives in a high-performance environment, values safety, and is committed to operational excellence. If you’re ready to take on this challenge and support the success of our Processing Plant, we’d like to hear from you.
Essential Duties
Execute daily instrumentation maintenance tasks in alignment with operational priorities.
erform preventative maintenance and inspections on plant instrumentation, ensuring a high standard of quality and reliability.
Promptly report and escalate issues that may affect task execution, timelines, or safety outcomes.
Maintain clear, concise, and proactive communication with Supervisors and cross-functional teams.
Actively support and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, including the recommendation and implementation of reliability enhancements.
Ensure compliance with all regulatory and internal maintenance standards.
Comply fully with Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) policies and procedures, including Fitness for Work requirements.
Undertake tasks only when associated hazards and potential risks are clearly understood and effectively controlled.
Collaborate positively and effectively within a diverse and inclusive team environment.
Take ownership of personal professional development and seek opportunities to improve performance.
Identify and propose initiatives to reduce maintenance costs and eliminate inefficiencies or waste across operations.
Training & Experience
Qualifications & Certifications:
Minimum Grade 10 education.
Trade Certification in Electrical or Instrumentation.
PNG Power Electrical License
Cert 3 in Instrumentation and Control
PNG National Driver’s License
Technical Competencies:
Ability to interpret and update electrical and instrumentation diagrams.
Proficient in installation, diagnostics, and Process Instrumentation such as Control Valves, Weightometers, Level,
Pressure, Flow, Density, pH, HCN gas measuring instruments and DCS control system
Knowledge of Australian Electrical Installation Standards (AS/NZS 3000).
Strong fault-finding and analytical skills.
Experience with process control systems and maintenance recordkeeping.
Experience:
Proven record of relevant working years of experience in a heavy industrial or mining environment
Demonstrated preventive maintenance on plant instrumentation.
Strong interpersonal and active listening skills.Good time management with high attention to detail.
Able to work independently and collaborate within a team.
Working Conditions
Willingness to work a FIFO roster.
Ability to complete a pre-employment medical assessment.
Must provide a valid Police Clearance issued within the last six months.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the advertised closing date of 19 January 2026 by quoting the role's reference number:41242 – we’d love to hear from you!

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The Manager – Markets
is responsible for leading and managing all municipal market operations within NCDC, ensuring markets operate as safe, clean, orderly, and accessible trading environments. The role oversees vendor management, revenue collection, infrastructure maintenance, and stakeholder engagement while driving improvements in market systems and service delivery. It plays a key role in supporting local economic activity, food security, and inclusive participation, particularly for women, youth, and small-scale traders.
Role Purpose
The role exists to provide strategic and operational leadership in the management of NCDC markets, ensuring compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards while delivering efficient, transparent, and inclusive market services. Through effective coordination, governance, and stakeholder engagement, the Manager supports sustainable market operations, improved vendor livelihoods, and safe public trading spaces.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and manage daily operations of all NCDC municipal markets
Ensure compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards
Oversee vendor registration, stall allocation, and vendor relations
Manage revenue collection systems and ensure financial accountability
Monitor and maintain market infrastructure, cleanliness, and functionality
Coordinate contractor performance (cleaning, security, maintenance)
Promote safe and inclusive trading environments for all users
Engage with vendors, communities, and stakeholders to improve services
Monitor performance and prepare operational and financial reports
Support emergency response and incident management within markets
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Public Administration, Economics, Community Development, or a related field
Preferred:
Other certifications and training, or a postgraduate qualifications relevant to the role.
Driver’s License (minimum Class 3).
Skills & Knowledge
Strong leadership and team management with the ability to drive performance across multiple market sites
Sound understanding of market operations, vendor management, and community-based economic activities
Knowledge of public health, sanitation, safety regulations, and municipal by-laws
Strong financial management capability, including revenue collection, budgeting, and procurement processes
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships with vendors, communities, and partners
Strong organisational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities
Ability to analyse operational challenges and implement practical, sustainable improvements
Understanding of community engagement approaches and inclusive service delivery practices
Work Experience
Demonstrated more than 5 years’ experience in managing operational service environments such as markets, facilities, community services, or similar public service operations.
Experience supervising staff and coordinating service delivery across multiple locations or teams.
Experience working with community stakeholders, vendors, or small business operators.
Experience managing operational budgets, revenue collection systems, or contractor services.
Experience working with government agencies, development partners, or community organisations is desirable.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
