PAPUA NEW GUINEA UNIVERSITY OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT
Preamble
On 19 March 2026, the Interim Council of the Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNG UNRE) approved the recruitment of a Dean for Position No.:
UNRE – GB
001
, Designation:
Dean for the School of Sustainable Resources Management and Business Studies
.
The incumbent for the position is required by the Council to lead the establishment of the
Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute
and a Momis Fellowship for the Institute as approved by the Council on 28 November 2025.
About the University
PNG UNRE is a specialised national university mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNG UNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific region.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from distinguished and highly motivated academics for appointment as
Dean / Fellow – Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute (MOCRI)
.
This is a flagship, internationally significant leadership role responsible for establishing and advancing the Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute as a centre of excellence in climate science, ocean research, disaster risk reduction, and environmental sustainability in the Pacific.
Based at the Vudal Campus with operational engagement in Rabaul and key field sites, the Institute will focus on cutting-edge research in ocean systems, climate change, environmental monitoring, and early warning systems. The successful appointee will lead multidisciplinary research programs, develop postgraduate training, and build global partnerships aligned with Papua New Guinea’s national priorities and international climate commitments.
The role reports directly to the Vice Chancellor and is central to PNG UNRE’s strategic ambition to strengthen its global research profile and leadership in climate resilience and sustainability.
Key Responsibilities
Provide strategic leadership in the establishment and growth of the Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute.
Lead high-impact, multidisciplinary research programs in climate science, oceanography, environmental systems, and disaster risk reduction.
Develop and oversee environmental monitoring systems and early warning mechanisms for climate-related hazards.
Establish and grow postgraduate (Masters and PhD) research programs in climate and ocean sciences.
Secure competitive research funding and build international research collaborations.
Publish in high-impact academic journals and contribute to global scientific discourse.
Build strong partnerships with government agencies, international institutions, and development partners.
Lead community-based research and outreach initiatives supporting climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.
Integrate traditional knowledge systems with modern scientific approaches in addressing environmental challenges.
Provide high-level advisory input to the University and national stakeholders on climate and environmental policy.
Oversee Institute governance, staffing, budgeting, and operational frameworks.
Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills & Experience
PhD in Climate Science, Oceanography, Environmental Science, Engineering, Geophysics, or a closely related discipline.
Minimum of 15–20 years’ experience in academic, research, or scientific leadership roles.
Demonstrated success in leading large-scale research programs or institutes.
Strong publications record with a high citation level and proven ability to secure research funding.
Expertise in areas such as climate systems, ocean science, environmental monitoring, or disaster risk management.
Experience working in developing country contexts or the Pacific region is highly desirable.
Proven ability to build and sustain international collaborations and partnerships.
Strong leadership, strategic planning, and organisational capabilities.
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, and policy advisory skills.
Commitment to sustainability, climate resilience, and community impact.
Salary Range
Professor Base Salary: PGK81,707.00 – PGK99,864.00
International Market Allowance: PGK76, 146.00 – PGK113, 092
(plus applicable allowances, housing, research support, and benefits)
Why Join PNGUNRE?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a transformative research institute positioned at the forefront of global climate science in one of the world’s most environmentally significant regions.
Papua New Guinea is home to some of the planet’s largest remaining rainforests and ocean ecosystems, making it a critical frontier for climate research, biodiversity conservation, and sustainability innovation.
The Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute offers:
A unique platform to shape global climate research agendas
Opportunities to influence national and international policy
Access to rich, under-researched environmental systems

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
About this Role
Our Lihir operation in the Power & Utilities department has an opportunity for a
Superintendent – Power & Utilities Electrical Maintenance
. Reporting to the Manager – Power & Utilities, the successful candidate will lead the electrical maintenance, engineering, planning, reliability & high voltage operations. Monitoring, diagnosing & improving electrical maintenance work & systems across the various power generation & distribution assets on Lihir Island.
Key Responsibilities
Lead Power & Utilities electrical maintenance, engineering, planning, reliability & high voltage operations across Power & Utilities assets, ensure safety is top priority & assets are maintained & available to support the site power demands.
Develop maintenance strategies, procedures and guidelines for effective maintenance of P&U assets, in line with site maintenance business practices & systems.
Adhere to compliance with safety, environmental & mining regulations.
Monitor, Diagnose & Improve teams’ performance & implement improvement strategies.
Run budget and resources for Power & Utilities electrical maintenance & reliability teams.
Accountable for Electrical reliability across Power & Utilities electrical assets.
Conduct regular inspections and safety audits all assets, work & systems.
Solve maintenance issues and streamline power and utilities processes.
Coach and guide the team on safe work practices & procedures.
Responsible for identifying relevant risks, implementing mitigation measures, and continuous risk monitoring.
Appointed Mine Electrician for the department.
Training & Experience
A bachelor’s degree in engineering, Electrical Engineering, diploma, Electrical Tradesman or a related field.
Several years of experience in power generation & high voltage management and systems, demonstrating progression through roles of increasing responsibility.
Advanced understanding of power generation & utilities such as reciprocating engine generation, control systems, high-pressure steam boilers, potable water plants, demineralization plants, incinerators, safety compliance, and stakeholder collaboration.
Advanced knowledge and practical application in maintenance scheduling, performance monitoring, budgeting, risk mitigation and compliance with safety and environmental policies.
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent understanding of cost management and financial principles.
Advanced understanding and application of maintenance systems, SAP, scheduling software programs and tools Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance.
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21  Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! Project Lead - GBV Training Program
FHI 360 is a global development organization with over 50 years of experience partnering with governments, civil society, and communities to deliver evidence-based solutions that improve health, promote gender equality, and strengthen social systems. In Papua New Guinea, FHI 360 works with national and subnational stakeholders to address complex development challenges, including gender inequality and violence against women and girls, while upholding strong safeguarding, ethical, and accountability standards in line with DFAT and international best practice.
Gender-Based Violence (GBV) remains a critical human rights and public health issue in PNG, driven by unequal power relations, harmful social norms, and structural barriers to accessing services. FHI 360 adopts a survivor-centred, trauma-informed, and rights-based approach to GBV prevention and response, focusing on strengthening the capacity of frontline service providers, improving referral and coordination mechanisms, and ensuring safe, confidential, and ethical engagement with survivors. This position will support the delivery of high-quality GBV training across selected provinces, contributing to improved service quality and strengthened GBV response systems.
Job Summary:
The Project Lead will provide overall technical, operational, and strategic leadership for the delivery of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) training across five selected provinces under the ABT–PATH subcontract. The role ensures high-quality implementation, strong stakeholder coordination, compliance with DFAT and FHI360 safeguarding standards, and timely delivery of outputs and reports.
Accountabilities
Program Leadership & Management
Lead planning, coordination, and implementation of GBV training activities across all five provinces.
Oversee development and adaptation of training schedules, workplans, and budgets.
Ensure alignment with ABT/PATH objectives, DFAT requirements, and national GBV policies.
Provide day-to-day supervision and mentoring of GBV Training Officers and M&E Officer.
Stakeholder Engagement
Act as the primary focal point with ABT, Provincial Health Authorities (PHAs), and key GBV stakeholders.
Strengthen coordination with health, police, welfare, and referral pathway actors.
Represent FHI360 in technical meetings and provincial engagements related to GBV.
Quality Assurance & Safeguarding
Ensure all training activities adhere to FHI360 and DFAT safeguarding, PSEAH, and child protection policies.
Maintain high technical and ethical standards in GBV training delivery.
Address implementation risks and escalate issues promptly.
Reporting & Compliance
Review and approve programmatic and narrative reports for submission to ABT.
Ensure accurate documentation of activities, lessons learned, and outcomes.
Support audits, performance assessments, and compliance reviews as required.
Required Qualifications & Experience
Postgraduate qualification in public health, social sciences, gender studies, development, or related field.
Minimum 7–10 years’ experience in GBV programming, training, or gender-focused development work.
Proven experience managing donor-funded programs (DFAT experience highly desirable).
Strong leadership, coordination, and stakeholder management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Typical office environment; ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (10-25%).
Occasional work outside regular office hours may be required for urgent project needs.

Microsoft Office Suite, project management software, and other standard office equipment.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. Joining our Fixed Plant Maintenance team, the Maintenance Planner ensures that all routine maintenance activities for our process plant are appropriately planned (with input from operations and maintenance) so that the work can progress in a safe, environmentally responsible, efficient, cost effective and repeatable manner.

Continually monitor compliance to, and optimize preventative maintenance programs and schedules, to deliver performance targets for equipment availability and reliability.

jobs.description:
Summary
We are seeking a highly experienced and reliable
Logistics Support Officer
to manage staff transport and vehicle maintenance. This role requires a mature professional with a minimum of
5 years of experience
behind the wheel.
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Passenger Transport & Transfer Services
Safely transport staff to and from work, meetings, project sites, and airport transfers as per the daily schedule.
Provide professional, polite service to external visitors, partners, and clients.
Ensure all routes taken are safe, secure, and efficient, avoiding high-risk areas where necessary.
2. Vehicle Care & Maintenance
Ownership:
Take full responsibility for the condition of the vehicle assigned to you.
Daily Checks:
Perform mandatory pre-start checks (oil, water, brake fluid, tyre pressure, lights) every morning.
Cleanliness:
Ensure the vehicle is washed and vacuumed regularly.
Strictly maintain a Buai-free (No Betel Nut) environment
inside the vehicle.
Reporting:
Immediately report any mechanical faults, scratches, dents, or service requirements to the Logistics Coordinator.
Fuel Management:
Refuel vehicles accurately and maintain a precise log of mileage and fuel usage.
3. Coordination & Reporting
Maintain an accurate daily
Vehicle Logbook
(Start/End Km, Trip details, Passenger names).
Communicate effectively with the Logistics Coordinator regarding traffic delays or schedule changes.
Assist with general logistics tasks, such as collecting mail, delivering documents, or moving light cargo.
4. Safety & Compliance
Adhere strictly to all PNG Road Traffic Rules and regulations.
Follow company security protocols regarding travel times and authorized routes.
Ensure all passengers wear seatbelts at all times.
Report any accidents, near-misses, or security incidents immediately.

Education & Certification
Mandatory:
Grade 12 Higher School Certificate (or equivalent).
Valid
Class 3 or Class 6 Driver’s License
with a clean driving record.

of professional experience in corporate transport, logistics, or fleet management.

Ability to change tyres, check fluids, and identify mechanical issues early.

Communication:

(Spoken and Written). Must be able to write clear reports.

Punctual, sober habits, honest, and well-groomed.

jobs.title: Maintenance Genset Technician
jobs.employer_address: P.O. Box 3177, Boroko, National Capital District
jobs.description:
Summary
The Genset Maintenance Technician is responsible for the preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and servicing of diesel and gas-powered generators across company facilities. This role ensures reliable backup power supply, compliance with safety standards, and optimal performance of all generator sets (gensets).
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Generator Maintenance & Servicing
Perform
scheduled preventive maintenance
(oil changes, filter replacements, coolant checks, battery testing).
Conduct
load bank testing
to verify generator performance under load.
Inspect and maintain
fuel systems, cooling systems, exhaust systems, and electrical components
.
2. Troubleshooting & Repairs
Diagnose and repair
mechanical failures
(engine issues, fuel injectors, turbochargers, belts, pumps).
Troubleshoot
electrical faults
(AVR, control panels, wiring, circuit breakers, voltage regulators).
Replace defective parts and ensure proper reassembly and testing.
3. Emergency Response
Provide
24/7 on-call support
for generator failures and power outages.
Rapidly diagnose issues and implement corrective actions to minimize downtime.
4. Documentation & Compliance
Maintain detailed
service logs, work orders, and maintenance records
(CMMS or manual logs).
Ensure compliance with
OSHA, NFPA 110, EPA emissions, and company safety policies
.
Track
fuel consumption, runtime hours, and spare parts inventory
.
5. Installation & Commissioning Support
Assist in
new generator installations, ATS setups, and synchronization checks
.
Verify proper operation before handover to operations.
Job Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
(required).
Technical certification
in Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Generator Maintenance, or related field (preferred).
Manufacturer certifications
(Cummins, Kohler, Caterpillar, Generac) are a plus.
3+ years
of hands-on experience in
generator maintenance and repair
.
Familiarity with
diesel/gas generators (10kVA – 2000kVA+)
.
Knowledge of
ATS, load banks, and paralleling systems
.
Mechanical:
Engine diagnostics (compression tests, fuel system troubleshooting). Ability to disassemble, repair, and reassemble generator components.
Electrical:
Proficiency with
multimeters, meggers, and diagnostic tools
. Understanding of
control panels, wiring diagrams, and synchronization
.
Soft Skills:
Strong problem-solving and attention to detail. Ability to work independently and under pressure. Good communication for reporting and team coordination.
Field Work:
On-site servicing at multiple locations.
Physical Demands:
Lifting (25 kg), working in confined spaces, outdoor repairs.
Shift Work:
Rotational on-call duty for emergencies.

jobs.title: Engineer, Process Safety
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Workplace Type: Onsite
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
We are seeking a proactive and technically skilled Process Safety Engineer to join our Health & Safety team. This role is responsible for implementing process safety strategies and providing subject matter expertise to enhance safety performance across our operations.
Essential Duties
Implement strategies to manage process safety risks across operations.
Develop and support Process Safety Management Plans and systems (e.g., Management of Change, operational readiness).
Facilitate HAZOP studies and operational risk assessments.
Support integration of Bowtie risk analysis into broader risk frameworks.
Provide expert advice to Operations Managers, Superintendents, and Supervisors on process safety matters.
Conduct assurance activities for Process Safety Standards and related systems.
Monitor and maintain process safety metrics to evaluate performance.
Investigate and report process safety incidents.

Daru
, Western Province, and Arawa, Autonomous Region of Bougainville.

Access, compile and share relevant technical information. Ensure that this information is available to program staff and partners (community members, government and others).

Establish and maintain contact with other organizations that carry out similar activities, to identify opportunities for improving project implementation as well as coordination and integration.

Carry out training support activities, such as tutoring community WASH volunteers ensuring that they have the necessary technical skills to carry out WASH activities and ensure sustainability.

Initiate and maintain dialogue with stakeholders where this will benefit the project's progress. This may include other NGOs, government units, or the private sector
Prepare reports of meetings; ensure that these are available to the program team and store them in easy-to-access location
Actively influence the implementation of government policies in ways that have a positive impact on the well-being of children, working with other organizations with similar goals.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENC
E
Degree/Diploma in Environmental Health, Clinical or Public Health, Water Engineering or Social Sciences.
At least two years’ hands on experience in working with rural or peri-urban public health or WASH programs, preferably related to community based rural development work at project coordinator or project Manager role preferably in the WASH sector.
Registration with national engineering or public health body or related institutions.
Hands on Experience in Program Management in a rural or peri-urban complex, international organization preferably NGO and humanitarian context
Experience in capacity building in sanitation, Hygiene and or public health such as training and mentoring

Exemplary people management skills.

Excellent skills in report writing.
Knowledge and understanding of World Vision operations would be an added advantage
Effective in written and verbal communication in English.
Excellent computer skills in MS application.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Mine Technician, you’ll play a key role in safely operating haul trucks and mobile plant to meet daily, weekly, and long‑term production targets. Your work ensures consistent, high‑quality ore supply to the crushers—directly contributing to Lihir’s monthly and annual gold output. You’ll be part of a team that values discipline, teamwork, and a strong commitment to safety, working in accordance with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environmental policies and the PNG Mine Safety Act.
As part of our team, you will:
Operate haul trucks and mobile mining equipment in the open‑cut mine to achieve production targets.
Deliver consistent ore feed to support crusher performance and gold production goals.
Maintain strict compliance with all safety, environmental, and operational procedures.
Conduct pre‑start inspections and ensure equipment is operated safely and efficiently.
Work collaboratively with supervisors and team members to maintain a productive, safe work environment.
Identify and report hazards, minimise waste, and support continuous improvement initiatives.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Prior experience in heavy industry, ideally within mining.
Ability to operate heavy earthmoving equipment is desirable
Certification on CAT 777/785 haul trucks and ancillary fleet.
Experience with modular mining systems.
Effectively manages own time to complete tasks in line with job expectations and requirements adjusting plans to cater for unforeseen events / disruptions. •
Recognises problems and proactively works towards resolution under the guidance of immediate Supervisor.
Recognises opportunities to minimise waste and addresses it according to the OHSE and operational standards and practices
Work in accordance with PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Safety System, Safety Policies and Procedures and Newmont Environment policies and all departmental operating procedures
Ability to communicate effectively both written and verbally
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 day/ night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.

At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are in one of the largest business schools in the country and offer degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruit of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts to help educate current and future citizens of Papua New Guinea.

At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learned skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but also enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us, and we believe that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression—this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.

The Assistant Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.

Contribute to departmental meetings, committees, and administrative tasks as required.

Support outreach programs, workshops, and seminars that promote business education.
Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.
Qualifications and Experience:
Education:
A Bachelor’s degree in Business Management, Commerce, or a related field is essential.
A Master’s degree (or working towards one) in Business Administration or a similar discipline is highly desirable.
Experience:
At least 1–3 years of teaching or professional experience in business or management roles.
Prior experience in teaching at the tertiary or vocational education level is an advantage.
Technical Skills:
Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.
Proficiency in using educational technology tools and learning management systems like Moodle and ERP

Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are seeking an experienced
Superintendent - Mine Control
to lead our Dispatch team and oversee the performance, integrity, and continuous improvement of our Fleet Management System (FMS). This role is critical in ensuring safe, efficient, and cost‑effective mining operations by combining technical system expertise with strong people leadership.
As the
Superintendent - Mine Control
, you will be accountable for the strategic and operational performance of the Dispatch function, ensuring high-quality data, system availability, and effective decision-making across the mine fleet. You will lead a team of Dispatchers, collaborate with multiple operational stakeholders, manage risks, and ensure alignment with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) expectations.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead and develop a team of Dispatchers, setting clear expectations and creating an inclusive environment where people feel safe to contribute ideas and raise critical issues.
Formulate the biennial Fleet Management Dispatch outlook, contributing to long-term operational planning.
Act as the custodian of the Fleet Management System, ensuring system health, reliability, and optimal fleet utilisation to improve safety, efficiency, and cost performance.
Plan, coordinate, and oversee technical system upgrades to maintain functionality, data quality, and operational integrity.
Collaborate with Operations and Maintenance to verify accuracy of Time Usage Model events and ensure alignment with FMS data.
Execute work in full compliance with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) standards, policies, and procedures.
Support dispatch operations by guiding daily tasks, providing system oversight, and stepping in as required to ensure continuity.
Identify operational and system-related risks, implement mitigation measures, and continuously monitor risk exposure.
Ensure all work within Mine Control aligns with Newmont’s HSE requirements, supporting a strong and proactive safety culture.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Significant experience in mine control, fleet management, or dispatch operations within a mining environment.
Proficiency with Dispatch 6 Modular
Strong technical knowledge of fleet management systems, system maintenance, and operational data accuracy.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including team development, coaching, performance management, and building inclusive team environments.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills with an ability to build strong relationships across departments.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data trends and make informed decisions.
Solid understanding of risk management, compliance requirements, and safe operational practices.
Qualifications in Mining, Operations Management, or a related field (preferred).
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a
22:20 roster
to Lihir Island, PNG. We are we are flexible in considering residential housing options or FIFO roster arrangements for the right candidate.
Our accommodation offers a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 24th March 2026 – we’d love to hear from you!

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Waste Management Officer (WMO)
– Waste Disposal & Illegal Disposal oversees daily waste disposal operations at Baruni Dump and leads NCDC’s response to illegal dumping across the National Capital District. The role involves supervising staff and contractors, monitoring operational risks, ensuring compliance with environmental, health, and safety standards, and coordinating community engagement and enforcement actions to maintain clean and safe communities.
Role Purpose
To ensure the safe, efficient, and compliant management of waste disposal operations, reduce illegal dumping, and improve community cleanliness through proactive monitoring, stakeholder coordination, staff supervision, and continuous operational improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Waste Disposal Oversight:
Supervise daily operations at Baruni Dump, including safe unloading, traffic flow, waste compaction, and contractor activities.
Illegal Dumping Response:
Monitor citywide illegal dumping, plan clean-ups, deploy teams or contractors, document incidents, and support enforcement actions.
Operational Reporting & Compliance:
Maintain accurate records of disposal operations and illegal dumping incidents, submit timely reports, and recommend improvements.
Safety & Environmental Monitoring:
Conduct inspections to identify hazards, ensure PPE use, manage environmental risks, and escalate issues requiring intervention.
Contractor Management:
Coordinate with contractors on attendance, machinery, and operational compliance, monitor performance, and recommend corrective actions.
Staff Supervision & Task Planning:
Support planning, delegation, and guidance to Supervisors and field teams to ensure efficient and compliant operations.
Community & Stakeholder Engagement:
Liaise with residents, local leaders, and internal teams to address concerns, promote responsible waste practices, and support public awareness campaigns.
Service Planning & Continuous Improvement:
Identify operational bottlenecks, safety risks, and service gaps, providing recommendations for improvements.
Procurement Support:
Obtain quotes, prepare purchase requests for operational resources, and monitor resource usage in line with budgets.
Professional Conduct & Development:
Participate in training, capacity-building, and appraisal processes while upholding NCDC’s values of professionalism, integrity, collaboration, and service excellence.
Other Duties:
Perform additional tasks as assigned by managers or the City Manager to support waste management operations.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health, Environmental Science, Waste Management, Public Health, or a related environmental or sustainability discipline.
Preferred:
Additional training or certification in waste operations, public health sanitation, OHS, environmental compliance, or community awareness.
Highly desirable:
Valid Driver’s Licence (minimum Class 3).
Skills & Knowledge
Strong understanding of waste disposal operations, including landfill/dump management, waste flows, compaction, cover procedures, and disposal-site safety requirements.
Knowledge of illegal dumping behaviours, common hotspot patterns, and environmental/public health risks associated with abandoned waste.
Familiarity with NCDC waste management policies, Public Health Act requirements, environmental protection standards, and safety regulations governing disposal-site operations.
Awareness of machinery operations at disposal sites, including loaders, compactors, excavators, and traffic management considerations.
Understanding of environmental risks such as odour, fire, pests, drainage issues, erosion, smoke, and pollution, and appropriate mitigation measures.
Strong operational coordination and site-monitoring skills for supervising disposal-site and illegal dumping activities.
Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills for interacting with contractors, communities, regulators, and internal NCDC teams.
Good organisational and planning skills to prioritise daily disposal and illegal dumping tasks efficiently.
Ability to prepare clear operational records, inspection notes, incident reports, and enforcement-related documentation.
Ability to identify hazards, assess risks, and apply safe work practices in high-risk waste environments.
Dedicated, reliable, and committed to supporting NCDC’s waste management objectives and service standards.
Work Experience
At least 1–2 years experience in waste disposal operations, environmental services, public health inspection, waste management fieldwork, or related operational roles.
Experience supervising contractors, working at landfill or disposal sites, or managing high-risk waste-handling environments is an advantage.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Manager – Settlements to Suburbs
provides strategic and operational leadership to plan, coordinate, and deliver settlement upgrading and formalisation initiatives across the National Capital District. The role oversees the development of land subdivision layouts, infrastructure improvements (including roads, drainage, utilities, public spaces, and community facilities), and the integration of social and environmental considerations in line with the Port Moresby Urban Development Plan and national policy frameworks.
The position works collaboratively with other NCDC Branches, external contractors, consultants, government agencies, and affected communities to ensure projects are well-designed, transparently implemented, and sustainable.
Role Purpose

jobs.description:
Build a Legacy: Lead transformative projects shaping the future of Port Moresby.
Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment.
Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.
NC Salary Grade:
NC.10
Location:
NCDC City Hall, Waigani, National Capital District
Reporting to:
Manager – Urban Planning
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Customary Lands Officer
supports traditional landowning groups within the National Capital District to document, protect, and manage their customary land interests in line with legislation and urban development priorities. The role acts as NCDC’s key liaison on customary land matters, working with landowners, government agencies, and statutory bodies to support tenure recognition, boundary verification, and dispute resolution.
Role Purpose
The purpose of the Customary Lands Officer is to ensure customary land interests are accurately identified and appropriately considered in planning and development processes. Through community engagement, documentation, and advisory support, the role promotes culturally respectful land governance, legal compliance, and inclusive urban development across Port Moresby.
Key Responsibilities
Verify and document customary land boundaries, ownership claims, and land use through field engagement and consultation.
Liaise with traditional landowners, DLPP, statutory bodies, and internal NCDC branches to support tenure recognition, planning decisions, and dispute resolution.
Provide advisory input, reports, and mapping information to inform development proposals, infrastructure planning, and land governance.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum: Diploma in Land Administration, Customary Land Studies, Urban and Regional Planning, or a related field, supported by relevant training in land management, dispute resolution, or community engagement.
Preferred: Bachelor in Land Management, Geography, Urban Planning, or Customary Land Tenure from a recognised institution.
Required: Valid PNG driver’s licence
Preferred: Eligible for membership with a recognised professional body (e.g., PNG Institute of Planners, Institute of Surveyors PNG, or equivalent).
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of customary land systems, traditional land ownership structures, and urbanisation impacts on customary land within the National Capital District
.
Familiarity with the
Land Act (1996)
,
Physical Planning Act (1989 & 2001)
,
Survey Act (1969)
,
NCDC Act (2001)
, and willingness to gain deeper understanding of customary land rights and dispute processes.
Understanding of formal lease conversion pathways and issues surrounding informal settlements on customary land.
Awareness of inter-agency roles and procedures involving DLPP, the Surveyor General’s Office, and community dispute mechanisms.
Knowledge of ethical and culturally sensitive practices when working with traditional landowners and clan-based landholding systems.
Customary Land Practice: Ability to document traditional land claims, support verification of landowner identities, and assist in resolving encroachment or land use disputes.
Community Engagement: Skilled in communicating respectfully with landowners, clan leaders, and community groups, and representing NCDC in culturally appropriate ways.
Documentation and Records: Competent in preparing tenure documentation, land history records, and correspondence relating to customary land.
Stakeholder Coordination:Strong liaison skills with DLPP, legal services, civil society partners, and internal NCDC teams.
Technical Proficiency: Proficient in Microsoft Office and capable of using basic GIS tools or mapping software.
Ethical Standards and Reliability: Demonstrated integrity, discretion, and commitment to responsible public sector land management.
Work Experience
Minimum of 3 years’ experience in customary land matters, community-based land management, or land dispute mediation
Experience working with or alongside DLPP, surveyors, or planning authorities in documenting or verifying land tenure.
Prior involvement in community awareness or advisory activities related to land rights, leasing options, or informal settlement impacts.
Experience supporting urban planning or development programs through customary land documentation or stakeholder engagement.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.

Terms of Reference (ToR)
Consultancy to Develop a Child Safeguarding Policy and Child-Friendly Version for the National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS), Papua New Guinea
Project:
Together for Safe Families
Organization:
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea
Location:
Port Moresby
Duration:
40 days over a period of five months
Background
Save the Children is implementing the
Together for Safe Families
project in Papua New Guinea, which aims to reduce violence against children by strengthening families, challenging harmful gender and social norms, empowering children, and improving child protection systems.
The project supports the Government of Papua New Guinea in strengthening the child protection system at provincial and national levels, including improvements to policy and legal frameworks and institutional capacity.
As part of this commitment, Save the Children will provide technical support to the
National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS)
to develop a comprehensive
Child Safeguarding Policy
. This policy will ensure that children are protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and harm when engaging with NOCFS staff and services. The policy will operationalize safeguarding standards within NOCFS to ensure that all staff, contractors, volunteers, and partners working with children uphold child-safe practices consistent with PNG’s legal framework. The policy will contribute to improving child protection services and strengthening institutional accountability.
In addition, a
child-friendly version
of the policy will be developed to ensure children understand their rights, available reporting mechanisms, and the responsibilities of adults working with them.
Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to:
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy for NOCFS aligned with Lukautim Pikinini Act and other relevant national laws, international standards, and best practices.
Ensure meaningful consultation with key stakeholders, including children, to help guide the development of this policy
Develop a child-friendly version of the (same) safeguarding policy.
Facilitate validation of the final policy and work with the NOCFS to develop a dissemination plan for the final policy (and child-friendly version).
Scope of Work
The consultant will undertake the following tasks:
3.1 Review and Analysis
Review existing national laws, policies, and regulations related to child protection and safeguarding in Papua New Guinea.
Review relevant international frameworks and standards.
Map safeguarding requirements under the Lukautim Pikinini Act to NOCFS operational mandates.
Identify gaps between current NOCFS practices and statutory child protection obligations.
Ensure the safeguarding policy complements statutory child protection responsibilities under the Act.
Clarify reporting obligations consistent with national referral pathways and legal requirements.
Align procedures with PNG’s existing case management and child welfare systems.
3.2 Stakeholder Engagement
Identify and engage key stakeholders including:
Relevant government agencies
NGOs and civil society organizations
Child protection experts, academic institutions
Development partners
Facilitate structured consultations to gather inputs and ensure the policy reflects local realities and institutional capacity.
Facilitate safe and ethical consultations with children to gather age-appropriate inputs into policy development.
3.3 Policy Development
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy including, but not limited to:
Policy statement and guiding principles
Definitions and scope
Code of conduct
Prevention measures (safe recruitment, background checks, staff training, supervision)
Reporting mechanisms and complaint procedures
Response protocols and case management guidance
Confidentiality and data protection
Risk assessment and mitigation measures
Roles and responsibilities
Monitoring and accountability mechanisms
Alignment with Papua New Guinea’s legal and regulatory frameworks
3.4 Validation and Finalization
Facilitate validation workshop(s) with stakeholders.
Incorporate feedback and finalize the policy.
Ensure the policy is practical, implementable, and context appropriate.
3.5 Child-Friendly Version
Develop an accessible, age-appropriate child-friendly version of the safeguarding policy.
Use simple language and culturally appropriate examples.
Ensure clarity on:
Children’s rights
Expected behaviour of adults
How and where children can report concerns
Deliverables
The consultant will deliver:
Inception report (methodology, timeline, stakeholder mapping)
Summary of stakeholder consultation findings
Draft Child Safeguarding Policy
Validation workshop report
Final Child Safeguarding Policy
Child-Friendly Version of the Policy
Required Qualifications and Experience
The consultant should have:
Advanced degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Law, Public Policy, International Development, or related field.
Minimum 7–10 years of experience in child protection or safeguarding or code of conduct policy development.
Demonstrated experience developing safeguarding and/or protection policies for government or large institutions is preferred.
Strong knowledge of Papua New Guinea’s child protection legal and policy environment.
Experience conducting participatory consultations, including with children.
Strong facilitation and drafting skills.
Experience developing child-friendly materials.
Excellent written and spoken English.
Ethical Considerations
The consultant must:

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Operational Services maintenance team, this role is responsible for the implementation and maintenance of mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and on our exploration sites in Kainantu. In addition, this position will also play an important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key Accountabilities
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a NATTB Trade Certificate as well a current electrical license. You will also need to demonstrate experience in the installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformers, motor control centres and starters. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) years’ experience working in a mining environment.
You must have a High Voltage switching ticket.
You must have a wide experience in installation and maintenance of Low and High Voltage transfers and starters.
Must be a self-starter and very resourceful with ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician – Geothermal Operations, you will play a vital role in supporting Lihir’s geothermal monitoring and safety systems. Your work ensures accurate data collection, reliable operation of geothermal systems or similar geotechnical operational systems, and strong hazard awareness across the open pit. By applying your technical skills, attention to detail, and commitment to safety, you’ll help maintain safe mining conditions, support geothermal project delivery, and contribute to the ongoing development of geothermal monitoring across operational teams.
As part of our team, you will
Ensure full compliance with all HSE requirements, policies, and Fitness for Work standards.
Complete HSE tasks only when hazards, risks, and controls are clearly understood and agreed with your Supervisor.
Work constructively within a diverse team and take accountability for your own development and performance.
Lead the installation and data collection of geothermal monitoring systems in the open pit.
Contribute to the execution of mine geothermal projects and support geothermal hazard training for operational and technical teams.
Conduct preventative maintenance inspections on geothermal equipment, including steam relief wells.
Identify cost‑saving opportunities and report any cost wastage within your area of responsibility.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Essential
Grade 12 education.
PNG Class 6 Driver’s Licence.
More than 1 year of experience in a mining or technical role.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work safely and effectively in a multicultural team.
Competency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and active listening skills.
High attention to detail, good time management, and the ability to work independently when required.
Desirable
Diploma in IT Networking, Electronics, Instrumentation, or a similar technical field.
Experience with data and software networking, system communications, and technical reporting.
Familiarity with geothermal or geotechnical monitoring systems.
Your work environment
This position is based at the Lihir Gold Operation on a
22:20 FIFO roster – days only
. You’ll be part of a small, supportive team within Mine Technical Services, working closely with the Supervisor – Geothermal Systems.
The role offers hands‑on fieldwork, exposure to geothermal monitoring technologies, and clear development pathways, including opportunities to progress into supervisory or geotechnical operations roles. You’ll thrive in an environment that values safety, teamwork, continuous learning, and technical excellence.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an ensuited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development and climate-resilient outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as
Tutor (Technical Instructor – Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering)
within the Department of Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering, School of Environment and Climate Change (SECC).
This position supports the delivery of tutorials, laboratory sessions, and applied practical learning in Renewable Energy and Environmental Engineering programs. The role contributes to undergraduate teaching, laboratory-based instruction, applied research support, and industry- and community-linked activities aligned with PNGUNRE’s mandate in renewable energy development, environmental sustainability, and climate change response.
The successful appointee will work under the direction of a Lecturer and report to the Head of Department, Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering.
Key Responsibilities
Assist Lecturers in the preparation and delivery of tutorials, laboratory sessions, and practical classes in Renewable Energy and Environmental Engineering.
Plan, prepare, and support engineering laboratories and applied practical classes to enhance student learning outcomes.
Provide technical assistance to students during laboratory work, practical assessments, and applied learning activities.
Assist in setting assessment tasks, marking scripts, and submission of student results in accordance with university procedures.
Support academic staff in applied research activities, including data collection, laboratory work, and research implementation.
Contribute to the preparation of teaching and learning materials and laboratory manuals.
Participate in short courses, workshops, seminars, and industry or community engagement activities facilitated by the Department.
Attend departmental, school, and University meetings, seminars, and training as required.

Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
The SGSC Senior Engineer plays a key role in establishing and strengthening the PNG national-led support centre in Port Moresby.
The role supports the safe, reliable and efficient production of oil and gas by delivering high-quality engineering services across Santos’ portfolio of assets. This includes providing technical stewardship, leading engineering deliverables, and ensuring strong risk management and governance within established systems and processes.
As part of the SGSC engineering support workstream, the Senior Engineer works closely with Santos’ operating assets and support teams, taking a leadership role in the delivery of defined engineering services to a consistently high standard. The role has a strong focus on building PNG technical capability through coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer, contributing to the long-term sustainability and technical depth of the SGSC engineering team.
SGSC Senior Engineers are expected to demonstrate Santos’ values and apply the LEAP behavioural framework in all aspects of their work.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide senior technical support to operations, maintenance, and engineering teams across Santos’ assets, including peer review and advice within delegated authority.
Lead the delivery of engineering scopes from problem definition to implementation and close-out, ensuring quality, schedule, and stakeholder alignment.
Act as a technical focal point for stakeholders, managing interfaces to deliver timely, accurate, and fit-for-purpose outcomes. Support operational risk management through Management of Change (MOC), hazard and risk assessments, and barrier management.
Provide technical stewardship and build capability in the SGSC team through mentoring, coaching, and on-the-job development.
Drive business improvement initiatives, including standardisation, technical quality and efficiency improvements, and cost and risk reduction opportunities. Contribute to the development of business plans and processes for the SGSC engineering support workstream.
Manage and coordinate daily engineering activities, prioritising work to meet team objectives while maintaining strong discipline compliance.
Represent SGSC in internal and external interactions, upholding Santos’ values and behavioural expectations.
Support and uphold Santos Health, Safety, and Environmental policies, participating in the implementation of relevant action plans.
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and corporate governance requirements.
Apply industry best practices, standards, and specifications in all engineering activities.
What you’ll bring:
As a Senior Engineer in the SGSC, you bring a combination of deep technical expertise, leadership, and operational insight. You have a strong understanding of engineering principles across your discipline, with awareness of multi-discipline interactions, and are experienced in applying process safety, risk management, and problem-solving in operational environments.
You are confident working with stakeholders across multicultural teams, translating technical issues into clear, actionable recommendations, and fostering an inclusive environment where all team members are respected, valued, and able to contribute. You are also proficient in computer applications, including MS Office and relevant technical software, enabling effective analysis, reporting, and delivery of engineering solutions.
Essential
10+ years’ experience and a proven track record in technical engineering within the oil and gas or related resources industry, supporting operational and maintenance activities.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex engineering scopes and provide technical assurance, including review, verification, and approvals within delegated authority.
Deep discipline knowledge - Process, Mechanical, or Instrumentation & Electrical Engineering with broad multi-discipline awareness.
Strong understanding of process safety, risk management and mitigation.
Strong knowledge of relevant technical standards and regulatory frameworks in the oil and gas industry.

Proficient computer literacy, particularly in MS Office and relevant technical software.
Bachelor of Engineering (Process, Mechanical, Electrical, or Instrumentation/Control) and Chartered Professional Engineer & RPEQ status, or eligibility.
Desired
Operational asset experience, including brownfield modifications and shutdown/turnaround support.
Experience in project engineering and understanding of project management best practices, or the ability to rapidly develop these skills.
Familiarity with Continuous Improvement methodologies and experience using data to inform decision-making.
Commercial awareness and understanding of economic principles that apply to Oil and Gas production.

Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.

Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.

The opportunity
A high-impact policing partnership is looking for a Police Prosecutions Capability Advisor based in Port Moresby to serve as a key pillar of the RPNGC Prosecutions Directorate. You will ensure that prosecution structures, workflows, and legal practices are managed with the highest level of professional excellence. The role provides the essential technical support and mentoring required to reduce case attrition and protect the interests of the justice sector while ensuring efficient organizational flow.
This is an ideal opportunity for a self-motivated, highly ethical professional in criminal law or justice sector advisory. You will interact with key actors in this key arm of Government, supporting police prosecutors, brief managers, and supervisors, ensuring seamless compliance with national laws and providing sound legal advice to the directorate. The role requires excellent analytical skills and deep technical knowledge to navigate a complex legal environment within an organization undergoing significant capacity development.
The role
The Police Prosecutions Capability Advisor plays a central role in safeguarding the Directorate’s legal and regulatory standing through meticulous capacity building. Responsibilities include assessing existing prosecution structures, supporting provincial functions, and providing expert advice on criminal procedure and rules of evidence. The role serves as a key point of contact for the Office of the Public Prosecutor and the judiciary, providing the mentorship needed to ensure successful case outcomes. The overarching goal is to maintain a legally sound prosecutorial environment through proactive coaching and standardized practices.
Main duties include:
Assess and strengthen police prosecution structures, staffing, and workflows within the Directorate.
Provide expert legal advice on criminal law, procedure, and evidentiary standards to support charge selection and trial preparation.
Provide ongoing mentoring and case-based coaching to prosecutors and brief managers to improve file quality.
Assist in developing and updating prosecution policies, SOPs, manuals, and standardized templates.
Strengthen working relationships between police prosecutors, the Office of the Public Prosecutor, and the judiciary.
Facilitate Prosecution Review Committees to identify and solve systemic issues contributing to case backlogs and failed prosecutions
Qualification and Experience:
Formal Education: Bachelor of Laws (LLB) or an equivalent recognized law degree.
Professional Admission: Admission as a legal practitioner in PNG or another common law jurisdiction.
Core Experience: Significant post-admission experience as a criminal prosecutor, defense lawyer, or legal practitioner with substantial criminal law practice.
Technical Expertise: Demonstrated experience in criminal procedure, evidence, written submissions, and courtroom advocacy.
Mentorship Background: Extensive experience advising or mentoring prosecutors or police legal officers is highly desirable.
Regional Context: Proven ability to build capability of local counterparts within developing countries or Pacific justice sector contexts is preferred.
