Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Reporting to the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation, this role will be required to ensure the installation of underground paste reticulation and infrastructure is carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures. Paste Crew personnel are also tasked with assisting paste filling operations in the function of conducting routine checks and responding to potential issues that may arise while backfilling.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain underground mobile plant including light vehicles, Volvo L120 IT and Normet scissor lift.
Perform prestart and troubleshooting of fleet and tooling to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Install Paste Reticulation and associated infrastructure, including Quattro diverter valves.
Operate airleg rock drills while working at heights.
Pre-start inspections of paste filling reticulation lines and exclusion zones.
Respond in a timely manner to any paste blockage events according to response plans.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair, service and/or support as required to ensure downtime on plant and equipment is minimised.
Support and assist the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation to ensure the rectification of identified clashes in planned paste reticulation areas.
Work closely with the Senior Specialist – Paste Operations to ensure that all installation QA/QC processes and routine condition monitoring are implemented to maximise results and reduce risk of unplanned downtime.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure equipment maintenance is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Experience underground or in a similar role
Tickets in LV, IT, scissor lift & handheld rock drill tools
Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
Ability to work autonomously with limited supervision
Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment to achieve a common objective
Knowledge of paste backfilling systems
General knowledge of underground equipment
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Location: Port Moresby
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our vehicles are everywhere — now we need someone who can help tell those stories properly, in a way that feels real, local, and worth watching.

You’ll help manage and create the content that keeps PNG Motors active online. You’ll be out in dealerships, at launches, on the road, and sometimes in the sun getting the shot because that’s where the good content happens.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Reporting to the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation, this role will be required to ensure the installation of underground paste reticulation and infrastructure is carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures. Paste Crew personnel are also tasked with assisting paste filling operations in the function of conducting routine checks and responding to potential issues that may arise while backfilling.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain underground mobile plant including light vehicles, Volvo L120 IT and Normet scissor lift.
Perform prestart and troubleshooting of fleet and tooling to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Install Paste Reticulation and associated infrastructure, including Quattro diverter valves.
Operate airleg rock drills while working at heights.
Pre-start inspections of paste filling reticulation lines and exclusion zones.
Respond in a timely manner to any paste blockage events according to response plans.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair, service and/or support as required to ensure downtime on plant and equipment is minimised.
Support and assist the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation to ensure the rectification of identified clashes in planned paste reticulation areas.
Work closely with the Senior Specialist – Paste Operations to ensure that all installation QA/QC processes and routine condition monitoring are implemented to maximise results and reduce risk of unplanned downtime.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure equipment maintenance is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Experience underground or in a similar role
Tickets in LV, IT, scissor lift & handheld rock drill tools
Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
Ability to work autonomously with limited supervision
Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment to achieve a common objective
Knowledge of paste backfilling systems
General knowledge of underground equipment
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.description:
Senior Marine Finance Officer
The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being. WCS PNG is recruiting a
Senior Marine Finance Officer
based in Kavieng, New Ireland Province and may be expected to travel within PNG, especially to WCS marine field sites. The position will report to the Kavieng Program Manager with a dotted line to the Finance Manager.
Role Dimension
The Senior Marine Finance Officer is responsible for managing the financial systems and administrative functions of the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) Kavieng office. The role ensures full compliance with WCS policies, donor requirements, and applicable local regulations, while supporting efficient, transparent, and accountable financial operations. The position also provides financial oversight and administrative support to the Kimbe and Manus offices, working closely with program and finance teams to ensure strong financial management and consistency across all locations.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
Financial Management & Oversight
Lead financial management and administrative functions for the Kavieng office and field operations.
Provide financial oversight and technical support to Kimbe and Manus offices.
Ensure compliance with WCS policies, donor requirements, legal agreements, and local laws.
Maintain high standards of financial accountability, transparency, and operational efficiency.
Banking and Cash Management
Monitor and control WCS-PNG Marine office cash positions, including daily bank monitoring and reconciliations.
Ensure adequate cash balances are maintained to support operational needs; notify the Finance Director of funding requirements.
Manage cash flow across WCS-PNG Marine bank accounts and facilitate inter-account transfers as needed.
Liaise with program teams to forecast cash needs and support timely monthly cash requests.
Process and reconcile banking transactions, petty cash, staff advances, and acquittals.
Verify supporting documentation for all bank and cash transactions.
Review weekly accounting records prior to submission to the Finance Director.
Perform monthly balance sheet reconciliations (payables, receivables, advances, bank, petty cash, and prepayments).
Monitor bank balances to ensure uninterrupted Marine field operations.
Petty Cash Management
Process petty cash advances and expenses daily in compliance with WCS and donor requirements.
Prepare journal vouchers and post petty cash transactions in SAP with correct coding.
Conduct daily petty cash reconciliations and month-end cash counts.
Maintain an imprest petty cash system with monthly reviews and approvals by the Program Manager.
Employee Advances and Expense Management
Process employee advances and expense claims in line with WCS and donor policies.
Review and reconcile employee acquittals, including necessary bank lodgments.
Prepare journal entries for advances and acquittals for month-end reporting.
Maintain monthly employee advance balance reports.
Ensure complete and organized documentation filing.
Provide guidance and training to program staff on financial procedures and timelines when required.
Processing of Local Expenses
Review and process non-employee program expenses in compliance with donor and procurement requirements, ensuring:
Proper procurement procedures are followed
Appropriate approvals and signatures are obtained
Accuracy of amounts and purchase requisitions
Correct financial coding
Process payments through online banking or petty cash as appropriate.
Prepare journal entries for expense postings in SAP.
Track expenditures against approved budgets and Allocate expenses accurately to donor-funded projects.
Reporting & Coordination
Prepare and submit financial reports to the Senior Finance Coordinator in Goroka.
Respond promptly to finance-related queries.
Support program managers with financial planning and budget monitoring.
Coordinate financial processes for major and complementary projects.
Administrative & Asset Management
Process office bills and authorized expenditures in a timely manner.
Maintain and update asset registers and support proper care and tracking of equipment.
Reconcile travel advances and reimbursements promptly.
Maintain organized filing systems for financial and personnel records.
Update staff leave databases and manage induction and exit documentation.
Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Minimum Requirements:
Education/Credentials
A degree in accounting / Business Administration or qualification from a recognized professional accounting body (CA/ACCA/CPA)
Experience
Requires a minimum of 3 years accounting and administrative management experience
Exposure to non-profit sector (NGO, International organisations) is an added advantage
Critical Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Good analytical and problem solving skills
Preferably familiar with requirements of different donors.
Good knowledge of accounting system.
Competent in the use of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint etc.
Require knowledge of financial systems, internal controls and procedures
Able to work and interact with diverse group of people
Experience in the most current technologies and products used in the industry.
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
Being a self-starter with drives and initiative and able to work as a team/individual with a positive attitude and open minded
Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure
Excellent multi-tasking, organized and follow-up skills,
Demonstrated work experience providing customer service.
Application process
Please send a CV and letter of interest to
[email protected]
with the subject line: Application for Kavieng Senior Marine Finance Officer. Applications accepted until
Friday 13 March 2026
. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews.

Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​

Contracts Administrator
to join our team. This is a permanent full-time position for our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, this is a 21/14 Roster.
The position will initially be based on site at Simberi, however in the future will be based in Port Moresby.
Reporting to the Contracts & Procurement Superintendent, the Contracts Administrator is responsible for developing, administering and evaluating international, national and local landowner Contracts. They will ensure that all parties understand the terms of the contract, while complying relevant Papua New Guinean laws. This role will provide support to the Contract Specialist and liaise as required with the Community Relations Business Development Officer in relation to Local and Landowner Contracts and new business opportunities.
Everyone at St Barbara Limited is required to understand and act in accordance with St Barbara’s Values, Code of Conduct and all Company Policies and meet all relevant internal and external compliance obligations.
The opportunity
Role accountabilities
Ensuring own Health & Safety as well as that of all other workers, identifying and maintaining safe work practices and completing all required safety training.
Prepare tender documentation and administer tender process, through to contract awarding and execution stage.
Coordinate with end user department to formulate scope of work for contract drafting
Involved in drafting and execution of local landowner contracts
Negotiate contract terms with internal and external business partners
Explaining terms and conditions to managers and landowner contractors
Where required, review invoices and claims and ensure compliance with contract
Reviewing and updating existing contracts and maintaining contract register

Maintain contracts filing system to ensure accurate and up to date record keeping of information
and effortless retrieval
Scheduling meetings with contractors and recording meeting minutes for circulation
Manage effective use of available resources, including own time, in support of the delivery of the objectives pertaining to the Commercial Department
Contributing to an effective team/crew
Ensuring own work performance meets all role requirements; and taking appropriate professional development actions
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​

Keen attention to detail, with an ability to spot errors
Strong analytical and organisational skills
Excellent writing skills
Desirable
Mining industry experience
Proven work experience as a Contract Administrator or relevant role
Qualifications in law, finance or contract management
Fresh graduates are encouraged to also apply
For further information on the
Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/BRC8E

Credit Corporation Properties Limited seeks an experienced person to fill in the role of Maintenance On-Call Officer.
The Maintenance On-call Officer provides after-hours support and emergency maintenance response for residential properties within the company’s portfolio. The role ensures tenant safety, protects company assets, and maintenance continuity of essential services in apartments and staff. This role is based in Port Moresby.
Primary Responsibilities:
A. Emergency Response (Residential Focused)
Respond immediately to tenant emergency calls (e.g., power outages, broken locks, water leaks, flooding, faulty air‑conditioning).
Prioritize tenant safety during incidents involving fire alarms, gas leaks, smoke, or security-related issues.
Secure units during emergencies (e.g., damaged doors or windows).
B. General Residential Maintenance
Perform minor and temporary repairs such as:
-Fixing leaks or burst pipes
-Restoring tripped breakers or power faults
-Replacing blown light bulbs or damaged fittings
-Temporary AC fault stabilization
-Clearing blocked drains or toilets
Provide temporary solutions until daytime technical teams conduct full repairs.
C. Residential Property Inspections:
Conduct checks on:
-Common areas (corridors, lighting, stairwells, parking areas)
-Water pumps, pressure systems, and tanks
-Perimeter lighting and security gates
-Smoke detectors and fire safety equipment
Identify hazards that could impact residents
D. Tenant Support & Communication:
Communicate effectively and professionally with residents, ensuring issues are understood and prioritized.
Explain temporary fixes or the next steps if a specialist is required.
Escalate issues to the Facilities Manager or contractors when urgent intervention is needed.
E. Coordination
Work together with:
-Security teams (access, safety, lockouts)
-Contractors (plumbing/electrical emergencies)
-Property officers/managers
Assist in escorting contractors for after-hours work, ensuring safety protocols.
F. Documentation & Reporting
Maintain an after-hours incident log including:
-Time of call
-Nature of issue
-Action taken
-Pending tasks
Provide daily reports for supervisor follow-up.
G. Safety & Compliance
Follow residential safety and access protocols, including secure handling of master keys.
Uphold tenant privacy and confidentiality.
Comply with building codes and HSE standards for residential spaces.
Qualifications & Experience:
Required
Trade qualification in maintenance, plumbing, electrical, or building services.
Minimum 2 years’ experience in residential or facilities maintenance.
Ability to diagnose and resolve common residential issues.
Strong communication skills and good attitude.
Driver's license (Class 3 or 6)
Preferred,
Experience in apartments, townhouses, or staff accommodation facilities.
Knowledge of residential electrical systems, water services, and HVAC basics.
Familiarity with PNG residential maintenance challenges (e.g., water pressure issues, tropical climate impacts).
Key Competencies:
Strong customer service mindset (tenant-centred)
Fast and effective problem-solving
Reliability and responsiveness
Ability to work independently at night
Awareness of safety and security risks in residential settings
Good record‑keeping and accountability
Working Conditions:
Part of an on‑call roster (after-hours, weekends, and holidays).
May be required to quickly travel to different residential sites.
Work may include climbing, lifting, confined spaces, and outdoor tasks.
Must remain contactable throughout on‑call duty.
Key Performance Indicators (KPI):
Response time to tenant emergencies
Number of issues resolved without contractor escalation
Tenant satisfaction and feedback
Accuracy and completeness of incident reports
Compliance with safety procedures

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You will drive local procurement initiatives that make a real impact on operational excellence and sustainable outcomes. You will lead key procurement projects, craft market documentation, evaluate bids, and build strong relationships with suppliers to deliver efficient, compliant, and high-value results. Your work will shape supplier development, strengthen community engagement, and enhance operational performance across the site.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support PNG and Lihirian procurement activities, including running RFPs, negotiating with suppliers, and managing commercial disputes.
Support site stakeholders and the Category Management teams to identify and develop local procurement opportunities.
Ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and company policies, including health, safety, environmental, ESG, and community engagement standards.
Build supplier capability through coaching, advisory documents, and ongoing support.
Contribute to the Local Procurement Plan and reporting, providing insights to improve processes and outcomes.
Present procurement outcomes to managers and other stakeholders, fostering collaboration and transparency.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Procurement, or related field is desirable.
Proven experience in procurement and supplier capacity building, ideally in a mining environment.
Skilled in supplier negotiations, both to achieve great contract value and resolving contract related disputes
Competence in SAP, Fieldglass and Ariba is desirable.
Excellent communication, negotiation, public speaking, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong cultural awareness, particularly in engaging with Lihirian communities and local businesses.
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with a focus on building long-term relationships and delivering value.
Ability to work independently as a motivated self-starter while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will engage with internal stakeholders including team leads, superintendents, and category management teams, as well as external stakeholders such as local suppliers and government officials. You will operate in a dynamic, collaborative environment, leading procurement activities that are critical to site performance and community impact.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on site operations while developing your career in a global mining environment. You will work with a team that values collaboration, innovation, and cultural awareness, and you will contribute to sustainable, ethical procurement practices that support local communities and operational excellence.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Job Summary:
NextGen Technology Limited is seeking a highly skilled and proactive IT Support Officer with a strong background in domain hosting to join our team.
The ideal candidate will provide technical assistance and customer support related to domain configuration, email setup, server security, and web hosting management. This role requires experience in DNS management, WHM/cPanel environments, and troubleshooting deliverability issues. Experience with Microsoft 365 setup and basic website development are strong pluses.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide email and technical support for clients experiencing issues related to hosting, domain services, and email configuration.
Configure and manage domain name settings, including DNS records (A, MX,CNAME, TXT, etc.), registrar setup, and name servers.
Troubleshoot and resolve email delivery issues, spam problems, and perform diagnostics using tools such as mail logs, DNS lookups, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and SMTP traces.
Perform hosting-related tasks such as creating and managing hosting accounts via WHM/cPanel, backups, resource monitoring, and server optimization.
Implement and maintain server security best practices including firewall configuration, SSL installation, malware protection, and intrusion detection.
Regularly monitor servers for performance, uptime, and security vulnerabilities.
Assist with Microsoft 365 setup and migration, including DNS configuration, tenant setup, and mail flow.
Assist with website creation or migration tasks when needed (WordPress or static HTML websites preferred).
Document procedures, configurations, and resolutions for internal and client reference.
Liaise with third-party providers (registrars, cloud vendors) as needed to resolve issues efficiently.
Requirements:
Technical Skills:
Strong knowledge of domain registration and DNS configuration.
Experience with email protocols (IMAP, POP3, SMTP) and tools to test deliverability.
Proficiency in WHM, cPanel, and other web hosting control panels.
Understanding of SPF, DKIM, DMARC, SSL, and general web/email security concepts.
Hands-on experience with server hardening, firewalls, and security monitoring tools.
Basic web development or website management skills (HTML/CSS, WordPress,etc.) is a plus.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online, DNS setup, migration) is a plus.
Soft Skills:
Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Strong communication skills for client-facing support.

Work with contractors and mechanical staff to maintain Generators so they are in good working order.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.
Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment and machines.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.
Be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.

Minimum Grades 10 or above.
Must be a Tradesman with NEA certification.
Must have experience in High Voltage Switching and Power Station Operation and Maintenance.
A certified electrician with 5 years’ work experience in a mining environment.

Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.

Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.

Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods

Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a School to Mine (STM) Teacher, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of young Lihirians. Through the delivery of high-quality education aligned to the Australian and PNG Curriculum, you will empower students with the skills, confidence and aspirations needed to succeed, whether in further education, employment or within the business.
Focusing on High School English, Humanities and Social Sciences, you will bring learning to life, preparing students and young adults to transition successfully from school to meaningful careers. Your work will directly contribute to nurturing local talent and strengthening education outcomes across Lihir.
As part of our team, you will
Create Safe and Supportive Learning Environments
– Provide social and pastoral care by actively listening to student concerns and responding in accordance with school policies. Maintain a strong focus on student wellbeing and safety, including completing first aid training, monitoring student behaviour and use of school equipment, and contributing to OHS risk management by identifying hazards, assessing risks, implementing mitigation strategies, and investigating/reporting incidents.
Learning Curriculum Delivery
– Prepare and deliver engaging subject material aligned to approved curriculum frameworks. Conduct research to support lesson preparation, design well-structured lesson plans, and create flexible, intellectually challenging learning experiences that cater to diverse learners.
Extra-Curricular Learning
– Enhance the broader student experience by contributing to learning beyond the formal curriculum. Design and support programs and initiatives that broaden engagement, build capability and encourage participation.
Assessment and Recording of Progress – Evaluate student performance, identify individual learning needs, and maintain accurate assessment records. Communicate outcomes effectively with students and the school administration team in accordance with assessment and reporting policies.
Co-Curricular Participation
– Actively participate in school co-curricular activities as directed by the Principal and Deputy Principal (STM), supporting a holistic educational environment.
Professional Representation and Compliance
– Operate in accordance with the standards and expectations of Newmont Corporation, demonstrating due diligence when representing Lihir International School and the School to Mine Campus. Uphold the values of both Newmont and the school community at all times.
Contribution to Professional Teams
– Establish and implement effective personal work practices to meet goals and priorities. Collaborate closely with STM and LIS teachers, Newmont personnel and other stakeholders to ensure strong team performance. Participate in school and STM meetings and represent the school at relevant internal and external functions.
Other Duties
– Perform additional responsibilities as assigned by the Principal and Deputy Principal, School to Mine.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Tertiary qualification in Education (Bachelor level or higher).
Accredited High School Teacher with Teacher Registration.
Specialisation in English, Humanities or Social Sciences (preferred).
Relevant teaching work experience (essential), particularly within secondary education.
Excellent understanding of current learning theory principles, practices and methodologies.
Excellent understanding of individual and group learning principles, approaches and delivery methods.
Experience working with secondary students; experience with young adults highly desirable.
Adult Education experience, including distance/flexible learning programs (advantageous).
Strong understanding of Australian and PNG Curriculum frameworks.
Ability to plan, deliver and continuously improve structured education programs.
Excellent communication, public speaking and interpersonal skills.
Confident use of Microsoft Office Suite, particularly PowerPoint.
Technically capable and data-literate, with the ability to analyse educational outcomes.
Self-motivated, adaptable and able to take initiative.
Strong teamwork capability and ability to foster inclusive, collaborative environments
Willingness to actively contribute to extra-curricular activities and broader school initiatives.
Current First Aid Certificate (desirable).
We recognise that no candidate will meet every requirement. If you are a passionate, capable educator with the ability to grow into the role, we encourage you to apply.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will be based on Lihir, collaborating closely with colleagues at Lihir International School and the School to Mine Campus. You’ll work within a supportive, professional team that values continuous learning, safety and collaboration.
This is a dynamic, evolving program. You will have the opportunity not only to deliver established modules, but also to enhance and refine them — conducting research, introducing improvements and helping shape the future direction of STM programs.
You will operate in a culturally rich and community-focused environment where your contribution has visible and lasting impact.
Why Join Newmont
Through the School to Mine initiative, Newmont invests in education and local capability building ensuring that future generations are equipped to thrive.
When you join us, you will:
Contribute to a program with genuine community impact.
Be part of a global organisation with strong safety and professional standards.
Work in a collaborative and values-driven culture.
Develop professionally within a respected international company.
Help shape the future of education and employment pathways on Lihir.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Director Finance – Site Business, you will play a pivotal leadership role in overseeing site financial performance to strengthen decision-making and deliver sustainable business outcomes. You will drive operating cost discipline and capital efficiency while ensuring the site meets its financial commitments. Your leadership will directly influence profitability, operational performance, inventory optimisation, and long-term value creation.
About the Role
Reporting to Head, Finance - Africa Asia Pacific you will oversee site financial performance to strengthen decision-making, and in this role you will:
Drive
annual business planning, cost management, variance analysis, and long-term budgeting to support profitable operations.
Lead
the development of Life of Mine (LOM) budgets and deliver accurate monthly and quarterly forecasts in line with corporate requirements.
Analyse
financial performance, identify key cost drivers, and provide actionable recommendations for cost reduction and capital optimisation.
Oversee
site reporting of operating costs and capital expenditure to regional leadership, including detailed variance analysis.
Establish and optimise
financial systems and processes to strengthen economic modelling and business decision-making.
Ensure
strong SOX compliance, internal controls, and adherence to accounting standards.
Embed
an Always Safe culture aligned with Newmont’s safety strategy.
Lead and mentor
a high-performing finance team, building capability, succession strength, and an inclusive, collaborative culture.
About You
You are a commercially astute leader with a strong background in mining operations and a proven ability to influence performance outcomes at site level. You bring strategic thinking, strong governance knowledge, and the leadership capability to drive financial discipline while partnering effectively with operational stakeholders.
To be successful in this role, you will have:
Proven mining industry experience, preferably within a site-based environment.
Tertiary qualification in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline.
Financial management experience within mining operations, including advanced proficiency in cost and capital management.
Experience leading diverse teams and driving performance across cross-functional environments.
A strong understanding of the financial metrics that underpin site performance and profitability.
Membership in a professional accounting or finance body is desirable.
Demonstrated experience leading diverse teams and influencing senior stakeholders.
Knowledge of US GAAP, SOX compliance, and internal control frameworks.
Advanced financial modelling, budgeting, and forecasting expertise.
Strong ERP proficiency (e.g., SAP) and familiarity with business planning systems.
Ability to analyse complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to non-financial stakeholders.
Strong commercial acumen and negotiation capability.
Proven ability to identify and implement process improvements and drive change.
Advanced verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to non-financial stakeholders.
Collaborative leadership style that fosters accountability, development, and inclusivity.
Your work environment
You will be a key member of the Site Leadership Team, partnering closely with operational leaders, regional finance teams, corporate supply chain, and external stakeholders including contractors and suppliers. This role operates at the intersection of strategy and execution, providing visibility across financial operations, and long-term planning. Safety, transparency, and continuous improvement underpin everything we do.
This is a full-time, two-year fixed-term residential role on a 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life. You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will join a global leader in gold mining with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and operational excellence. You will be empowered to influence strategic decisions, lead meaningful change, and contribute to long-term value creation for our people, communities, and shareholders. We foster a culture where accountability, collaboration, and innovation drive success.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

This position supports the Community Infrastructure & Asset Delivery Standard under the Social Performance Management System (SPMS) and contributes to the material issue of Community Infrastructure & Access.
Key Accountabilities
This role supports the delivery of community infrastructure projects across the mine life cycle, ensuring outcomes are sustainable and beneficial beyond mine operations.
Project Supervision & Delivery:
Supervise day-to-day site activities, contractors and community labour to ensure construction projects meet technical specifications, schedules and budgets.
Leadership & Workforce Coordination:
Supervise project assistants, site supervisors and community labourers; prepare weekly work plans and schedules aligned with overall project timelines; provide on-the-job technical guidance and capacity building to local workers.
Safety, Quality & Compliance:
Monitor contractor performance, safety and workmanship to ensure compliance with site safety requirements, engineering standards and approved designs.
Technical Implementation & Reporting:
Implement SOPs and workflows under the Community Infrastructure & Asset Delivery Standard; monitor material usage and site-level budget performance; maintain accurate daily logs, attendance records and progress reports.
Collaboration & Integration:
Coordinate with Social Development, Agriculture Projects and Business Development teams to align infrastructure delivery with broader community programs and local contractor participation.
Stakeholder & Government Engagement:
Interface with local government engineers, inspectors and relevant authorities to ensure regulatory compliance and technical approvals.
Commitments & Expectations Management:
Deliver infrastructure commitments under the MOA and local development agreements; manage community expectations through clear communication on project scope, timelines and standards; provide transparent updates during construction and communicate changes as required.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring practical construction supervision experience and the ability to work effectively with contractors and local communities.
You will also demonstrate:
• Diploma or degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management or a related discipline
• At least 5 years of experience supervising infrastructure or construction projects, preferably in PNG or rural development contexts (experience with Community Projects is highly regarded)
• Experience implementing or monitoring compliance with site safety policies in construction or mining environments
• Experience using AutoCAD, Civil Cad and MS Project
• Sound understanding of Occupational Health & Safety principles, risk assessments and safe work procedures
• Proven ability to manage contractors, community labour and site-level reporting
• Strong record-keeping and project monitoring skills
• Proficiency in Tok Pisin and English (local dialects advantageous)
• PNG Driver’s Licence (mandatory)
Life at K92

Applications must be submitted through the Palladium application portal only. Applications submitted through other methods will not be considered.
Please find the application link at:
https://palladium.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/2/home/requisition/24789?c=palladium
Fixed term contract up to 30 June 2027
Salary range: K140,000 – K160,000
Based in Port Moresby
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 4,000 employees operating in 90-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
The Program
The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.
The program aligns with the broader goals of the
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasizes locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.
The Role
As MEL Senior Coordinator you will be responsible for supporting the Senior MEL Manager and MEL Lead in the development, implementation, monitoring, and period review and strengthening of the SWLT MEL Framework and system.
The
Senior MEL Coordinator
will be required to take leadership of several components of the SWLT MEL system. These will include:
Leading the collection, quality assurance and management of program data to support timely, accurate reporting.
Drafting MEL activity reports and contributing to key sections of client deliverables.
Preparing research outputs including case studies, learning notes and good practice summaries.
Facilitating program MEL processes such as quarterly, six‑monthly and annual reviews, reflections and learning sessions.
Supporting stakeholder consultations and feedback processes to inform adaptive, high‑quality programming.
Developing and maintaining MEL tools and templates, ensuring consistent use and ongoing improvements across the program.
Providing administrative and technical support for MEL-related training and capacity building for SWLT staff and partners.
Contributing to DFAT reporting requirements, GEDSI objectives, safeguarding standards, climate‑friendly practices, and SWLT’s learning and improvement culture.
About you
You will have experience in:
Supporting the development, implementation, review, and strengthening of monitoring, evaluation and learning systems, including MEL frameworks, plans, tools, and templates
Knowledge and understanding of DFAT MEL Standards and/or other donor-funded program monitoring and evaluation systems in a development context
Contributing high quality inputs to internal and external program reporting
Data collection, quality assurance, analysis, interpretation, and representation
Good research, analytical, and problem-solving skills
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion
As a MEL practitioner, demonstrate commitment to excellence and self-improvement
An understanding of tertiary and vocational education in the Pacific Islands context, particularly within PNG provincial environments would be a benefit but is not mandatory
Strong relationship skills and ability to work well with a diverse group of team members and other stakeholders
Demonstrated experience to principles or values of inclusion, positivity and flexibility.
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.
To Apply
Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position.

11.59pm AEST

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Database & GIS Superintendent and will oversee management of all data and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) files emanating from the exploration teams activities.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Maintain safety incident records and manage geological databases.
Validate and QA/QC all field and drill data; compile weekly, monthly, and drill grade reports.
Create maps, tables, and 3D geological models for reporting and interpretation.
Prepare internal and statutory reports, forecasts, and SOPs.
Ensure accurate core logging, sampling, and adherence to QA/QC protocols.
Conduct regular database checks and monitor drilling productivity.
Train and mentor geologists and technicians on data entry, validation, and SOPs.
Promote high-performance culture and provide feedback on team performance.
Support talent development and succession planning.
Review historical data and update geological interpretations.
Participate in target reviews, ranking, and planning exploration programs.
Conduct technical reviews with senior geologists and assist in report compilation.
Promote and enforce a safe work culture and legal compliance.
Ensure drilling and sampling are conducted safely and competently.
Maintain housekeeping and uphold HSE standards.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Bachelor’s Degree in Geology (Preferable), Geophysics or Geoscience or Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
10+ years relevant exploration, mining or GIS work experience essential.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite, including Access and SQL Database systems software. Proficiency in GIS software. The ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

jobs.description:
Heavy Duty Dump Truck Driver Job Description
We are seeking a skilled and safety-conscious Heavy Duty Dump Truck Driver to join our dynamic construction and materials transport team. In this vital role, you will be the key link in our supply chain, ensuring the timely and secure delivery of essential materials that keep our projects moving forward. The ideal candidate is a reliable professional with a strong work ethic, exceptional driving skills, and a steadfast commitment to safety protocols and equipment care.
Position Overview
As a Heavy-Duty Dump Truck Driver, your primary mission is to operate and maintain heavy-duty dump trucks to transport bulk materials such as gravel, sand, topsoil, asphalt, and construction debris to and from various job sites. You will work in a fast-paced environment, often navigating challenging terrain and tight spaces, while coordinating closely with site supervisors and dispatchers to optimize delivery schedules and maintain project efficiency.
Reporting to:
Fleets Coordinator
Key Responsibilities & Duties
Daily Operations & Driving
Safely operate a heavy-duty dump truck to transport loose materials to designated locations.
Manoeuvre and position the vehicle for efficient loading and unloading at pits, quarries, and construction sites.
Navigate public roads and private job sites, adhering to all traffic laws and on-site safety rules.
Perform controlled dumping of materials in specified areas as directed by site personnel.
Coordinate with loaders, excavators, and ground crew to ensure safe and accurate loading/unloading cycles.
Vehicle Maintenance & Safety
Conduct thorough pre-trip and post-trip inspections of the vehicle, including brakes, tires, lights, hydraulics, and fluid levels.
Complete mandatory Driver Vehicle Inspection Reports (DVIR) and report any mechanical defects or safety issues immediately.
Perform basic maintenance tasks such as cleaning the truck, checking and adding fluids, and greasing fittings.
Secure all loads properly to prevent spillage during transit.
Maintain a clean and organized cab and logbook.
Site Coordination & Compliance
Communicate effectively with dispatchers and site supervisors via radio or mobile device.
Follow detailed delivery instructions and site-specific safety plans.
Ensure all documentation, including delivery tickets and hours-of-service logs, is accurately completed and submitted.
Represent the company professionally in all interactions with clients and the public.
Qualifications & Requirements
Mandatory Requirements
Valid required licence with a clean driving record.
Minimum of 5-7 years of verifiable experience operating heavy-duty dump trucks or similar commercial vehicles.
Current Medical Examiner's Certificate.
Strong knowledge of RTA regulations and road safety rules.
Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screen and background check.
Preferred Skills & Experience
Experience hauling construction materials in a live-bottom, end-dump, or transfer dump configuration.
Familiarity with operating in active construction zones and uneven terrain.
Basic mechanical aptitude for performing minor roadside repairs and troubleshooting.
Proven record of safety and reliability.
Physical Demands & Work Environment
This role is physically demanding and requires working in all weather conditions. Candidates must be able to:
Sit for extended periods and climb in and out of a tall truck cab repeatedly.
Perform physical tasks such as tarping loads, connecting/disconnecting trailer lines, and minor clean-up.
Work variable hours, including early mornings, overtime, and occasional weekends as project demands require.
Wear all required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety vest, steel-toe boots, and glasses.
What We Offer
Competitive remuneration package
Opportunity to contribute to workforce capability development
Professional and respectful working environment
Opportunity to support systems strengthening within a growing national company

Location: Port Moresby

Overview:
T.E.(PNG) Limited is seeking an experienced Accountant responsible for maintaining accurate financial records, ensuring compliance with Papua New Guinea taxation and statutory requirements, and supporting management through timely financial reporting. The role requires hands-on accounting work, including Accounts Payable (AP), Accounts Receivable, Bank reconciliations, GST Reconciliation, Profit & Loss (P&L), Balance Sheet preparation, and effective use of the Odoo ERP system.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Financial Accounting & Reporting
Prepare monthly Profit & Loss Statements and Balance Sheets
Maintain accurate general ledger records
Perform month-end and year-end closing activities
Ensure all financial transactions are properly recorded in Odoo
Assist in preparation of financial reports for Management
Accounts Payable (AP) & Accounts Receivable (AR)
Process supplier invoices accurately and on time
Match invoices to purchase orders and delivery notes
Prepare payment schedules and process payments
Manage customer invoicing and follow up on outstanding receivables
Reconcile supplier and customer accounts
Reconciliations

Reconcile cash, EFTPOS, and other payment systems
Reconcile GST control accounts
Reconcile inventory, payroll, and inter-company accounts as required
Taxation & Statutory Compliance (PNG)

Ensure correct GST treatment on transactions
Assist with salary & wages tax, superannuation, and statutory deductions
Support audits, inspections, and information requests from authorities
Ensure compliance with PNG labour, tax, and financial regulations

Ensure accuracy of data entered into Odoo

Support other departments in correct system usage where required
Internal Controls & Support

Provide support during audits and financial reviews

Proven experience in:

Experience with audits and compliance reporting
Experience in inventory or project-based accounting

High level of integrity and confidentiality

Parts Interpreter
(The detail-focused kind — the ones who get the right part, the first time)

Kokopo
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Behind every vehicle on the road is a parts operation that has to be accurate, efficient, and responsive. When the right part is supplied quickly, workshops run smoothly and customers stay loyal.
We’re looking for a capable Parts Interpreter to join our Kokopo team.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be the link between the workshop, the customer, and the warehouse.
Your role is to correctly identify, source, and supply parts for service jobs, retail customers, and trade clients. That means interpreting parts using catalogues and systems, checking availability, preparing quotes, processing orders, and ensuring accurate documentation.
You’ll work closely with technicians to confirm specifications and avoid errors. You’ll liaise with suppliers when required, follow up backorders, and keep customers informed. Accuracy is critical — one incorrect part can delay a job, increase costs, and damage trust.
You’ll also support stock control processes, assist with inventory management, and help maintain an organised and professional parts counter environment.
Speed matters. Accuracy matters more.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone organised, technically minded, and confident communicating with both workshop staff and customers.
You’re comfortable using parts catalogues and computer systems. You pay attention to detail. You double-check part numbers. You don’t guess.
Experience in automotive parts interpretation is strongly preferred, particularly within dealership or branded environments. However, strong automotive knowledge, discipline, and willingness to learn will also be considered.
If a technician asks for a part — you confirm it properly.
If stock is low — you flag it early.
If a customer needs clarity — you explain it clearly.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is a national business with established brands, structured systems, and long-term investment in the PNG market.
Safety, accuracy, and professionalism are taken seriously. Performance is recognised, and capable operators have room to grow.
If you want a role where technical knowledge, accuracy, and professionalism are valued — this is it.

jobs.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as Tutor – Forest Conservation within the Department of Forestry, School of Natural Resources.
The position is based at the Vudal Campus, East New Britain Province, and supports teaching, applied research, and community engagement activities in forest conservation and sustainable forest management. The role contributes to curriculum delivery, student supervision, and field-based learning aligned with Papua New Guinea’s environmental and conservation priorities.
The appointee will report directly to the Head of Department, Forestry.
Key Responsibilities
Deliver lectures, tutorials, and practical sessions in Forest Conservation and related subjects.
Supervise student assignments, projects, and field-based learning activities.
Assist in the development and review of teaching materials, course outlines, and assessment tools.
Participate in applied research activities in forest ecology, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable forest management.
Support student involvement in research and field studies.
Contribute to community engagement and extension activities, working with local communities, government agencies, and NGOs.
Assist with departmental planning, reporting, quality assurance, and accreditation-related activities.
Maintain forestry tools, equipment, and teaching facilities used in practical training.
Prepare basic technical reports and maintain records of field and teaching activities.
Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety standards during field and laboratory work.
Perform other duties as reasonably directed by the immediate supervisor.
Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in forestry, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline from a recognised institution (master’s degree desirable).
Demonstrated knowledge of forest conservation, ecology, and sustainable forest management practices.
Teaching experience at tertiary or secondary level will be an advantage.
Strong interest in applied research and conservation studies, with basic research and analytical skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with students, staff, and external partners.
Commitment to capacity building, community development, and sustainable forestry in Papua New Guinea.
Willingness to work in diverse and field-based environments, including remote locations.
High standards of integrity, professionalism, and ethical conduct.

(plus applicable allowances and benefits)
