jobs.title: Lead Agreements Implementation
jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are looking for a dynamic Lead – Agreements Implementation to join our Social Performance Team on Lihir Island, PNG. This exciting opportunity is a residential role on an attractive 5:2 roster.
Reporting directly to the Director of Social Performance Lihir, the Lead - Agreements Implementation will manage community agreement obligations and facilitating agreements between Newmont and the host communities of Lihir Island. This role is essential for maintaining Newmont’s social license to operate, fostering sustainable community and mine development, and ensuring mutual benefits for all parties involved.
As part of our team, you will
Lead community engagement initiatives to reinforce Newmont’s social license, gain community and government support, and strengthen relations.
Oversee and coordinate the implementation and tracking of community agreement obligations, addressing challenges to achieve sustainable and long-term benefits for both the community and Newmont’s operations.
Manage the execution and ongoing support of the Mine Management Plans (MMP) across accountable areas of Lihir Island, ensuring all obligations are fulfilled.
Serve as the secretariat for the Lihir Interim Agreement Committee (IIA), ensuring effective and transparent committee functions.
Oversee the resolution of outstanding issues from past agreements by monitoring commitments, engaging stakeholders, developing action plans, and ensuring transparent communication and compliance.
Build trust-based relationships with community leaders and stakeholders, foster collaborative partnerships, and integrate community perspectives into decision-making.
Ensure transparency and accountability through open communication and systematic reporting in line with Newmont’s ethical and sustainable practices.
Promote a collaborative culture within the Social Performance team to advance strategic initiatives and achieve positive outcomes for the Lihir host communities.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will be a strategic and business-savvy professional with proven experience in bridging business objectives and community interests. You will have a track record of managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading cross-functional teams, and influencing outcomes to achieve sustainable results.
You will also bring:
Tertiary qualifications in stakeholder engagement, planning, management, or commercial (essential).
Experience in cost management, account reconciliation, and budgeting.
PNG National Driver’s License (essential).
Actively promote and demonstrate a strong safety culture, leading by example to prioritize the well-being of all stakeholders.
Establish trust-based relationships with host communities and stakeholders to support mutual benefits and sustainable engagement.
Experience facilitating complex multi-party negotiations with landowners.
Ability to find middle ground between business interests and community needs.
Knowledge of traditional negotiation protocols in PNG communities.
Ability to facilitate resolution of historical grievances.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and collaborate effectively to achieve results.
Proficiency in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated success in developing team capacity and fostering growth.
Proficiency in the MS Office suite, with strong planning, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.
Excellent organisational and time management skills to meet deadlines and maintain high-quality standards.
Active listening, rapport-building, and conflict resolution abilities to effectively handle diverse stakeholder interactions.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a residential 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life. You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will make a tangible difference in the lives of communities while contributing to one of the world’s leading gold mining operations. You will join a supportive, high-performing team, with opportunities for professional growth, leadership development, and the chance to deliver sustainable outcomes that matter.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 37600 before the advertised closing date: 5 March 2026.

About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The
Quality Control Officer
is responsible for monitoring, maintaining, and continually improving the laboratory’s Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure the laboratory demonstrates competence and operates consistently in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements.
Essential Duties
QMS Maintenance & Document Control
Maintain the laboratory’s Quality Manual, ensuring all policies reflect current operations and ISO 17025 requirements.
Manage the Document Control System: Ensure all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), forms, and work instructions are current, and accessible to staff.
Archive obsolete documents and ensure strict version control to prevent the use of invalid procedures.
Prepare and provide weekly summaries on Labs compliance to the management system to lab management.
Internal Audits & Compliance
Develop and execute the Annual Internal Audit Schedule covering all elements of the management and technical requirements.
Conduct vertical and horizontal audits to verify compliance with methods and standards.
Non-Conformance & Corrective Action (CAPA)
Lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations for all non-conformances and customer complaints.
Monitor Corrective and Preventive Actions to ensure they are implemented effectively and verify their long-term effectiveness.
Equipment & Metrology
Oversee the equipment master list, ensuring all critical equipment is calibrated by ISO 17025 accredited providers (metrological traceability).
Review calibration certificates for compliance with required specifications before equipment is returned to service.
Ensure intermediate checks (e.g., balance verifications, pipette checks) are performed and recorded as scheduled.
Training & Experience
A commitment to Safety
Minimum 2–3 years of experience working within an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory environment.
Technical Knowledge: Strong understanding of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standards, particularly regarding risk-based thinking and impartiality.
Formal Internal Auditor Training certificate (based on ISO 19011).
Experience with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS).
Statistical analysis skills

jobs.description:
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG national candidates only
Fixed term contract up to three years
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program will work closely with TVET stakeholders and select technical colleges to grow the number of skilled individuals with industry relevant skills.
This Opportunity
As
Procurement Manager
you will be responsible for leading on all procurement activities for the program, ensuring it is conducted in accordance with company and client compliance requirements and is delivered with considerations towards value-for-money, localisation and other program and government objectives.
This will include:
Planning, directing and coordinating all procurement activities in compliance with the
Australian Commonwealth Procurement Rules (CPR’s)
, DFAT
Value for Money
principles, and Palladium procurement and due diligence standards.
Advising management on procurement strategies and sourcing options. Managing the full procurement cycle, including planning, market engagement, solicitation, evaluation, contracting and mobilisation. Procurement may range from simple three quote evaluations to complex competitive tender processes, requiring in-depth preparation and evaluation.
Integrating social procurement principles into all sourcing activities by prioritising suppliers that deliver measurable social, economic and environmental benefits to local businesses, women, youth owned enterprises, people with disability and marginalised groups
Developing and maintaining procurement plans, schedules and templates, and ensuring all procurement documentation—including due diligence records, vendor/contractor files, contract registers and tracking tools—is complete, accurate, auditable, up to date, and fully compliant with DFAT and Palladium requirements.
Reviewing procurement requests to ensure clarity, accuracy, and alignment with SWLT objectives, and support specification and scope development.
Preparing bidding documents (RFQs, RFPs) and leading tender evaluations to ensure transparent bid analysis. Negotiating contracts, pricing and terms with suppliers.
Managing vendor performance to support high‑quality delivery and value‑for‑money outcomes and maintain an up‑to‑date vendor database with performance tracking and quality assurance.
Providing regular reports on procurement progress, risks, timelines and delivery status, including up-to-date strategic advice to senior management.
Developing and maintaining an approved supplier database. Conducting supplier performance evaluations.
Identifying and mitigating procurement risks, escalating critical issues—including conflicts of interest, integrity concerns or suspected fraud—as required, and promote ethical, transparent procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Understanding and contributing to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.
Adhering to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
Championing ethical procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Modelling, contributing to and supporting an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts, building procurement capability across the SWLT team through coaching, guidance and practical support.
Supporting and upholding the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as integrating environmental sustainability considerations into procurement decisions, including climate‑friendly options and reduced resource use.
Contributing to the implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles
[1]
are embedded within program delivery.
About you
You will have experience in:
Procurement in PNG, ideally within DFAT‑funded or donor‑funded development programs
A strong understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules, DFAT procurement requirements and PNG Government procurement processes.
Managing full procurement cycles including complex tenders.
Using strong analytical thinking and proactive problem solving.
Working with suppliers and stakeholders across PNG, including provincial contexts.
An understanding of tertiary and vocational education and training development in the Pacific Islands context is desirable.
Excellent organisational and computer skills especially with MS Word and Excel.
Operate with high levels of integrity, consistent with the intent of
DFAT’s Ethics, Integrity and Professional Standards Policy Manual.
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Officer Emergency Response will coordinate the preparation, execution, and improvement of emergency response plans and procedures including emergency drills and compliance.
Essential Duties
Support in the preparation and execution of emergency response plans and procedures, ensuring alignment with site-specific needs and regulatory requirements.
Provides coordination and technical guidance to Voluntary ERT members.
Perform regular inspections and maintenance checks of emergency response equipment.
Engage in emergency drills and simulations, helping to prepare and conduct these exercises and deliver feedback for continuous improvement
Provides coordination and guidance for ERT training activities.
Training & Experience
A personal commitment to Safety
Certification in fire and rescue, medical response or other emergency response discipline
Industry recognized emergency response systems, standards and processes
Relevant regulations and compliance requirements
Communication and Influencing skills
Risk Management processes
Emergency incident management
Competent proficiency in implementing occupational emergency response systems
Foundational proficiency in managing and applying operational risk management processes
Foundational proficiency in implementing emergency response standards, best-fit practices, monitoring processes, regulatory compliance
Advanced proficiency in executing emergency response activities
Foundational commercial skills: budgets, forecasting, planning, analysis, reporting and communicating result
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program will work closely with TVET stakeholders and select technical colleges to grow the number of skilled individuals with industry relevant skills.
This Opportunity
As
Senior Project Coordinator
you will be responsible for providing cross pillar support to manage the implementation and delivery of a range of SWLT activities under the direction of the senior leadership team and in-consultation with technical advisers and partners.
You will provide flexible and adaptive project management support to technical leads across policy reform and advisory activities across the TVET and skills system. Activities will cover a diverse portfolio of technical assistance including grants, infrastructure, organisational capacity assessments, labour market analysis, gender and inclusion work, safeguards and sector coordination activities.
The Senior Project Coordinator will work under an agile reporting framework and will report to different technical leads or members of the senior leadership team at different times, depending on activity requirements.
This will include:
Support technical leads in engagement with Government of PNG counterparts, DFAT, technical partners and consultants to support activity design, consultation, and delivery.
Lead and support the preparation of Concept Notes, Terms of Reference, briefing papers, draft deliverables and other outputs from early scoping through drafting, review, approval, and completion.
Lead and maintain program trackers, delivery schedules, and workplans to support effective decision-making.
Identify delivery risks and bottlenecks across activities and proactively support mitigation actions with technical leads.
Monitor alignment between approved budgets, scopes of work, and delivery progress across multiple activities.
Support preparation and follow-up for steering committees, technical advisory groups, coordination forums, workshops, and consultations.
Work with the operations focal points including SWLT Procurement and Finance Managers on activity procurement processes including scoping, scheduling and documentation.
Assist the technical leads and Operations Senior Coordinator with managing consultants and partners, including contract milestones, deliverable tracking, and reporting requirements.
Contribute to monitoring and reporting against program outputs, priorities, and agreed indicators, including dashboard and tracker inputs as required.
Provide responsive, ad‑hoc program management and coordination support as priorities shift, new requests emerge, or activities are brought forward or deferred.
Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.
Ensure adherence to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
Contribute to office learning culture by seeking out knowledge, sharing fresh perspectives and ideas, and taking initiative in problem-solving.
Support SWLT to be climate friendly by thinking about and implementing ways to reduce waste and use environmental practices.
Understand and work in line with SWLT principles at all times.
About you
You will have demonstrated experience in:
Strong program management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple activities at the same time and at different stages, and with varying stakeholders
Proven ability to manage complex workplans and trackers that maintain oversight of activity performance.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders and act as a trusted coordination point across diverse audiences
Demonstrated understanding of MEL tools underpinning results monitoring frameworks
A practical understanding of procurement processes and financial management, including an ability to understand and analyse activity budgets
Capacity to support adaptive management, responding to shifting priorities and changes in direction
Strong skills in writing, reviewing, and being able to interpret and synthesise information readily
High level of organisation, initiative and self-management and the ability to work across priority tasks and adhoc requests while also working collaboratively with senior, technical staff and driving progress
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
Please note:
This role is being advertised early in the program’s inception phase. Some aspects of the role may be revised before or shortly after commencement. Any changes will be discussed and agreed upon between Palladium and the successful candidate.

jobs.description:
LANDS OFFICER
Hargy Oil Palms Limited (HOPL) is an Oil Palm plantation company based in Bialla, West New Britain Province. A remote location situated approximately 2 and half hours’ drive east of Kimbe town.
HOPL currently has a vacancy for a suitably qualified and experienced Lands Officer who will join its General Administration Department and deliver support services to HOPL, its Oil Palm Growers and stakeholders.
Primary Objectives:
Reporting to the Lands Manager, the Lands Officer will be required to provide support to the Small Holder Oil Palm growers and facilitate the dissemination of land instruments related to the acquisition and granting of state leases and where possible assist in the processing of land applications for Oil palm land settlement schemes and Village Oil Palm blocks. The role will also be required to assist in the maintenance and registration of any Oil Palm extension projects for the HOPL and ensure that all statutory requirements are fully ascertained for the company under the RSPO, free, prior informed consent process.
Competencies
To perform the job successfully, it is expected that the applicant can demonstrate the following competencies:
Arrange community engagement message tracks for Free, Prior and Informed consent for land acquisition expansion projects.
Assist in the facilitation and formation of ILGs to ensure that all have proper constitutions and work closely with the district commerce officers to establishing solid business practices for the registered groups.
To facilitate the process of registration of all Lease-Leaseback land dealings involving ILGs desirable in new Oil Palm development projects and guide them on the rights and obligations conversant with the laws of PNG.
Able to assist in the delivery of alternate dispute resolution mechanism approaches where there is dispute over ownership of land with the support from the relevant government agencies.
Work with Smallholder Extension services officers and the OPIC to ensure that Clan Land Use Agreements (CLUA for all Village Oil Palm blocks are appropriately registered using the FPIC process.
Assist in the preparation and delivery of awareness on important land matters to the Bialla Smallholder Oil Palm growers.
Be responsible for the lodgement of all land title instruments at the National Department of Lands, the WNB Provincial Lands Division and other relevant government authorities.
Follow up with Provincial lands division and the National Department of lands and other relevant authorities to ensure that documentation related to the granting of state leases and any land applications are processed in a timely manner.
Review and implement Standard Operating Procedures for the land payment system, Lease-Leaseback and other internal land administrative matters.
Technical knowledge on the use of a hand-held GPS in undertaking GPS surveys to identify land boundaries and any conflicting or overlapping areas.
Willing to live and work in a remote area or setting.
Any other relevant duties as required.
Education and Background
Degree in Land Studies or related with 2-5 years of job experience in a similar role.
Experience in ADR techniques, deep understanding of clan structures and the social norms of West New Britain Province.
Some experience in the formulation of message tracks, delivery of community engagement consultations in public meetings, and public speaking.
Knowledgeable of the Land Act 1996, Customary Land Registration Act, RSPO rules and regulations and other related laws of PNG
Class 3 drivers Licence desirable.

•             Crushing and ore handling system
•             Comminution circuit comprising the SAG and Ball mills and gravity concentrator
•             Flotation circuit
•             Thickening and filtration circuits
•             Concentrate loading
The Processing plant operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.

Machinery licences including loader, skid steer, telehandler (desirable)

High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation

Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.

The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are in one of the largest business schools in the country and offer degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and future citizens of Papua New Guinea.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learned skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
Position Overview:
The Assistant Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Teaching and Learning:
Assist in preparing and delivering lectures, tutorials, and workshops in Business Management and related subjects.
Facilitate interactive learning experiences to engage students and enhance their understanding of core business concepts.
Develop teaching materials, lesson plans, and assessment tools in collaboration with senior lecturers.
2. Curriculum Development:
Support the development and periodic review of the Business Management curriculum to ensure it meets industry and academic standards.
Integrate contemporary business practices, case studies, and trends into teaching content.
3. Student Support:
Provide academic guidance and mentoring to students to help them achieve their learning objectives.
Assess and evaluate students’ performance through assignments, projects, and examinations.
4. Research and Professional Development:
Participate in research activities and encourage student involvement in research projects.
Stay updated with current business trends, practices, and theories to inform teaching methods.
5. Administrative Duties:
Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and assessment outcomes.
Contribute to departmental meetings, committees, and administrative tasks as required.
6. Community Engagement:
Support outreach programs, workshops, and seminars that promote business education.
Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.

Education:
A Bachelor’s degree in Business Management, Commerce, or a related field is essential.
A Master’s degree (or working towards one) in Business Administration or a similar discipline is highly desirable.

Prior experience in teaching at the tertiary or vocational education level is an advantage.
Technical Skills:
Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.

Soft Skills:

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and futures citizens on Papua New Guinea.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
The Senior Lecturer plays a pivotal role to ensure we have a highly engaged and productive students that enriched through education in unison to prosper in their life goals and achievements. As the gatekeeper of our student’s success, you will promote student management best practices that can be easily digested and embraced across the organisation.
The Senior Lecturer is responsible for designing, implementing and maintaining a modern Academic function that is digital on the inside—harnessing digital + cloud technologies to effectively capture and manage all aspects of delivering the best student experience for the Institution. Overseeing and managing the entire lecturing process, you will ensure all students are engaged both academically and socially to maintain a healthy balance and effectively utilising our finite academic infrastructure resources.
The Senior Lecturer reports to the Head of School - Business and Management. This position incorporates a high degree of unsupervised work; as an outcome-focused person, you will display strong conflict resolution skills and enjoy managing your workload and being part of a productive team.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
In a highly student-focused role, the Senior Lecturer should focus on strong collaboration, communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills. It is also essential that you understand Global Management Best Practices, and local industry trends. Senior Lecturer duties will involve managing and monitoring undergraduate programmes. This includes associated operational administration, curriculum development, course materials review and quality management and enhancement.  Senior Lecturer duties include but are not limited to the following:
Learning & Teaching
Ensure quality of tutor classes and complete the assigned syllabus within the scheduled time
Use all the available teaching aids for better understanding and delivery of the units
Ensure the benchmark for lectures is achieved in the KPM’s at the end of the semester
Tutor specific academic subjects to individuals or small groups
Monitor student’s attendance and progress
Use pre-determined Institution resources to deliver the tutoring as outlined
Lesson Preparation, Assessment & Examination Duties
Design, develop and prepare and conduct face-to-face, online and co-operative programs as allocated that inspire strong discussions and keep students interested and engaged
Ensure that unit / course design and delivery comply with quality standards and regulations of the University and College
Assist in the conduct of examinations (e.g., paper setting, marking, supervision and invigilation)
Prepare and Submit DRMS in a timely manner
Student Learning Experience
Provide a high-quality learning experience to students, assisting them to achieve prescribed learning outcomes
Supervise student projects and academic elements of field trips as and when required
Supporting students’ extra-curricular activities
Coordinate meetings and schedules with tutees as appropriate
Student Pastoral Care
Research, Scholarship & Innovation:
Engage in research, scholarly activity and/or innovation, subject to the approval of the Head of School
Engage with other researchers internally, nationally & internationally to contribute to the research objectives of the respected School and Institutions research centres
To engaged in subject and professional research development as required and relevant to support teaching activities
Be active and recognised contributor to subject association and relevant professional bodies
Curriculum Development:
Develop & produce appropriate learning materials
Responsible for designing and delivery of modules and assessment methods
Develop course / unit materials of relevance to the highest quality for undergraduate programmes
Designing and delivery of Curriculum
General Duties:
Attend and present at relevant conferences and share knowledge and insights gained with the other schools when required
Liaise closely with teaching, technical and administration
Taking administrative responsibilities as requested by your Head of School, Division, and Registrar
Participate in professional development activities to improve tutorial skill and continue to grow cultural competence.
Provide support as a team member in other operational activities as and when requires
Participate in Institutions staff development initiatives relating to learning & teaching
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA:
The following criteria is considered to be ESSENTIAL:
Master’s Degree or Higher in any of the following fields: Business, Economics or any related course
At least 3 years experience in teaching
Well-developed interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate effectively with students and all levels of employees and management
Excellent business judgement, analytical and decision-making skills
Ability to review programme design on a regular basis to ensure compliance with quality standards and academic regulations and to make alterations where appropriate.
Ability to demonstrate equivalent core knowledge in units taken
Ability to use a range of delivery techniques to enthuse and engage students
Capacity to develop and maintain effective working relationships with students, staff, management, other organizations and external stakeholders
Ability to communicate and impart complex conceptual ideas in a variety of way – presentations, reports, journal articles etc.
Ability to plan workloads and projects and manage resources effectively
Sound Computer skills
Good work ethics, of sober habits and with the right attitude
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Great customer focus and team player
Excellent active listening and presentation skills
Managing succession planning of staff
Ability to develop ideas and new student-centered approaches responding to individual learning styles
Effective time management skills and attention to detail
The following criteria is considered to be DESIREABLE:
Experience working in a tertiary environment
Experience in educating and coaching staff
Demonstrated teaching skills
Demonstrated research skills

Head of Research
Research - Port Moresby, NCD
IBSUNIVERSITY
ROLE DESCRIPTION
ROLE TITLE : Head of Research
ROLE ID : HOR-001
DEPARTMENT : RESEARCH
DIVISION : IBSUniversity
ROLE TERM : 24 MONTHS
ROLE TYPE : FULLTIME
EFFECTIVE DATE: : TBA
REPORTING TO : PRO VICE-CHANCELLOR (Academic)
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a
difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999
and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The
affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer
internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea.
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments
to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching,
learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and
partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically
positioned.
POSITION OVERVIEW
The Head of Research will provide strategic leadership and operational oversight to promote a
research culture of excellence, innovation, and integrity at IBSUniversity. This role is central to
strengthening the University’s research systems, advancing staff capacity, fostering student
research engagement, and ensuring alignment with national higher education priorities.
The role includes academic engagement through teaching two units - one each from
IBSUniversity and Southern Cross University - to strengthen the connection between teaching
and research, and to better understand student expectations and academic progression.
The Director of Research will also support the broader institutional strategy by ensuring that all
research activities are in harmony with the expectations of the Department of Higher Education,
Research, Science and Technology (DHERST), contribute to the University’s strategic goals, and
uphold the Vision, Mission, Values, and non-negotiable IBS Culture.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
1.1. Strategic Research Leadership
Implement the University’s research strategy, policies, and annual research plan.
Promote a culture of research excellence, innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration across schools and faculties aligning research priorities with Papua New Guinea’s national development goals.
2.2. Academic Contribution through Teaching
Undertake two units per semester (one IBSU, one SCU) to maintain academic connection and student engagement.
Use teaching to identify talent and cultivate a research mindset among students and faculty.
2.3. Research Management and Capacity Building
Oversee the planning, execution, and dissemination of research projects.
Organize and conduct of National and International Conference.
Continue to publish “IBSU Journal of Business and Research” biannual journal.
Support faculty and postgraduate students (Commencement of master’s Programme from 2026) in developing research proposals, securing grants, and publishing in reputable journals.
Student Satisfaction – Support University with regular surveys on teaching quality, campus facilities, learning resources, and career support and employee satisfaction.
New program recommendations-Support university to identify the requirements for future programs/courses.
Analysis & Reporting – Consolidating findings into actionable recommendations for  curriculum design, student services, and industry engagement. Organize training, workshops, and seminars to strengthen research skills and capacity within the University.
2.4.  Research Partnerships and Funding
Establish and maintain collaborations with local and international universities, industry partners, government agencies, and NGOs.
Lead efforts to secure research grants and external funding to support institutional projects.
Represent IBSUniversity at national and international research forums.
2.5. Research Governance and Quality Assurance
Chair the University Research Committee and oversee research ethics and compliance processes for the publication by the faculty members.
Monitor research outputs, impact, and performance indicators to ensure continuous
improvement.
2.6. Administration and Documentation
Prepare research reports, policy briefs, and publications for internal and external stakeholders.
Manage the research budget and allocate resources effectively.
Contribute to the University’s accreditation and quality assurance processes.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
The following criteria are considered to be ESSENTIAL:
Master’s degree or higher in Research, Education, Social Sciences, Business, or a related field (PhD preferred).
Proven track record in research leadership, academic publishing, or managing research projects.
Strong ability to analyze and synthesize complex data into clear, evidence-based insights.
Demonstrated capacity to secure research funding, develop proposals, and manage grants.
Excellent academic writing and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate research findings to diverse audiences.
Proven critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to design and implement innovative research strategies.
Ability to foster and maintain effective collaborative relationships with colleagues, research partners, funding agencies, and external stakeholders.
High standards of research ethics, integrity, and professionalism, with a proactive and positive attitude.
Strong project management and time management skills, with the ability to deliver outputs within tight deadlines.
Exceptional attention to detail in research design, analysis, and reporting.
The following criteria are considered to be DESIRABLE:
Experience working in a tertiary education or higher education research environment.
Experience in mentoring, supervising, or coaching academic staff and/or student researchers.
Demonstrated skills in developing research policies, frameworks, and institutional strategies.
Experience in community-based research, applied research, or projects with measurable social impact.
OTHER ROLE RELATED INFORMATION
The role is based at IBS Mt Eriama Campus but is required and support the responsive delivery of services and to maintain liaison with all key stakeholders.
The role is also required to liaise with external regulatory authorities at their place of business outside University premises.
Some attendance outside normal working hours may be required from time to time for effective performance of the position.

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Processing -Department as a
Autoclaves Supervisor - Processing.
About the role
Reporting to the Process Foreman, the Autoclave Supervisor is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the autoclave circuit, leading a team of operators to deliver reliable production performance while upholding the highest standards of process safety and environmental compliance. This role requires hands-on autoclave operational experience, a strong understanding of high-pressure process safety, and the ability to drive positive change in work practices, team culture, and plant performance. A key accountability of this role is the development and training of both national and local staff, ensuring the transfer of technical knowledge and building long-term operational capability within the workforce.
In this role, you will:
Lead day-to-day operation of the autoclave and associated circuits to ensure production targets are met safely and efficiently.
Supervise, coach, and develop autoclave operators, ensuring adherence to safe operating procedures and compliance with permits and regulatory standards.
Monitor process conditions, troubleshoot deviations, and coordinate corrective actions to maintain plant stability and product quality.
Champion process safety by enforcing critical controls, conducting safety interactions, and fostering a strong safety culture.
Drive the structured development and training of national and local staff, ensuring competency growth, knowledge transfer, and career progression opportunities.
Collaborate with maintenance, engineering, and technical teams to plan and execute shutdowns, inspections, and repairs.
Ensure accurate reporting of shift activities, production data, and incidents into plant systems.
Contribute to operator training programs, competency assessments, and continuous skills development.
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To
succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Proven operational experience in POX autoclave circuits.
Demonstrated leadership ability in supervising teams in a processing environment.
Strong understanding of process safety principles (e.g., high pressure, high temperature, hazardous materials).
Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to communicate effectively across teams and disciplines, with a focus on mentoring and capability development.
Commitment to fostering a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
High level of initiative with an eagerness to drive positive change and challenge the status quo.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Autoclaves Supervisor - Processing
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a
Autoclaves Supervisor - Processing
. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The
Reliability Engineer
will improve the safety, availability, and life-cycle performance of process plant assets by preventing mechanical failures through proactive reliability engineering, data-driven analysis, and continuous improvement.
Essential Duties
Identify issues/defects and improvement opportunities by analyzing equipment performance, process delays, costs, asset management KPI’s and maintenance history in SAP
Develop project plans for reliability improvement initiatives in line with Newmont’s Defect Elimination Process
Develop and manage equipment maintenance strategies using Reliability Centered Maintenance methodology and PM optimization for existing strategies on equipment not meeting availability or reliability requirements
Compile and distribute key asset performance indicators including availability and utilization
Facilitate Root Cause Analysis (RCA) sessions using RCA guidelines to identify failure causes, containment and counter measures as necessary
Develop lifecycle cost models for critical assets and monitor and quantify equipment lifecycle costs
Investigate and adopt alternative strategies to support capital replacement plan
Actively participate and contribute to safety improvements and environmental awareness.
Training & Experience
A committment to Safety
Bachelor’s Degree qualification in Mechanical Engineering
Registered with IEPNG
Demonstrated fixed plant reliability engineering experience in large-scale mine operations
Understanding of mining industry asset maintenance and reliability methods i.e. defect elimination, criticality analysis, asset strategy development, operate for reliability, condition monitoring, etc
Understanding of safety compliance and regulations
Knowledge of root cause analysis, problem solving, and other analytical techniques
Knowledge of mine operations Fixed Plant and mine processing equipment
Knowledge of maintenance strategies, Master data management and Reliability Centred Maintenance principles
Experience in Failure Modes Effects Analysis facilitation and workshop delivery
Skills in mining industry specific failure metrics and data analytics – i.e. MTBF, MTTR
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21:21 roster.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.

jobs.description:
Provincial Trainer – Education and Social Emotional Learning Project
ChildFund PNG is seeking a committed and skilled Provincial trainer to deliver School Leadership and Social Emotional Learning (SEL) training to secondary school leaders, teachers, and students in project target areas. The role plays a key part in strengthening school leadership, promoting safe and inclusive school environments, and building the leadership capacity of young people.
This position require regular travel to remote and rural communities and close collaboration with provincial education offices, school leaders, students, and ChildFund project staff.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
Provincial Trainer is responsible for delivering training and monitoring progress against project targets for Head Teachers, Principals, School Boards of Management (BoM), using the School Leadership Management Training Package. This role is responsible for working closely with secondary school students and building leadership, GEDSI skills to ensure proper peer to peer support mechanism in targeted schools using Rights, Responsibility and Resilience  for Respectful Relationship training. The role requires regular travel to remote locations to conduct trainings within schools. Provincial Trainers will also follow up with schools to support the development and implementation of School Learning Improvement Plans (SLIPs) and Behaviour Management Plans. In addition, the Provincial Trainer will work closely with provincial partners to coordinate training logistics, including school and teacher selection, preparation of training venues, and scheduling of district-level trainings. The position requires maintaining regular, open communication with Lead Trainers and the Provincial Liaison Officer (PLO) to ensure smooth coordination of training activities, logistics, and provincial office requirements.
Key Duties
Deliver School Leadership and 5R Learning Resource Manual (LRM) trainings to achieve project targets and outcomes, ensuring GEDSI, Child Protection, and Safe Schools principles are mainstreamed across all sessions.
Facilitate Safe Schools and respectful relationships sessions with secondary school students, strengthening student leadership, peer-to-peer support mechanisms, and positive behaviour.
Provide follow-up support to trained school leaders on the development and implementation of School Learning Improvement Plans (SLIPs), Behaviour Management Plans, and delivery of 5R sessions, in collaboration with provincial and district-level staff.
Review and provide technical advice on draft plans to strengthen quality, effectiveness, and stakeholder engagement.
Participate in regular coordination meetings with project staff to review progress, identify challenges and risks, and develop corrective or mitigation actions in consultation with Lead Trainers, PDOE, and District Officers.
Work with school leaders and teachers to strengthen parental and community engagement in children’s learning, school planning, and the implementation of school development and behaviour management plans.
Prepare timely training and activity reports for each project target area, highlighting effective practices, lessons learned, and challenges encountered.
Contribute to training planning in target areas, anticipate operational risks, and support contingency planning; assist with administrative and financial requirements as required.
Work closely with sub-national NDOE counterparts (provincial and district levels) to plan, deliver, and monitor project activities.
Ensure full compliance with ChildFund’s policies, safeguarding standards, and procedures.
Qualification & Experience:
Degree or Diploma in Education, Social Work, Adult Education, or a related discipline recognized in PNG.
Experience working with secondary school students and young people, including facilitating Safe Schools or respectful relationships activities.
Experience working in INGO in implementing, managing, coordination educational programs
Sound understanding of the PNG education system, school leadership, and school management processes.
Demonstrated experience in training, mentoring, and coaching teachers, school leaders, or young people to achieve positive outcomes.
Experience delivering training in diverse and remote settings in PNG.
Sound knowledge of quantitative and qualitative monitoring and reporting
Desirable:
Experience trainer, school Inspector in PNG.
Knowledge of participatory adult learning methodologies.
Experience in child rights, Safe Schools, SLIP training.
Skills:
Strong training skills – confidence, clarity and responsiveness
Ability to engage trainees from a diverse setting.
Strong organizational and planning skills and ability to meet deadlines.
Sound evaluative skills, able to assess trainees progress and make adjustments where necessary.
Flexible and willing to travel to project target areas.
Safeguarding
Remain alert and responsive to any child safeguarding or sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment (SEAH) risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child safeguarding and PSEAH policy and procedures, and conduct yourself consistent with those policies
Appointment to this position is subject to
criminal background checks and reference checks.

This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.

Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.

Provide coaching for performance improvement.

Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.

Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.
7+ years relevant work experience essential.
Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.

Leading digital banking transformation.
Customer-centric financial growth.
Strategic legal impact for PNG expansion.
The opportunity
A leading corporation expanding its footprint across Papua New Guinea is looking for an Assistant Company Secretary in Port Moresby to serve as a key pillar of its corporate governance team. The successful candidate will ensure that board operations and statutory compliance are managed with the highest level of professionalism. The role provides the essential legal and administrative support required to protect the interests of stakeholders and management while ensuring efficient organizational flow.
This is an ideal opportunity for a self-motivated, well-organized professional
in corporate governance or legal administration. The successful candidate will elevate their career by supporting the Board of Directors, ensuring seamless statutory compliance, and providing sound governance advice to the business. The role requires excellent analytical skills and attention to detail to navigate a complex regulatory environment within an organization undergoing significant and rapid change.
The role
The Assistant Company Secretary plays a central role in safeguarding the corporation’s legal and regulatory standing through meticulous governance management. Responsibilities include overseeing all in-house corporate secretarial functions, managing the lifecycle of board meetings, and ensuring the timely submission of all statutory returns to relevant authorities. The role serves as a key point of contact for external legal and regulatory bodies, providing clear instructions to ensure compliance goals are met. The overarching goal is to maintain a legally sound corporate environment through proactive management and cost-efficient administrative practices.
Main duties include:
Ensure the Board fulfills all statutory and regulatory obligations across multiple operating jurisdictions.
Provide legal advice and administrative support to the Company Secretary and Group CEO.
Manage board processes, including agendas, training plans, fee administration, and performance reviews.
Record meeting minutes and maintain action item trackers for all Board and Committee meetings.
Oversee regulatory compliance, corporate records maintenance, and communications with stock exchanges and share registries.
Administer the Diligent Boards portal and coordinate logistics for annual stockholder meetings.
Qualification and Experience:
Formal Education: Bachelor of Laws Degree and a Certificate of Admission to the Supreme and National Courts of Papua New Guinea.
Core Experience: Between 3 to 5 years of professional practice as a Company Secretary or Assistant Company Secretary is required.
Corporate Background: Previous experience must be within a large, multi-jurisdictional corporate environment.
Regional Expertise: At least 5 years of general professional practice in Papua New Guinea or other relevant operating jurisdictions.
Industry Knowledge: Practical experience within the Financial Services industry is considered highly desirable for this role.
Regulatory Clearance: Candidates must be able to obtain "Fit & Proper" certification granted by the Bank of Papua New Guinea.

jobs.description:
Secretary to the Council and the Vice Chancellor
Administration & Corporate Services - Port Moresby, NCD
Job Title: Secretary to the Council and the Vice Chancellor                                                                    Department: Administration and Coorporate Services
Location: IBSUniversity, 11mile Campus                                                                                              Reporting To: Vice Chancellor
Employment Type: Fulltime
ORGANATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically positioned.
Job Summary:
The Secretary will assist the Council and the Vice Chancellor by managing official communications, preparing documents, and organizing meetings. The ideal candidate must be a qualified lawyer with at least one year of legal practice experience. The role requires strong organizational skills, professional handling of legal and administrative tasks, and the ability to support high-level university governance.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepare agendas and organize meetings for the Council and the Vice Chancellor.
Take minutes and keep records of meetings.
Handle official correspondence and document filing.
Provide legal advice when needed, based on your legal background.
Assist in drafting and reviewing legal and administrative documents.
Ensure timely follow-up on action points from meetings.
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.
Support the Vice Chancellor and Council members with administrative tasks.
Requirements:
Qualification: Bachelor's degree in Law or related field (LL.B.) with at least one year of legal practice.
Good knowledge of legal procedures and documentation.
Strong organizational and communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Responsible, reliable, and detail-oriented.
Working Hours:
Full-time, Monday to Friday, with occasional extra hours for meetings or urgent tasks.
Who Can Apply:
Qualified lawyers with at least one year of legal practice and administrative experience, preferably with experience supporting executive or academic bodies in a university setting.
