PNG Motors is not a short-term operation. We’re a national business with strong brands, established systems, and real aftersales support.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Engineer, Maintenance will provide mechanical engineering support for safe and efficient plant operations by delivering fit for purpose designs, driving reliability and delivering cost effective maintenance and improvement projects.
Essential Duties
Provide Mechanical Engineering support to the site’s production and maintenance teams.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives to improve reliability, reduce downtime, and lower lifecycle costs.
Undertake Mechanical design tasks from concepts through to execution.
Delivering OPEX projects within budget and time constraints. This includes conducting engineering trials on assets to achieve extended life.
Participating in CAPEX projects as part of a stakeholder.
Monitor plant performance metrics and collate engineering reports.
Analysing losses and conducting investigations using Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) standards.
Assessing criticality of assets and developing, recommending, and implementing strategies for improving equipment reliability.
Champion Change through Management of Change (MOC).
Mentor and provide technical guidance to tradesmen, planners and junior/ graduate engineers.
Working collaboratively with personnel across all business units.
Training & Experience
A bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, or related fields.
Registered IEPNG member would be an advantage
Project and Asset management Experience
At least 5 years of experience in mining or related industry
Knowledge of Fixed Plant systems including crushers, conveyors, grinding mills, flotation, tanks & tailings.
Ability to provide mechanical engineering support to Fixed Plant Assets. Must have CMMS experience - preferably SAP.
Have practical understanding of crushers, conveyors, grinding mills, flotation, tanks, and tailings systems.
Effective organisation and planning skills
High attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work under less supervision
Mechanically minded, self-motivated, result driven individual with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Working Conditions
This is a Fly-In-Fly-Out (FIFO) role on a 21:21 roster.

New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.

Reporting to the Superintendent – Metallurgy, you will be responsible for the development, implementation, and monitoring of metallurgical systems across the Porgera process plant. This includes leading technical projects, supporting plant performance, and mentoring the metallurgy team.

Proven ability to mentor team members and build technical capability
Project management and business improvement experience

ining

ngineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Geological Engineering, or related field.

In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Taric, Bougainville, Gulf Province and NCD Province. jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Group Accounting Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating accounting activities across multiple entities within the Group. This role ensures accurate financial records and reporting, compliance with statutory and internal and external requirements, timely month-end and year-end closings, and effective supervision of accounting staff. The position supports the Group Finance Manager by providing reliable financial information and maintaining strong internal controls across the Group. The position also requires hands-on involvement and the ability to step in and perform accounting officer duties when required to ensure business continuity.
Key Responsibilities
Group Accounting & Reporting

Oversee daily accounting operations for all companies within the Group.

Review and ensure accuracy of general ledger entries, journal postings, and account
reconciliations.

Prepare and review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports for group
consolidation.

Ensure timely month-end and year-end closing for all entities.

Assist in the preparation of consolidated financial statements and management
reports.
Compliance & Statutory Requirements

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax regulations, and
statutory requirements.

Coordinate external audits and liaise with auditors, tax agents, and regulators.

Review tax computations, GST/VAT returns, and statutory filings before submission.

Ensure proper documentation and audit trails are maintained across all entities.
Budgeting & Analysis

Assist in annual budgeting and forecasting processes for the Group.

Monitor actual results against budgets and provide variance analysis.

Support the Finance Manager with financial analysis and cost control initiatives.
Internal Controls & Process Improvement

Implement and monitor internal control procedures across the Group.

Review accounting processes and recommend improvements for efficiency and
accuracy.

Ensure adequate coverage of duties within the accounting team and reallocate or
personally assume responsibilities during staff absences or peak periods.

Ensure consistent accounting policies and procedures are applied across all entities.
Team Supervision & Coordination

Supervise and guide accountants and finance officers within the Group.

Review work performed by subordinates and provide technical guidance and training.

Assist in performance evaluation and workload planning for the accounting team.
Other Responsibilities

Support Finance Manager on special projects and ad-hoc reporting.

Assist in system implementation, upgrades, or integration across group companies.

Perform other duties as assigned by management.
Qualifications & Requirements
Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

Professional qualification (CPA, ACCA, CA or equivalent) is an advantage.


Strong knowledge of accounting standards and financial reporting.

Experience in group consolidation and multi-entity accounting is an advantage.

Proficient in accounting software (Quickbooks preferred) and Microsoft Excel.

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Good leadership and communication skills.

Leading the organisation and facilitation of assessments, including data collection and report preparation, to support the development of new activities in Hela Province
Maintaining accurate and up-to-date filing and records for all Santos Foundation program activities in Hela Province
Ensuring compliance with Santos health, safety, environmental, security, and HR policies while sourcing resources or delivering program activities

Complying with the Santos Management System, Delegation of Authority, and corporate governance and safety requirements

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are seeking a committed and safety‑focused
Barge
AB Seaman
to join our high‑performing Marine Operations team. This position plays a crucial role in supporting the safe movement, berthing, and operational readiness of our barges, ensuring that all marine activities are carried out efficiently and in full compliance with Newmont’s world‑class safety and environmental standards.
Working closely with the Marine Barge Supervisor and Barge Masters, you will contribute to the smooth running of daily operations while helping maintain the integrity of our marine assets and the wellbeing of everyone on board. This is an opportunity to be part of a team that values professionalism, teamwork, and a strong safety culture in a dynamic marine environment.
As part of our team, you will be
Assisting the Barge Master with safe berthing and un‑berthing operations.
Reading, understanding, and signing off on all Newmont Barge Operations SMS requirements.
Always maintaining personal and team safety, applying Zero 3 and hazard identification practices.
Conducting shift‑based inspections of all FFA and life‑saving equipment, including life buoys and buoy lights.
Performing general housekeeping on the barge, including deck washdowns and maintaining clean, hazard‑free work areas.
Reporting defects, damages, or near‑miss incidents immediately to the Barge Master.
Applying Newmont’s Safety and Environmental Protection Policies, including pollution prevention during bunkering.
Maintaining clear communication with the Barge Master and wharf rope personnel during operations.
Participating in all scheduled safety and emergency drills.
Ensuring mooring ropes are well maintained, stored correctly, and kept clear of operational areas.
Supporting weekly barge servicing, inspections, and PM maintenance activities.
Assisting with marine tasks such as wharf dredging, depth soundings, and debris removal using small workboats.
Filling in as Rope Man when required.
Managing fatigue by ensuring adequate rest before each shift.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Must have at least General Purpose Deck Rating Certificate of Competency with all valid SOLAS certificates and current seafarer medical fitness certificate.
Proven experience in a similar role within a mining or a like industry
Communicate clearly and work well within a marine operations team
Proactive, reliable, and committed to maintaining high operational standards
Can adapt to a dynamic work environment and support additional marine tasks as needed
Ability to build positive working relationships across different disciplines.
Determination, persistence, and commitment to delivering productive, high-quality work.
Alignment with Newmont’s values, culture, and expectations for safe and reliable operations.
Your work environment
This role is offered on 28 days on 14 days off day/night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suite and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Senior/Sustainable Livelihoods Officer
jobs.description:
Position
:                                                      Sustainable Livelihoods Officer
Reports to (Supervisors)
:                           Senior Community Relations Manager
Location:
Goroka Eastern Highlands, Papua New Guinea
Country Program
:                                       WCS Papua New Guinea Program
Position Type
:                                             Full-Time
Expected travel
:                                          If/when needed to field offices or other location
Organization Background
:
The Wildlife Conservation Society (“WCS”) is a New York not-for-profit corporation founded by statute in 1895 as the New York Zoological Society. WCS saves wildlife and wild places worldwide through research, science, conservation action, education, and inspiring people to value nature. That mission is achieved through our global conservation programs (WCS currently oversees a portfolio of more than 500 conservation projects in 65 countries in Asia, Africa, Latin America, and North America, and the oceans between them) and through the management of the world’s largest system of urban wildlife parks–the Bronx Zoo; the New York Aquarium; and the Central Park, Queens, and Prospect Park Zoos (the City Zoos).
Program Overview:
WCS is the longest established international non-government conservation organisation within Papua New Guinea (PNG). At key and representative landscapes and seascapes, from the country’s coral islands to its forested highlands, WCS works with local communities and provincial, national and international partners, to sustainably manage and conserve the biodiversity and cultural values of Papua New Guinea’s wildlife and wild places. WCS PNG vision is “Gutpela sindaun, gutpela bus, gutpela solwara” (“Empowered people with healthy forests and seas”). The WCS PNG program is headquartered in Goroka. WCS PNG employs about 52 full time staff and implement and administer about 10 projects annually funded by governments and private donors.
Job Summary:
The Sustainable Livelihoods Officer will design, implement, and support community-based livelihood initiatives that strengthen household resilience while reducing pressure on biodiversity. The role focuses on developing environmentally sustainable, culturally appropriate income-generating activities in partnership with local communities, aligning livelihood outcomes with conservation goals. The position works closely with Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), customary landowners, women and youth groups, and local leaders to co-design, implement, and monitor sustainable livelihood activities. The officer will support participatory planning, community consultation, and capacity building while strengthening community ownership and long-term sustainability of interventions. The position requires travel within PNG, especially to WCS field sites in the Highlands and to the marine programme sites in New Ireland, West New Britain and Manus.
This Job Description is progressive in nature and shall be reviewed and amended from time to time to meet the current program needs.
While the position focuses on livelihoods, individuals who demonstrate an interest in leading project activities across other programmatic areas as and when required will be preferred. We are looking for a dynamic individual interested in and excited about taking on significant programmatic responsibilities beyond their existing skillsets.
Major Responsibilities:
Conduct assessments to understand livelihood needs and opportunities in partner communities
Lead implementation of nature-positive livelihood interventions through ongoing projects
Ensure livelihood interventions are inclusive and culturally appropriate.
Document impacts of livelihood interventions, including but not restricted to harvests, sales, profits, etc.
Support and conduct trainings on family business management, financial literacy, etc.
Work with partner CBOs to widen the impact of livelihood interventions
Translate scientific information into simple English and Tok Pisin to allow it to be easily understood by a variety of stakeholders, including those with low literacy skills.
Provide capacity building to local staff and partners.
Represent WCS during stakeholder/partner engagement and outreach
Other duties as directed by your supervisor.
Minimum Requirements:
Education/Credentials
A bachelor’s degree or higher qualifications in a relevant discipline. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in other fields but with full-time professional experience in implementing livelihood projects will also be considered.
Experience
At least 2 years’ full-time, professional experience in implementing livelihood projects with an NGO or a government agency or equivalent
Strong understanding of and experience with conducting financial and business management trainings for communities
Good interpersonal skills and experience in liaising with a range of stakeholders, including traditional owners, local and state government, special interest groups and individuals regarding natural resource management issues.
Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Experience in community engagement, facilitation, and participatory planning.
Experience working with Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and customary institutions.
Strong facilitation and conflict-sensitive communication skills.
Understanding of social safeguards, inclusion, and gender-sensitive approaches.
Ability to work respectfully within diverse cultural contexts.
Excellent computer literacy & skill of MS office applications (Word/PowerPoint/internet etc.)
Good analytical and problem-solving skills
Good knowledge of written and spoken English and Tok pisin
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
Being a self-starter with drives and initiative and able to work as a team/individual with a positive attitude and open minded
Excellent organizational and leadership skills
Excellent communication skills
Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure
Excellent multi-tasking, organized and follow-up skills
Willingness and enthusiasm for being in the field in remote locations with very basic facilities

Plan work in SAP/CMMS with clear job instructions, safety analyses, OEM specs, and drawings.
Estimate resources, materials, and duration in collaboration with requesters/supervisors.Plan modular shutdowns and overhauls, including scope, risk assessment, and scheduling.
Update work orders with task lists, documentation, materials, and resource requirements.
Order materials via SAP and arrange vendor purchases or external services.
Expedite materials and adjust schedules to align with plant downtime.
Create and update ARs for BoMs, task lists, and improvements.
Hand over work orders to the scheduler and ensure readiness for execution.
Review completed work packs for improvements and submit ARs.
Ensure all approved work orders have complete information for scheduling.
Training & Experience
Technical Diploma or Trades Certificate in Electrical Engineering, Maintenance or similar

Skilled in the use of CMMS & SAP software to manage the day-to-day planning of maintenance activities.
Proficient in planning concepts and sound understanding of Work Management processes.
Proficient in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Computer proficiency in the MS Office suite.
Sound planning, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.

You’ll be part of the Planning team on a 22:20 FIFO roster, helping ensure maintenance work is sufficiently planned and ready for scheduling.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You will provide critical auto-electrical support for heavy vehicles and associated equipment across our mining operations. Your expertise will ensure safe operation, effective fault diagnosis, and preventative maintenance, maximising equipment availability and uptime to support uninterrupted production. Your contribution directly impacts operational efficiency, safety, and overall mine performance.
As part of our team, you will
Comply with all safety protocols and actively participate in safety discussions.
Conduct routine inspections of light vehicles and equipment, documenting defects and follow-up actions.
Diagnose and repair minor electrical faults on-site to minimise downtime.
Complete accurate maintenance records for inspections, repairs, and adjustments.
Maintain electrical safety standards across work areas, ensuring regulatory and policy compliance.
Support spare parts inventory management, confirming availability and updating records.
Monitor vehicle conditions, identifying wear or performance issues, and report to the Supervisor – Maintenance.
Stop unsafe work and report hazards or incidents in line with site procedures.
Collaborate with internal teams, including Maintenance, Operations, HSE, and Supply Chain.
Engage with external suppliers and service providers as required.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Experience working on heavy machinery within a mining environment.
Relevant Electrical Trade Qualification recognised by the National Trade Testing Body.
Valid PNG Class 3 and 7 Driver’s Licence.
Experience within a dealership setting and with oil or pump systems is highly regarded.
Demonstrated knowledge of auto-electrical systems for light vehicles and heavy mobile mining equipment, including CAT 785 haul trucks.
Proven experience using CAT SIS and a solid working knowledge of SAP maintenance management systems.
Practical experience using diagnostic tools, equipment, and systems to perform maintenance and repairs.
Strong understanding of Caterpillar systems, with particular expertise in electrical systems and fault diagnostics.
Demonstrated knowledge of auto-electrical systems for light vehicles and mobile mining equipment.
Ability to interpret electrical schematics and troubleshoot complex electrical systems effectively.
Strong understanding of electrical safety standards, maintenance procedures, and regulatory requirements relevant to mining.
Willingness to work outside the workshop, including field-based tasks and breakdown support.
Strong understanding of electrical safety standards, maintenance procedures, and regulatory requirements relevant to mining.
Practical experience using diagnostic tools, equipment, and systems to perform maintenance and repairs.
Problem-solving skills and the ability to apply practical judgement to routine issues or escalate when necessary.
Ability to communicate effectively, seek feedback, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to coach, train, and support apprentices and team members.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgement, take initiative, and escalate issues when required.
A proactive, team-focused attitude, with a genuine willingness to help, contribute, and take ownership of tasks.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will work in a dynamic and hands-on mining environment, supporting maintenance activities across light and heavy vehicles. The role involves a mix of workshop-based tasks, on-site inspections, and field diagnostics, with a strong focus on safety, teamwork, and operational efficiency.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will join a team that values safety, innovation, and collaboration. You will have opportunities to grow your technical skills, work with experienced professionals, and make a real impact on mining operations. With a culture that encourages learning, feedback, and continuous improvement, you’ll be part of a high-performing team where your contributions are recognised and valued.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mineral Resources Department as
Mine Geologist - Open Pit
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Mine Geologist (Open Pit), the Mine Geologist is responsible for collecting, interpreting, and reporting geological data to support efficient and safe mining operations. This includes grade control, ore body interpretation, and liaising with mine planning and production teams to optimize ore recovery and minimize dilution. The role plays a critical part in the short-term and long-term success of mining activities.
In this role, you will:
Conduct daily geological mapping, sampling and ore control in active open pit mining areas
Monitor ore and waste boundaries to ensure adherence to grade control plans
Assist in the design and execution of RC grade control drilling programs (e.g. Leapfrog, Vulcan).
Interpret geological data and produce models to support mine planning and forecasting
Collaborate closely with the mining, planning and processing teams to ensure proper material handling
Provide timely geological input for daily, weekly and monthly production reports

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
This is an opportunity to lead where it matters most. You will be at the forefront of keeping Newmont’s Hydraulic Shovel, Excavator, drill and pump fleet operating at its best. Your leadership and technical expertise will shape high-quality rebuilds and maintenance programs that enhance equipment reliability, uphold the highest safety standards, and deliver maximum asset availability to support uninterrupted production.
As part of our team, you will
You will be at the forefront of planning, supervising, and executing rebuild and maintenance programs that make a real impact on operational reliability and safety.
Your key responsibilities will include:
Lead and coordinate the safe, efficient rebuild, repair, and preventive maintenance of Shovels, Excavators drill rigs, pumps, and associated systems.
Plan, schedule, and allocate PCR and Shutdown work work for mechanics and technicians engaged in major overhauls and rebuild programs.
Supervise rebuild activities to ensure compliance with engineering specifications, OEM standards, and quality benchmarks.
Conduct inspections in workshops and the field to verify equipment functionality, reliability, and safety compliance.
Champion safety by enforcing policies, leading risk assessments, promoting Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO) practices, and embedding a “stop unsafe work” culture.
Provide hands-on technical leadership in diagnosing complex mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic faults.
Manage critical spare parts inventory and coordinate with Supply Chain to ensure timely availability for rebuild activities.
Maintain accurate maintenance, labour, and parts records within the maintenance management system.
Monitor rebuild project costs and labour utilisation, identifying opportunities to improve productivity and reduce downtime.
Build a positive, high-performing team environment through coaching, recognition, and by developing and executing training plans to transfer technical skills to workforce.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will bring a combination of technical expertise, hands-on experience, and strong leadership skills that ensure safe, reliable, and high-quality maintenance outcomes.
Trade Certificate in Heavy Equipment, Diesel Fitting, or Maintenance Fitting.
Extensive experience in open-cut mining, including the mechanical and hydraulic rebuild of large Shovels, Excavators and drill rigs such as CAT6060, CAT6020, HIT2600, D65 & Pit Viper 231.
Hands-on experience in mobile equipment shutdowns and major overhaul programs.
Advanced knowledge of slurry and dewatering pump systems.
Proven ability to interpret OEM manuals and restore assets to zero-hour lifecycle standards.
Strong troubleshooting skills for complex hydraulic systems, with the ability to read and interpret detailed schematics.
Eligible for appointment as a Statutory Supervisor (Section 44/45) under the PNG Mineral Resources Authority.
Solid understanding of the PNG Mining (Safety) Act, with expertise in LOTO, stored energy, and high-risk work controls.
Demonstrated experience leading and mentoring diverse teams, including developing and executing training plans to transfer technical skills to staff.
Competence with maintenance management systems such as SAP, Ellipse, or AMT.
Valid PNG Driver’s Licence and high-risk work tickets (Overhead Crane, Dogging, Rigging).
Strong communication skills in English; working knowledge of Tok Pisin is highly regarded.
Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse complex information and turn insight into action.
Experience in risk management and supporting technical training initiatives.
Proactive, energetic, and capable of working independently.
Adaptable and creative, with the ability to think “outside the box”.
Self-aware, collaborative, and confident in giving and receiving feedback.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 FIFO roster from Australia to Lihir Island, PNG, operating on day shifts.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will work in a dynamic mining environment where safety, teamwork, and operational excellence are paramount. This role interfaces closely with Maintenance Planning, Operations, Supply Chain, and Safety teams, as well as OEMs and specialist contractors. You will have access to well-equipped workshops, advanced diagnostic tools, and the support of a globally recognised mining organisation committed to continuous improvement and capability development.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our people are at the heart of our success. We offer the opportunity to work for a global industry leader with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and inclusion. You will be empowered to lead, innovate, and make a lasting impact while developing your career in a supportive and values-driven environment. Join us and be part of a team shaping the future of responsible mining.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 41094 before the advertised closing date: 10 February 2026.

jobs.description:
TITLE
Finance and Operations Coordinator
REPORTING TO
Senior Programs Manager
LOCATION
Kokopo or Rabaul, East New Britain Province
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
START DATE
END DATE
Full time
1
st
January 2026
31 December 2028
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG, guided by the National WASH Policy (2015-2030).
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented
Finance and Operations Coordinator
to support the delivery of our East New Britain programs.
The
Finance and Operations Coordinator
is a critical support role responsible for ensuring strong financial management, compliance, and efficient operational systems for WaterAid’s East New Britain Program.
The position oversees financial and operational management for two key grants:
the
PacFresh H2O Program
in Rabaul and Pomio Districts; and
the
KIWA Initiative Grant
in Rabaul District.
Working across finance, administration, procurement, and operations, the role ensures accurate financial reporting, adherence to donor and WaterAid policies (including
GIZ and AFD procurement requirements
), and effective support to program implementation. The Finance and operations coordinator will manage internal control procedures to ensure WaterAid and donor policies and procedures are followed; support on project budget development, expenditure tracking and budget monitoring, and coordinating project audits. The position works closely with WaterAid’s East New Britain program team, local government partners, WaterAid PNG headquarters in Port Moresby, and the WaterAid regional support team in Australia.
About the Grants
The Finance and Operations Coordinator will provide support across two key grants:
Funded by GIZ, the
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
Funded by AFD, the
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Financial Management and Compliance
Oversee day-to-day financial management of PacFresh H2O and KIWA grants, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and donor compliance.
Lead project budget development, budget conversions, reforecasting, and ongoing budget monitoring using WaterAid financial systems (including WAPS and SunSystems)
Prepare and submit timely and accurate financial reports for internal management and donors.
Manage internal control procedures to ensure compliance with WaterAid and donor financial policies.
Lead the Finance Compliance Checklist to ensure all documentation is complete before and after payment authorisation
Coordinate and support internal and external audits, including preparation of documentation and follow-up actions.
Lead quarterly project expenditure transactions review to ensure that all project expenditure is correctly coded. If there are any errors or any missing transactions must advise the Operations Manager for adjustments.
Lead the accurate monthly and quarterly cost recovery process for the projects and ensure sufficient supporting documents are attached such as payslips, payroll transactions and timesheets.
Payments, Accounting, and Systems
Support preparation and processing of payments, ensuring approvals are obtained prior to payment.
Maintain general ledgers and ensure correct coding, GST treatment, and documentation.
Upload payment journals to SunSystems weekly and payroll journals fortnightly.
Create payments via corporate online banking when required.
Ensure all payments complete required Anti-Terrorism checks.
Payroll, Statutory and Tax Obligations
Support or process payroll using Able Payroll software and ensure timely distribution of payslips.
Upload staff NCSL and Nasfund contributions in line with statutory requirements.
Remit Salary and Wages Tax (SWT) and file GST with the IRC, ensuring records are accurate and safely stored
Ensure all project staff's timesheets are signed off and maintained in safe place
Procurement and Administration
Ensure procurement processes comply with GIZ, AFD and WaterAid procurement policies.
Support procurement planning, supplier engagement, contract documentation, and filing.
Follow up with suppliers to ensure complete and accurate supporting documentation.
Maintain organised digital and physical filing systems for financial and procurement records
Maintain project asset registers
Operations and Program Support
Provide operational and administrative support to the East New Britain Program team to enable timely and effective activity delivery.
Work closely with program staff to align financial planning with implementation needs.
Assist with monthly and quarterly reporting processes.
Support capacity building of WaterAid PNG staff and partners through finance training and coaching, in collaboration with the Senior Grants Accountant and Operations Manager.
Undertake other duties as required to support the effective implementation of the Country Program.
People
Ensure the WaterAid Values are understood and followed by all staff.
Provide regular orientation to all staff on People related policies and procedures to ensure adherence, including on the People Manual and Operations Manual.
Supervise the team (Administration, Logistics Officer and Boat Skipper) and ensure performance management reviews are conducted.
Resolve people issues as required, especially Operations staff in sub-offices
Communications and Working Relationships
Internal
WaterAid PNG
WaterAid Australia (support and collaboration with Regional Finance and Program Operations Team)
External
Multiple governmental and non-governmental stakeholders
Donor
Physical Environment and Demands
Moderate travel requirements within East New Britain and occasional travel to Port Moresby.
Level of contact with children
The role may involve engaging with communities and schools to program activities and as such may come into contact with children.  The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.
Qualification, Skills & Attributes (Key Capabilities/Selection Criteria)
All applicants must address these criteria in their application:
Essential
Knowledge, skills and experience
Minimum five years’ experience in a finance and/or operations role within NGO or donor-funded environments.
Demonstrated experience using accounting and financial management systems.
Strong understanding of donor compliance and procurement requirements.
Education
Minimum Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Management, or a related field.
Personal qualities
Commitment to WaterAid’ values and standards of safety of children and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in all our activities.
Personable with a sensitivity to the communication styles of external stakeholders and internal staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
An ability to manage confidentiality and handle sensitive information
Attention to detail
Commitment to the ‘Do No Harm’ approach to aid and development work.
Applications for this role must comprise of:
An application letter addressing the essential person specification criteria outlined above (maximum 2 pages).
A curriculum vita

TITLE
Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator

Senior Programs Manager
LOCATION
Kokopo or Rabaul, East New Britain Province
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
START DATE
END DATE
Full time

Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG, guided by the National WASH Policy (2015-2030).
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Purpose of the Role
The Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator supports the Operations and Programs teams by coordinating the financial and compliance aspects of donor-funded grant agreements.
The role focuses on grant-level financial tracking, compliance oversight, donor requirements (including GIZ and AFD), procurement compliance, and budget monitoring, while working under the technical leadership of the Senior Grants Accountant. The position plays a key capacity-building role by leading training and induction for staff and partners on grant compliance, donor rules, and financial procedures.
Position Summary
This role is responsible for ensuring that donor-funded grants are implemented in line with approved budgets, contractual obligations, and WaterAid policies. The Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator acts as a focal point for grant compliance, providing hands-on support to program teams on budgeting, procurement processes, and financial reporting requirements.
The role works closely with the Senior Grants Accountant to support accurate accounting, reporting, audits, and risk management, and contributes to strengthening organisational grant management systems.
The role works closely with program teams, finance colleagues, and senior management to ensure grants are implemented efficiently, transparently, and in accordance with contractual obligations.
About the Grants
The Grant Accountant and Compliance Coordinator will provide support across two key grants:
Funded by GIZ, the
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
Funded by AFD, the
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Grant Financial Management
Support financial management of donor-funded grants, ensuring expenditures are tracked accurately against approved budgets.
Assist with grant budget development, conversions, reforecasting, and updates in collaboration with program teams and the Senior Grants Accountant.
Monitor grant expenditure and identify variances, risks, and compliance issues, escalating as required.
Support the preparation of monthly and quarterly grant financial reports.
Verify all project expenditures to ensure the budget codes and account codes are selected correctly and that all required supporting documents are complete such as request form, AT check, tax invoice and any additional documents required by donors.
Support quarterly project expenditure transactions review to ensure that all project expenditure is correctly coded.
Support monthly and quarterly cost recovery process for the projects in accordance with staff timesheets, payroll, and payslips, ensuring the appropriate approval process is followed.
Support in maintaining organised digital and physical filing systems for financial and procurement records and all documents both digital and physical will be available when needed.
Donor Compliance and Reporting
Coordinate grant compliance processes to ensure adherence to donor agreements, financial guidelines, and WaterAid policies.
Support preparation of donor financial reports, working closely with the Senior Grants Accountant and Operations Manager.
Maintain organised grant documentation and internal filing systems to support reporting and audits.
Support internal and external audits related to grant-funded programs and assist with implementation of audit findings.
Procurement Compliance and Support
Act as a focal person for program teams on donor-compliant procurement processes, particularly GIZ and AFD requirements.
Review procurement documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance prior to submission or approval.
Provide guidance to program staff on procurement planning, thresholds, and documentation
Maintain general suppliers, preferred suppliers and consultants/ contractor registers
Capacity building and Training
Lead regular training and induction sessions for staff and partners on donor requirements, grant compliance, and financial procedures (including GIZ and AFD compliance).
Support budget holders and program staff to understand budgets, expenditure tracking, and financial reports.
Develop and maintain practical tools, checklists, and guidance materials to support compliance and financial management.
Systems, Coordination and Advisory Support
Work with the Senior Grants Accountant and Finance and Operations Coordinator to support effective use of financial systems (including SunSystems and WAPS).
Contribute to strengthening internal controls and grant management processes.
Provide day-to-day advisory support to program teams on grant finance and compliance matters.
Support risk management related to financial mismanagement and fraud by identifying and escalating concerns.
Key Relationships
Senior Grants Accountant
Operations Manager and Finance Team
Program Managers and Program Teams
WaterAid PNG Leadership Team
Donors, Auditors, and Implementing Partners
WaterAid Regional and Australia-based Teams
Physical Environment and Demands
Moderate travel requirements within East New Britain and occasional travel to Port Moresby.
Qualification, Skills & Attributes (Key Capabilities/Selection Criteria)
All applicants must address these criteria in their application:
Essential
Knowledge, skills and experience
Minimum three years’ experience in grants accounting, financial management, or donor compliance roles.
Demonstrated experience using accounting and financial management systems.
Strong understanding of donor compliance and procurement requirements.
Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
Ability to deliver training and provide clear guidance to non-finance staff.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Management, or a related field.
Personal qualities
Commitment to WaterAid’ values and standards of safety of children and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in all our activities.
Personable with a sensitivity to the communication styles of external stakeholders and internal staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
An ability to manage confidentiality and handle sensitive information
Attention to detail
Commitment to the ‘Do No Harm’ approach to aid and development work.
Applications for this role must comprise of:

Applications which do not address the Selection Criteria specified and the page limits will NOT be considered.
Late and incomplete applications will not be accepted.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Advisor People Training (Safety) will develop training programs, deliver training, coach, mentor and assess Newmont personnel in all aspects including but not limited to regulatory compliance on-the-job delivery, and a safe work environment.
Essential Duties
Develops training materials, delivers training and aligns with Newmont standards, Industry standards and HSE standards
Creates opportunities for people to work together to enable them to contribute to the business and learn from each other.
Deliver theory and 'on the job' training for all operators in various sections.
Communicating training plans to Team Lead and Peers
Conduct’s field observations and engagement with Operational Supervisors and Superintendents to understand the skill gap of employees and the business needs. Using that understanding to then modify training curricula to bridge the gap to ensure employees are fully developed upon completion of the training to contribute to safe production.
Drives and influences proactive safety and productive behaviors.
Sets objectives and expectations for themselves.
Ensures the recording of data into the LMS (Learning Management System) as required.
Prepares resource requests (PPE, Tools, Materials, etc) of their work area and justification for the Team Lead for review.
Actively seeks cost reduction opportunities.
Training & Experience
Minimum of 5 year’s experience in an industrial workplace.
Certificate 3 Trainer/Assessor or equivalent training in Professional Education/Training.
Subject matter expertise in OHS Training, Equipment qualifications.
Developing training materials and curricula, proficiency in Facilitation/Presentation skills and understanding of Learning Databases.
Well-developed computer skills – proficient in MS Word, excel & power-point.
Driver License PNG Class 6 and 7
Good interpersonal, oral and written communications skills in English.
Working Conditions
You’ll be part of the People team on a 21:21 roster, helping maintain regulatory compliance and a safe work environment.

About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as Tutor (Technical Instructor) – Language, Communication & Ethics within the Department of Tourism & Hospitality.
This position supports the delivery of foundational communication and language competencies for tourism and hospitality students, with emphasis on English for Special Purposes (Tourism English), business and professional communication skills, and ethical conduct. The role contributes to teaching, research, curriculum development, and community engagement activities aligned with industry and University expectations.
The successful appointee will report directly to the Head of Department, Tourism & Hospitality.
Key Responsibilities
Design, prepare, and deliver lectures, tutorials, and practical sessions to first- and second-year undergraduate students.
Teach English for Special Purposes, including Tourism English, business communication, and professional communication skills.
Conduct research in areas of specialisation and contribute to scholarly publications where appropriate.
Review, propose, and design new courses in line with industry partner feedback and the University’s academic review cycle.
Establish and maintain linkages with relevant industry bodies, including the PNG Tourism Promotion Authority (PNGTPA), government departments, tourism operators, and research organisations to support teaching and research activities.
Provide academic and technical expertise through the University’s community engagement and outreach programs.
Support departmental teaching and administrative functions as directed by the Head of Department and the Dean of School.
Qualifications, Experience & Competency Profile
Postgraduate qualification at Honours or Master’s degree level from a recognised university in English for Special Purposes (ESP), English Communication, Journalism, Education, or a closely related discipline.
Minimum of two (2) years’ experience as a Lecturer or Tutor, or equivalent tertiary teaching experience in English or Communication Arts.
Relevant post-qualification professional experience in research, consultancy, or applied work related to the tourism, travel, or hospitality industry.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
The Geotechnical Engineer will support safe and efficient mining operations by providing operational geotechnical monitoring, analysis, inspections, and technical input to identify and manage geotechnical and geothermal hazards.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Assist with ground control management, slope monitoring, data analysis, and field inspections to minimize risk to safety and production in a dynamic geothermal environment.Conduct routine geotechnical inspections of pit walls, dumps, stockpiles, harbour waste platform, and marine dumps.
Monitor slope stability using radar, prism, GNSS, and other monitoring systems.
Review and analyse monitoring data and report abnormal movement or trends.
Assist with geotechnical drilling, logging, mapping, and instrumentation programs.
Support slope reconciliation through Design, Implementation, and Verification processes.
Assist with geotechnical and geothermal risk assessments and implementation of controls.
Prepare technical reports, monitoring summaries, and presentations for stakeholders.
Support investigations into ground movement, instability, and incidents.
Provide input into short- and medium-term mine planning and operational designs.
Assist in maintaining and improving geotechnical monitoring systems and databases.
Support technical mentoring programs under guidance of senior engineers.
Actively promotes and demonstrates safe work practices and compliance with site HSE requirements.
Works collaboratively with geotechnical, mining, planning, survey, and operations teams.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Minimum of 2–4 years’ experience in open pit geotechnical engineering or related mining roles.
Experience in slope monitoring, field inspections, and geotechnical data collection.
Exposure to operational mining environments is desirable.
Sound understanding of open pit geotechnical principles and ground control practices.
Awareness of operational safety and risk management systems.
Working knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and Regulations.
Competency in MS Office applications.
Knowledge of slope stability monitoring and analysis software.
Basic knowledge of geological and mining modelling software (e.g., Minesight).
Familiarity with cost control systems (e.g., SAP).
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Strong analytical and problem solving abilities.
Good organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
Working Conditions
You’ll be part of the Geotechnical team on a 22:20 roster, requiring hands-on engagement and collaboration across disciplines.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our commercial team, the Team Lead – Contracts provides leadership and guidance to the Contracts team, ensuring high standards of contract administration, negotiation, and compliance. This role combines mentoring of team members with a strong technical focus, taking a lead role in procurement planning and market engagements under the direction of the Principal and Superintendent – Contracts. The position plays a pivotal role in achieving effective commercial outcomes, strengthening supplier relationships, and ensuring compliance with company policies, procedures, and applicable legislation.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring, and guidance to Contracts Officers, fostering capability development and professional growth.
Allocate tasks, set priorities, and oversee workload to ensure deadlines and quality standards are consistently met.
Conduct regular feedback, coaching, and performance development for team members.
Act as a role model in professional conduct, supplier engagement, and commercial practice.
Oversee the drafting, review, and negotiation of contractual agreements to secure favourable terms and conditions.
Personally handle high-value or complex contracts to ensure strategic alignment and optimal outcomes.
Ensure all contracts comply with legal requirements, organisational policies, and industry standards.
Identify and mitigate potential contractual risks to protect the organization's interests.
Monitor compliance with contractual obligations, escalating significant risks, disputes, or performance issues to the Superintendent/Principal as appropriate.
Conduct audits and reviews of contract performance, ensuring adherence to obligations.
Foster and maintain strong relationships with vendors and service providers.
Act as a primary point of contact for contractual matters, facilitating communication and collaboration with external partners.
Collaborate with internal departments, including operations, supply and finance, to support contract-related initiatives.
Drive improvements in procurement and contract management processes, including development of templates, evaluation methods, and best practice approaches.
Capture and share lessons learned from market engagements to strengthen future strategies.
Stay abreast of industry trends, regulatory changes, and emerging risks incorporating these into contract strategies.
Provide training and guidance to internal teams on contract management processes and best practices.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Degree Qualified tertiary qualifications in a relevant field (business or legal etc) essential.
Procurement or contract management certification (e.g., CIPS, WCC, or equivalent) desirable.
5 – 8 years’ relevant work experience in a Commercial Contracts role, preferably in mining or similar environment.
Demonstrated knowledge of contract administration, negotiation, and management.
Strong experience in leading tenders, supplier evaluations, and market engagements.
Demonstrated behaviours consistent with K92 Mining core values.
Demonstrated problem solving and decision-making capability.
Strong commercial analysis and evaluation capabilities.
Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, and develop team members with diverse skills and backgrounds.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly to, and influence, internal and external stakeholders.
Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally.
Proficient in the operation of Pronto (desirable)
Experience in Microsoft suite office tools
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
