Surveyor - Survey Underground
Porgera, Enga, Papua New Guinea
Hot Job
Be the First to Apply
Job Description
Surveyor, Survey - Underground
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mine Technical Services Department as a
Surveyor, Survey Underground
.
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Surveyor, the Surveyor, Survey Underground is responsible for providing accurate and timely survey services to support safe and effective mine development and production activities. The role ensures the integrity of underground control networks, compliance with statutory mine survey standards and the availability for reliable spatial data for planning, engineering and operational decision -making.
In this role, you will
:
Establish and maintain the underground survey control network.
Conduct regular validation and adjustment of survey control stations
Manage spatial database, survey files and digital models in compliance with company procedures.
Carry out development surveys, including mark-ups for heads, backs, walls and floors
Conduct production surveys such as drives, stopes, draw points and blast ring surveys
Perform cavity monitoring, void scanning and laser scanning as required
Monitor underground excavation progress and reconcile with plans
Provide survey data for mines design, scheduling, drill and blast layouts and infrastructure installation
Assist in volume calculations, stopes reconciliation and deformations monitoring
Generates 3D models, plans and reports for engineering and geology teams
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Tertiary Qualifications in Surveying
Experience working in Underground Mining environment
Proficiency with surveying instruments (total stations, scanners, gyros, GNSS where applicable)
Competency with CAD/survey software (Surpac, Deswik, Vulcan, Maptek, AutoCAD)
Strong understanding of underground mine plans, drilling layouts and mine development methods
Valid underground induction and medical fitness for mine work.
Compiling of yearly mine plans as per PNG Mining (Survey) Act 1977 (Sect 35-39)
Exposure to automated data capture and digital mine technologies.
Promote a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and compliance with the NPL Occupational Health, Safety and Environmental Policy.
Planning and undertaking underground development heading set out and face markups, laser installations, void pickups, subsistence/deformation monitoring, computation, processing, and reporting.
Working Conditions
Underground work environment with rotating or fixed shift roster
Exposure to typical mining conditions – confined spaces, noise, dust and variable temperatures
Use of PPE and adherence to all safety protocols required
Some manual handling associated with survey equipment
Mobilization Requirement
In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge. This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve NPL’s social performance and people knowledge.
You will be joining an operation that values safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contributing to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.
This role is offered on a FIFO basis with a 21/14 roster and a highly competitive remuneration package.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Underground Mining team you will be an integral part of K92’s Mine Control Centre (MCC). The SIC Officer will assist the Shift Supervisors and Mine Coordinators throughout the shift to optimse the outcomes in line with the weekly plan, using the information flowing through the MCC and the use of the live Deswik.OPS Gantt mine schedule.
The SIC Officer will collaborate with the Supervisors throughout the shift, guiding them on opportunities, status updates from the MCC, coordinating requirements from technical services and generally assisting wherever possible.
The SIC officer will prepare a draft 36-hour shift plan for the Supervisors in readiness for the shift hand over, manage Deswik.OPS live weekly schedules, maintain compliance to plan dashboards and have daily reports prepared with validated data.
In addition, the SIC Officer will be required to identify data driven improvement opportunities, using PowerBI dashboards and analytics of the data recorded into Deswik.OPS.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Ensure all personnel, contractors and visitors comply with site and contractual HSE requirements.
Ensure work is planned so it can be conducted safely, with consideration for environmental conditions, nearby activities, people, and other resources needed to complete the work.
Ensure housekeeping activities within and around the work area are performed to a high standard.
Actively promote a safety first, zero harm culture.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (HSE, Supervisors, Coordinators, Superintendents, MTS personnel, Mine Controllers) to support the Mining Supervisor to execute their responsibilities on a shift-by-shift basis.
Promote a data-driven continuous improvement by reviewing Power BI dashboards and completing data analytics to identify improvement opportunities.
Maintain, in real time the Deswik.OPS Gantt schedule through the shift to weekly time horizons,
Collaborate with the Mine Supervisors across the mine radio to prepare a detail 36-hour shift plan for review in each shift planning meeting.
Provide Supervisors with any mobile equipment status changes because of either Planned or Breakdown maintenance
In consultation with the underground supervisors, provide the Mobile Maintenance teams with clear priorities for break down repairs.
Inform the Supervisor of upcoming planning conflicts based on the live shift progress (on the Deswik.OPS Gantt), to proactive make changes throughout the shift, optimising the shift plan.
Coordinate with the Underground Supervisors to ensure shotcrete orders and delivery time frames are managed to achieve the shift and weekly objectives
Coordinate with the stores department to ensure consumables are available for the mining team to deliver the plan
Maintain the compliance to plan control charts (Development, Production, Slot Drilling) on the muster room dashboards, meeting rooms and daily reports
Maintain the end of week forecast of mining key physicals
The SIC Officer will maintain a dashboard and memo register to clearly identifying the upcoming requirement for development designs and survey control
Maintain KPI’s on a daily, weekly and monthly basis as defined in the K92 MOS
Produce delay Pareto charts each day, week and month to understand key operational improvement opportunities
Use the Deswik.OPS data and Power BI to identify continuous improvement opportunities
Use the Deswik.OPS data and Power BI to produce reports which measure the success of current CI projects.
Escalate delays through the K92 MOS escalation TARP as required
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Minimum of 3 years' experience in underground mining, with an in depth understanding of the mining cycle
Preferably tertiary qualifications in a Mining related field
High level of computer literacy in MS Office suite and data management
High degree of analytical, planning and scheduling skills
Strong communication skills with ability to communicate with wide range of disciplines on site
Experience in directing, monitoring and adjusting shift plans and reports
Experience in Deswik Software or Similar
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Specialist, External Relations, you will drive Newmont’s success by developing and leading stakeholder engagement plans, supporting operations, and enhancing our license to operate across Asia Pacific. Your work will build strong relationships with government agencies and help shape policy and regulatory outcomes that matter.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Apply government relations strategies at national and provincial levels
Build and sustain networks with government agencies, regulators, and policymakers
Advise on policy, regulatory, and political trends impacting operations
Develop and manage stakeholder engagement plans
Support Newmont’s interests within national and provincial governments
Implement governance and policies for government affairs
Proactively identify and mitigate external risks
Collaborate with peers to develop and implement country strategies
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Degree in law, economics, international relations, social science, or related field (preferred)
Advanced knowledge in stakeholder management, government engagement, policy, or advocacy
Strong skills in strategy development, advocacy, political risk management, and communications
Proficiency with major office systems (e.g., MS Office)
Self-awareness, adaptability, and commitment to continuous improvement
Ability to build relationships, influence, and negotiate effectively
Your Work Environment
You will operate in a dynamic, high-impact environment at the intersection of business, government, and society. This role involves regular engagement with senior government officials, regulatory bodies, and internal executive leadership. As part of Newmont’s Corporate Affairs function, you will play a key role in supporting the company’s long-term success and sustaining its social license to operate in Papua New Guinea.
Based in Port Moresby, this position presents a unique opportunity to make a lasting impact on government relations and policy engagement in support of responsible mining and sustainable development in the region.
If you're ready to take on a meaningful challenge where your expertise can shape the future of mining in Papua New Guinea, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now and lead the change!
Why Join Newmont
Newmont is the world’s leading gold company, committed to sustainable and responsible mining. As part of our team, you will:
Influence national policy and drive meaningful change in the mining sector.
Work alongside global leaders in a values-driven, inclusive organization.
Access world-class professional development and leadership opportunities.
Be part of a company that prioritizes safety, integrity, sustainability, and respect in everything we do.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 11 December 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

EMPLOYEE TERMS OF REFERENCE
POSITION TITLE:
Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Coordinator
LOCATION:
KTF Port Moresby Office
TYPE / DURATION:
Full time, 12-month contract
REPORTING TO:
Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Advisor
ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improved
equality
and safety for women and girls; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.
KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
Come and join the KTF family and enjoy working in a fast -paced, challenging environment with a great team in our Port Moresby office.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Coordinator plays a key role in our Port Moresby office supporting high-quality data collection, analysis and reporting across the organisation. This position works closely with the MEL Advisor and project teams to ensure monitoring systems are efficient, accurate and aligned with project outcomes and donor requirements
as we seek to impact lives and futures in remote and rural PNG.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
The role will be responsible for:
Work with the MEL Advisor to ensure timely and accurate reporting on all projects and in alignment with funding agreements and regulatory compliance;
Support the end-to-end M&E process across all projects, including coordination of planning, data collection, data management, analysis and reporting.
Assist in the design and administration of monitoring tools such as surveys and consultation guides, ensuring alignment with project indicators and donor requirements.
Coordinate logistics for data collection, including printing and packaging of monitoring tools, shipment to provinces, and providing technical support for in-field staff and partners.
Manage data quality processes including scanning, data entry and validation to ensure accuracy and completeness.
Conduct data analysis and contribute to interpretation of findings, including preparation of reports and data visualisations and key insights.
Contribute to quarterly reporting and the annual Effectiveness Results process by organising and presenting monitoring data.
Support in the management of KTF’s monitoring systems in Monday, Google Sheets, and Google Looker Studio (and others as developed/required)
Work with project teams to strengthen and streamline monitoring systems and promote consistent data collection practices across sites.
Assist in developing, maintaining and updating Monitoring & Evaluation Plans.
Support evaluation activities, including coordination of fieldwork logistics, preparation of data and evidence for evaluators.
Support impact reporting efforts, including managing, collating and filing case studies.
Provide training on MEL to partners and assist them with procedures to ensure efficiency of activities.
The role may be required to assist with some project support tasks.
The role may require assisting the Programs team with safeguarding, GEDSI and other cross-cutting issues.
YOUR SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES:
The ideal candidate will have:
A degree in a relevant field (social sciences, statistics, business, etc.)
A can-do attitude with fantastic problem-solving skills and thinks outside the box
Team player
Exceptional organisational skills
Advanced administrative skills – filing documents, scanning, printing, etc.
Ability to manage complex details across multiple projects
Ability to prioritise, think ahead, and use time management skills
Ability to work independently, as well as part of a team
Strong capability with the use of Microsoft Word/Google Docs, Excel/Google Sheets
Data Analysis skills – ability to analyse data sets in Excel/Sheets and understand data findings
Writing skills – ability to write engaging reports summarising findings, using quotes effectively
Familiarity with Dropbox and Google Drive
Ability to build a rapport with people and conduct interviews
Fluency in English & Tok Pisin – and the ability to translate documents
Ability to travel to remote and rural areas of Papua New Guinea.
Desired:
Some work experience (casual, part-time, or full-time)
Familiarity with survey platforms such as Google Forms, Kobotoolbox, Jotform, etc.
Interest or experience in community development or working in the NGO sector
Demonstrated research experience
Understanding of M&E principles
Willingness to work with remote teams in other locations in PNG and Australia

As part of the selection process, shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a skills assessment based on a realistic MEL task. This will involve analysing a small dataset and producing a short report that communicates key findings and recommendations. Further shortlisted applicants will then be invited for an interview.
The position is open to applicants based in Port Moresby who will work from our Port Moresby office. Domestic travel will be required from time to time. The position does not include housing or other benefits, nor support for relocation to Port Moresby if the successful applicant is not based there. We will prioritise Papua New Guinean applicants.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Superintendent – Mine Control, you will lead the optimisation of mine control operations, ensuring efficient fleet management and seamless coordination across departments. To succeed in this role, you will need to be a collaborative leader who actively breaks down silos, fosters strong cross-functional teamwork, and builds a culture of shared accountability. Just as importantly, you will be skilled in developing and empowering your team members—setting them up for success through coaching, support, and clear direction. Your leadership will directly influence safety, productivity, and cost-effectiveness across Newmont’s mining operations.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Oversee the health and performance of the Fleet Management System (FMS).
Plan and implement technical upgrades to maintain system integrity.
Collaborate with Operations and Maintenance to ensure accurate time usage data.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 18 Dispatchers, including training and performance management.
Ensure compliance with safety standards and project specifications.
Identify and mitigate operational risks.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Proven experience in fleet management and dispatch operations.
Proficiency with Dispatch 6 Modular is essential.
Strong technical knowledge of FMS and system maintenance.
Demonstrated leadership and team development skills.
Proficiency in risk management and contractor compliance.
Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration abilities.
Your Work Environment
This role is based in Lihir and we are flexible in considering residential housing options or FIFO roster arrangements for the right candidate.
Based at Newmont’s operational site.
Collaborative, safety-focused, and technologically advanced environment.
Cross-functional engagement with internal teams and external partners.
Leadership role with direct reports and strategic responsibilities.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in sustainable mining.
Work in a culture that values safety, inclusion, and innovation.
Access to professional development and career growth opportunities.
Competitive compensation and benefits.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 10 December 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

In this role you will assist the Mining Manager and Superintendents to provide medium, long term and /or strategic mine planning including underground mining optimization, design, production scheduling, cost estimations, underground expansion studies, administration of the computerized dispatch system, short term production and capital projects and to supervise, mentor and develop graduate mining engineers.

Complete to the required standards, all medium, long term and/or strategic mine planning activities for underground mine incline operations, including production scheduling, reconciliation, reporting, portal optimization, design, cost estimations, along with conduct of meetings, and supervision, development and mentoring of mine planning and projects graduate.

To be considered for this role it is essential that you must have a bachelor’s degree in mining engineering and must have mining operational experience with 5 years of technical experience in a similar role. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in mining engineering, preferably in an underground environment, with sound exposure to production activities including production planning.

Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational and administrative skills.

Experience in mining engineering, preferably in an underground environment, with sound exposure to production activities including production planning.
Strong computer skills with mine design (Surpac) and scheduling programs.
Sound knowledge of safe mining practices and standards in an underground Narrow Vein Mine.
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational and administrative skills.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role, you will manage the implementation and ongoing development of all aspects of processing training including safety, workplace inductions, personal development and training for personnel within the Process Plant.
To ensure that all activities meet the K92 Mining business needs and consistently high standards of occupational health, safety and environment are met, you will ensure the continuous improvement of safety best practice in line with K92 Mining Safety System and Environmental Policies and Procedures
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Manage scheduling of training for all Process plant personnel.
Co-ordinate or conduct Process Plant inductions and / or safety training
Maintain up to date training matrix for all Processing employees
Oversee graduate development programs within the Processing department
Monitor training provided for Processing personnel and develop effective training materials, evaluations and record keeping systems consistent with existing site document control.
Ensure accurate training records are maintained.
Accurately identify training requirements for all Processing personnel through effective Training Needs Analysis, Performance Management data and through liaison with key personnel and attending appropriate meetings.

Undertake the design and continuous development of training modules, materials, and procedures.
Liaise closely with the Coordinator Training and Development (Master Trainer) and other training personnel to maximise consistency and maintain a uniform approach to training across site.
Actively promote a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrate personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Possess an appropriate Trade Certification with a Diploma in Tech Teaching or a Certificate IV in Workplace Training
Have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in technical training role in a mineral processing plant.
Prior experience in a supervisory role.
Well-developed computer skills with competence in MS Office Suite and Pronto.
Well-developed interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills in English

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor - Registered Mine Electrician (RME) Delegate, you will play a critical role in ensuring electrical safety, compliance, and operational excellence across site operations. Your work will directly support a safe and efficient workplace by upholding standards, mentoring others, and maintaining regulatory compliance.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Conduct field critical control checks and ensure proper isolation processes.
Lead investigations into electrical safety incidents and implement corrective actions.
Authorize and issue electrical permits, access keys, and maintain compliance records.
Support training, coaching, and development of electrical personnel.
Ensure all electrical work meets Australian standards and Newmont specifications.
Liaise with departments to clarify site electrical requirements and standards.
Review and approve energization notifications and electrical licenses.
Participate in audits, risk assessments, and compliance documentation.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Qualifications: Certificate III in Electrotechnology is essential. A High Voltage Switching Certificate, LVR/CPR, and EEHA certification are preferred.
Licensing: PNG Power Authority or Australian/NZ State Electrical License is essential.
Knowledge: Familiarity with PNG Mining (Safety) Act, AS/NZS 3000, 3007, 4871, 3012, and 60079 standards is essential.
Skills: Strong problem-solving, practical judgment, and ability to work independently.
People Skills: Effective communicator, team collaborator, and adaptable to diverse work environments.
Your Work Environment
This role is based at Newmont’s Lihir Island site within the Asset Management team, supporting Fixed Plant Maintenance and Reliability. It is an individual contributor position focused on fieldwork, compliance, and stakeholder engagement.
For this opportunity, Lihir offers a 22:20 FIFO roster from a range of designated marshalling points. FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, with en-suited, air-conditioned rooms equipped with a mini fridge, TV, and Wi-Fi. Healthy meals are provided at the mess, and the wet mess offers a relaxed social setting with pool and darts. Recreational facilities include an on-site gym and basketball court, while paid members can enjoy the Lihir Sports and Social Club, featuring a swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, a restaurant/bar, and a deck with stunning Pacific Ocean views. A café and deli are also available for takeaway coffee, snacks, and groceries.
Newmont employees benefit from a competitive salary package, salary packaging options, and an annual incentive program.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in mining committed to safety, sustainability, and innovation.
Work in a collaborative environment that values your expertise and supports your growth.
Make a meaningful impact by ensuring the safety and reliability of critical infrastructure.
Access to ongoing training, development, and career advancement opportunities.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond.
We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 8th December 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated individual with strong leadership, capacity development abilities, program and grant management expertise, and technical experience in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) to join our team as the Senior Program Manager (SPM) for our East New Britain programs.
In line with the National WASH Policy (2015-2030), WaterAid is committed to supporting the Government of PNG to reach universal access to water, sanitation and hygiene. The SPM will support WaterAid’s East New Britain Program team through overseeing two key grants, the PacFresh H2O program
[1]
in Rabaul and Pomio Districts, and the KIWA initiative grant in Rabaul District.
The Senior Program Manager (SPM) will oversee a wide range of responsibilities, including leading program implementation, ensuring quality and compliance and managing a team of approximately 12 East New Britain based professionals. The role will involve close collaboration with local and national government partners, as well as WaterAid PNG Port Moresby based HQ and regional team based in Australia.
About the Grants
The SPM will also provide strategic and operational leadership for two key grants:
The
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
The
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Program Management
Be responsible for managing and reporting on all grant activities whilst building the grant and program management capacity of the team. To do this the SPM will work closely with Programs Team members, the Operations Team in PNG and the Program support team in WaterAid Australia Melbourne Office to ensure compliance with grant management requirements.
Ensure all WaterAid Programs are high quality from a WaSH technical and a development effectiveness perspective, reflecting latest evidence and thinking, and adapted to suit the PNG context.
The SPM reports to the Country Director in Port Moresby and as a member of the Senior Management Team, will support the Country Director in leading WaterAid PNG, and shaping our strategies and work with the sector.
Strengthen capacity of the WaterAid’s East New Britain team to manage and develop programs.
Ensure that programs and projects satisfy minimum criteria defined in WaterAid Guidelines and PNG Government policy, law and regulation and WaterAid’s Quality Program Standards.
Work with staff to prepare project plans and arrange team meetings to monitor progress and manage any risks that may be identified.
Ensure that Partner organisations and contractors are sensitised on approaches for ensuring that water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services are sustainable.
Support the strengthening of the sector based on clear objectives for improving local government capacity to increase access to WASH services.
Assist the Operations Manager and Country Director to monitor expenditure, manage fraud risks and ensure that WaterAid and donor standards regarding financial management are met by WaterAid staff and partner organisations.
Ensure timely processing of acquittals and follow up audit findings and recommendations, as appropriate.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge and Learning
Build capacity of the team to monitor and evaluate activities and foster a culture within the team conducive to learning, sharing and innovation.
Support advocacy work with partners and engage constructively with a range of stakeholders to progress advocacy objectives.
Facilitate reflection on project delivery and promote a culture of continuous learning among WaterAid staff and our partners.
Support the documentation of learning and work with the team to measure the impact of programs and the efficacy of program implementation.
Lead and coordinate the programs team in timely reporting, documenting progress and achievement of project outputs and outcomes in line with donor requirements.
Equity and Inclusion
Support partners and staff to engage effectively with women, people with disabilities and marginalised members of the community throughout project planning and review processes.
Identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.
Build the capacity and understanding of the WaterAid Team on gender, equity and inclusion and how to ensure WaterAid programs are inclusive.
Consult with the regional GEDSI Advisor on the equity and inclusion aspects of the work and ensure that WaterAid staff and external stakeholders are sensitive to gender and social inclusion considerations.
Promote a ‘Do No Harm’ approach amongst WaterAid staff and partners and ensure that referral pathways are accessible for stakeholders and beneficiaries.
Staff Management
Support and mentor the development of WaterAid staff and build their capacity, personal and professional development.
Conduct staff appraisals and provide ongoing, constructive feedback on staff performance and opportunities for growth and development.
Identify staff capacity development needs, prepare staff development plans and provide staff training in coordination with the Operations Manager and Country Director.
Promote a culture of respect, collaboration. Learning and sharing building on WaterAid’s values.
Ensure WaterAid security policy and protocols are adhered to by staff.
Partner Engagement
Maintain constructive working relationships with WaterAid’s local partners.
Attend regular meetings with partners to discuss project design and delivery, reflect on progress, identify risks and challenges and jointly propose solutions.
Coordinate field visits with partners and donors with sensitivity to security and accessibility issues.
Represent WaterAid through local sector coordination bodies.
The role requires engagement with a moderate degree of complexity, due to the need to:
Coordinate with multiple stakeholders, including formal program partners, as well as community leaders, traditional landowners and government agencies.
Assist the Country Director and Operations Manager with management of a large grant with complex financial and compliance requirements, with multiple separate activities
Ensure that risks concerning financial mismanagement and fraud are adequately managed.

ABOUT BALIMO COLLEGE:
Balimo College is Western Province’s newest Higher Education Institute. In 2025, Balimo College opened the new School of Nursing and commenced a 4-year Bachelor of General Nursing program. The College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality education, research and community engagement. The institute will foster pathways for teachers and nurses who are committed to improving access to vital services in Western Province.
Balimo College is a safe and supportive place for graduates and other professionals across the Western Province catchment region to return for life-long learning and ongoing professional development. The College will develop a community of education and health professionals committed to innovation, excellence and community advancement; by being the training College of choice for Papua New Guineans.
Balimo College is a PNG Sustainable Development Program (SDP) initiative delivered in partnership with KTF, Divine Word University, and Western Sydney University. Balimo College School of Nursing is an affiliate of Divine Word University.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Balimo College School of Nursing Deputy Principal is responsible for upholding the College’s Vision, Mission, Core Values, Educational Philosophy and Goals. The Deputy Principal will operate within the Balimo College School of Nursing leadership structure as determined by the Deputy Principal to disseminate strong, effective educational leadership, and manage all information technology within the parameters identified in this position description.
The Deputy Principal will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College School of Nursing and the principles by which it operates. The Deputy Principal will have a firm understanding of the Western Province health context and the objectives of Balimo College School of Nursing to create pathways for rural communities into the field of nursing.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
Applicants must demonstrate that they are able to meet the following Key Selection Criteria:
Master’s Level Health qualification.
Bachelor’s degree in nursing.
Education qualification.
Minimum 5 years of teaching experience.
Demonstrated strong leadership skills with experience in a leadership role.
Knowledge of a range of educational theories, techniques, and methodologies of personnel and management and a strong interest in current educational and technological trends.
Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills.
Be willing to relocate to Balimo College campus.
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
Knowledge of:
State-of-the-art theories, techniques, and methodologies of personnel and management.
Principles and practices of administration and supervision.
PNG Nursing Council Standards.
Bachelor of Nursing Curriculum.
DHERST requirements for a School of Nursing.

Provide leadership and direction to Staff.
Analyse problems, make decisions, and be responsible for those decisions.
Communicate effectively with staff, students and community.
Prepare comprehensive narrative reports.
Interpret, apply, and explain rules, regulations, policies, procedures and statistics.
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others.
Operate a computer to a high level of competence and other office equipment.
Analyse situations accurately and adopt an effective course of actions.
Meeting schedules and timelines.
Work independently with little direction.
Plan and organise work.
Personal Skills & Attributes:
Strong health education background.
Care for young people.
Intellectual capacity.
Proven ability to lead and work with teams.
Relational style which commands loyalty.
Problem solving ability.
Multi-tasking capability.
Strong interest in current educational trends.
High administrative ability.
Strong sense of justice.
Ability to confront difficult situations.
Resilience and energy.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Deputy Principal is responsible for:
Supporting the Principal in establishing and upholding a management vision for the Balimo College School of Nursing.
Exercising discernment and care in leading staff, students and parents.
Supporting the Principal in developing and leading a school executive team that will cultivate and strengthen a positive teaching, learning and working environment for all staff and students at every level of operations.

Human Resources

Administration

K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.

The successful person will lead and coordinate recruitment team reporting role. Partner with key internal stakeholders to provide effective recruitment services required for the delivery of the employee life cycle.
Key / Major Accountabilities

Develop appropriate social media to be used as sourcing tools and candidate database information.

jobs.title: Supervisor, Geotechnical Design Engineer
jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
Joining our geotechnical team, you will support safe and efficient mine operations by managing geotechnical hazards that could impact safety and business performance. Your expertise in slope design, stability analysis, and geotechnical data management will directly contribute to the success of short, medium, and long-term mine planning across the Lihir Operations.
As part of our team, you will
As a Supervisor (senior equivalent) Geotechnical Design Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping safe and efficient open-pit mining operations at Lihir. You will lead geotechnical investigations, deliver high-quality slope designs, and provide expert technical guidance that supports confident mine planning and risk management. This is an opportunity to influence major operational outcomes while developing and mentoring a high-performing technical team.
You will:
Provide technical expertise on pit slope design and slope management practices.
Collect, interpret, and analyse geotechnical data, including core logging, sampling, field testing, geological mapping, and UAV photogrammetry.
Conduct 2D and 3D slope stability modelling using software such as Rocscience suite (SLIDE2, SLIDE3D, RS2, RS3, DIPS, SWEDGE), FLAC 2D/3D (optional), GeoStudio, and other relevant tools.
Prepare detailed stability analysis reports and clearly communicate recommendations to support short, medium, and long-term mine planning.
Perform stability back-analysis for all fall-of-ground incidents and develop mitigation measures.
Support operational teams by integrating geotechnical monitoring data and contributing to risk management decisions.
Support mine operations in implementing and managing slope processes and systems, under the direction of the Geotechnical Superintendent.
Collaborate with consultants and stakeholders to collect data, refine models, and integrate monitoring information for long-term slope design and risk management.
Work with the Group Geotechnical team on slope designs with significant safety or operational implications, including LOPP and MTP projects.
Mentor and develop team members, graduates, and trainees in modelling, slope stability analysis, and geotechnical risk management.
Update and maintain geotechnical Ground Control Management Plan (GCMP).
Champion proactive safety behaviours and ensure full compliance with HSE standards.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You bring strong technical expertise in geology or engineering, with hands-on experience in open-cut mine sites in both soft and hard rock. Safety, leadership, and adaptability are at the core of your approach. You take ownership of outcomes, embrace challenges, and deliver results under pressure while developing and guiding your team.
You will also bring:
Tertiary qualification in Bachelor of Science (Geology) or Engineering (Civil or Mining).
Currently holds, or is willing to obtain, accreditation from the Institute of Engineers Papua New Guinea (IEPNG).
Postgraduate qualifications in geotechnical engineering or project management are desirable.
Extensive geotechnical management experience in open-pit mining operations, including time spent in senior-level roles.
Strong proficiency in geotechnical modelling software (Rocscience suite, GeoStudio; FLAC desirable).
Experience with geotechnical database management (e.g., acQuire) and geological/mine planning software (Leapfrog, MineSight preferred).
Highly proficient in MS Office applications, including advanced use of Excel for data analysis and reporting.
Strong leadership, coaching, and interpersonal skills; able to mentor teams while embodying Newmont’s values and vision.
Open-minded, adaptable, and able to take on diverse challenges with effective prioritisation and time management.
Comprehensive knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and regulations.
Excellent analytical, planning, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Your work environment
This role is based at Newmont’s Lihir Operations in Papua New Guinea and follows a 22:20 Fly-In, Fly-Out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island. The position primarily operates on a day shift, with occasional night shift callouts as required.
You will work closely with the Geotechnical, Mine Operations, and Planning teams in a dynamic open pit environment. The role provides exposure to technically challenging geotechnical conditions and offers the opportunity to influence large-scale, complex mining projects.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of one of the world’s leading gold mining companies with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and community.
Work within a collaborative team of technical specialists and leaders who value innovation and continuous improvement.
Access opportunities for professional development, career mobility, and leadership growth.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! You will ensure safe operations of the equipment to meet drilling targets and report any irregularities immediately, while upholding the Company’s Code of Conduct, by displaying the appropriate work attitude and teamwork.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate in compliance with site instructions, including Survey Memos, Geology direction, and Ground Support Standards.
Ensure equipment is safe to operate and kept in clean working order. Report any defects to the superintendent or fitters.
Report any accidents, incidents, or hazards to the superintendent immediately.
Assess ground conditions at the face and implement ground control according to site requirements.
Ensure compliance with all underground regulatory and mine standards.
Any other Mining Operations duties as delegated from time to time by the Mine Superintendent
Work closely with the Mining shift boss to assess performance and identify improvements to maximise results, reduce risk and minimise wastage of jumbo consumables.
Responsible for ongoing communication with supervisors.
Responsible for processing of detailed daily reports to the supervisors and his oncoming shift.
Responsible for housekeeping as per standard.
Maintain work relationship with all working crews during shift hours.
Responsible for stope charging, stope mining and rise mining.
Responsible for production drills – long holes.
Responsible for timbering and cable bolting.
Responsible to safely operate the equipment.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Possess current 5+ years plus of underground mining experience (Essential)
Must have a shot firers licenses or evidence to proof handling of explosives.
Must understand the different explosives and charging principles.
Relevant operating permits endorsed by the Site Registered Manager
Heavy Lifting/Manual Handling Training
Must have at least 3 or more years of Solo Operation on a production rig, pneumatic and or electric.
Must understand the critical components of the drill rig and the functions.
Must be trained and able to charge the drilled holes with explosives.
Has certified Miner certificate in area of handling hand drill machine.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.

jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:
Security and Safety Support
Under the direction of the Security Manager, the Field Security Officer (FSO) will perform descriptive and active functions by maintaining effective World Vision (WV) S&S policies and approved standard operating procedures (SOPs). The FSO must operate at an intermediate level of work practices, supporting the WV International Security Manager (SM) to ensure adherence to all security and safety protocols
Reporting Requirements
The FSO is to receive, analyze, advise, and disseminate all relevant S&S information to the Security Manager, WV staff, contractors attached to WV projects, and visitors. They are responsible for monitoring the security situation, advising the Security Manager of any major shifts in crime trends, and ensuring that all buildings are safe and secure daily. Additionally, the FSO assists with visits to WV properties for assessments and updates, manages incident reports in liaison with authorities, and maintains a tracking register of all WV staff and visitors.
Communication Requirements
The FSO will be required to establish and maintain an effective line of communication to WV staff, security providers, other NGOs, and visitors. They may also be required to conduct an S&S brief for visitors and the WV senior management team (SMT) when required.
Training and Compliance Requirements
The Field Security Officer (FSO) is responsible for completing all WV online security training courses and supporting the Security Manager in implementing Capacity Building Plan (CBP) topics and training activities. Key duties include maintaining compliance records such as Core Security Requirements (CSR), Security Risk Assessments (SRA), and Emergency Evacuation Contingency Plans (EECP), as well as updating training registers and spreadsheets. The FSO also provides safety briefs, issues building access cards, monitors CCTV serviceability, and conducts safety appliance checks. Additionally, they review CCTV footage for security incidents and attend SLT briefings in the Security Manager's absence to ensure seamless operations.
Educational Qualification/Skills, Knowledge & Experience
Graduated with a minimum grade 12 certificate qualification (original certificate required as proof).
Police / Law enforcement training
Minimum of five (5) years of work experience in the security industry either in a supervisory / management role
Proven experience in security field either in public, private, government or NGO Sector
Knowledge of First Aid. Certification in first Aid would be a bonus
Excellent verbal communication skills
At an intermediate level in English comprehension and writing (WV verbal and written test to be conducted)
Must hold a Valid passport and PNG Drivers License (Class 6, proof required)
Experience in teaching & training
Able to work under pressure
High Level of organization and Management skills
Willing to support the WV International Security Manager (SM) in maintaining effective World Vision (WV) S&S policies and approved standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Able to work competently and confidently with Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, PowerPoint, and Excel spreadsheets (IT test to be conducted).
Competent with all applications.
No criminal or traffic convictions (current police clearance required).
Disciplined & decent citizen.
Able to work on the weekends occasionally.
Working Environment / Conditions:
Work environment: Office-based 10%, field-based 90%.
Regular travel to project communities with overnight stays in the communities as required.
Ability to adapt to varying field conditions and maintain flexibility in challenging situations.
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.

Tebbutt Research PNG - Graduate Field Coordinator
Are you a young professional looking for an exciting and challenging career in the market and social research industry with a regional market leader and internationally recognised firm?
Do you have a degree qualification from a recognised university?
Do you have up to 2 years of commercial work experience?
Are you a motivated team player?
If this sounds like you, then you might be the person we are looking for!
The Company
Tebbutt Research is an ISO-20252-certified business that specialises in market and social research. We have been established for over 30 years and our clients include prominent multinational corporations, respected donor organizations and governments. We are the industry leader in the Pacific Islands, where we work across 22 countries. We have won numerous awards over the years and have a great, close-knit team and a supportive work culture.
Research fields include customer satisfaction, ad and communications testing, brand development, media ratings, segmentation studies, product testing, and monitoring and evaluation surveys. jobs.title: Logistics Supervisor
jobs.description:
Logistics Supervisor
Position Summary
The Logistics Supervisor
is responsible for coordinating the services in P.N.G to support the flow of materials for client projects on an end-to-end basis.
Position Responsibilities
The Logistics Supervisor is responsible and accountable for overseeing and coordinating all logistics operations to ensure the efficient and compliant movement of goods to and from project sites. This includes managing team performance, ensuring adherence to company procedures, and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders.
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to):
Supervise and coordinate the logistics team to ensure the efficient flow of goods from various origins to project sites, in line with delivery SOPs, including freight booking, document control, packing, storage, and quarantine compliance.
Oversee and confirm the arrival of goods at ports of import/export within PNG, ensuring clearance procedures are managed effectively in coordination with customs agents and service providers.
Monitor and review customs processes to ensure timely release of cargo, taking proactive measures to prevent delays, port storage, or detention costs.
Identify and implement improvements to streamline logistics operations and reduce cycle times between cargo arrival, customs clearance, and final delivery.
Maintain oversight of the release and movement of goods from wharf to site or warehouse, ensuring timely, accurate, and transparent status updates.
Supervise inspection activities, including visual checks and line-item verification to confirm cargo accuracy against packing lists and documentation.
Ensure compliance with domestic and international transport requirements, coordinating repacking, fumigation, or certification activities with relevant service providers as needed.
Coordinate and oversee import and export clearances, working closely with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and internal stakeholders to ensure documentation accuracy and timeliness.
Maintain and review shipment tracking reports, ensuring accurate and up-to-date visibility of cargo movement and performance metrics.
Ensure data integrity through accurate and timely entry of logistics information into internal systems, and review entries completed by the logistics team.
Oversee job file management, verifying the completeness and accuracy of records for invoicing, accruals, and third-party billing.
Support and guide the Logistics team, providing leadership, mentoring, and performance feedback to ensure consistent delivery of high-quality service.
Maintain professional communication with internal teams, clients, and service providers, proactively addressing and resolving operational or compliance issues.
Report to the Logistics Lead, providing regular operational updates, data insights, and recommendations for process improvement.
Selection Criteria – Essential
Strong planning, organizing, and attention to detail.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Strong communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently and within a team.
Selection Criteria – Desirable
+5 years operational experience in freight forwarding and customs clearance.
Familiarity with  logistics systems.
Experience working with shipping or freight forwarding companies.
Financial understanding of logistics cost drivers and structure.
Qualifications / Licences
Minimum Year 12 Accreditation
Current unrestricted drivers licence – Manual preferred

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our underground mining team, this role reports to the Shotcrete Supervisor and is required to ensure that all aspects of shotcrete spraying are carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate a shotcrete rig and underground equipment to apply fibrecrete
Inspect ground conditions,
Conduct QA/QC tests, maintain equipment, and support daily mining operations.
Work closely with the Mining shift boss to assess performance and identify improvements to maximise results, reduce risk and minimise wastage of consumables.
Responsible for ongoing communication with supervisors.
Responsible for processing of detailed daily reports to the supervisors and his oncoming shift.
Responsible for housekeeping as per standard.
Maintain work relationship with all working crews during shift hours.
Responsible to safely operate the equipment.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You

Experience in shotcrete spraying
Must have operating certificate.
Ability to work with close supervision.
Must have Underground Mining experience preferred.

K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
